title: [DEFERRED] Opt 9: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (IVF/HNSW)
description:
## Status: DEFERRED

This optimization is intentionally deferred. See rationale below.

## Overview (from PLAN Section 6 and 8)
Replace O(n) linear scan with O(√n) approximate nearest neighbor search using IVF (Inverted File Index) or HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World).

## Why Deferred

### 1. Precision Concerns
CASS is a precision-focused code search tool. Users expect exact results. Approximate search could return different results than exact search, which is unacceptable without explicit user opt-in.

### 2. Complexity vs Benefit
- Current optimizations (Opt 1-3) already achieve 20-30x speedup
- 56ms → 2-3ms with exact search preserved
- Additional speedup from ANN has diminishing returns

### 3. Implementation Effort
- HIGH effort: requires new index structure, rebuild logic, query path
- Lower confidence than other optimizations
- More testing burden for approximate equivalence

## Future Implementation Notes

If implemented later:
- **Require explicit opt-in**: `--approximate` flag
- **Show confidence/recall metrics** to user
- **Index format**: IVF with 100-1000 clusters or HNSW with M=16, efConstruction=200
- **Libraries**: Consider `hnsw` crate or implement from scratch

## Opportunity Matrix Score
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Impact | O(n) → O(√n) |
| Confidence | LOW |
| Effort | HIGH |
| Score | 2.0 (lowest) |

## Dependencies
- Should only consider after Opt 1-8 are complete and measured
- Part of Epic: coding_agent_session_search-rq7z
notes:
Implemented foundation for HNSW-based ANN:
- Added hnsw_rs dependency
- Created src/search/ann_index.rs with HnswIndex wrapper
- Added --approximate flag to Search command (CLI)
- Added --build-hnsw flag to Index command (CLI)
- Integrated HNSW building into semantic indexer
- Updated IndexOptions struct to include build_hnsw field
- All tests pass

Remaining work:
- Wire up --approximate flag to use HNSW at search time
- Implement proper HNSW loading (currently placeholder)
- Add recall/confidence metrics display
- Test with real datasets

title: [HIGH] atomic-swap publish retains every prior lexical index indefinitely under .lexical-publish-backups/
description:
INTRODUCED BY: commit 109560e5 (feat(indexer): atomic swap publish for staged lexical index with retained-backup rollback).

FILE: src/indexer/mod.rs

publish_staged_lexical_index() at line ~10720 renames the prior live lexical index into <index_parent>/.lexical-publish-backups/<unique-name> on every successful publish (both the Linux renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) path at lines ~10742-10767 and the non-Linux rename-based path at lines ~10772-10805). unique_lexical_publish_backup_path always produces a fresh path, so every publish adds ONE more retained copy of the entire prior Tantivy index tree. Nothing ever reads the backups_dir to prune. Verified via rg on src/ tests/: only ensure_lexical_publish_backups_dir and unique_lexical_publish_backup_path touch that directory, and neither removes anything.

IMPACT:
- Real cass corpora see ~50k+ docs per index per project (per project memory and ibuuh.29 E2E fixtures). A single Tantivy index at that scale is multi-hundred MB to multi-GB on disk.
- Over N rebuilds (full + stale-refresh + watch-triggered), disk usage under .lexical-publish-backups/ grows linearly and unboundedly. No log or status surface warns the operator.
- This silently regresses the user-visible promise of the original prior publish code, which deleted the old index.
- Operators on small dev workstations (SSDs, laptops) will exhaust disk within days of heavy indexing, breaking all subsequent writes — rebuild attempts fail with 'database is busy' / 'No space left' errors.

EXISTING COVERAGE GAPS:
- Neither test in the 109560e5 commit (publish_staged_lexical_index_replaces_live_index_and_retains_prior_backup, publish_staged_lexical_index_recovers_interrupted_backup_before_replacing_live_index) exercises a SECOND publish.
- No test asserts a retention cap, age-based prune, or ability-to-disable-retention knob.

PROPOSED FIX:
1. Introduce a bounded retention policy: keep only the last K backups (K=1 by default, configurable via env such as CASS_LEXICAL_PUBLISH_BACKUP_RETENTION). After a successful publish + backup retention, prune older backups beyond the cap.
2. Emit a structured tracing::info! event when a backup is pruned, including freed bytes so operators can correlate disk recovery.
3. Add a regression test that performs 3 successive publishes and asserts the backup count stays bounded.

RELATED:
- Discovered during the test-green-gate cross-review for bead 3e3qg.6 on 2026-04-23.
- Affects every code path that calls publish_staged_lexical_index (rebuild_tantivy_from_db_via_staged_shards and downstream callers).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2ae0018a: bounded retention for .lexical-publish-backups/ with CASS_LEXICAL_PUBLISH_BACKUP_RETENTION env knob (default 1, 0=disabled, N=keep-most-recent). New prune_lexical_publish_backups() runs after each successful publish, sorts by mtime newest-first, removes excess, emits structured tracing::info! with freed_bytes per pruned backup + final summary. Regression tests: _prunes_retained_backups_to_default_retention_cap (4 publishes with default cap 1 → exactly 1 retained) and _retention_cap_is_env_configurable (cap=0 and cap=3 with 5 publishes each → exactly 0 and 3 retained). Two existing serial tests updated to set env=2 internally to preserve their recovery-semantics invariants. All 10 publish_staged_lexical_index tests pass; prune failure is non-fatal (logged warn only) so publish never fails due to hygiene issues.

title: [Task] Opt 8.1: Design streaming indexing architecture
description:
## Objective
Design the streaming architecture for per-connector data flow with backpressure.

## Design Tasks
1. Map current batch collection flow
2. Identify all connectors and their batch generation patterns
3. Design channel topology (fan-in from N connectors to 1 consumer)
4. Determine optimal channel buffer size
5. Design error propagation strategy
6. Ensure deterministic ordering for reproducible indices

## Architecture Decisions

### Channel Sizing
- Too small: Producer stalls frequently, poor throughput
- Too large: Defeats purpose of backpressure
- Recommendation: 16-64 based on typical batch sizes

### Ordering Strategy
Options:
1. **No ordering guarantee** - fastest, but may affect reproducibility
2. **Per-connector ordering** - maintain order within connector, interleave across
3. **Global ordering** - sequence numbers, more complex

### Error Handling
- Producer error → send error on channel → consumer aborts
- Consumer error → drop receiver → producers unblock and exit
- Timeout handling for slow connectors

## Output
- Architecture diagram
- Channel sizing rationale
- Ordering guarantee specification
- Error handling matrix

## Parent Feature
coding_agent_session_search-ug6i (Opt 8: Streaming Backpressure)

title: P1.2 Add sources table to SQLite
description:
# Add sources Table to SQLite Storage

## Context
We need a place to persist Source configurations. Each source (local, work-laptop, etc.) has metadata that should survive restarts.

## Location
src/storage/sqlite.rs

## Schema
\`\`\`sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sources (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- source_id (e.g., "local", "work-laptop")
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,            -- "local", "ssh", etc.
    host_label TEXT,               -- display label
    machine_id TEXT,               -- optional stable machine id
    platform TEXT,                 -- "macos", "linux", "windows"
    config_json TEXT,              -- JSON blob for extra config (SSH params, path rewrites)
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
\`\`\`

## Bootstrap
On DB creation, automatically insert the "local" source:
\`\`\`sql
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO sources (id, kind, host_label, created_at, updated_at)
VALUES ('local', 'local', NULL, strftime('%s','now')*1000, strftime('%s','now')*1000);
\`\`\`

## API Methods
Add to SqliteStorage:

\`\`\`rust
/// Get source by ID
pub fn get_source(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Source>>;

/// List all sources
pub fn list_sources(&self) -> Result<Vec<Source>>;

/// Create or update a source
pub fn upsert_source(&self, source: &Source) -> Result<()>;

/// Delete a source (and optionally cascade to conversations)
pub fn delete_source(&self, id: &str, cascade: bool) -> Result<()>;
\`\`\`

## Migration
This is a new table, so it's additive. The migration path is:
1. Check if sources table exists
2. If not, create it
3. Insert "local" source if not present

No need for table rewrite - this is purely additive.

## Schema Version
Bump SCHEMA_VERSION in sqlite.rs

## Dependencies
- P1.1 (Source types must exist)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] sources table created on init
- [ ] "local" source auto-created
- [ ] CRUD methods implemented
- [ ] Schema version bumped
- [ ] Tests for source CRUD
close_reason: Added sources table to SQLite with MIGRATION_V4. Schema version bumped to 4. Implemented get_source, list_sources, upsert_source, delete_source methods. Local source auto-created on DB init. 28 storage tests pass, all 281 tests pass.

title: Port PRAGMA/WAL/connection configuration to frankensqlite
description:
TRACK: cass storage migration (Track 3B)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensqlite Integration

WHAT: Port the PRAGMA and connection configuration from rusqlite to frankensqlite, and determine the optimal storage backend configuration.

CURRENT CONFIGURATION (src/storage/sqlite.rs lines 3844-3865):
- PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL
- PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL
- PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 1000
- PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY
- PRAGMA cache_size = -65536 (64MB)
- PRAGMA mmap_size = 268435456 (256MB)
- PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON
- conn.busy_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))

DEEP AUDIT FINDING (2026-02-27):
frankensqlite's storage architecture is fundamentally different from C SQLite:
- Phase 4 (current default): in-memory MemDatabase with file snapshot persistence
- Phase 5 (exists but not yet default): pager/WAL/B-tree layers
- MVCC with SSI is the concurrency model — WAL semantics are different
- PRAGMAs are executed via conn.execute("PRAGMA ...") as SQL strings
- Not all C SQLite PRAGMAs may be implemented or meaningful

This means PRAGMA porting is NOT a simple 1:1 mapping. Many PRAGMAs may be no-ops or errors.

STORAGE BACKEND DECISION (depends on 3vvqa gate result):
If frankensqlite can open existing C SQLite WAL-mode files:
  -> Use Phase 5 pager (file-format compatible) for existing databases
  -> Configure PRAGMAs that Phase 5 supports
If frankensqlite CANNOT open existing files:
  -> Use Phase 4 (in-memory) for new databases
  -> Build migration tool to transfer data from old to new format

3. What is frankensqlite's equivalent of WAL mode?

4. What happens when you set a PRAGMA it doesn't support? (error? silent ignore? panic?)
5. Does busy_timeout have meaning with MVCC? (With BEGIN CONCURRENT, the retry strategy is different)

2. Document results in the bead (update this description)
3. Implement FrankenStorage::apply_config() with only the PRAGMAs that work
4. Skip PRAGMAs that are no-ops in frankensqlite (document why with comments)

## Overview

```css
@media print {
  /* Hide interactive elements */
  .collapse-toggle, .copy-btn, .search-controls { display: none !important; }

  body { background: white !important; color: black !important; }

title: Add InMemoryVectorIndex to frankensearch-index for zero-latency TUI search
description:
TRACK: frankensearch upstream (Track 1A)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensearch Integration

WHAT: Add an in-memory vector storage backend to frankensearch-index. This is CONFIRMED as not existing — frankensearch currently only has file-backed FSVI (memory-mapped) via VectorIndex.

WHY THIS IS NEEDED (not just FSVI mmap):
- Cass TUI loads ALL embeddings into RAM at startup for deterministic sub-millisecond search
- FSVI mmap has page fault latency on first access (cold paths), unacceptable for TUI responsiveness
- Cass's current TwoTierIndex in two_tier_search.rs stores f16 vectors in a flat Vec<half::f16> for guaranteed-resident brute-force scan
- frankensearch's VectorIndex uses MmapMut (file-backed), which can page fault
- InMemoryVectorIndex would give frankensearch a fully-resident search path

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE:
- VectorIndex struct has: path, data (MmapMut), metadata, records_offset, strings_offset, vectors_offset, wal_entries
- TwoTierIndex wraps two VectorIndex instances (fast + quality), both file-backed
- TwoTierIndex.search_fast() is SYNC and takes &[f32] query vectors (converts internally)
- No in-memory alternative exists anywhere in frankensearch

DESIGN:
- New struct InMemoryVectorIndex that stores vectors in contiguous resident memory (not mmap)
- Constructor: InMemoryVectorIndex::from_fsvi(path) — reads FSVI file entirely into heap-allocated memory
- Constructor: InMemoryVectorIndex::from_vectors(doc_ids: Vec<String>, vectors: Vec<Vec<f32>>, dimension: usize)
- Search API: search_top_k(query: &[f32], k: usize, filter: Option<&dyn SearchFilter>) -> SearchResult<Vec<VectorHit>>
- Internal storage: f16 quantized row-major flat layout (matching cass's current approach for 50% memory savings)
- Brute-force dot product with optional Rayon parallelism above threshold (10K+ vectors)
- Must implement same VectorHit result type as file-backed VectorIndex

ALSO NEEDED: InMemoryTwoTierIndex that wraps two InMemoryVectorIndex instances (fast + quality) with the same search_fast() / quality_scores_for_hits() API as TwoTierIndex.

PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS:
- Must match or exceed cass's current two_tier_search.rs in-memory search latency
- f16 quantization: store as f16, convert to f32 only during dot product
- Parallel threshold: 10,000 vectors (matching frankensearch's FSVI default)
- Binary heap top-k selection (matching cass's current approach)

FILES TO CREATE: frankensearch-index/src/in_memory.rs
FILES TO MODIFY: frankensearch-index/src/lib.rs (pub mod, re-export)
FILES TO MODIFY: frankensearch/src/lib.rs (re-export InMemoryVectorIndex, InMemoryTwoTierIndex)

TESTS: from_fsvi loading matches file-backed search results, from_vectors construction, search_top_k correctness vs reference f32, f16 precision tolerance (<0.001), parallel search, filter integration, empty index edge case, dimension mismatch error.
close_reason: Completed: wired in-memory index exports and added from_fsvi parity test in frankensearch

title: Unit tests for frankensqlite adapter layer and migration framework
description:
TRACK: frankensqlite upstream prep (Track 3A)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensqlite Integration

WHAT: Comprehensive unit tests for the frankensqlite compat adapter layer and migration framework.

TEST PLAN:

1. PARAMS MACRO:
   - params![1i64, \"hello\", 3.14f64] produces correct SqliteValue array
   - params![] produces empty array
   - params![None::<i64>] produces SqliteValue::Null
   - params![true] produces SqliteValue::Integer(1)
   - params![false] produces SqliteValue::Integer(0)
   - params![vec![1u8, 2, 3]] produces SqliteValue::Blob

2. FROM IMPLS:
   - From<bool>: true → Integer(1), false → Integer(0)
   - From<Option<i64>>: Some(42) → Integer(42), None → Null
   - From<u32>, From<u64>: correct conversion (with overflow check for u64 > i64::MAX)
   - From<usize>: correct conversion

3. TYPED ROW EXTRACTION (RowExt):
   - row.get_typed::<i64>(0) on Integer column → correct value
   - row.get_typed::<String>(1) on Text column → correct value
   - row.get_typed::<Option<i64>>(2) on NULL → None
   - row.get_typed::<f64>(0) on Integer column → type coercion (or error)
   - row.get_typed::<i64>(99) → index out of bounds error
   - row.get_typed::<bool>(0) on Integer(1) → true, Integer(0) → false

4. QUERY WITH CLOSURE (ConnectionExt):
   - query_row_map: returns closure-transformed value
   - query_map_collect: returns Vec of closure-transformed values
   - query_row_map on empty result → QueryReturnedNoRows error
   - query_map_collect on empty result → empty Vec (not error)

5. EXECUTE_BATCH:
   - Multi-statement SQL separated by ';': all statements execute
   - SQL with comments (-- and /* */): handled correctly
   - Empty string: no-op, no error
   - Single statement without ';': executes correctly
   - PRAGMA blocks (typical cass usage): all PRAGMAs applied

6. TRANSACTION:
   - transaction() + commit() → changes persist (verified by re-query)
   - transaction() + drop (no commit) → changes rolled back
   - execute within transaction → works correctly
   - query_row_map within transaction → works correctly
   - Error during transaction → clean rollback on drop

7. OPTIONAL EXTENSION:
   - Ok(value).optional() → Ok(Some(value))
   - Err(QueryReturnedNoRows).optional() → Ok(None)
   - Err(other_error).optional() → Err(other_error) (passes through)

8. OPEN FLAGS:
   - open_with_flags(READ_ONLY) → writes fail with appropriate error
   - open_with_flags(READ_WRITE | CREATE) → creates new DB
   - open_with_flags(READ_WRITE) on existing DB → succeeds

9. PARAMS_FROM_ITER:
   - params_from_iter(vec![1i64, 2, 3]) → correct Vec<SqliteValue>
   - params_from_iter(std::iter::empty()) → empty Vec
   - params_from_iter(mixed types via Into<SqliteValue>) → correct conversion

10. MIGRATION FRAMEWORK:
    - Fresh DB: all migrations applied in order (V1, V2, ..., V13)
    - Existing DB at V5: only V6-V13 applied
    - Idempotent: running twice applies nothing second time
    - Failed migration: rolls back, version unchanged, error reported
    - Migration result: applied list, current version, was_fresh flag all correct

11. RUSQLITE PARITY (golden test):
    - For 10 representative SQL patterns from cass, execute via both rusqlite and compat adapter
    - Compare results: row counts, column values, NULL handling
    - Patterns: INSERT, SELECT with JOIN, UPDATE, DELETE, UPSERT, GROUP BY + HAVING, FTS5 MATCH, LIKE, subquery

FILES: frankensqlite/fsqlite/tests/compat_tests.rs, frankensqlite/fsqlite/tests/migration_tests.rs

title: Wire SyncTwoTierSearcher into production search pipeline (Phase 2 - optional)
description:
TRACK: cass enhancement (optional)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensearch Integration

OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENT: Wire frankensearch's SyncTwoTierSearcher into cass's production search pipeline to enable progressive two-tier search in the TUI.

PREREQUISITES:
- Phase 1 bead (2fu7e) must be complete (internal TwoTierSearcher delegated to frankensearch)
- SyncTwoTierSearcher must exist in frankensearch-fusion (bead cgh4s)
- InMemoryVectorIndex/InMemoryTwoTierIndex must exist (bead 14mzc)

WHAT THIS DOES:
1. Modify search_semantic() in query.rs to optionally use SyncTwoTierSearcher instead of single-tier VectorIndex.search_top_k()
2. Add progressive delivery: show fast results immediately in TUI, refine when quality tier completes
3. Use SyncSearchIterator for TUI polling: next() returns Phase 1 (fast), then Phase 2 (quality-refined)
4. This improves search result quality by blending fast + quality tier scores

CURRENT STATE: Production semantic search at query.rs:2280 uses fs_index.search_top_k(&embedding, fetch, fs_filter) — single-tier, no progressive refinement.

NEW BEHAVIOR (with this bead):
- TUI search calls SyncTwoTierSearcher.search_iter()
- Phase 1 (fast): sub-10ms, f16 brute-force, shows results immediately
- Phase 2 (quality): 50-200ms, full embedding comparison, re-ranks results

title: Fix Windows binary builds in CI release pipeline (GH#66)
description:
## Problem

Windows binaries are missing from v0.1.63 and v0.1.64 releases. Scoop install and PowerShell install script both 404. The CI release workflow at `.github/workflows/release.yml` includes a Windows matrix entry (lines 51-55: `os: windows-latest, target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) but the artifacts are not appearing in releases.

## Investigation Plan

### 1. Check GH Actions run logs for recent release tags

Run `gh run list --workflow=release.yml -L 5` to see if Windows jobs failed or were skipped. Check `gh run view <id> --log-failed` for the specific Windows job.

### 2. Common Windows build failure modes

- **fastembed/ort ONNX runtime**: The project uses `fastembed` (Cargo.toml line 70) with `ort-download-binaries` feature. ONNX runtime download can fail on Windows runners due to network timeouts or path length issues.
- **Nightly vs stable toolchain**: Recent commit `59835155` switched from nightly to stable. If the Cargo.toml uses nightly-only features, Windows builds could fail silently.
- **PowerShell script syntax**: The Windows zip creation step (release.yml:91-104) uses PowerShell. Check for encoding issues with `Out-File -Encoding ASCII`.

### 3. Potential fixes

- Add `continue-on-error: false` to Windows build step to ensure failures are visible
- Add explicit error checking after the Compress-Archive step
- Verify ONNX runtime downloads work on windows-latest runner
- Test with `cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` locally via cross-compilation or CI debug run

### 4. Install script verification

Check `install.ps1` exists at repo root and correctly constructs download URLs for the Windows zip artifact.

## Files to Investigate

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` lines 51-55 (Windows matrix), 91-104 (Windows packaging)
- `Cargo.toml` line 70 (fastembed/ort dependency)
- `install.ps1` (PowerShell installer)
- `src/lib.rs:11245-11260` (Windows self-update code path)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Windows binary (cass.exe) present in next release
2. `cass-windows-amd64.zip` and `.sha256` artifacts attached to release
3. Scoop install succeeds: `scoop install cass`
4. PowerShell installer succeeds: `irm install.ps1 | iex`
5. Windows CI job completes successfully (not skipped, not failed)
6. Self-update from Windows works: `cass --update`
notes:
## Diagnostic Steps

1. `gh run list --workflow=release.yml -R Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search -L 5` -- check if Windows job shows as failed/skipped
2. `gh run view <latest-release-run-id> --log-failed` -- get actual error message
3. `gh release view v0.1.64 --json assets -q '.assets[].name'` -- confirm what artifacts exist

## CI Verification

After fix, trigger a test release:
1. Create a pre-release tag: `git tag v0.1.65-rc1 && git push --tags`
2. Monitor: `gh run watch`
3. Verify Windows artifacts: `gh release view v0.1.65-rc1 --json assets -q '.assets[] | select(.name | contains("windows"))'`
4. Download and test: `gh release download v0.1.65-rc1 -p "cass-windows-amd64.zip"`

2. Test Scoop manifest: verify JSON points to correct URL and SHA256
3. Test PowerShell installer: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.ps1 | iex`

title: [Feature] Performance Metrics Collection
description:
## Feature: Performance Metrics Collection

Emit performance metrics during E2E tests for regression detection.

### Metrics to Collect
| Metric | Unit | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `indexing_duration_ms` | ms | Time to index test corpus |
| `search_latency_p50_ms` | ms | Median search query time |
| `search_latency_p99_ms` | ms | 99th percentile search time |
| `memory_peak_kb` | KB | Peak memory usage |
| `index_size_bytes` | bytes | Size of search index |
| `files_processed` | count | Number of files indexed |
| `queries_per_second` | qps | Search throughput |

### Implementation
```rust
// In tests/util/e2e_log.rs
pub fn emit_metric(name: &str, value: f64, unit: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let event = json\!({
        "ts": Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),
        "event": "metric",
        "name": name,
        "value": value,
        "unit": unit,
        "run_id": run_id()
    });
    writeln\!(log_file(), "{}", event)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### Usage
```rust
let start = Instant::now();
indexer.index_all()?;
emit_metric("indexing_duration_ms", start.elapsed().as_millis() as f64, "ms")?;
```

### Baseline Tracking
- Store baselines in `test-results/baselines.json`
- Alert if metric exceeds baseline by >20%
- Update baseline after confirmed improvements

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `emit_metric` function in e2e_log
- [ ] 7 metrics collected per E2E run
- [ ] Baseline comparison implemented
- [ ] Alert on regression >20%
- [ ] Metrics visible in JSONL output

title: Cursor-Based Pagination
description:
# Cursor-Based Pagination

## Problem Statement
Offset-based pagination (`--offset N`) has issues:
- Results can shift if index changes between pages
- Hard to track position reliably
- Inefficient for large offsets

## Proposed Solution
Add cursor-based pagination:
```bash
cass search "error" --json --limit 10
# Returns: {"next_cursor": "abc123", "hits": [...]}

cass search "error" --json --limit 10 --cursor "abc123"
# Returns next page
```

## Design Decisions

### Cursor Encoding
Cursor contains:
- Query hash (to validate same query)
- Last seen sort key (score + id)
- Expiration timestamp

Encoded as base64 for URL safety.

### Cursor Expiration
Cursors expire after 1 hour to prevent stale state issues.

### Fallback
If cursor is invalid/expired, return error with hint to restart.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--cursor` parameter for continuing pagination
- [ ] `next_cursor` in response when more results available
- [ ] Cursor validates query hasn't changed
- [ ] Expired cursors return clear error
- [ ] Works with all output formats

## Effort Estimate
Medium - 3-4 hours. Requires cursor encoding and validation logic.

title: [P3] Opt 8: Streaming Backpressure for Indexing
description:
# Optimization 8: Streaming Backpressure for Indexing

## Problem Statement

Current indexing collects ALL `pending_batches` from ALL connectors before starting ingestion:

### Current Flow
```
1. Discover all sources (Claude, Cursor, Gemini, etc.)
2. For each source: scan filesystem, parse JSONLs, collect batches
3. Store ALL batches in memory
4. Ingest ALL batches into Tantivy + SQLite
```

### Memory Impact
- 3000 conversations × 12 messages = 36,000 messages in memory
- Peak RSS: 295 MB (from profiling)
- All data must fit in RAM before processing starts

### Allocation Profile Evidence
```
Indexing total allocated: ~1,375 MB for 36k messages
```

This is well above the 295 MB peak RSS because of:
- Batch collection → ingestion → deallocation cycle
- Rust's allocator holding onto freed pages

## Proposed Solution

Stream per-connector with bounded channel to single ingest worker.

### Architecture
```
┌───────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐
│ Claude Conn.  │────▶│               │     │               │
├───────────────┤     │   Bounded     │────▶│   Ingest      │
│ Cursor Conn.  │────▶│   Channel     │     │   Worker      │
├───────────────┤     │   (N=100)     │     │               │
│ Gemini Conn.  │────▶│               │     │               │
└───────────────┘     └───────────────┘     └───────────────┘
     Producers             Buffer              Consumer
```

### Implementation Location
- File: `src/indexing/mod.rs` (or wherever batch coordination happens)
- Modify connector → ingestion flow

### Code Sketch
```rust
use std::sync::mpsc::{sync_channel, SyncSender, Receiver};
use std::thread;

const BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 100;

struct StreamingIndexer {
    tx: SyncSender<ConversationBatch>,
    ingest_handle: thread::JoinHandle<Result<IndexStats>>,
}

impl StreamingIndexer {
    fn new(tantivy_index: TantivyIndex, sqlite_conn: Connection) -> Self {
        let (tx, rx) = sync_channel(BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE);
        
        let ingest_handle = thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut stats = IndexStats::default();
            for batch in rx {
                // Ingest one batch at a time
                tantivy_index.add_conversation(&batch)?;
                sqlite_conn.insert_conversation(&batch)?;
                stats.conversations += 1;
                stats.messages += batch.messages.len();
            }
            Ok(stats)
        });
        
        Self { tx, ingest_handle }
    }

    fn send_batch(&self, batch: ConversationBatch) -> Result<()> {
        // Blocks if channel is full (backpressure!)
        self.tx.send(batch)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn finish(self) -> Result<IndexStats> {
        drop(self.tx); // Signal completion
        self.ingest_handle.join().unwrap()
    }
}

// Usage in connector
for conversation in claude_connector.discover() {
    let batch = parse_conversation(conversation)?;
    streaming_indexer.send_batch(batch)?;  // Blocks if ingest is slow
}
```

### Backpressure Mechanism
- `sync_channel(100)` creates a bounded channel
- When buffer is full, `send()` blocks the producer
- This prevents memory from growing unboundedly
- Connectors automatically slow down when ingestion is the bottleneck

## Expected Impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Peak RSS | 295 MB | ~100-150 MB |
| Total alloc | 1,375 MB | ~same (but spread over time) |
| Memory spikes | Large | Controlled |
| Indexing latency | ~same | ~same (possibly +5% overhead) |

The main benefit is **predictable memory usage**, not speed improvement.

## Risk: Ordering Changes

### The Risk
If ingestion becomes interleaved differently (e.g., Claude batch 1, Cursor batch 1, Claude batch 2), the order of database inserts may change.

### Impact Analysis
- **Search results**: Unaffected (ordering by score, not insert order)
- **Message IDs**: May differ between runs (if auto-increment)
- **Tie-breaking**: If messages have same score and different IDs, order may change

### Mitigation
- Ensure stable sort with secondary key (e.g., source_path + timestamp)
- Document that message IDs are not stable across reindexing
- Add equivalence test comparing search results (not IDs)

## Isomorphism (Relaxed)

This optimization has **weaker** guarantees than others:
- Same **set** of indexed content
- Potentially different **ordering** of inserts
- Same **search results** (hit set, not necessarily order for tied scores)

### Property to Preserve
```
∀ query: set(search(query).hits.message_id) ≡ set(search_streaming(query).hits.message_id)
```

Note: This is set equality, not sequence equality.

## Implementation Complexity

This is rated **HIGH effort** because:
1. Significant architectural change to indexing flow
2. Need to handle errors in worker thread
3. Progress reporting becomes async
4. Cancellation handling
5. Testing concurrent code

## Verification Plan

1. **Metamorphic test**: Batch vs streaming indexing yield same search results
2. **Memory test**: Peak RSS stays below threshold during streaming
3. **Stress test**: Large corpus (100k messages) doesn't OOM
4. **Cancellation test**: Ctrl-C during indexing doesn't corrupt index

## Rollback Strategy

Feature flag `CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=0` (or `1` to enable) to:
- Revert to batch collection mode
- Useful if streaming introduces bugs

## Dependencies

- None technically, but should be implemented after P0/P1 optimizations are stable
- Lower priority because memory usage is acceptable currently (295 MB)
- Consider only if targeting memory-constrained environments

# Search UI Component

**Parent Phase:** Phase 3: Web Viewer
**Depends On:** P3.3 (sqlite-wasm Integration)

## Goal

Build the search interface with query input, agent/time/workspace filters, and virtualized result list.

Main responsibilities:
- Query input with debounce
- Agent/time/workspace filter dropdowns
- FTS5 query routing (natural language vs code search)
- Virtual scrolling for large result sets
- Click handling to open conversations

### FTS5 Query Strategy

Two indexes serve different search patterns:
1. messages_fts (porter stemmer): English prose
2. messages_code_fts (unicode61): snake_case, paths

Auto-detect based on query pattern (/[_.]|[a-z][A-Z]/).

### FTS5 Query Escaping (Critical)

Wrap terms in double-quotes to prevent injection:
"term1" "term2" instead of raw input.

### Virtual List for Performance

For 10K+ results, only render visible items:
- Track scroll position
- Calculate visible range
- Render buffer items above/below
- Transform content position

### Snippet Display

Use FTS5 snippet() function for context:
snippet(table, 0, "<mark>", "</mark>", "...", 64)

## Test Cases

1. Empty search shows recent conversations
2. Text search returns FTS5 results
3. Agent filter limits results
4. Time filter limits results
5. Code patterns route to code FTS
6. FTS5 special chars escaped
7. Virtual scroll handles 10K+ results

- src/pages_assets/search.js
- src/pages_assets/fts-utils.js
- src/pages_assets/virtual-list.js

## Exit Criteria

1. Search input works
2. Filters work independently and combined
3. Results render with snippets
4. Virtual scrolling smooth for large sets
5. FTS5 queries do not throw errors
6. Click on result opens conversation

title: Phase 6: Workspace Path Rewriting (Optional Enhancement)
description:
# Phase 6: Workspace Path Rewriting (Optional Enhancement)

## Overview
When sessions are synced from remote machines, the workspace paths in conversations
refer to the remote filesystem (e.g., /home/user/projects/foo on remote, but
/Users/me/projects/foo on local). This phase adds optional path rewriting rules
so that file references in search results point to valid local paths.

## Goals
1. Define path mapping rules in source configuration
2. Apply mappings when displaying results (not when indexing)
3. Provide fallback behavior when mapping unavailable

## Example Configuration
```toml
[[sources]]
name = "laptop"
host = "user@laptop.local"
[sources.path_mappings]
"/home/user/projects" = "/Users/me/projects"
"/opt/work" = "/Volumes/Work"
```

## Technical Considerations
- Mappings applied at display time, not storage (preserve original data)
- Multiple mappings may match; use longest prefix match
- Unmapped paths displayed as-is with visual indicator

## Why Optional
This feature is complex and may not be needed by all users. Some users may prefer
to see original paths. Making it opt-in reduces confusion.

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 5 completion (sources config exists)
- Could be deferred to post-MVP

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Path mappings configurable per source
- [ ] Mappings applied to displayed workspace paths
- [ ] Unmapped paths clearly indicated
- [ ] Original paths preserved in storage
- [ ] Documentation explains mapping syntax

title: export-html: message count is highly misleading (reports 577 for a 19-turn conversation)
description:
## Problem

`cass export-html` reports '577 messages' for a session that had 19 actual human turns. The count includes tool call results (267), assistant responses (408), system injections, and progress events. This is highly misleading to both humans and agents.

## Root Cause

`lib.rs:12404`: `let message_count = messages.len()` counts ALL messages that pass the filter (user + assistant + system + tool roles). It doesn't distinguish between human-typed prompts and tool result returns.

The filter at `lib.rs:12346-12401` correctly excludes empty messages and non-message records (queue-operation, etc.), but still includes:
- 267 tool_result messages (automatic returns from tool calls)
- 408 assistant messages (each tool call generates one)
- 30 system messages (hook injections)

## Fix

Report multiple counts in the metadata:
- `conversation_turns`: Count of human-typed user messages (exclude tool_result content blocks)
- `tool_calls`: Count of messages with tool_call data
- `total_rendered`: Current count (for internal use)

Display in the HTML header as: '19 turns, 284 tool calls' instead of '577 messages'.

The key heuristic: a 'user' role message is a human turn ONLY if its content is NOT a list of tool_result blocks. In Claude Code JSONL, tool results come back as user messages with `content: [{type: 'tool_result', ...}]`.

## Files

- `src/lib.rs:12346-12404` (message filtering + counting)
- `src/html_export/template.rs:459-463` (display rendering)
close_reason: Fixed: shows 'N turns, M tool calls' instead of misleading total message count

Design responsive breakpoints: (1) Wide (>=160 cols): side-by-side results + detail panes (current horizontal split), (2) Medium (100-159 cols): stacked results/detail with adjustable ratio, (3) Narrow (<100 cols): single pane with tab switching. The current layout hardcodes Percentage(70)/Percentage(30) for results/detail based on focus -- replace with grow factors that smoothly animate between states. Also use Flex gap for consistent spacing between sections. This makes cass look great on any terminal size from 80x24 to ultrawide.

title: Fix results PageUp/PageDown to page selection deterministically
description:
## Goal
Make results-surface `PageUp`/`PageDown` navigation deterministic and user-visible by advancing selection page-wise while keeping viewport/scroll state coherent.

## Background
During post-close revalidation of the FrankenTUI results regression suite, we confirmed a semantics mismatch:
- `CassMsg::PageScrolled` currently manipulates virtualized scroll state, then synchronizes selection from stale state.
- In practice this can behave like a weak/no-op page action depending on viewport initialization and subsequent selection syncing.

Users expect page keys to provide clear navigation progress (selection + viewport movement), especially in long result lists.

## Scope
- Update results-focus handling for `CassMsg::PageScrolled` in `src/ui/app.rs` so page navigation:
  - advances/retreats selection by one viewport page (with clamped bounds),
  - keeps virtualized list offset consistent with selected row visibility,
  - remains deterministic before and after render cycles.
- Preserve existing detail-pane page scroll behavior (`FocusRegion::Detail`) unchanged.
- Keep `Home/End` semantics unchanged.

## Test Plan
Add/adjust unit tests in `src/ui/app.rs` covering:
1. PageDown from top advances selected row by at least one page when enough rows exist.
2. PageUp from a paged position retreats selected row and never underflows.
3. Repeated paging reaches terminal bounds deterministically.
4. Selection remains visible after render (no snap-back regressions).
5. Detail-pane page scroll path still adjusts `detail_scroll` and does not affect result selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PageUp`/`PageDown` provide obvious selection movement in long result sets.
- No regression in detail-pane scroll behavior.
- Existing results navigation tests continue to pass.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` all pass.

## Risks / Tradeoffs
- Changing page-key semantics may affect any tests or implicit assumptions that treated page keys as offset-only behavior.
- Mitigation: keep behavior explicit, covered by tests, and scoped to results-focus path only.
close_reason: Completed deterministic PageUp/PageDown selection paging + regression coverage

title: [EPIC] HTML Session Export: Beautiful, Encrypted, Cross-Platform
description:
# Epic: Premium HTML Session Export

## Overview
Create a world-class feature for exporting coding agent sessions as beautifully formatted, 
self-contained static HTML files. This feature provides both TUI and robot mode access,
with optional password-based encryption using Web Crypto API for client-side decryption.

## Strategic Goals
1. **Knowledge Preservation**: Allow users to archive and share valuable coding sessions
2. **Cross-Agent Value**: Export sessions from ANY agent (Claude, Codex, Cursor, etc.)
3. **Security-First**: Optional encryption ensures sensitive content stays protected
4. **Universal Access**: Files work offline, on any device, with or without internet
5. **Stripe-Level UX**: Premium visual design matching cass's TUI quality standards

## Key Features
- Self-contained HTML files with embedded CSS/JS
- Progressive enhancement: works offline, enhanced with CDN (Tailwind, Prism.js)
- Optional AES-256-GCM encryption with PBKDF2 key derivation
- Cross-platform download folder detection (Linux, macOS, Windows)
- Smart file naming: agent_project_datetime_topic.html
- Beautiful conversation rendering with syntax highlighting
- Dark/light mode toggle in exported file
- Print-friendly styles for PDF export from browser
- Search within exported conversation
- Collapsible tool calls and code blocks
- Full TUI modal with preview and options
- Complete robot mode API for automation

## Technical Approach
- Rust-side: HTML template generation with minified inline CSS/JS
- Encryption: PBKDF2 (WebCrypto-compatible) + AES-GCM with explicit salt/iv/iterations
- Web Crypto: PBKDF2 for key derivation (client-side compatible)
- File naming: Sanitize and slugify with chrono timestamps
- Downloads: dirs::download_dir() with fallback strategies

## Research Sources
- StatiCrypt: https://github.com/robinmoisson/staticrypt (static HTML encryption patterns)
- Web Crypto API: https://gist.github.com/chrisveness/43bcda93af9f646d083fad678071b90a
- Tailwind Chat UI: https://flowbite.com/docs/components/chat-bubble/
- Prism.js CDN: https://prismjs.com/ (syntax highlighting)
- Print CSS: https://print-css.rocks/ (print-friendly styles)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Export works for all 11 supported agents
- [ ] File opens correctly in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge
- [ ] Encryption/decryption works in all browsers
- [ ] Offline mode displays conversation correctly
- [ ] Print to PDF produces readable output
- [ ] TUI modal is intuitive and polished
- [ ] Robot mode provides complete API coverage
notes:
### QA Gate (must satisfy before closing)
- Unit tests for renderer, encryption, filename, JS/CSS injection, and CLI arg parsing.
- Integration tests for full export pipeline + log verification.
- E2E browser tests across Chrome/Firefox/Safari (or WebKit) with detailed logs and metrics.
- Publish a consolidated test report (JSON + markdown) with version, data hash, and environment.
close_reason: All 16 subtasks completed. HTML export feature fully implemented with: core rendering, encryption (AES-256-GCM), CDN fallback, print styles, TUI modal, robot API, test fixtures, logging, unit tests, integration tests, and E2E browser tests (171 passing across Chrome/Firefox/Safari). Acceptance criteria verified through comprehensive test coverage.

title: FrankenTUI UX revelation pass for cass TUI
description:
FrankenTUI UX Revelation Program for cass.

Why this exists:
The current cass TUI has strong fundamentals (virtualized rendering, adaptive degradation, robust tests), but still under-leverages FrankenTUI's differentiators: explainable runtime decisions, evidence-driven interaction UX, and regime-aware responsiveness under input/resize stress.

Strategic intent:
1. Make the UI feel materially more responsive under real-world terminal conditions.
2. Make adaptive behavior debuggable and explainable in-product.
3. Raise interaction quality so command, resize, and pointer behavior are stable and predictable.
4. Keep implementation decisions auditable via tests and explicit acceptance criteria.

Program structure:
- .1 Command palette migration to evidence-driven FrankenTUI patterns.
- .2 BOCPD resize coalescer + decision evidence surfaced in cass UI.
- .3 Explainability cockpit overlay/paneling (diff/resize/budget/timeline).
- .4 Structural responsive layouts by breakpoint topology.
- .5 Input smoothness pass (event coalescing + hover stabilization) [already completed].
- .6 Program-level hardening + release gates.

Dependency policy:
- Runtime evidence plumbing (.2) must precede full cockpit timeline capabilities (.3).
- Palette migration (.1) and responsive layouts (.4) can progress in parallel.
- Hardening/release gate (.6) blocks final close of this epic.

Success definition:
- Core workstreams .1 .2 .3 .4 implemented with green quality gates.
- .6 hardening confirms no regressions in stability/perf/usability.
- New behavior is self-explanatory through inspector/cockpit signals.
- Beads are sufficient for future contributors without external planning docs.
design:
Architecture principle: observable adaptivity.

Every adaptive decision (diff/resize/budget/interaction) should be represented as:
1) deterministic runtime behavior,
2) evidence that can be surfaced in UI,
3) tests that lock in expected behavior.

This avoids black-box UX drift and enables root-cause debugging directly from cass.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Program note: prioritize functional responsiveness and explainability over visual novelty. If a proposed UI change looks flashy but does not improve operator speed, stability, or debuggability, it is out of scope for this epic. description:
## Epic: E2E Verbose Logging Enhancement

Enhance E2E test logging beyond basic JSONL events to include detailed debugging information, performance metrics, and failure context.

### Goals
1. **Every test failure is debuggable from logs alone** - No need to re-run locally
2. **Performance regressions are detectable** - Timing data for critical operations
3. **Resource leaks are traceable** - Memory, file handles, temp files

### Current State
- Basic JSONL events: run_start, test_start, test_end, run_end
- Missing: verbose step-by-step output, metrics, failure state dumps

### Features in This Epic

1. **Verbose Debug Logging Mode** (395v)
   - `E2E_VERBOSE=1` environment variable
   - Detailed step-by-step logs to separate file
   - Does not affect JSONL event stream

2. **Performance Metrics Collection** (1bqi)
   - Emit `metrics` events with timing data
   - Track: indexer duration, search latency, memory usage, index size

3. **Failure State Dump** (rtpd)
   - On panic/failure, automatically dump:
     - Environment variables
     - Temp directory listing
     - Last 100 lines of logs
     - Database state

### Success Metrics
- 100% of test failures can be triaged from CI logs
- P95 operation times available in test-results/
- Resource leak reports generated automatically

GOAL: Transform franken_agent_detection (FAD) from a detection-only library into a full agent connector library. Move ALL 15 connector implementations (scan/parse logic) from cass src/connectors/ into FAD at /data/projects/franken_agent_detection. CURRENT STATE: FAD provides installation detection for 16 agents (~400 lines of filesystem probing). Cass provides 15 full connector implementations (~21,400 lines across 15 files) that parse agent-specific session formats into NormalizedConversation. The detect() method already delegates to FAD. The scan() method (parsing) does NOT.

CONNECTORS TO MOVE (by complexity): Simple (<500 LOC): vibe.rs(378), clawdbot.rs(327). Medium (500-1100 LOC): aider.rs(826), openclaw.rs(935), copilot.rs(934), factory.rs(1080), cline.rs(1108). Complex (1100-1500 LOC): amp.rs(1291), pi_agent.rs(1395), claude_code.rs(1465). Very Complex (1500+ LOC): gemini.rs(1594), chatgpt.rs(1748), codex.rs(1961), opencode.rs(2041), cursor.rs(2148).

NEW DEPS REQUIRED IN FAD: rusqlite (Cursor/OpenCode), aes-gcm+pbkdf2 (ChatGPT), serde_json, walkdir+glob, anyhow, tracing, regex, blake3, chrono, unicode-normalization. These MUST be feature-gated so detection-only users stay lightweight: default=['detection'], connectors=['rusqlite','aes-gcm',...], chatgpt=['aes-gcm','pbkdf2'].

EXPECTED OUTCOME: ~21,400 lines removed from cass src/connectors/. FAD becomes reusable agent connector library. Clear separation — FAD owns 'talk to agents', cass owns 'index+search+TUI'. Easier to add new agent support.

APPROACH: Move shared types/traits first, add feature-gated deps, move connectors simplest-to-most-complex, move factory/registry last.

title: FAD: Move NormalizedConversation + associated types to franken_agent_detection
description:
WHAT: Move the core normalized types from cass src/connectors/mod.rs to franken_agent_detection. These are the lingua franca types that ALL connectors produce.

TYPES TO MOVE (from src/connectors/mod.rs approximately lines 50-250):
- NormalizedConversation: agent_slug, workspace, title, source_path, messages, metadata, timestamps, source_id, origin_host, approx_tokens
- NormalizedMessage: idx, role, author, created_at, content, snippets, extra_json
- NormalizedSnippet: file_path, line_start, line_end, language, text
- MessageRole: User, Agent, Tool, System, Other(String)
- DetectionResult: detected (bool), evidence, root_paths

NOTE: ScanContext and ScanRoot are NOT in this task. They live in FAD task 4 (PathTrie/WorkspaceCache/ScanRoot/ScanContext) because ScanContext depends on ScanRoot which depends on PathTrie.

title: FAD: Add serialization compatibility tests for NormalizedConversation types
description:
WHAT: Before moving NormalizedConversation types to FAD, create golden-file serialization tests that PROVE the JSON shape is preserved exactly after the move.

WHY: NormalizedConversation, NormalizedMessage, and NormalizedSnippet are serialized to:
- SQLite storage (via serde_json::to_string and rmp_serde for MessagePack)
- Robot mode JSON output (via serde_json)
- Daemon protocol messages
- HTML export data
If the serde attributes or field order change during migration, existing data becomes unreadable. This is a SILENT DATA CORRUPTION risk.

APPROACH:
1. BEFORE moving types: Create golden JSON files for each type with known test data
2. AFTER moving types: Deserialize golden files with the new FAD types and verify field-by-field

GOLDEN FILES TO CREATE (in tests/fixtures/golden/):

title: FAD: Add feature-gated heavy dependencies for connector support
description:
WHAT: Add all dependencies needed by the 15 connectors to FAD Cargo.toml, behind feature gates so detection-only users stay lightweight.

CURRENT FAD DEPS: serde, serde_json, chrono, dirs (minimal)

NEW DEPS NEEDED:
- rusqlite (bundled) — Cursor and OpenCode parse SQLite databases
- aes-gcm + pbkdf2 + argon2 — ChatGPT v2/v3 encrypted conversations
- walkdir — filesystem traversal for session discovery
- glob — pattern matching for session file discovery
- anyhow — error handling in scan() methods
- tracing — structured logging throughout connectors
- regex — pattern matching in various parsers
- blake3 — content hashing for deduplication
- unicode-normalization — NFC text canonicalization
- thiserror — typed error variants

FEATURE GATE DESIGN:
[features]
default = ['detection']  # Keep current behavior as default
detection = []  # Filesystem probing only (current FAD)
connectors = ['dep:rusqlite', 'dep:walkdir', 'dep:glob', 'dep:anyhow', 'dep:tracing', 'dep:regex', 'dep:blake3', 'dep:unicode-normalization', 'dep:thiserror']
chatgpt = ['connectors', 'dep:aes-gcm', 'dep:pbkdf2', 'dep:argon2']  # Heavy crypto only for ChatGPT
cursor = ['connectors', 'dep:rusqlite']  # SQLite for Cursor
opencode = ['connectors', 'dep:rusqlite']  # SQLite for OpenCode
all-connectors = ['connectors', 'chatgpt', 'cursor', 'opencode']

WHY FEATURE GATES: Without feature gates, anyone who just needs detection (does this agent exist?) would pull in rusqlite, ONNX crypto, etc. That violates the principle of minimal dependencies.

STEPS:
1. Audit all 15 connectors to catalog every external crate they use
2. Design feature gate hierarchy (which deps serve which connectors)
3. Add deps to FAD Cargo.toml with optional = true
4. Create feature definitions
5. Add cfg attributes to connector modules
6. Verify: 'cargo check' with default features = detection only
7. Verify: 'cargo check --features all-connectors' = everything

CONSIDERATIONS:
- rusqlite with 'bundled' feature compiles SQLite from C source — this adds build time. Consider making the bundled feature optional.
- aes-gcm + pbkdf2 are security-critical — pin to exact versions, not wildcard
- Some deps may already be transitive (e.g., serde_json through serde)
- Test that 'default' feature (detection only) compiles without any connector deps
- The 'connectors' feature should be the common base, with per-connector features adding heavy deps

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- 'cargo check' with default features succeeds (detection only)
- 'cargo check --features all-connectors' succeeds
- No unnecessary deps pulled in for detection-only use
- Feature documentation in Cargo.toml comments

title: FAD: Move PathTrie, WorkspaceCache, and shared connector utilities to FAD
description:
WHAT: Move shared connector infrastructure from cass src/connectors/mod.rs to FAD. This includes data structures AND utility functions used by multiple connectors.

DATA STRUCTURES (~300 lines):
1. PathTrie (lines ~53-178, 125 lines): O(k) longest-prefix-match trie for workspace path rewriting. Uses HashMap of path components. AtomicU64 counters for observability. Thread-safe. Used by ScanRoot::rewrite_workspace().
2. WorkspaceCache (lines ~217-390, 173 lines): Bloom filter (1% FP rate) + HashSet two-phase lookup. 10x speedup for negative lookups. Used by indexer for fast workspace membership testing.

UTILITY FUNCTIONS (spread through mod.rs):
3. file_modified_since(path, since_ts) -> bool (~20 lines): Checks file mtime for incremental scanning
4. parse_timestamp(val: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<i64> (~50 lines): Handles i64 epoch, string epoch, ISO-8601 formats. Used by ALL connectors.
5. flatten_content(val: &serde_json::Value) -> String (~25 lines): Extracts text from arrays of content blocks (handles tool_use blocks, text blocks, mixed arrays). Used by ALL connectors.
6. reindex_messages(msgs: &mut Vec<NormalizedMessage>) (~5 lines): Re-numbers message indices after filtering

SCAN INFRASTRUCTURE (~160 lines):
7. ScanRoot struct (lines ~488-602, 114 lines): Wraps path + origin + platform + workspace rewrites. rewrite_workspace() method uses PathTrie. LazyLock for trie caching.
8. ScanContext struct (lines ~605-650, 45 lines): data_dir, scan_roots, since_ts. Methods: local_default(), with_roots(), use_default_detection().

TOTAL: ~600 lines of shared infrastructure

DEPENDS ON: FAD task 1 (types — ScanContext/ScanRoot reference NormalizedConversation types) AND FAD task 3 (deps — needs walkdir, glob, blake3, bloom)

NOTE: Simple connectors (vibe, clawdbot) only use parse_timestamp, flatten_content, file_modified_since. Complex connectors use PathTrie and WorkspaceCache. We keep all utilities together since they're a cohesive module.

STEPS:
1. Read all utility functions and data structures in mod.rs
2. Create FAD src/connectors/utils.rs for simple functions
3. Create FAD src/connectors/path_trie.rs
4. Create FAD src/connectors/workspace_cache.rs
5. Create FAD src/connectors/scan.rs for ScanRoot + ScanContext
6. Port all unit tests (PathTrie and WorkspaceCache have tests)

TESTING:
- PathTrie: test prefix matching, longest match, no match, empty trie, platform paths
- WorkspaceCache: test bloom filter FP rate, positive lookups, negative lookups, capacity
- parse_timestamp: test i64 epoch, string epoch, ISO-8601, invalid input, null
- flatten_content: test string, array, nested tool_use, empty, null
- ScanRoot: test workspace rewriting with PathTrie

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- All utilities compile in FAD
- Unit tests for PathTrie, WorkspaceCache, parse_timestamp, flatten_content pass
- ScanRoot + ScanContext work with migrated types
- All connectors that depend on these utilities compile

# Perf: Lazy SQLite Open to Cut Startup Cost

## Goal
Delay opening SQLite until a command actually needs it, reducing CLI/TUI startup time.

- Integration: commands that should not touch DB (help/health) do not open it.
- E2E: startup benchmark script logs cold start times before/after.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Measurable startup reduction (record ms).
- No regressions in DB-required commands.
- Logs include open reason and duration.

title: Adapt cass QueryCache and dedup for frankensearch hit types
description:
TRACK: cass migration (Track 1B)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensearch Integration

CORRECTED SCOPE (2026-02-27 pass-4 deep audit):

CachedHit wraps cass's internal SearchHit struct (query.rs:876), NOT frankensearch types.
SearchHit is a cass-defined output type that remains unchanged regardless of which search backend produces it. The cache and dedup layers sit ABOVE the frankensearch pipeline — they operate on cass's own result types.

VERIFIED STATE:
- CachedHit (query.rs:1488): wraps SearchHit + lowercase content + bloom filter
- CacheShards (query.rs:1515): LRU cache keyed on query string, values are Vec<CachedHit>
- deduplicate_hits(): operates on Vec<SearchHit>, uses content_hash (u64) for dedup
- is_tool_invocation_noise(): pattern-based content filtering on String — no type dependency

WHAT ACTUALLY NEEDS CHANGING (minimal):
The migration from tantivy to frankensearch does NOT change the SearchHit type. The only changes are:

1. QueryCache embedding storage — currently stores Vec<f32> from SyncEmbed. This ALREADY uses frankensearch's SyncEmbed (embedder.rs:21 pub use frankensearch::SyncEmbed as Embedder). No change needed.

2. CacheShards invalidation — if SyncTwoTierSearcher (Phase 2 optional enhancement) changes result ordering, cached results would be stale. Add a cache_version field that increments when search backend changes. LOW PRIORITY.

3. deduplicate_hits() doc_id parsing — currently parses doc_id format embedded by cass indexer. If frankensearch changes the doc_id format, dedup parser needs updating. But cass controls the doc_id format during indexing, so this is unlikely to change.

CONCLUSION: This bead is NEARLY A NO-OP for the core migration. The cache and dedup layers are already compatible with frankensearch because they operate on cass-internal types (SearchHit, CachedHit), not on frankensearch types (VectorHit, ScoredResult).

REMAINING WORK (small):
- Verify QueryCache.get_embedding() still works after any import changes from uc0qs/ltbab
- Add cache_version field for future-proofing (optional)
- Run existing search_caching.rs tests to verify no regression

FILES TO MODIFY: src/search/query.rs (minimal — verify imports, optionally add cache_version)

title: P2.1 Extend ScanContext with scan roots
description:
# Extend ScanContext with Multi-Root Support

## Context
Currently ScanContext has just data_root (single path) and since_ts. For remote support, we need multiple scan roots, each with provenance.

## Location
src/connectors/mod.rs (ScanContext definition)
src/indexer/mod.rs (ScanContext usage)

## Current Structure
\`\`\`rust
pub struct ScanContext {
    pub data_root: PathBuf,
    pub since_ts: Option<i64>,
}
\`\`\`

## New Structure

### Option A: Add scan_roots alongside data_root (backward compatible)
\`\`\`rust
pub struct ScanContext {
    /// Primary data directory (cass internal state)
    pub data_dir: PathBuf,
    
    /// Scan roots to search for agent logs
    /// If empty, connectors use their default detection logic
    pub scan_roots: Vec<ScanRoot>,
    
    /// High-water mark for incremental indexing
    pub since_ts: Option<i64>,
}

pub struct ScanRoot {
    /// Path to scan (e.g., ~/.claude, or /data/remotes/work-laptop/mirror/home/.claude)
    pub path: PathBuf,
    
    /// Provenance for conversations found under this root
    pub origin: Origin,
    
    /// Optional platform hint (affects path interpretation)
    pub platform: Option<Platform>,
    
    /// Optional path rewrite rules (src_prefix -> dst_prefix)
    pub workspace_rewrites: Vec<(String, String)>,
}
\`\`\`

### Option B: Keep ScanContext simple, pass provenance separately
Keep ScanContext as-is, but indexer tracks provenance externally and injects after scan.

## Recommendation
Option A is cleaner - ScanRoot bundles everything needed for a scan pass.

## Migration Path for Connectors
Most connectors currently check ctx.data_root for tests/overrides. Update them to:
1. If scan_roots is non-empty, iterate over matching roots
2. If scan_roots is empty, use existing default detection logic (maintains backward compat)

## Dependencies
- P1.1 (Origin type)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ScanContext extended with scan_roots
- [ ] ScanRoot struct defined with provenance
- [ ] Backward compatibility: empty scan_roots = old behavior
- [ ] At least one connector updated to use new structure
- [ ] Tests pass
close_reason: Added ScanRoot struct with origin, platform, workspace_rewrites. Extended ScanContext with scan_roots vec and data_dir. Connectors updated to use data_dir. Backward compatible via local_default() and use_default_detection(). 5 new unit tests.

title: [MEDIUM] reality-check: robot-docs paths advertises <data-dir>/cass.log but only cass tui creates it
description:
## Claim (\`cass robot-docs paths\`)
\`\`\`
paths:
  data dir default: /home/ubuntu/.local/share/coding-agent-search
  db path default: /home/ubuntu/.local/share/coding-agent-search/agent_search.db
  log path: <data-dir>/cass.log (daily rolling)
  trace: user-provided path (JSONL).
\`\`\`

The \`log path\` line reads as a universal property of cass — wherever cass runs, it writes \`<data-dir>/cass.log\` with daily rolling. Agents reading the robot-docs output will expect this file to exist after ANY cass invocation and use it for triage.

## Reality
Log-file initialization is gated on \`Commands::Tui\` in src/lib.rs:2954–2970:

\`\`\`rust
match &command {
    Commands::Tui { data_dir, .. } => {
        let log_dir = data_dir.clone().unwrap_or_else(default_data_dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&log_dir).ok();
        let file_appender = tracing_appender::rolling::daily(&log_dir, \"cass.log\");
        ...
    }
    ...
}
\`\`\`

Other variants (\`Search\`, \`Index\`, \`Stats\`, \`Health\`, \`Diag\`, \`Status\`, \`Doctor\`, \`Capabilities\`, \`Sessions\`, \`Export\`, \`Models\`, \`Timeline\`, \`Expand\`, \`View\`, \`ApiVersion\`, \`Introspect\`, \`RobotDocs\`, \`Sources\`, \`Analytics\`) do NOT hook up the rolling file appender — they only configure the stderr subscriber. No cass.log is produced.

Experimental confirmation:

\`\`\`bash
# Fresh HOME, cass tui --once → log appears:
XDG_DATA_HOME=\$TMP HOME=\$TMP TUI_HEADLESS=1 cass tui --once
find \$TMP -name 'cass.log*'
# /tmp/.../coding-agent-search/cass.log.2026-04-23

# Fresh HOME, cass index --full + cass search → NO log:
XDG_DATA_HOME=\$TMP2 HOME=\$TMP2 cass index --full
XDG_DATA_HOME=\$TMP2 HOME=\$TMP2 cass search matrix --robot
find \$TMP2 -name 'cass.log*'
# (empty)
\`\`\`

Also note: \`src/lib.rs:13620\` emits the user-facing hint \"check cass.log for details\" from \`cass doctor\`, even though \`cass doctor\` doesn't produce a cass.log either.

## Impact
Agents running cass in pure robot mode (never touching the TUI) will never find the file that robot-docs points them at. Triage flows that depend on \"consult cass.log\" silently have no artifact to consult — operators end up running \`cass -v\` or \`CASS_TRACE_FILE=...\` instead.

## Suggested fix
Two options:

1. **Docs fix (easy)**: Update \`cass robot-docs paths\` to tell the truth. Replace the \`log path\` line with something like:
   \`\`\`
   log path (TUI only): <data-dir>/cass.log.YYYY-MM-DD (daily rolling)
   trace: user-provided path via CASS_TRACE_FILE or --trace-file (JSONL)
   \`\`\`
   Update \`cass doctor\` hint text at src/lib.rs:13620 to remove the \"check cass.log\" reference unless doctor actually writes one (or add logging to doctor).

2. **Behavior fix (larger)**: Install the rolling-daily file appender for every long-running command (at least \`index\`, \`search\`, \`doctor\`, \`models install\`, \`models backfill\`) so the advertised log actually materializes. Keep the quick one-shot commands (\`health\`, \`api-version\`, \`diag\`) on stderr-only to avoid creating noisy files for 50ms invocations.

Option 1 is the smaller-risk fix and truthfully reflects shipped behavior. Option 2 is more useful but needs a broader review of what to log and where.

Severity: MEDIUM — a documented artifact that isn't there breaks triage assumptions; corrected docs restore operator trust without code changes.

Labels: documentation, cli, reality-check, logging.
close_reason: Fixed in commits 95f9d26f (source: src/lib.rs:6894-6910 robot-docs paths emitter rewritten to 'log path (cass tui only): <data-dir>/cass.log.YYYY-MM-DD (daily rolling). Non-TUI subcommands emit to stderr; redirect with 2> /path/to/cass.log or use -v / CASS_TRACE_FILE=<path> for a persistent artifact'; src/lib.rs:14274-14282 cass doctor hint explicitly notes 'cass doctor does not produce a cass.log file itself (the rolling cass.log.YYYY-MM-DD appender is installed only for cass tui)') + bdc49adb (tests: regenerated tests/golden/robot_docs/paths.txt.golden to match shipped accurate output). robot_docs_paths_matches_golden passes. Triage flows no longer mistakenly expect a universal cass.log — operators get explicit stderr-redirect / CASS_TRACE_FILE guidance instead.

title: Fix End key and Page Down scroll boundary in conversation detail view (GH#67)

    if ! grep -q "use.*e2e_log\|mod.*e2e_log" "$f"; then
        echo "  ERROR: $name missing e2e_log import"
        ((E2E_ERRORS++))
    fi
    
    # Check for PhaseTracker usage (after consolidation is complete)
    if ! grep -q "PhaseTracker" "$f"; then
        echo "  WARNING: $name not using PhaseTracker (may need migration)"
    fi
done

# Check shell scripts
for f in scripts/e2e/*.sh; do
    if [ -f "$f" ] && [ -s "$f" ]; then
        name=$(basename "$f")
        if ! grep -q "e2e_log.sh" "$f"; then
            echo "  WARNING: $name not sourcing e2e_log.sh"
        fi
    fi
done

if [ $E2E_ERRORS -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "  FAILED: $E2E_ERRORS E2E logging compliance error(s)"
    exit 1
fi
echo "  OK: E2E logging compliance checks passed"
```

title: [Feature] Assertion Quality Audit
description:
## Feature: Assertion Quality Audit

Improve assertion messages throughout the test suite. Many tests use bare `assert!()` or `assert_eq!()` without context, making failures hard to debug in CI.

### Goals
1. All assertions include context messages
2. Assertions explain expected vs actual values
3. Complex comparisons show diffs
4. Test names describe the scenario being tested

### Scope
- `tests/*.rs` files (integration tests)
- `src/**/tests` modules (unit tests)

### Anti-Patterns to Fix
```rust
// BAD - no context on failure
assert!(result.is_ok());
assert_eq!(count, 5);

// GOOD - context helps debug failures
assert!(result.is_ok(), "parse_session failed: {:?}", result.err());
assert_eq!(count, 5, "expected 5 messages but got {} for fixture {:?}", count, fixture_path);
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All `assert!()` calls have context messages
- [ ] All `assert_eq!()` calls explain what values represent  
- [ ] Test names use `test_<scenario>_<expected_outcome>` convention
- [ ] Fixture tests document what scenario each fixture tests
- [ ] CI failures are debuggable without re-running locally

title: Build rusqlite-compatible adapter layer in frankensqlite
description:
TRACK: frankensqlite upstream prep (Track 3A)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensqlite Integration

WHAT: Build a rusqlite-compatible adapter module in frankensqlite. With a solid adapter, the cass migration across 13 files becomes mostly mechanical import swaps.

VERIFIED ADAPTER COMPONENTS NEEDED (with grep-verified counts):

1. PARAMS MACRO (covers 96 cass call sites across 10 files):
   macro_rules! params { ... } → &[SqliteValue::from(...)]

2. PARAMS_FROM_ITER (covers 26 call sites across 6 files):
   fn params_from_iter(iter: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl Into<SqliteValue>>) → Vec<SqliteValue>

3. ADDITIONAL From IMPLS FOR SqliteValue:
   - From<bool> → Integer(1)/Integer(0)
   - From<Option<T>> → Null/from(inner)
   - From<u32>, From<u64>, From<usize> → Integer(i64) with overflow check
   NOTE: Existing: i64, i32, f64, String, &str, Vec<u8>, &[u8]
   CORRECTED: Box<dyn ToSql> is NOT used (0 occurrences) — no ToSql trait needed

4. TYPED ROW EXTRACTION:
   trait FromSqliteValue with impls for i32, i64, u32, u64, f64, String, Vec<u8>, bool, Option<T>
   trait RowExt { fn get_typed<T: FromSqliteValue>(&self, index: usize) -> Result<T>; }

5. QUERY WITH CLOSURE (covers 118 query_row + 64 query_map = 182 total sites):
   trait ConnectionExt {
       fn query_row_map<T, F>(&self, sql, params, f) -> Result<T>;
       fn query_map_collect<T, F>(&self, sql, params, f) -> Result<Vec<T>>;
   }
   This is the HIGHEST-VOLUME adapter component.

6. EXECUTE_BATCH (covers 115 call sites across 10 files — biggest: sqlite.rs=95):
   trait ConnectionExt { fn execute_batch(&self, sql: &str) -> Result<()>; }
   Implementation: split on ';', filter empty, execute each.
   IMPORTANT: sqlite.rs uses execute_batch for PRAGMA blocks and CREATE TABLE sequences.
   Simple semicolon split is sufficient for cass's SQL patterns.

7. TRANSACTION WRAPPER (covers 9 call sites across 2 files):
   struct Transaction<'a> with execute, query methods, Drop auto-rollback, explicit commit().
   trait TransactionExt { fn transaction(&self) -> Result<Transaction>; }

8. OPTIONAL EXTENSION (covers 9 call sites across 2 files):
   trait OptionalExtension<T> { fn optional(self) -> Result<Option<T>>; }
   Converts QueryReturnedNoRows → Ok(None)

9. OPEN FLAGS MAPPING (pages/secret_scan.rs and sqlite.rs):
   struct OpenFlags with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE, CREATE
   fn open_with_flags(path, flags) → maps to VfsOpenFlags

FILES TO CREATE: compat/mod.rs, compat/params.rs, compat/row.rs, compat/transaction.rs, compat/batch.rs, compat/optional.rs, compat/flags.rs

title: Audit and tune degradation thresholds to prevent premature visual stripping
description:
## What

Audit and document the degradation system to verify it does NOT prematurely strip visual styling on modern terminals. Based on code verification, the frame budget is already set to "quality-first" (120ms total, no frame skip, relaxed defaults). This task is primarily **verification + documentation + escape hatch**, not a tuning task.

## Verified Current State

**FrameBudgetConfig (app.rs:~12626-12631)**:
```rust
FrameBudgetConfig {
    total: Duration::from_millis(120),      // 120ms = ~8fps floor (very generous)
    allow_frame_skip: false,                // Never skip frames
    degradation_cooldown: 12,               // 12 ticks before upgrading
    upgrade_threshold: 0.25,                // Upgrade when frame < 25% of budget
    ..FrameBudgetConfig::relaxed()          // All other fields relaxed
}
```

Comment: "Quality-first budget profile: favor full visuals and avoid aggressive degradation."

## Scope (Reduced from Original)

Since the defaults are already quality-first, this task focuses on:

1. **Document degradation levels in code**: Add doc comments to the DegradationLevel usage sites in view() explaining what each level strips (borders, colors, chrome).

2. **Add CASS_NO_DEGRADATION env var**: When set, force DegradationLevel::Full always. This is a debugging escape hatch to definitively rule out degradation as a visual issue.

3. **Add telemetry logging**: When degradation level changes, log to stderr (behind a `CASS_DEBUG_DEGRADATION=1` flag) so users can see if and when degradation triggers:
   ```
   [degradation] Full → SimpleBorders at frame 142 (budget=120ms, actual=135ms)
   ```

4. **Verify initial render starts at Full**: Check that the very first frame renders at Full degradation (not pre-degraded).

## Required Tests

### Unit tests:
1. `test_degradation_initial_level_is_full` — Construct a new CassApp, verify the first frame's degradation level is Full (not pre-degraded).
2. `test_degradation_env_override` — Set CASS_NO_DEGRADATION=1, verify degradation is always Full regardless of frame time.
3. `test_degradation_level_strips_borders` — At SimpleBorders level, verify view() uses BorderType::Square (not Rounded).
4. `test_degradation_level_strips_color` — At NoStyling level, verify view() uses `plain` style (not themed).
5. `test_degradation_level_strips_all` — At EssentialOnly level, verify view() uses Borders::NONE.

### E2E validation:
6. `test_no_degradation_with_normal_data` — Render a screen with 20 results at 120×40 terminal size. Verify degradation stays at Full for all frames (the budget should never be exceeded with normal data on modern hardware).

## Considerations
- The Inspector cockpit (Ctrl+Shift+I → Budget tab) already shows frame timing. This task adds ENV-based overrides and stderr logging for headless/automated debugging.
- If verification confirms degradation never triggers on normal terminals, this task is largely documentation. Mark it as such in the closing comment.
- The 120ms budget is deliberately generous. Typical frame render is <5ms. Only extreme cases (10K+ results, slow SSH, very old hardware) should trigger degradation.

## Acceptance
- DegradationLevel usage sites in view() have doc comments
- CASS_NO_DEGRADATION env var implemented and documented
- CASS_DEBUG_DEGRADATION env var logs level transitions to stderr
- Initial render verified as Full level
- 5 unit tests + 1 e2e test pass
- No clippy warnings

title: Update robot-docs and help text for sources setup
description:
# Update robot-docs and help text for sources setup

## What
Update the cass documentation to cover the new `sources setup` command, including:
- Robot-docs content for LLM consumption
- CLI help text
- AGENTS.md section
- Architecture diagram
- Configuration reference
- FAQ/troubleshooting

## Why
New features need documentation for:
1. Users to discover and learn the feature
2. AI agents (via robot-docs) to understand how to use it
3. Future maintainers to understand the design

## Documentation Updates

### CLI Help Text (clap doc comments)
```rust
/// Interactive wizard to set up remote sources
/// 
/// Discovers SSH hosts from your ~/.ssh/config, checks each for existing cass
/// installations and agent session data, then guides you through selecting
/// which machines to configure for remote search.
/// 
/// The wizard can:
/// - Install cass on remotes that don't have it
/// - Run initial indexing on remotes
/// - Configure sources.toml with correct paths and mappings
/// - Sync data to your local machine
/// 
/// Examples:
///   cass sources setup                    # Interactive wizard
///   cass sources setup --hosts css,csd    # Configure specific hosts
///   cass sources setup --dry-run          # Preview without changes
///   cass sources setup --resume           # Resume interrupted setup
///   cass sources setup --non-interactive  # For scripting (uses defaults)
///   
/// For more details: cass docs sources-setup
Setup {
    /// Configure only these hosts (comma-separated SSH aliases)
    #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',')] 
    hosts: Option<Vec<String>>,
    
    /// Preview what would be done without making changes
    #[arg(long)]
    dry_run: bool,
    
    /// Resume an interrupted setup from saved state
    #[arg(long)]
    resume: bool,
    
    /// Skip interactive prompts, use auto-detected defaults
    #[arg(long)]
    non_interactive: bool,
    
    /// Don't install cass on remotes that don't have it
    #[arg(long)]
    skip_install: bool,
    
    /// Don't run initial indexing on remotes
    #[arg(long)]
    skip_index: bool,
    
    /// Don't sync data after setup
    #[arg(long)]
    skip_sync: bool,
    
    /// Output progress as JSON (for scripting)
    #[arg(long)]
    json: bool,
}
```

### Robot-Docs (robot_docs.rs)
Add comprehensive section:
```rust
("setup", r#"
# cass sources setup - Interactive Remote Sources Wizard

## Overview
The setup wizard automates configuring cass to search across multiple machines.
It discovers your SSH hosts, checks their status, and handles installation,
indexing, and configuration automatically.

## Quick Start
```bash
# Interactive (recommended for first-time setup)
cass sources setup

# Non-interactive (for scripting)
cass sources setup --non-interactive --hosts css,csd,yto
```

## Workflow Phases

### Phase 1: Discovery
- Parses ~/.ssh/config to find configured hosts
- Filters out wildcards and patterns (*, ?)
- Uses SSH aliases as host identifiers

### Phase 2: Probing
- Connects to each host via SSH (parallel, with timeout)
- Checks if cass is installed (and version)
- Detects existing agent session data:
  - ~/.claude/projects (Claude Code)
  - ~/.codex/sessions (OpenAI Codex)
  - ~/.cursor (Cursor editor)
  - ~/.gemini/tmp (Gemini CLI)
- Collects system info (OS, disk space, memory)

### Phase 3: Selection
- Displays discovered hosts with status
- Shows what data was found on each host
- Marks unreachable hosts (not selectable)
- Marks already-configured hosts (grayed out)
- Supports search/filter for many hosts

### Phase 4: Installation (optional)
- Installs cass on hosts that don't have it
- Tries multiple methods:
  1. cargo binstall (fastest)
  2. cargo install (most reliable)
  3. Download binary (no cargo needed)
- Shows progress, handles failures gracefully

### Phase 5: Indexing (optional)
- Triggers `cass index` on remote hosts
- Runs in background, polls for progress
- Can skip with --skip-index

### Phase 6: Configuration
- Generates sources.toml entries
- Shows preview before saving
- Allows customization of paths/mappings
- Creates backup of existing config
- Validates TOML before writing

### Phase 7: Initial Sync (optional)
- Runs `cass sources sync --source <name>` for each new source
- Downloads session data to local machine
- Can skip with --skip-sync

## Flags Reference

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--hosts <names>` | Only configure these hosts (comma-separated SSH aliases) |
| `--dry-run` | Preview what would be done, don't make changes |
| `--resume` | Resume from saved state after interruption |
| `--non-interactive` | Skip all prompts, use auto-detected defaults |
| `--skip-install` | Don't install cass on remotes |
| `--skip-index` | Don't run remote indexing |
| `--skip-sync` | Don't sync after setup |
| `--json` | Output progress as JSON for scripting |

## State and Resume

If setup is interrupted (Ctrl+C, connection lost), state is saved to:
`~/.config/cass/setup_state.json`

Resume with:
```bash
cass sources setup --resume
```

State includes:
- Hosts probed
- Hosts selected
- Installation progress
- Indexing progress

## Non-Interactive Usage

For automation/scripting:
```bash
# Configure specific hosts with all defaults
cass sources setup --non-interactive --hosts css,csd

# Skip install and index, just configure
cass sources setup --non-interactive --hosts css --skip-install --skip-index

# JSON output for parsing
cass sources setup --non-interactive --hosts css --json
```

## Generated Configuration

The wizard generates sources.toml entries like:
```toml
[[sources]]
name = "css"
type = "ssh"
host = "css"
paths = [
    "~/.claude/projects",
    "~/.codex/sessions",
]
sync_schedule = "manual"

[[sources.path_mappings]]
from = "/data/projects"
to = "/Users/username/projects"
```

## Troubleshooting

### "Host unreachable"
- Verify SSH config: `ssh <host>` manually
- Check if host is up: `ping <hostname>`
- Ensure SSH key is loaded: `ssh-add -l`

### "Permission denied"
- Add SSH key to agent: `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa`

### "cargo not found"
- Install Rust on remote: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`

### "Compilation failed"
- Check disk space on remote
- Ensure build dependencies: `apt install build-essential` (Debian/Ubuntu)

- Large session histories can take minutes
