title: P6.4: Security Audit Checklist
description:
# P6.4: Security Audit Checklist

## Goal
Systematically review all security-sensitive code paths against a comprehensive checklist, documenting findings and ensuring no known vulnerability patterns exist in the implementation.

## Background & Rationale

### Why Formal Security Audit
1. **Cryptographic Code**: Small mistakes have catastrophic consequences
2. **Web Security**: XSS, injection, and other web vulnerabilities
3. **Trust Boundaries**: Data flows between trusted and untrusted contexts
4. **Defense in Depth**: Multiple security layers must all be correct

### Audit Scope
- Rust cryptographic implementation
- JavaScript browser crypto code
- Web viewer UI and input handling
- Service worker and caching
- Generated documentation and configuration

## Audit Checklist

### 1. Cryptographic Implementation

#### Key Derivation
- [ ] Argon2id parameters meet minimum security (m≥64MB, t≥3, p≥4)
- [ ] Salt is unique per archive (not reused)
- [ ] Salt length is at least 16 bytes
- [ ] Password is properly encoded (UTF-8 normalized)
- [ ] Memory is zeroed after use (where possible)

#### AES-GCM Encryption
- [ ] 256-bit keys used (not 128 or 192)
- [ ] Nonces are never reused with same key
- [ ] Nonce generation is counter-based or random with collision resistance
- [ ] Authentication tags are verified before any processing
- [ ] Tag length is 128 bits (not truncated)
- [ ] AAD binds ciphertext to context

#### Key Management
- [ ] DEK is generated with CSPRNG
- [ ] DEK is never stored in plaintext
- [ ] KEK derivation uses separate salt/context
- [ ] Key slots are independent (compromising one doesnt leak others)
- [ ] No key material in logs or error messages

#### HKDF Usage
- [ ] Proper salt handling (can be empty, but documented)
- [ ] Context/info parameter differentiates key uses
- [ ] Output length matches algorithm requirements

### 2. Web Security

#### Input Handling
- [ ] All user input is validated/sanitized
- [ ] No innerHTML with user content
- [ ] Query parameters are escaped before display
- [ ] Form inputs have appropriate types
- [ ] File uploads are validated (if any)

#### Content Security Policy
- [ ] CSP header is set and restrictive
- [ ] No unsafe-inline for scripts
- [ ] No unsafe-eval
- [ ] No data: URLs for scripts
- [ ] frame-ancestors restricts embedding

#### Cross-Origin Security
- [ ] CORS headers are minimal/absent (static site)
- [ ] COOP: same-origin is set
- [ ] COEP: require-corp is set
- [ ] No sensitive data in URLs

#### Authentication
- [ ] Password entry clears on navigation
- [ ] Decrypted data not cached in localStorage
- [ ] Session timeout implemented
- [ ] Failed attempts dont leak timing info

### 3. Data Handling

#### Sensitive Data
- [ ] Passwords cleared from memory after use
- [ ] Decrypted content not persisted to disk
- [ ] No sensitive data in console.log
- [ ] Error messages dont leak content
- [ ] Browser autofill disabled for password

#### Export Process
- [ ] Secret scan runs before export
- [ ] User confirms understanding of risks
- [ ] No accidental plaintext copies
- [ ] Temporary files are securely deleted

### 4. Service Worker Security

#### Caching
- [ ] Only static assets cached (not decrypted data)
- [ ] Cache invalidation on update
- [ ] No credential caching
- [ ] Fetch interception doesnt leak data

#### Installation
- [ ] Update prompts user to refresh
- [ ] Old versions are properly cleaned up
- [ ] No downgrade attacks possible

### 5. Build and Distribution

#### Dependencies
- [ ] All dependencies audited (cargo audit, npm audit)
- [ ] No known vulnerable versions
- [ ] Lockfile committed and verified
- [ ] Minimal dependency surface

#### Supply Chain
- [ ] Build is reproducible
- [ ] Release artifacts are signed
- [ ] No post-install scripts with network access
- [ ] Subresource integrity for CDN resources (if any)

### 6. Code Quality

#### Error Handling
- [ ] Crypto errors dont reveal key material
- [ ] Decryption failures are indistinguishable
- [ ] Panics dont leak sensitive state
- [ ] All error paths tested

#### Timing Attacks
- [ ] Password comparison is constant-time
- [ ] Tag verification is constant-time
- [ ] No early exit on partial match
- [ ] Benchmarks dont reveal timing

### 7. Documentation

#### Security Documentation
- [ ] Threat model is documented
- [ ] Limitations are clearly stated
- [ ] Key rotation procedures documented
- [ ] Incident response guidance

#### User Guidance
- [ ] Password strength requirements explained
- [ ] Recovery procedures documented
- [ ] Public hosting risks explained
- [ ] Key backup importance emphasized

## Audit Procedure

### For Each Checklist Item

```markdown
## Item: [Checklist item description]

**Status:** PASS / FAIL / N/A

**Evidence:**
[Link to code, test, or documentation]

**Finding:**
[Description of finding if any]

**Remediation:**
[Required fix if FAIL]

**Reviewer:** [Name]
**Date:** [YYYY-MM-DD]
```

### Audit Report Template

```markdown
# CASS Security Audit Report

## Summary
- Total items: 47
- Passed: 45
- Failed: 1
- N/A: 1

## Critical Findings
[None / List]

## High Findings
[None / List]

## Medium Findings
[List with remediation status]

## Low Findings
[List with notes]

## Recommendations
[Future improvements]
```

## Files to Create

- `docs/SECURITY_AUDIT_CHECKLIST.md`: Full checklist
- `docs/SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md`: Audit results
- `scripts/security_scan.sh`: Automated checks
- `tests/security/`: Security-focused tests
- `.github/workflows/security.yml`: Automated security CI

## Exit Criteria
- [ ] All checklist items reviewed
- [ ] No critical or high severity findings
- [ ] All medium findings have remediation plan
- [ ] Audit report published
- [ ] Automated checks integrated in CI
- [ ] Third-party dependencies audited
close_reason: Completed security audit: Fixed HIGH-001 XOR nonce derivation issue in both Rust and JS. Created comprehensive 56-item audit checklist and detailed report. Added 7 security tests verifying nonce uniqueness. All tests pass.

# Phase 2: Plumb Provenance into Indexing Pipeline

## Overview
Now that storage supports provenance, we need to wire it through the indexing pipeline so every conversation gets proper origin metadata.

## Key Changes

### 1. Extend ScanContext
Current ScanContext only has data_root and since_ts. We need:
- List of scan roots (not just one)
- Per-root provenance information
- Platform hints for path mapping

### 2. Indexer Multi-Root Support
The indexer should:
- Build list of scan roots (local defaults + remote mirrors)
- For each root, track which source it belongs to
- Inject provenance into normalized conversations

### 3. Connector Changes (Minimal)
Connectors should NOT need to know about provenance. The indexer:
- Calls connector.scan() with a scan root
- Receives NormalizedConversations
- Injects provenance before persistence

### 4. Deduplication Fix
Current dedup erases origin distinctions. After this phase:
- Dedup key includes source_id
- Same content from different sources = distinct results

## Dependencies
- Phase 1 complete (storage supports provenance)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] ScanContext supports multiple roots with provenance
- [ ] Indexer injects provenance for each root
- [ ] Connectors unchanged (provenance injected externally)
- [ ] Local source works exactly as before
- [ ] Dedup respects source boundaries

title: Phase 5: Remote Sources Configuration & Sync Engine
description:
# Phase 5: Remote Sources Configuration & Sync Engine

## Overview
This is the centerpiece of the remote sources feature. It adds:
1. Configuration system for defining remote sources
2. Sync engine that pulls sessions from remote machines via SSH/rsync
3. CLI commands for managing sources (add, list, sync, doctor)

## Goals
1. `cass sources add ssh://user@host` to register a remote source
2. `cass sources list` to show configured sources with sync status
3. `cass sources sync` to pull latest sessions from all remotes
4. `cass sources doctor` to diagnose connectivity/permission issues

## Technical Approach
- Config stored in `~/.config/cass/sources.toml` or similar
- Sync uses rsync over SSH for efficiency (delta transfer)
- Remote agent session directories are synced to `~/.local/share/cass/remotes/{hostname}/`
- After sync, normal indexing pipeline picks up the sessions with provenance set

```toml
[[sources]]
name = "laptop"
type = "ssh"
host = "user@laptop.local"
paths = [
  "~/.claude/projects",
  "~/.cursor",
]
sync_schedule = "manual"  # or "hourly", "daily"

[[sources]]
name = "workstation"
type = "ssh"
host = "user@work.example.com"
paths = ["~/.claude/projects"]
```

- Requires Phase 2 completion (indexer knows about provenance)
- Independent of Phases 3-4 (can run in parallel)

title: Build reconstructed candidate DB and indexes in isolated staging
description:

title: Fault-inject corrupt DB, WAL/SHM, locks, and interrupted repairs
description:
Background: recovery code is only trustworthy if tests exercise ugly states: corrupt pages, missing sidecars, stale locks, active locks, partial candidates, failed promotion, malformed manifests, and repeated failures. These are exactly the situations where a doctor can accidentally make things worse if the safety gates are vague.

Scope: build fixtures and tests for unreadable DB, frankensqlite open/query failure, quick_check failure where available, WAL without DB, DB without WAL after writes, stale lock, active lock, interrupted candidate build, interrupted promotion, backup verify failure, checksum mismatch, malformed receipt/event log, verification-failed marker, and source coverage shrink after attempted salvage. Each fixture should declare expected anomaly class, outcome_kind, repair eligibility, required forensic behavior, and whether retry is safe.

Acceptance criteria: doctor reports each state accurately; mutating repair refuses unsafe active locks; forensic bundles are captured before planned mutation; interrupted operations are recoverable or safely inspectable; repeated failures stop with verification-failed markers instead of retry loops. Unit tests cover anomaly classification, lock handling, sidecar interpretation, malformed manifest parsing, marker persistence, and retry-safety decisions. E2E/fault-injection scripts emit detailed artifacts for each failure mode: injected corruption, expected safety gate, observed doctor JSON, human output when relevant, receipt/event log, failure_context, before/after filesystem diff, checksums, and assertion summary proving no archive evidence was deleted or overwritten.

title: [MEDIUM] reality-check: README 'self-contained HTML' claim is inaccurate (uses CDN for Tailwind + Prism)
description:
## Claim
README.md line 307-308 (section '📄 HTML Session Export'):

> Self-Contained: All CSS and JS inlined for offline viewing—no external dependencies required
> Progressive Enhancement: CDN resources (Tailwind, Prism.js) enhance styling when online, graceful fallback when offline

The two bullets contradict each other, and the first one is false.

## Actual behavior
`cass export-html <file> --output-dir /tmp` produces a 72 KB HTML that contains:
- 7 `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/...">` tags (Tailwind + Prism core + 5 Prism language components)
- 2 `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/...">` tags (Tailwind CSS, Prism theme)
- 2 inline `<style>` blocks (some but not all CSS)
- 0 inline `<script>` bodies (no JS is inlined)

Prism resources have `onerror` fallbacks that add a `.no-prism` class, so syntax highlighting degrades gracefully offline.

**Tailwind CDN has NO fallback.** When offline, the entire Tailwind runtime fails to load and every `flex`, `p-4`, `text-gray-700`, etc. utility class is unstyled. The page reduces to barely-readable unformatted content.

## Minimal repro
```bash
cat > /tmp/t.jsonl << 'E'
{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}
E
cass export-html /tmp/t.jsonl --output-dir /tmp --filename plain.html
grep -c 'cdn.jsdelivr.net' /tmp/plain.html   # prints 10 (should be 0 if self-contained)
```

Then open `/tmp/plain.html` with network disabled — layout collapses because Tailwind CDN does not load.

## Suggested fix
Either:
1. **Update README to be truthful** — the easy path. Rewrite the bullet to match reality:
   > Mostly Self-Contained: Critical CSS inlined. Uses CDN for Tailwind utility runtime + Prism.js syntax highlighting; Prism has graceful fallback via `.no-prism` class, Tailwind does not.
2. **Actually inline the CDN assets** — the harder path. Bundle Tailwind CSS (compile down to just the utility classes we use via `@tailwindcss/cli`) + Prism.js + language components at build time, embed base64 or escaped into the HTML template. Eliminates network dependency entirely and lives up to the original claim.

Option 1 is the smaller change and matches the existing 'Progressive Enhancement' reality.

Severity: MEDIUM (documentation correctness; does not break the product, but misleads users who rely on the offline claim for air-gapped archival).

Labels: documentation, html-export, reality-check.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2dac41c2: rewrote README.md:307-308 to match shipped behavior — 'Mostly Self-Contained' with explicit Tailwind + Prism CDN callout; 'Progressive Enhancement / Graceful Degradation' clarifies Prism falls back via onerror while Tailwind does not. No code changes — docs now match reality (7 external script tags + 2 external link tags verified via cass export-html).

title: mock-finder: indexer save_watch_state uses fs::write for tmp file with no fsync before atomic-rename (crash-window watch-cursor loss)
description:
Mock-code-finder durability audit follow-up to bead
coding_agent_session_search-j7hqe (closed as fd190dbe).

Fresh sweep of `fs::write` + `File::create` call sites in src/daemon/,
src/indexer/, src/html_export/, and src/bookmarks.rs surfaced two
production-path durability gaps. This bead covers the higher-impact
one; the heartbeat lock write is tracked in a sibling bead.

## Location
`src/indexer/mod.rs:14606-14622` — `save_watch_state`:

```
fn save_watch_state(data_dir: &Path, state: &HashMap<ConnectorKind, i64>) -> Result<()> {
    let path = state_path(data_dir);
    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
        fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
    }
    let watch_state = WatchState { version: 1, map: state.clone() };
    let json = serde_json::to_vec(&watch_state)?;
    // Atomic write: write to temp file then rename, so a crash mid-write
    // cannot leave a truncated/corrupt watch_state.json.
    let tmp_path = unique_atomic_temp_path(&path);
    fs::write(&tmp_path, json)?;                         // <-- NO FSYNC
    replace_file_from_temp(&tmp_path, &path)?;           // rename + sync_parent_directory
    Ok(())
}
```

## Why this is a durability gap
The comment claims the write is atomic, but the atomicity protects only
against torn in-place writes — it does NOT cover the crash window
between `fs::write` returning (data in page cache) and the OS actually
persisting the tmp-file contents to disk. The subsequent
`replace_file_from_temp` fsyncs the *parent directory* (so the dirent
pointing at the new name survives) but never fsyncs the *file bytes*.

Contrast with `write_json_pretty_atomically` at src/indexer/mod.rs:5188,
which gets it right:

```
let file = File::create(&temp_path)?;
let mut writer = BufWriter::new(file);
serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut writer, value)?;
writer.flush()?;
writer.get_ref().sync_all()?;   // <-- fsync the tmp file
drop(writer);
replace_file_from_temp(&temp_path, path)?;  // rename + sync_parent_directory
```

The `save_watch_state` path is missing the `sync_all()` before the
rename. If power fails after the rename returns but before the tmp-file
data reaches disk, the dirent `watch_state.json` points at a file whose
inode is allocated but whose data blocks are zeroed or partially
populated.

## Impact
watch_state.json stores per-connector `last_message_id_ms` cursors.
Losing or zeroing it means on next start-up the indexer cannot resume
from the last-processed message and must either:
- re-walk every source from the beginning (expensive; hundreds of
  thousands of messages), or
- skip sources entirely if the code treats corrupt state as a hard
  error.

Loss pattern matches exactly the class called out in j7hqe/92o31:
"file appears empty after reboot despite a successful-looking write".

## Fix
Either:
(a) Route through the existing `write_json_pretty_atomically` helper
    (preferred — avoids duplicating fsync logic), or
(b) Inline the sync_all step before `replace_file_from_temp`:

```
let file = File::create(&tmp_path)?;
file.write_all(&json)?;
file.sync_all()?;
drop(file);
replace_file_from_temp(&tmp_path, &path)?;
```

## Test
Mirror the pattern from `pages::tests::write_file_durably_surfaces_parent_fsync_error`:
negative-side guard that exercises the fsync code path and surfaces
the error. Happy path: assert that after save_watch_state returns,
a subsequent read sees the exact bytes written.

## Verification
`rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_cass_pane2 \
   cargo test --lib save_watch_state`
plus the full indexer suite: `cargo test --test indexer_*`.
close_reason: Fixed: save_watch_state now uses File::create + BufWriter + sync_all before replace_file_from_temp (commit bb14069a)

title: Build deterministic doctor fixture factory for provider logs and cass data dirs
description:
Background: comprehensive doctor testing needs reusable fixtures rather than one-off temp directory setup hidden inside individual tests. The hardest cases involve multiple providers, mirrored raw bytes, missing upstream files, DB-only legacy rows, WAL and SHM sidecars, corrupted derived assets, stale locks, and redacted sensitive paths. A fixture factory makes those cases cheap and consistent, but only if each fixture declares what it is meant to prove.

Scope: implement a test fixture factory for synthetic cass data dirs, provider source trees, raw mirror blobs, SQLite archive states, lexical and semantic derived assets, stale locks, receipts, backups, source ledgers, support-bundle inputs, and redaction sentinels. Include fixtures for Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Aider, Amp, Cline, OpenCode, Pi Agent, Copilot, OpenClaw, ClawdBot, Vibe, ChatGPT, and FAD-backed providers at the level needed to exercise doctor coverage logic. Every fixture should emit a scenario manifest with fixture_id, provider set, expected source inventory, expected coverage state, expected anomalies, expected mutability/no-mutation contract, privacy sentinels, and cleanup expectations.

Acceptance criteria: fixtures can create healthy, partially indexed, source-pruned, mirror-missing, DB-corrupt, index-corrupt, stale-lock, interrupted-repair, backup-available, low-disk, backup-exclusion, support-bundle, and multi-source states; every fixture emits an expected coverage manifest; fixture setup never writes outside its temp root or real user HOME; tests can request deterministic timestamps, hashes, stable source ids, and stable redaction sentinels; fixture logs follow the structured log contract. Unit tests cover root confinement, deterministic output, hostile paths, no real ~/.codex or ~/.claude writes, privacy sentinel placement, and manifest validation. E2E runner tests use the manifests to assert doctor output instead of duplicating expectations in each scenario.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic doctor fixture factory with provider matrix, scenario manifests, raw mirror/source inventory assertions, privacy and confinement tests, and verified doctor fixture/cli_doctor/check/clippy gates.

title: Isolate CASS semantic daemon protocol and enforce frame identity
description: Fresh-eyes daemon archaeology found that CASS claims and uses the same default UDS path as xf, but the two current protocols are structurally incompatible (different envelope, version width, correlation ID, requests, and responses). The CASS server also executes mismatched-version requests, and the client does not verify response correlation IDs.
acceptance_criteria: CASS defaults to a CASS-owned socket namespace; module/protocol documentation no longer claims current xf wire compatibility; the server rejects a mismatched request protocol version before any side effect; the client rejects a response whose request_id differs from the in-flight request; focused regression tests cover namespace isolation, side-effect-free version rejection, and correlation rejection; mandatory check/clippy/fmt and scoped UBS pass.
close_reason: Implemented CASS-owned daemon socket namespace and strict request/response frame validation. Rejected mismatched request versions before side effects; invalidated client state on malformed, oversized, wrong-version, or wrong-ID responses; corrected health-cache invalidation and host-independent doctor goldens. Verified daemon unit tests 67/67, daemon integration 6/6, robot goldens 49/49 plus final doctor subset 3/3, cargo check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings, fmt, git diff --check, and UBS baseline parity (37 critical/791 warning; no increase).

title: Epic: Operational resilience from 2026-06-08 CASS fleet/session analysis
description:
Source report: COMPREHENSIVE_ISSUES_AND_PROBLEMS_WITH_CASS_BASED_ON_COMPLETE_SESSION_HISTORY_ANALYSIS.md, dated 2026-06-08.

Background:
A broad mining pass across local plus reachable remote CASS/session-history stores found that cass is useful but not yet operationally reliable across the fleet. Every reachable host had degraded, stale, missing, old-version, slow, or partial health/readiness surfaces. The dominant theme is not search ranking; it is resilience and truthful guidance around derived assets: canonical SQLite archive state, scan watermarks, lexical/Tantivy metadata, semantic vector tiers, quarantines, source-path mappings, remote-source state, and host/dependency pressure.

Evidence scope to preserve in this backlog:
- Reachable hosts: local, ts1, ts2, css, csd, mac-mini-max.
- Unreachable evidence gap: mac-mini-old via Tailscale SSH timeout.
- Version skew observed: local/ts1/css at 0.6.13, ts2 at 0.6.10, csd/mac-mini-max at 0.4.1.
- Current/fleet symptoms: stale indexes, missing lexical metadata, status/doctor timeouts, old doctor capability gaps, semantic unavailable, quarantine/OOM, database-busy/OpenRead/FTS evidence, workspace/source-path mismatch, remote sync/auth fragility, dependency noise from frankensqlite/frankensearch/asupersync, and very large session corpora that defeat naive raw scans.

Overarching goal:
Make cass safe and boring for future agents: stale-but-searchable states remain usable, missing/corrupt derived assets rebuild through bounded and archive-preserving paths, high archive-risk hosts demand backup/inspection first, robot commands are quiet and bounded, quarantines explain exactly what is excluded, fleet probes preserve slow/unreachable hosts as data, and incident/history mining is native rather than reimplemented by every agent.

Governing constraints:
- SQLite archive is the source of truth; lexical and semantic indexes are derived assets.
- No destructive cleanup or source-log mutation; quarantine and backup/repair flows must be explicit and fingerprinted where risky.
- New SQLite work must use frankensqlite, not rusqlite.
- Robot output must remain parseable: stdout is data only, diagnostics stay in stderr or trace artifacts.
- Existing guided-ops/swarm epics are related, but this epic is specifically the operational-resilience backlog extracted from the 2026-06-08 full session-history analysis.

Success criteria for the whole epic:
A future agent does not need the original markdown report. The Beads graph itself tells them the problem classes, why each matters, where to work, which prerequisites block which slices, and what proof is required before closing work.

Acceptance: the complete resilience graph remains self-contained and traceable to the report, every implementation leaf has explicit proof requirements, the subsystem matrix covers all report failure-mode files, dependency cycles remain absent, and future closure must cite the required unit/integration/E2E/golden/log artifacts instead of relying on prose-only claims.

title: Add integrated golden and E2E gate for the full resilience graph
description:
Goal: after the underlying streams land, add an integrated gate that runs representative scenarios through readiness, robot boundedness, quarantine, liveness, semantic fallback/model acquisition, fleet, workspace/archive fallback, remote source configuration, storage integrity, attribution, incident mining, user-facing recovery guidance, and the peripheral subsystem matrix for connectors, daemon/cache, HTML export/encryption, bookmarks, analytics, update checks, pages, and TUI surfaces.

Why this gate exists: the report shows real incidents are bundles, not single strings. A realistic failure can combine stale derived metadata, storage busy/OpenRead symptoms, connector partial ingest, daemon/cache staleness, missing semantic assets, remote/source drift, workspace mismatch, and misleading human output. The final proof must therefore exercise integrated product behavior rather than isolated unit success.

Acceptance: fixtures combine multiple problem classes; the gate proves deterministic JSON, stable redaction, useful safe next commands, no robot stdout pollution, no contradictions between robot and human surfaces, and no coverage gaps in the subsystem matrix. Closure must cite the .12.1 matrix rows, the .15.5 subsystem coverage gate, structured logs/artifact manifests, reviewed golden diffs where applicable, and E2E/CI-browser evidence for user-visible surfaces.

title: Epic: Comprehensive test scripts and proof logging for resilience rollout
description:
Background: The first-pass resilience plan deliberately captured the product/runtime problems from the complete session-history report, but the proof requirements were concentrated mostly in the final regression/proof epic. That is not optimal for implementation planning: if test strategy and logging standards are defined only at the end, feature work can land with inconsistent coverage, weak evidence, or hard-to-debug E2E failures.

Goal: create a first-class proof workstream that overlays every resilience stream with explicit unit-test, integration-test, E2E-script, fixture, logging, and CI/local verification expectations before implementation begins.

Principle: no functionality is removed or simplified. This epic exists to preserve the full feature set by making verification cheaper, earlier, and more uniform. Every report-derived behavior must be testable through deterministic fixtures or bounded opt-in live probes, and every proof artifact must explain exactly what ran, what binary/data/config was used, what passed, what failed, and what was skipped.

Acceptance: each workstream has a mapped test matrix; E2E scripts emit structured detailed logs; proof artifacts are redaction-aware and reviewable; local/CI commands are documented; integrated gates fail when logs are missing, ambiguous, stale, or generated-only; and implementers can close leaf beads without consulting the original markdown report.

title: Define per-workstream unit/E2E test matrix and closure checklist
description:
Background: The resilience graph spans readiness, robot boundedness, quarantine, long-operation liveness, semantic fallback and model acquisition, fleet doctor, storage integrity and legacy DB repair, workspace/archive fallback, remote sync and source configuration, root-cause attribution, incident mining, proof logging, user-facing recovery journeys, and peripheral user-visible subsystems such as connectors, daemon/cache, HTML export/encryption, bookmarks, analytics, update checks, generated pages, and TUI/human surfaces. Those streams touch different modules and failure modes, so a single vague "add tests" instruction would let important cases fall through.

Goal: define a self-contained test matrix that maps every resilience epic and leaf implementation task to the exact proof expected.

Required contents:
- Unit tests for pure schema/classifier/planner/copy-projection logic, including negative and boundary cases.
- Integration tests for storage/index/search/source/doctor/workflow interactions with isolated temp data dirs and frankensqlite-backed fixtures.
- Real-binary E2E scripts for robot JSON and human-facing surfaces that are most likely to regress in actual operator use.
- CI-only browser E2E coverage where local browser runs are inappropriate, especially HTML export rendering/security and page/TUI-adjacent human surfaces.
- Golden/snapshot tests only where they freeze intentional JSON or human-output contracts; generated goldens must be reviewed, not blindly blessed.
- Fixture provenance: which report-derived failure class or host state the fixture represents, what data is synthetic, and which privacy/redaction assumptions apply.
- Logging expectations: command, binary identity, env knobs, fixture id, data dir, start/end timestamps, duration, exit status, timeout state, stdout/stderr locations, parsed JSON status, assertions, and redaction summary.
- Subsystem coverage rows for analytics, bookmarks, cache, cli_robot, connectors, daemon, html_export, indexer, models, pages, search, sources, storage, tui, and update_check, with an owning bead and proof path for each.

Acceptance: the matrix covers epics .1 through .15, including semantic model-acquisition, source-config, storage, connector ingest, daemon/cache, HTML export/encryption, bookmark/analytics/update/pages/TUI surfaces, and the subsystem coverage matrix itself; it names at least one unit or integration target for every feature family; it names E2E or CI-browser coverage for user-facing robot and human surfaces; and it makes clear which tests are mandatory for closure versus optional live diagnostics.

title: Build shared bounded E2E runner with structured detailed logs
description:
Background: The report repeatedly shows commands that were too slow, noisy, blocked by dependency logs, or ambiguous when run against real binaries. A useful E2E gate must be bounded, parseable, and easy to debug after failure.

Goal: specify and implement a shared E2E script runner for CASS robot-mode resilience tests.

Required behavior:
- Runs the installed/test-built cass binary, never bare interactive cass.
- Uses explicit robot/json flags, `--color=never` where appropriate, bounded timeouts, isolated CASS data/config/model directories, and non-destructive fixtures.
- Captures stdout and stderr separately, preserving the stdout=data / stderr=diagnostics contract.
- Emits one structured JSONL event stream per run with command line, binary path/version/hash when available, environment overrides, cwd, fixture id, phase, start/end timestamps, elapsed_ms, exit_code, signal/timeout status, parsed_json_ok, assertion results, and artifact paths.
- Produces concise human-readable summaries while retaining full logs for CI artifacts.
- Supports local quick mode, full CI mode, and opt-in live fleet mode without making live hosts mandatory for deterministic CI.

Acceptance: at least one representative command from health/status/search/view/doctor/source/fleet surfaces can be executed through the runner; failures identify whether the problem is command failure, timeout, invalid JSON, assertion failure, missing fixture, or log/artifact loss; and logs are detailed enough for a future agent to debug without rerunning immediately.

title: Define proof logging schema, artifact manifest, and retention policy
description:
Background: Proof artifacts are only useful if they distinguish actual verification from stale output, generated docs, partial timeouts, and tests that exercised a mock path instead of the real operator surface. The session-history report specifically criticized cases where green-looking evidence did not prove the user-facing behavior.

Goal: define the proof logging schema and artifact-retention policy used by the E2E runner, golden gates, and final closeout reports.

Required schema fields:
- run_id, scenario_id, issue_ids_covered, fixture_id, command_id, phase, started_at, finished_at, elapsed_ms.
- cass_binary_path, cass_version, git_revision when available, cargo profile, feature flags, target dir, data dir, config dir, model dir, source roots.
- argv as executed, sanitized_env, timeout_ms, exit_code, signal, timed_out, retry_count.
- stdout_path, stderr_path, parsed_stdout_json, parsed_stderr_json_if_expected, robot_contract_ok, ansi_free_stdout_ok.
- assertions with names, expected values, actual values, pass/fail/skip, and failure hints.
- redaction_status, privacy_notes, artifact_manifest_path, stale_artifact_check, generated_artifact_check.

Acceptance: proof logs make it impossible to confuse "command passed", "command timed out after partial output", "old artifact was reused", "JSON was invalid", and "test did not run"; retention rules keep enough artifacts for debugging while avoiding private session content leaks; and final proof reports cite structured artifacts rather than prose-only claims.
close_reason: Shipped in commit fca7ea4c: src/search/proof_log.rs. ProofOutcome + OutcomeSignals::outcome() derive a single mutually-exclusive verdict distinguishing the five confusable outcomes (passed, timed_out_partial, stale_artifact_reused, invalid_json, did_not_run, plus explicit failed) in an order where not-run/timeout/stale-reuse are decided before pass/fail (a timed-out run with a stale zero exit never reads as passed). ProofLogRecord carries all required fields: run/scenario/issue_ids_covered/fixture/command ids, phase, started/finished/elapsed; ProofRunMeta (binary path, version, git revision, cargo profile, feature flags, target/data/config/model dirs, source roots); ProofExecution (argv, sanitized_env, timeout_ms, exit_code, signal, timed_out, retry_count); ProofArtifacts (stdout/stderr paths, parsed stdout/stderr JSON, robot_contract_ok, ansi_free_stdout_ok). RetentionPolicy keeps most-recent-N + all non-pass and drops old passes past max_age; a redaction guard (secret_leak_keys / is_redaction_safe) refuses to retain records whose sanitized_env carries secret-bearing keys so artifacts never leak private content. Acceptance proven: cargo test --lib search::proof_log 7 passed 0 failed covering snake_case wire forms, each confusable outcome distinguished (incl timeout-never-pass), full record JSON round-trip with required fields, retention keep/drop rules, redaction guard; ubs exit 0 (0 critical); module clippy-clean. Consumed by .12.2 runner / .12.5 scenarios / .12.6 CI recipe.

title: Specify comprehensive unit-test harness requirements by feature family
description:
Background: Several proposed fixes are schema, planner, classifier, resolver, or state-machine work. Those need fast unit tests that fail close to the defect, before slower E2E scripts run.

Goal: specify the unit-test harness requirements for every feature family in the resilience rollout.

Coverage expectations:
- Readiness truth table: every lexical/semantic/archive/quarantine/source-existence combination, including conflicting states.
- Command envelopes: safe versus unsafe next command classification, timeout/partial-result envelopes, stdout/stderr hygiene, ANSI behavior, and err.kind stability.
- Quarantine: cause/version/eligibility grouping, retry eligibility, incomplete metadata, and migration from legacy quarantine records.
- Liveness: progress heartbeat, stalled versus slow versus complete states, resume checkpoints, and parseable watch-mode errors.
- Semantic fallback: model absent, disabled, stale vectors, catch-up in progress, fingerprint mismatch, lexical-only fallback, and truthful realized mode.
- Fleet/source/remote: host capability differences, unreachable hosts, stale source paths, archive-only drilldown, additive remote mirror preservation, SSH/rsync fallback selection.
- Root-cause and incident mining: deterministic category classification, bounded scan caps, redaction, host rollups, and privacy-safe snippets.

Acceptance: unit tests are explicit enough that implementers know where to add them; tests cover happy path, negative path, boundary/empty cases, and representative report-derived regressions; and no new SQLite tests introduce rusqlite in new code.

title: Add report-derived E2E scenario scripts for fleet and archive states
description:
Background: The report's important failures were fleet-shaped, not isolated toy cases: local stale/quarantine states, ts1 archive risk, ts2 timeout, css dependency noise, csd old or missing metadata, mac stale/path mismatch, and mac-mini-old unreachable or intermittent sync. CI cannot depend on those live hosts, but implementation must still prove the behavior.

Goal: define deterministic E2E scenarios that simulate the report-derived fleet states, plus an opt-in live mode for operators who want to replay against actual machines.

Required scenarios:
- Local healthy lexical with semantic unavailable: search succeeds with truthful lexical fallback metadata.
- Local stale derived assets plus quarantined ingest entries: health/status/doctor explain rebuild/quarantine state without data-loss advice.
- Archive-risk state: outputs are backup-first and never recommend deletion or destructive cleanup.
- Long rebuild/watch stall: status reports progress/stall fields and command envelopes remain bounded.
- Dependency-noise state: robot stdout stays parseable while dependency/runtime diagnostics are routed to stderr or trace artifacts.
- Stale source path / moved workspace: search exposes archive provenance and view/expand can drill into archived content when originals are missing.
- Remote unreachable/old host: fleet/source doctor preserves host config, reports reachability/version/tooling gaps, and gives safe next commands.
- Incident-mining large corpus: bounded scan emits partial-success metadata, top categories, redaction summary, and artifact paths.

Acceptance: every scenario has fixture setup, command sequence, expected JSON assertions, expected log artifacts, and privacy notes; live-host execution is clearly opt-in and never required for default CI; and failures point to the owning implementation bead.

title: Define CI/local proof recipe and log-completeness gate
description:
Background: Even good tests fail to protect users if the required local/CI invocation is unclear, too slow, or silently omits artifacts. The repo already has strict compiler, clippy, fmt, UBS, golden, and real-binary expectations; the resilience rollout needs a single execution recipe that joins those gates without replacing them.

Goal: define the local and CI proof recipe for the resilience rollout, including log review and artifact sanity checks.

Required recipe:
- Compiler/lint/format commands follow AGENTS.md: `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-check-target cargo check --all-targets`, clippy with `-D warnings`, and fmt check after substantive code changes.
- Targeted cargo tests for unit/integration feature families, using isolated target dirs where useful.
- Golden update flow only through reviewed `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` runs when JSON contracts intentionally change.
- Shared E2E runner quick/full modes with artifact directory, timeout budget, and structured log manifest.
- UBS changed-file preflight for implementation changes.
- Log completeness gate: fail when required stdout/stderr/log/manifest artifacts are missing, stale, unparseable, generated-only, or internally inconsistent.
- Human review checklist: inspect changed goldens, inspect failed/skipped scenarios, confirm no live-host dependency slipped into default CI, and confirm proof logs do not leak private session content.

title: Epic: User-facing recovery journeys and human/robot guidance parity
description:
Background: The resilience plan is strong for agent/robot JSON surfaces, but the system also has human operators who need to understand what cass is doing without reconstructing state through jq, logs, or tribal memory. title: Define end-to-end user recovery journey scenarios

title: Mirror robot readiness in bounded human CLI/TUI summaries
description:
Background: Robot JSON is the source of truth for agents, but humans still need concise CLI/TUI summaries that do not contradict the machine contract. A human should not need to learn the internal distinction between SQLite archive, lexical metadata, semantic vectors, quarantines, and source mappings before deciding what to do safely.

- Human text includes the dominant state, why it matters, whether search is usable now, what is missing or stale, and the safest next action.

- It never recommends destructive cleanup, bare interactive automation, or rebuilds that violate archive-risk preconditions.
- It preserves nuance: stale-searchable is different from missing; semantic-unavailable is different from lexical-broken; quarantine-incomplete is different from no results; unreachable remote is different from removed source.

title: Epic: Storage integrity, legacy DB interop, and concurrency-safe repair
description:
Background: The report contains a direct storage failure cluster that is too important to leave implicit under generic readiness or dependency attribution. Historical and generated failure-mode evidence includes frankensqlite OpenRead cursor failures, integrity-check failures after crashes or WAL truncation, schema-version drift, busy/lock timeouts across daemon/CLI/indexer/TUI access, stale WAL/SHM sidecars, legacy rusqlite/frankensqlite interop risks, and FTS/search paths that fail only after storage drift. Users experience these as stale indexes, zero results, doctor repair confusion, or unsafe rebuild advice, but the real risk is archive integrity and repair correctness.

Goal: make storage integrity, legacy database readability, and concurrency-safe repair a first-class recovery stream. CASS must distinguish derived-index drift from source-of-truth archive damage, require backup-first repair when archive integrity is uncertain, and produce precise robot/human guidance that prevents destructive guesswork.

Principle: SQLite/archive data is the source of truth. Derived indexes can be rebuilt; archive databases must be diagnosed, backed up, fingerprinted, and repaired through explicit plans. New SQLite work must use frankensqlite or fix frankensqlite when a needed capability is missing; do not add new rusqlite code as an escape hatch.

Acceptance: health/status/doctor/fleet/search surfaces can name storage-integrity families, safe/unsafe next commands, backup/restore preconditions, and whether search remains usable. Unit tests cover classifier/planner logic; integration tests cover frankensqlite-backed fixtures; E2E scripts exercise real-binary robot and human surfaces with structured logs and artifact manifests.

title: Define storage-integrity diagnostic taxonomy and JSON contract
description:
Background: Storage failures currently show up as scattered symptoms: OpenRead cursor errors, integrity-check failures, stale WAL/SHM sidecars, schema-version drift, busy locks, FTS metadata mismatch, legacy database readability problems, SQL construction/bind-risk patterns, and zero-result search regressions. Without a shared taxonomy, doctor/status can give generic stale-index advice when the operator actually needs archive-risk handling.

Goal: define the storage-integrity diagnostic contract used by health, status, doctor, triage, fleet, search metadata, and support bundles.

Required fields:
- storage_state: ok, derived_only_drift, busy_or_locked, wal_sidecar_suspect, schema_drift, openread_failed, integrity_failed, legacy_interop_failed, fts_metadata_failed, unsafe_sql_shape, unknown_deferred.
- source_of_truth_risk: none, low, medium, high, unknown.
- archive_readability: readable, partially_readable, unreadable, not_checked, timed_out.
- checks_attempted with elapsed_ms, timed_out, skipped_reason, and whether each check is read-only.
- safe_next_commands, unsafe_commands, preconditions, backup_required, repair_plan_available, and expected mutation scope.
- dependency_attribution fields that distinguish CASS code, frankensqlite engine, host pressure, stale sidecar, unsafe SQL construction/query shape, and old binary skew.

Acceptance: contract tests cover every enum value and ensure kebab/snake-case stability; fixtures cover OpenRead, integrity failure, schema drift, busy lock, stale WAL/SHM, unsafe SQL construction/query-shape diagnostics, FTS metadata failure, and legacy DB readability; robot JSON and human summaries share the same vocabulary; implementation tests use bound parameters for variable SQL values and do not add new rusqlite code.

title: Add backup-first storage salvage and repair planner
description:
Background: The report cites doctor and storage repair cases where unsafe or misleading recovery guidance is worse than no guidance. Storage repair must not delete source logs, overwrite archive databases, or silently convert formats without a reviewed plan.

Goal: define and implement a backup-first storage salvage and repair planner with dry-run JSON, explicit manifests, and safe abort behavior.

Required behavior:
- Dry-run plan lists source DB path, backup path, fingerprints, sidecars, schema version, integrity/readability checks, expected mutations, and estimated cost/risk.
- High-risk storage states require backup and explicit operator confirmation before mutation; read-only diagnostics remain available without mutation.
- Repair paths distinguish rebuild-derived-index, checkpoint/recover WAL, recreate sidecar, migrate legacy metadata, targeted FTS repair, and archive reconstruction from source connectors.
- Every mutating plan records before/after fingerprints, command provenance, elapsed_ms, partial failure status, and rollback/restore guidance.
- No new rusqlite code is introduced; if frankensqlite lacks a required read/repair capability, the plan should create/fix that capability in frankensqlite first.

Acceptance: unit tests cover planner decisions and unsafe-command suppression; integration fixtures cover each storage state; E2E scripts verify dry-run, refused unsafe mutation, successful low-risk derived repair, high-risk backup-required flow, and structured proof logs. The plan never recommends deleting archive files or raw session logs.

High-risk archive states require backup+confirmation; unsafe SQL/unknown/no-source refuse and preserve evidence; no command is ever bare/destructive. 20 unit tests + proof-log scenarios pass; 0 UBS critical, 0 production warnings; no rusqlite. Real-binary E2E gate is dependent bead 14.4.

title: Harden concurrency, busy-lock, WAL sidecar, and stale-cache diagnostics
description:
Background: Several failure classes involve concurrent writers/readers or sidecar state rather than corrupt user data: CLI plus daemon plus indexer can hit busy locks, killed processes can leave WAL/SHM artifacts, and stale cached searchers can serve old segments after publish. Users need CASS to explain contention as contention, not as missing data.

Goal: harden and test the diagnostic behavior around concurrent storage access, busy locks, stale sidecars, and cached derived-search state.

Required behavior:
- Classify busy/locked, busy-recovery, stale WAL/SHM, stale searcher/cache, and host-pressure variants separately.
- Provide retry/backoff guidance and bounded wait recommendations without blocking robot commands indefinitely.
- Surface which process/lock evidence was observed when available, while avoiding fragile platform-specific assumptions.
- Keep read-only probes safe under concurrent index/watch/daemon/TUI activity.
- Ensure stale cached searchers or derived artifacts are invalidated or reported, not silently treated as archive loss.

Acceptance: unit tests cover lock-state classification and retryability; integration tests simulate reader/writer contention with frankensqlite-backed temp DBs; E2E tests run bounded health/status/search/doctor probes under contention fixtures and emit detailed logs proving partial-result behavior, timeout classification, and no archive mutation.

Unit tests cover classification+retryability+bounded-wait+cache-staleness+platform-tolerance. title: Migrate 83 legacy dotted Beads IDs through a lossless br-supported mapping; unblock doctor and sync
description: CASS tracker JSONL contains 83 structurally valid issue records whose legacy dotted IDs are rejected by br 0.2.19 as invalid format expected prefix-hash. The canonical SQLite DB is page-healthy and operational for current issues but has 1,924 issues while JSONL has 2,279 unique records. br sync --flush-only correctly refuses because export would lose 355 issues; br sync --reconcile --dry-run stops at the first invalid legacy ID; br doctor reports workspace unsafe with 83 malformed records and has no registered fixer for this class. Our current valid changes are already present in JSONL and DB. Do not force export, rebuild from the invalid JSONL, hand-edit JSONL, delete recovery artifacts, or silently discard legacy rows. This requires a supported br migration path.
design: Add or use a br CLI migration that first emits a dry-run mapping and recovery witness, then atomically renames each invalid legacy issue to a valid stable ID while rewriting every parent, dependency, comment, label, event and external reference edge. Preserve the original ID in an explicit legacy_id or external_ref field and emit an old-to-new mapping artifact. Mapping must be deterministic, collision-checked, prefix-correct, stable across reruns, and preserve hierarchy semantics without pretending dotted suffixes are valid new IDs. The transaction must fail closed on any unknown reference, duplicate target, count loss, dependency cycle change, or JSON/schema error. It must operate through br tooling only, use br doctor run backups and undo support, and never delete the existing DB, JSONL, WAL/SHM, or recovery directories.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only dry run inventories exactly all invalid IDs and all incoming/outgoing references and emits deterministic old-to-new mapping and pre-migration witness hashes. The real br migration preserves at least all 2,279 current unique JSONL issues plus any later additions, all 83 legacy records, comments, labels, close state, timestamps, parent/child structure and dependency edges with zero orphan or duplicate records. title: Epic: Peripheral subsystem resilience and user-visible surface regression coverage
description:
Background: The 2026-06-08 report did not only identify core storage/search/readiness failures. It also cited 15 subsystem failure-mode files: analytics, bookmarks, cache, cli_robot, connectors, daemon, html_export, indexer, models, pages, search, sources, storage, tui, and update_check. The existing resilience graph already owns many core index/storage/fleet/model/source issues, but several user-visible surfaces were still under-modeled as first-class work: connector ingest edge cases, daemon/cache freshness, HTML export and encryption safety, bookmark/analytics persistence, update-check safety, generated pages, and TUI/human output parity.

Why this matters: users experience cass as a complete tool, not as a storage engine. A connector collision can merge unrelated conversations; a locked Cursor database or encrypted ChatGPT directory can look like zero imported data; a stale daemon/searcher cache can keep showing old results after a successful publish; an unsafe export can leak or execute user content; bookmark/analytics drift can silently misrepresent important history; and update/page/TUI regressions can steer operators toward wrong or unsafe action. These are not cosmetic edges. They affect trust in the archive, search results, recovery guidance, and shared proof artifacts.

Goal: give every report-backed subsystem a clear owner, explicit acceptance criteria, unit/integration/E2E proof expectations, and structured logging requirements so future agents do not need the original markdown report to know what must be preserved.

Scope boundaries:
- This epic complements, rather than replaces, the existing core epics for readiness, storage, semantic models, sources, incident mining, proof infrastructure, and human/robot guidance.
- It should not duplicate every low-level implementation detail already covered elsewhere. It should own the subsystem-specific failure modes and the cross-subsystem coverage gate.
- No functionality should be dropped to make the plan easier. If a subsystem is user-visible in README or present in a report failure-mode file, the coverage matrix must either assign it to an existing bead or create a targeted bead here.

Acceptance: the graph has explicit beads for connector ingest diagnostics, daemon/cache freshness, HTML export/encryption safety, bookmark/analytics/update/pages/TUI drift, and a subsystem coverage matrix. Each leaf requires comprehensive unit tests, isolated integration fixtures where applicable, bounded E2E scripts or CI-only browser tests for user-facing surfaces, and detailed structured proof logs with redaction checks.

title: Harden connector ingest diagnostics and per-provider failure fixtures
description:
Background: The report's connector findings included a P0 Aider external ID collision, malformed JSONL panic/whole-file abort risk, Cursor state.vscdb locked by the live app, ChatGPT encrypted directories that are undecipherable on Linux/headless hosts, and Amp filename-prefix assumptions that are fragile if provider schemes change. README positions connectors as the front door for 20 local agents, so connector failures directly become lost, merged, duplicated, or misleading search history.

Goal: make connector ingest failures explicit, provider-specific, retry-aware, and testable. A connector should never silently turn a provider-specific limitation into a fake zero-message import or merge unrelated conversations under the same external ID.

Required behavior:
- Define a connector ingest diagnostic taxonomy with provider, source path, workspace/source provenance, line/row identifier when available, external_id/canonical_id context, severity, retryability, and safe next action.
- Aider external IDs include stable disambiguators such as workspace/source identity so distinct project histories cannot collide and merge conversations.
- Malformed or truncated JSONL preserves valid records where safe and quarantines the bad line/session with an actionable diagnostic instead of panicking or aborting the whole file/root.
- Cursor locked vscdb reads report lock-busy/retryable state with a clear hint and do not claim successful zero-message ingestion.
- ChatGPT encrypted directories on Linux/headless hosts report unsupported/credential-required or keychain-unavailable state; legacy unencrypted conversations still index normally.
- Amp and other filename/path parsers avoid unsafe byte slicing and validate assumptions against non-ASCII and future-looking fixture names.
- Provider summary output distinguishes discovered, skipped, quarantined, partially indexed, locked, unsupported-encrypted, and successfully indexed sources.

Acceptance: unit tests cover the taxonomy and per-provider classifier decisions; connector fixtures cover Aider collision, malformed JSONL, Cursor lock, ChatGPT encrypted/unencrypted, Amp Unicode/path variants, and at least the README's major provider families; an isolated E2E index run over a mixed fixture corpus proves counts, quarantines, warnings, and searchability of valid records; proof logs include connector_summary, per-provider counts, fixture IDs, elapsed_ms, retryable flags, and no private payload leakage.
close_reason: Added src/connector_ingest_diagnostics.rs: pure-logic provider-specific ingest diagnostic taxonomy. IngestSeverity + IngestFailureKind (external-id-collision-risk/malformed-json-line/truncated-session/source-locked/encrypted-unsupported/keychain-unavailable/filename-assumption-violated/unreadable-source) + SourceIngestDisposition (the non-silent discovered/indexed/partially/quarantined/skipped/locked/unsupported-encrypted breakdown) + classify() per-provider (Cursor lock=retryable not zero-import, ChatGPT encrypted=explicit limitation w/ legacy-unencrypted-still-indexes, etc.) + ProviderIngestSummary + disambiguated_external_id (collision-safe Aider id via blake3 workspace hash). 18 tests, 0 critical UBS (panic-free production), clippy/fmt clean. Live ingest-summary wiring + per-provider connector hardening (much in franken_agent_detection) + fixture E2E deferred to follow-on stmh6.

title: Add daemon socket pidfile cache and stale-searcher recovery coverage
description:
Background: The report called out daemon stale pidfile/socket behavior, an FD leak on try_clone failure, and stale SearcherManager cache behavior after atomic lexical publish. README promises zero-stall updates, reader reloads, background daemon behavior, and cache warming; stale daemon/cache state makes cass appear healthy while serving old or inaccessible search results.

Goal: make daemon runtime artifacts and searcher caches self-diagnosing and recoverable without risking user data or requiring operators to guess whether they are attached to a ghost process or stale generation.

Required behavior:
- Daemon startup and client attach validate pidfile/socket state against a live process/generation; stale runtime artifacts are treated as disposable runtime state, not archive data, and are safely replaced or reported according to platform rules.
- Socket and pidfile diagnostics appear in robot status/doctor/fleet outputs with state, owning pid if known, socket path, data_dir, generation, last heartbeat, and safe next action.
- try_clone and other socket-handling failures close file descriptors promptly and emit structured diagnostics rather than leaking handles over long sessions.
- SearcherManager or equivalent cache holders detect lexical publish generation changes and reload before serving stale segments after atomic publish.
- Cache metrics distinguish cache hit, stale-generation miss, forced reload, reload failure, and fallback behavior without polluting robot stdout.
- Long-running daemon/cache checks remain bounded and produce partial JSON if platform probing is slow.

Acceptance: unit tests cover stale pidfile/socket classification, FD cleanup paths, cache-generation comparison, and metric serialization; integration tests simulate atomic publish then verify fresh search visibility; bounded E2E scripts exercise daemon start, stale runtime-artifact recovery in a temp data dir, publish/reload, and parseable status output; proof logs include daemon pid/generation, socket_state, cache_generation_before/after, reload reason, fd-count checks where supported, timing, and stdout/stderr separation.
close_reason: Added src/daemon_runtime_state.rs: pure-logic daemon runtime-artifact + searcher-cache classification. DaemonRuntimeState (ok/not-running/generation-skew/stale-socket/stale-lock/ghost-process/unresponsive) + classify() precedence + safe_recovery() with the disposable-runtime-artifact-never-touches-archive invariant (test-proven); SearcherCacheOutcome taxonomy (hit/cold-miss/stale-generation-miss/forced-reload/reload-failure/fallback) + classify_cache_outcome() + SearcherCacheMetrics serialization. 22 tests pass, 0 critical UBS (panic-free production), clippy/fmt clean. Bounded daemon probe + status/doctor wiring + query.rs metric-counter integration + restart E2E deferred to follow-on b7tb0 (matches the epic's diagnostic-module pattern).

title: Secure HTML export encryption and content-rendering regression coverage
description:
Background: README advertises portable HTML export, optional encryption, print/search features, and robot JSON output. The report identified markdown/HTML injection, opaque encryption metadata failures, nonce type-safety risk, and UTF-8 byte-slicing risk as concrete problems. Exported sessions often contain private code, tool output, tokens, and sensitive debugging context, so this surface needs security-grade regression coverage instead of casual snapshot checks.

Goal: make HTML export safe, deterministic, diagnosable, and trustworthy for both unencrypted archival use and password-protected sharing.

Required behavior:
- User/session content is escaped or sanitized consistently across markdown, HTML tables, code blocks, tool-call renderers, inline search highlights, and print/search UI.
- Malicious content fixtures cannot execute script, break out of containers, corrupt tables, or alter the export control surface.
- Encryption code uses fixed-size nonce/key/tag types or equivalent compile-time/runtime validation so byte-slice length mistakes cannot silently ship.
- Encryption metadata fully records the KDF/parameters/version/salt/nonce/tag format required for future decrypt, and decrypt failures identify wrong password, unsupported metadata, corrupt payload, or implementation bug without exposing secrets.
- Password stdin and explicit password paths are covered; logs never include the password, decrypted payload, or raw sensitive fixture content.
- UTF-8 and non-ASCII session content is sliced/truncated/rendered through character-safe logic rather than raw byte indexing that can panic or corrupt output.
- Offline/air-gapped rendering behavior is explicit: CDN-dependent enhancement failures degrade to readable content and are captured by browser logs when browser E2E is run in CI.
- Robot JSON reports output path, size, encryption state, message count, warnings, and error kinds in the documented envelope.

Acceptance: unit tests cover sanitizer escaping, markdown/table/code rendering, fixed-size nonce validation, KDF metadata roundtrip, wrong-password/corrupt-payload errors, UTF-8/non-ASCII content, safe truncation, and redaction of logs; integration tests export synthetic malicious and encrypted sessions; CI E2E/browser scripts open exports, assert no console/page errors for allowed fixtures, assert malicious content is inert, and verify encrypted export/decrypt flow; proof logs include fixture id, export path, byte size, encryption_metadata_summary, browser-console artifact references, stderr/stdout paths, and redaction summary.
close_reason: Added tests/html_export_sanitization_security.rs: real-binary malicious-content security-regression suite (12-vector injection corpus proven inert: script/img-onerror/attr-breakout/close-script/svg/iframe/event-handler/style/pre-encoded-entities/markdown-js+data URLs) + encrypted-export-no-body/secret-leak (stdin channel) + stable error envelopes (session-not-found code3, password-required code6). Closes the no-prior-coverage malicious-content gap; existing suites (crypto_vectors/spec_crypto_roundtrip_proptest/spec_export_html_envelopes/crypto_tracing_safety/metamorphic_html_export) cover nonce/KDF/envelope/log-redaction/UTF-8. 3 tests pass, 0C/0W UBS, fmt clean. Browser-E2E console/CDN + pages decrypt taxonomy follow-on filed.

title: Protect bookmarks analytics bakeoff pages update and TUI surfaces from silent drift
description:
Background: The report listed bookmark silent row decode, non-atomic bookmark import, analytics aggregate incompatibility/zero token counts, bakeoff divide-by-zero/NaN metrics, charts masking intent with saturating zero behavior, update shell-injection/clock-rollback risks, and generated pages/TUI failure-mode files. README presents bookmarks, analytics dashboards, bakeoff/validation helpers, update notifications, pages/exported surfaces, and rich TUI behavior as product features. Silent drift in these surfaces can make users trust wrong data or run unsafe update/recovery flows.

Goal: make these auxiliary-but-user-visible surfaces strict, transactional, and aligned with robot truth instead of silently smoothing over data, schema, or environment problems.

Required behavior:
- Bookmark row decode fails with structured schema/version diagnostics instead of defaulting through incompatible rows; import/export operations are transactional and report partial/failure state without partial commits.
- Analytics rollups distinguish true zero usage from missing data, failed grouped aggregates, schema incompatibility, and rebuild-required state; charts and TUI summaries expose no-data versus zero-data intentionally.
- Bakeoff/evaluation metrics detect empty baselines, zero denominators, missing corpora, and invalid score inputs as structured no-data or invalid-input outcomes, never NaN/Inf success.
- Update-check and self-update helpers validate version/URL/command arguments, avoid shell interpolation, handle clock rollback with saturating/non-panicking time math, and remain quiet/offline-safe in automated contexts.
- Pages and TUI views consume the same underlying readiness/error/proof state as robot output wherever practical, so human summaries do not contradict JSON truth surfaces.
- Any human-facing warning or toast has a robot/log equivalent that tests can assert.

Acceptance: unit tests cover bookmark decode/import transactionality, analytics aggregate edge cases, bakeoff no-data/zero-denominator handling, chart no-data rendering decisions, update argument validation, clock rollback, and TUI/page projection helpers; integration tests use isolated bookmark/analytics/temp data dirs; E2E scripts exercise bookmark import/export, analytics rebuild/status, bakeoff no-data behavior, update dry-run/offline paths, and headless TUI/page snapshots where available; proof logs include operation, fixture id, before/after row counts, transaction outcome, aggregate status, metric status, update validation result, human/robot parity assertions, and detailed stdout/stderr artifacts.
close_reason: Added src/metric_integrity.rs: pure-logic metric-integrity taxonomy unifying the silent-drift theme. MetricOutcome keeps true-zero distinct from no-data/aggregate-failed/schema-incompatible/rebuild-required/invalid-input; safe_ratio/classify_aggregate/bakeoff_quality_ratio/improvement_pct compute through it so a zero baseline/denominator or NaN/Inf input is structured no-data/invalid, never a passing NaN/Inf (the reported bakeoff div-by-zero class); chart_cell renders missing=— vs true-zero=0; saturating_age_ms is clock-rollback-safe. 16 tests, 0 critical UBS (panic-free), clippy/fmt clean. Analytics/bakeoff/chart/TUI adoption + bookmark transactionality + update arg-safety + pages/TUI human-robot parity deferred to follow-on.

title: Add subsystem coverage matrix and closeout gate for all report failure-mode files
description:
Background: The report explicitly names 15 generated subsystem failure-mode files: analytics, bookmarks, cache, cli_robot, connectors, daemon, html_export, indexer, models, pages, search, sources, storage, tui, and update_check. The purpose of converting the report into beads is to make the Beads graph self-contained so future agents never need to reopen the original markdown plan. That only works if every subsystem file has an owner, proof expectations, and a closure rule.

Goal: add a coverage matrix and closeout gate that maps every report subsystem and representative failure mode to one or more beads, unit/integration tests, E2E or golden proof, and structured log artifacts.

Required behavior:
- Matrix rows cover all 15 subsystem files and the high-signal findings inside them: connector collisions/locked/encrypted/malformed inputs, daemon/cache stale state, export/encryption injection/decrypt failures, bookmarks/analytics drift, update safety, pages/TUI parity, plus the core storage/search/source/model/indexer/cli_robot areas already covered by earlier epics.
- Each row identifies the owning bead(s), mandatory tests, optional/live diagnostics, fixture provenance, required logs, privacy/redaction expectations, and closure evidence format.
- The gate fails or blocks closeout when a report subsystem has no owner, no proof path, no logging expectation, or only prose evidence.
- The matrix references existing epics rather than duplicating work where coverage is already owned; it creates targeted follow-up beads only for true gaps.
- The final integrated proof gate consumes this matrix so subsystem coverage remains required in the full resilience closeout.

Acceptance: a durable docs/test artifact or robot-readable matrix exists; it covers analytics, bookmarks, cache, cli_robot, connectors, daemon, html_export, indexer, models, pages, search, sources, storage, tui, and update_check; it links each row to beads and test/log gates; CI/local proof recipes verify matrix completeness; and closure of this bead includes a reviewed matrix diff plus representative unit/E2E/golden proof artifacts with detailed logs.

title: Harden config data-dir test-isolation and auxiliary CLI safety
description:
Background: The report's cli/config findings included robot schema drift, exit-code regressions, golden snapshot drift, test isolation leaks that scan the user's real huge corpus, inaccessible data-dir paths that partially proceed and write nothing, and missing config files that make commands silently no-op. Some of these are covered by broader robot/proof gates, but config and test isolation deserve an explicit owner because a single bad HOME/XDG/data-dir setup can make every other test and diagnostic lie.

Goal: make configuration, data-dir selection, test isolation, and auxiliary CLI safety fail closed with structured diagnostics instead of silently using the user's real state or returning misleading success.

Required behavior:
- Tests and E2E scripts must run with isolated HOME/XDG/CASS_DATA_DIR/CASS_DB_PATH/config/model/source roots unless explicitly marked live-mode.
- Missing config is distinguishable from empty/default config and intentional no-config mode; commands report which default was chosen and why when it affects behavior.
- Data-dir permission denied, not-a-directory, read-only, disk-full, and partial-write states return structured error envelopes with err.kind, retryable, hint, and no hidden partial success.
- Robot schema and exit-code contracts are checked against real-binary dispatch for config-driven command variants.
- Golden updates for config/CLI surfaces are reviewed and cannot mask actual output drift.
- Auxiliary developer/diagnostic tools such as bakeoff or validation helpers must treat division-by-zero/empty-baseline and missing-corpus states as structured no-data errors, not NaN/Inf or success.

title: Implement bounded retry for eligible quarantine entries
description:
Goal: provide a targeted retry path for entries that are eligible because they are legacy, version-stale, schema-version-stale, or otherwise explicitly marked retryable. The command must be bounded, resumable, and safe under huge corpora.

Non-goals: do not clear irreducible entries silently; do not delete source logs; do not run full index rebuild when a targeted retry is enough.

Acceptance: command supports dry-run/plan JSON, eligible-only retry, limit/budget controls, per-entry outcome, and no-progress/stall reporting. Tests cover successful retry removal, repeated same-version suppression, source-missing skip, OOM re-quarantine, and interrupted retry resume.

title: Define universal progress and stall contract for long operations
description:
Goal: define and wire a shared progress contract for full index, incremental index, watch cycle, semantic backfill, historical salvage, lexical rebuild, and repair. It must separate heartbeat from forward progress.

Fields: phase, subphase, current, total, units, last_forward_progress_at, heartbeat_at, elapsed_ms, stall_threshold_ms, stalled bool, stall_reason, active_lock owner, and safe next command.

Source evidence: current: 0 appeared fleet-wide; #196/#137 taught that a live process is not proof of progress.

Acceptance: status can distinguish building, repairing, stalled, stale, missing, ready, and waiting-on-lock. Tests simulate heartbeat-without-progress, true progress, timeout, and completed publish.
close_reason: Shipped in commit 36acc632: src/search/progress_contract.rs defines the universal progress/stall contract. ProgressReport (raw inputs: operation kind, phase/subphase, current/total, units, started/last-forward-progress/heartbeat clocks, stall_threshold_ms, active_lock owner) + ProgressReport::resolve(now_ms) -> ProgressSnapshot deriving elapsed/since clocks, single OperationState {missing,building,repairing,stalled,stale,waiting_on_lock,ready}, stalled bool + stall_reason, active_lock owner, and ProgressNextStep. Core invariant: heartbeat separated from forward progress (heartbeat advances while alive even mid-stall; forward-progress advances only when current increases), so status distinguishes building/repairing/stalled/stale/missing/ready/waiting-on-lock. All enums snake_case (matches readiness vocab); all derivations take explicit now_ms (no clock calls) for determinism. Acceptance proven by tests: heartbeat-without-progress->stalled, true progress->building, repair->repairing, timeout/dead-heartbeat->stale(restart), completed publish->ready, no-progress-with-lock->waiting_on_lock, missing, indeterminate-total-never-ready, snake_case JSON round-trip. title: Checkpoint watch-mode OOM recovery decisions
description:
Goal: after OOM or killed watch/index jobs, restart should choose a checkpointed bounded recovery path instead of repeatedly falling into full deferred_authoritative_db_rebuild without evidence.

Source evidence: issue #248 showed cass index --watch after OOM-kill repeatedly selecting a full rebuild path after sparse Tantivy detection.

close_reason: Shipped in commit 1eacb7a4: src/search/watch_recovery.rs. RecoverySignals::plan() returns RecoveryPlan {decision, reason, derived_assets_trusted, rebuild_required, work_remaining}. Decision order: (1) restart-loop guard halts after N no-progress restarts (HaltRestartLoop) instead of rebuilding again; (2) checkpoint matching current DB resumes (ResumeFromCheckpoint); (3) trusted assets with sparse metadata OR incomplete lexical stage do BoundedLexicalRepair -- the #248 fix: sparse Tantivy detection alone never forces a full rebuild; (4) trusted+complete needs nothing; (5) only nothing-trusted + no-usable-checkpoint yields FullRebuild, with recorded evidence. Every plan records why a rebuild is/isn't needed, trusted assets, and work remaining. Acceptance proven without a watch loop: cargo test --lib search::watch_recovery 9 passed 0 failed covering OOM before publish (resume), OOM after lexical stage (no rebuild), sparse metadata (bounded repair not full rebuild), restart-loop prevention (halt not rebuild), unknown-checkpoint conservatism, clear-status JSON round-trip; ubs exit 0 (0 critical); module clippy-clean (crate clippy --all-targets -D warnings green as of the .4.2 run). title: Add fleet-safe upgrade rehearsal and post-upgrade verification
description:
Background: The report found real fleet version skew: local/ts1/css were on 0.6.13, ts2 on 0.6.10, and csd/mac-mini-max on 0.4.1. The existing plan covers detecting version skew and recommending upgrades, but that is not enough for users. Operators need confidence that the upgrade path itself is bounded, archive-safe, and followed by a proof check that confirms cass is actually healthier afterward.

Goal: add a fleet-safe upgrade rehearsal and post-upgrade verification workflow that turns version recommendations into a tested operator journey.

Required behavior:
- Provide a dry-run/rehearsal mode that explains which hosts are old, which installer/channel/path would be used, what will be checked before mutation, and what is explicitly not touched.
- Require archive-risk and source-coverage preflight before recommending any upgrade or repair that could affect indexed/archive state.
- Distinguish binary upgrade, data/schema migration, model install, source sync, and derived-index refresh as separate actions with separate safety and proof requirements.
- Support deterministic fixture mode for old-host states and opt-in live mode for real fleet upgrade probes.
- After upgrade, run bounded post-checks for api-version, health/status readiness, source coverage, quarantine status, lexical/semantic fallback state, and human/robot summary parity.
- Emit structured logs and artifact manifests so users can compare before/after state and know whether an upgrade truly fixed the problem or only changed the binary.

Acceptance: tests and E2E scripts cover old but reachable host, unreachable host, high archive-risk host, failed installer/channel probe, successful binary upgrade with stale derived assets remaining, and successful upgrade plus readiness improvement. Proof logs include before/after versions, command provenance, elapsed time, skipped live steps, safe/unsafe next commands, and redaction status. No default path silently mutates source logs, deletes archives, auto-downloads semantic models, or hides partial failure.

title: Suggest canonical workspaces for zero-result filtered searches
description:
Goal: when a workspace-filtered query returns zero hits but the global query or nearby workspace keys would match, cass should explain that the filter is probably wrong and suggest canonical workspace values.

Source evidence: the report found many workspace mismatch and zero-hit mentions, especially on mac-mini-max. Agents can overtrust a false empty result.

Acceptance: search JSON includes zero_result_diagnosis, candidate_workspaces, confidence, and a suggested rerun when applicable. Tests cover exact miss, moved checkout, case/path normalization, macOS/Linux path variants, source_id filtered searches, and genuinely no-match queries.
close_reason: Shipped in commit c5eb8157: src/search/zero_result_diagnosis.rs. diagnose_zero_result(requested_workspace, known_workspaces, global_had_hits) returns ZeroResultReport with diagnosis, ranked candidate_workspaces (each match_kind plus confidence), overall confidence, and suggested_rerun. Layered strongest-first matching: exact, path-normalized, case-insensitive (macOS), platform path variant (Users vs home prefixes), basename-moved (moved checkout). global_had_hits gates genuine-no-match; exact-but-empty becomes workspace-has-no-match (real per-workspace empty, not wrong filter); bare numeric filter becomes source-id-filter (no workspace suggestion); suggested_rerun never uses a bare cass or bv. Acceptance proven without a DB: cargo test --lib search::zero_result_diagnosis 11 passed 0 failed covering exact miss, moved checkout, case and path normalization, macOS-Linux path variants, source_id filter, genuine no-match, candidate ranking, snake_case JSON round-trip; ubs exit 0 (0 critical).
