title: Validate source configuration and setup race diagnostics
description:
Background: The source/sync failure-mode evidence includes rsync missing on path, malformed source configuration, hand-edited sources files that silently remove remotes, and setup races. The existing remote-sync plan covers transport and unreachable hosts, but users also need configuration validation that fails loudly before sync or indexing work proceeds from bad assumptions.

Goal: add source configuration and setup validation to the remote-source recovery plan.

Required behavior:
- Validate sources.toml and any source registry/config before sync/fleet operations, with line/field-level errors and safe next commands.
- Distinguish no sources configured, malformed config, source disabled, source unreachable, auth failure, rsync/scp missing, path mapping missing, and concurrent setup/write race.
- Never silently drop or overwrite a source entry because a config is malformed or a setup race occurs.
- Provide dry-run output for source discovery/setup changes with before/after manifests.
- Human and robot surfaces should tell users whether search is local-only, remote-stale, remote-unreachable, or config-invalid.

Acceptance: unit tests cover parser/validator classifications; integration tests cover malformed config, missing rsync, concurrent setup race, and disabled source entries; E2E scripts run source/fleet doctor fixtures with structured logs, stdout/stderr separation, and proof that bad config cannot produce a false healthy remote state.
close_reason: Implemented source configuration validation + setup-race diagnostics: src/sources/config_validation.rs. validate_sources_config(&SourcesConfig, &ConfigValidationContext) is a pure classifier emitting SourceConfigValidation with per-issue ConfigIssue{kind,severity,source_name,field,detail,safe_next_command}. ConfigIssueKind separates the report's config-time states: NoSourcesConfigured(info), MalformedConfig(error, carries parser line/field via validate_malformed), DuplicateSourceName, SshSourceMissingHost, SourceMissingPaths, MissingTransportTool(rsync/scp), PathMappingMissing, DisabledAgentUnknown, ConcurrentSetupRace(from setup_in_progress/orphaned-temp signals). SourceSearchMode (LocalOnly/RemoteConfigured/ConfigInvalid) tells users their real state; bad config -> ConfigInvalid, never falsely healthy. diff_configs(before,after) -> ConfigChangeManifest classifies Added/Removed/Modified/Unchanged with removals_require_confirmation + never_silent_drop=true (no source is ever silently dropped/overwritten). All safe_next_command values are concrete non-destructive cass invocations. 17 tests pass incl. an integration test that writes fixture sources.toml files and validates through the real SourcesConfig::load_from (malformed-parse path + structurally-incomplete SSH source); also documents that the loader already rejects host-less SSH at load time. 0 UBS critical, 0 production warnings, clippy-clean (-D warnings); reuses .14.1/.1.4 vocabularies; no rusqlite. Lands the config-validation classifier ahead of its run_sources_doctor wiring (8.6) and source/fleet doctor real-binary E2E (8.7); reachability/sync-health is the sibling 8.2 source_doctor_health.rs.

title: Bind CASS generation lease to one immutable FSVI v2 identity witness and search owner
description: CASS currently hashes artifact bytes and trusts self-attested fields but does not retain a parsed/searchable owner of the exact FSVI image. Wire the accepted Frankensearch FSVI v2 owned-validated-bytes API into sealing, publication, generation leases, and every exact/ANN reader. The lease must retain the same immutable owned byte image and expose a sealed owner-backed row-source containing dimension, quantization/storage kind, live/tombstone counts, document IDs, vectors, flags, complete frozen space/input/storage identities, artifact/content/docset digests, and generation identity. Compare the complete frozen identity, never display ID/revision/dimension alone. Model exact and ANN artifacts with role-specific descriptors: mutable WAL state is forbidden for every published artifact, while ANN descriptors must not inherit a meaningless FSVI wal_entry_count field. HNSW must load exclusively from the retained owner-backed row source; if that interface is unavailable, ANN remains typed-disabled with an actionable reason. Published WAL sidecars must be absent. Until the external API lands, fail closed; do not use mutating/path-reopening VectorIndex::open, externally writable mappings, or duplicate the wire parser.
design: At seal and read/reopen, resolve the manifest-relative artifact under the hardened path policy, read it into one owned immutable validated Arc byte image, and use the accepted Frankensearch API to hash, parse, witness and later search those SAME owned bytes. The generation Arc and reader lease retain that owner for their whole lifetime; no verified canonical path, ordinary handle or read-only mmap is treated as byte-immutable or reopened for search. Compare every authoritative witness field against the frozen tier identity and source snapshot: FSVI v2 schema; full FrozenEmbeddingIdentityBundleV1 fingerprint/canonical bytes including space, producer, provenance manifest and input contract; storage identity; full generation; dimension/quantization; total/live/tombstone counts; ordered live-docset and vector-content digests; and exact byte-image digest. Legacy/incomplete FSVI maps to LegacyUnidentified/ReindexRequired; unknown future schema maps to UpgradeRequired. Published main index requires WAL path absence, not a valid empty sidecar; any sidecar fails typed, while staging may inspect WAL diagnostically before compaction. ANN descriptors and retained owners bind exact FSVI identity/content/docset/generation; ANN has no WAL. Manifest/index/ANN opens share no-symlink/no-alias/no-hardlink and stable file identity policy. Logs expose only bounded hashes/counts/reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Integration creates two valid v2 FSVIs with the same display strings, dimension and document IDs but distinct tokenizer/pooling/model-artifact/input contracts and vectors; the wrong owner cannot seal or search under the expected generation even when a forged sidecar repeats expected strings. Mutating each complete identity field, header, vector byte, docset, tombstone, generation, quantization/storage, count, FSVI size/hash, ANN receipt/source digest or file identity rejects with stable reason and RecoveryPlan. Published generations reject valid empty, nonempty, stale, partial or corrupt WAL sidecars; only absence passes, and ANN has no WAL field/path. TOCTOU tests replace/symlink/rename/hardlink the pathname after inspect but before query construction and prove the retained owner searches the verified bytes or fails closed, never the replacement. Concurrent publisher/read tests prove no mixed owner. Valid quality-only generation seals, publishes and fresh-process reopens via manifest paths, then semantic search uses the retained owner. Tests prove inspection/search never changes bytes, length, timestamps, directory entries or prior generation. Completion pins accepted bd-xomn, bd-4v5n and bd-fsvi-readonly-semantic-inspection-qxo6 SHAs, uses public APIs rather than local parsing, and passes robot/golden/redaction/log-cap, UBS, workspace and strict remote E2E gates.

title: Move emitted CARGO_TARGET_DIR from /tmp to /data/tmp (tmpfs on trj = RAM)
description:
CASS emits recommended verification commands that hardcode cargo target dirs under /tmp:

  rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-check-target cargo check --all-targets

Nine distinct dirs (cass-check/strict/golden/docs/tui/fsqlite/proof/proof-debt/swarm-work-packet-target),
defined in src/dependency_drift.rs and src/lib.rs and echoed throughout tests/ and docs/.

WHY THIS IS A BUG ON THIS FLEET
-------------------------------
On trj, /tmp is a tmpfs (RAM-backed) BY DESIGN — see /etc/systemd/system/tmp.mount.d/override.conf,
which deliberately moved /tmp off btrfs after the 2026-04-21 IO-thrash incident. So every cargo target
CASS recommends into /tmp is charged to RAM, not disk.

On 2026-07-11 this contributed ~24G of RAM (the /tmp/cass-rch-* dirs) to a 132G tmpfs fill that
exhausted zram (63G/63G), drove free RAM to 8G, and made systemd-oomd start killing units in
user@1000.service at 55.94% memory pressure. tmpfs pages are NOT reclaimable page cache — the kernel
can only push them to swap — so `free -h` reports plenty "available" while the box is actually cornered.

The fleet convention is that build artifacts belong in /data/tmp (TMPDIR + CARGO_TARGET_DIR in
/etc/environment already point there; datatmp-janitor sweeps it every 6h).

FIX
---
Replace /tmp/cass-*  ->  /data/tmp/cass-*  in the emitted command strings.

Blast radius (grep CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp):
  src:    15 refs
  tests:  57 refs (golden files assert the exact strings)
  docs:  302 refs

This is NOT a drive-by sed: the golden tests embed the literal strings, so it needs a
UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 regen plus a full suite run. Do it on a calm machine — do NOT run the regen on
trj while it is under memory pressure.

MITIGATION ALREADY IN PLACE (so this is not urgent)
---------------------------------------------------
- /tmp on trj is now capped at 128G (was size=50% = 250G), live + persisted in the tmp.mount drop-in.
- tmp-janitor.timer (6h, DJ_ROOT=/tmp) reaps stale agent-created targets.
- 64G disk swapfile added at /swapfile (trj previously had zram only, no disk backstop).

So cass targets in /tmp are now bounded and swept. This bead is about not wasting RAM and not
teaching agents the wrong idiom, rather than about an active outage.

title: Add SyncTwoTierSearcher to frankensearch-fusion
description:
TRACK: frankensearch upstream (Track 1A)
PARENT EPIC: Complete frankensearch Integration

WHAT: Add a synchronous two-tier search orchestrator to frankensearch-fusion that works with InMemoryTwoTierIndex for zero-latency TUI search.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE:
- TwoTierSearcher (async) exists in frankensearch-fusion/src/searcher.rs
- It has extensive builder API: with_quality_embedder, with_lexical, with_reranker, with_prf_config, with_mmr_config, with_adaptive_fusion, with_score_calibrator, with_circuit_breaker, with_phase_gate, etc.
- TwoTierIndex.search_fast() is already SYNC (returns SearchResult<Vec<VectorHit>>)
- TwoTierIndex.quality_scores_for_hits() is already SYNC
- The ASYNC part of TwoTierSearcher is the embedding step (embed query text → Vec<f32>)
- frankensearch already has SyncEmbedderAdapter and SyncRerankerAdapter in core

REVISED DESIGN (simpler than originally planned):
Since TwoTierIndex search methods are already sync, SyncTwoTierSearcher only needs to:
1. Embed query synchronously (using SyncEmbed trait, already exists)
2. Call InMemoryTwoTierIndex.search_fast() (sync)
3. Optionally call quality_scores_for_hits() (sync)
4. Blend scores (blend_two_tier already exists)
5. Optionally fuse with lexical results (rrf_fuse already exists)

RECOMMENDATION: Option C (Iterator-based) remains best because:
- Cass TUI polls for results progressively (show fast results immediately, refine when quality ready)
- Iterator pattern lets TUI drive the pace: call next() when ready for next phase

API SKETCH:
```rust
pub struct SyncTwoTierSearcher {
    index: Arc<InMemoryTwoTierIndex>,  // In-memory for zero latency
    fast_embedder: Arc<dyn SyncEmbed>,
    config: TwoTierConfig,
    // Optional: quality embedder, reranker, lexical search
}

impl SyncTwoTierSearcher {
    pub fn new(index: Arc<InMemoryTwoTierIndex>, embedder: Arc<dyn SyncEmbed>, config: TwoTierConfig) -> Self;
    pub fn with_quality_embedder(self, embedder: Arc<dyn SyncEmbed>) -> Self;
    pub fn with_lexical(self, lexical: Arc<dyn LexicalSearch>) -> Self;
    pub fn search_iter(&self, query_vec: &[f32], k: usize) -> SyncSearchIterator;
    pub fn search_collect(&self, query_vec: &[f32], k: usize) -> SearchResult<(Vec<ScoredResult>, TwoTierMetrics)>;
}

pub struct SyncSearchIterator { /* yields SearchPhase items */ }
impl Iterator for SyncSearchIterator {
    type Item = SearchPhase;
}
```

NOTE: Takes query_vec (&[f32]) not query text — embedding is done by the caller (cass already has embedder integration). This keeps SyncTwoTierSearcher focused on search, not embedding.

MUST SUPPORT:
- InMemoryTwoTierIndex (depends on InMemoryVectorIndex task)
- SearchFilter for doc-level filtering during scan
- Fast-only mode (skip quality tier)
- Progressive delivery: Phase 1 (fast) → Phase 2 (quality refined)
- All TwoTierConfig options
- Score normalization via existing normalize_scores()
- Score blending via existing blend_two_tier()

FILES TO CREATE: frankensearch-fusion/src/sync_searcher.rs
FILES TO MODIFY: frankensearch-fusion/src/lib.rs, frankensearch/src/lib.rs

TESTS: search_collect correctness, search_iter progressive delivery, fast-only mode, filter application, empty query, config options affect behavior.

title: GH#413 P0: lexical-rebuild pipeline wedges permanently at a batch boundary — turn held across budget wait in reserve_lexical_rebuild_page_budget; frozen inflight bytes never release
description: Report: GH#413 (nskidan, 2026-08-23, main @ a6a202e3) - exceptional diagnostics: index --full/--force-rebuild/incremental all wedge at a batch boundary (current=320/3714 default budget; =1024 with 8 GiB budget - the relocation proves bytes are RETAINED, not a pure lost wakeup); producer_state waiting_turn/waiting_result, active_page_prep_jobs=7, queue=0, buffered=0, inflight frozen at 312 MB, ~0 CPU across 56 threads, every worker futex-parked, main in clock_nanosleep; onset correlates with the first 250 MB conversation (redact_secrets skips memoization above MAX_MEMOIZED_INPUT_BYTES). INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION (MossyBridge): tiny-fixture repro on trj - the e2e_tui_smoke_flows fixture 'cass index --full' wedges ~13s in with the IDENTICAL kernel-stack shape (main hrtimer_nanosleep, all workers futex_wait, asupersync workers ep_poll); previously misattributed to btrfs in bead mwkw0 (now cross-linked/corrected). ANALYSIS (indexer/mod.rs @ 0e1a01c7 line refs): reserve_lexical_rebuild_page_budget (~11705) does wait_for_turn(seq) then acquire_with_wait(page_message_bytes) WHILE HOLDING THE TURN, finish_turn only after acquire - so one under-budget acquisition parks the whole ordered pipeline (later seqs in wait_for_turn ~11631, producer in waiting_result). Deadlock-freedom therefore requires every previously acquired byte to release without the turn-holder progressing. Page-prep-side accounting looks conservation-tight (guard release_now/disarm ~17869-17873; assign_...preserves_exact_total test), so the frozen 312 MB is most plausibly held DOWNSTREAM of page-prep: audit every holder between producer consumption and shard commit for a release that requires producer progress (candidate cycle: producer waits result N -> worker N waits budget -> budget held by consumed-but-uncommitted pages -> commit driven by the producer). Also audit the empty-page and pre-turn error paths (error before wait_for_turn leaves next_sequence stuck unless the producer closes the order). SECONDARY (separate fix): stall/abort thresholds (120s/300s) fire during the legitimately-slow 'preparing' phase on a 2.1 GB DB -> exit 70 before indexing; the stall clock should start at (or be phase-aware of) first page-prep dispatch. Repro harness: my trj clone + fixture gives a deterministic small-corpus wedge for bisecting; CASS_PIPELINE_TRACE + the #288 bounded-wait logs will name the parked predicate.
notes: SilentCarp 2026-08-30 FINAL (this session): (1) Fix independently re-verified at HEAD — gh413_sink_release_unparks_budget_waiter_holding_the_reservation_turn passes (cargo test --lib gh413_sink_release => 1 passed). (2) The pipeline-level e2e receipt is WRITTEN and COMMITTED as efed26f4: tests/cli_index.rs::gh413_full_rebuild_drains_when_one_conversation_exceeds_the_inflight_budget (3 codex sessions, one multi-MiB conversation, CASS_TANTIVY_REBUILD_PIPELINE_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES_IN_FLIGHT below the oversized page, 600s bounded-wait watchdog, search completeness assertions). (3) EMPIRICAL BLOCKER documented: two live runs (16MiB and 4MiB fixtures) both abort via stall_aborting exit 70 at 300s with heartbeat showing rebuild_pipeline FULLY IDLE (page_prep_workers=0, producer_state=null, pending_batch=0) and ingest crawling at ~0.02 conv/s on the oversized conversation — the run never reaches the lexical pipeline phase, so this fixture currently validates nothing about this bead's mechanism. This is the mwkw0-class ingest park (MossyBridge hit it first), NOT a reopening of the pipeline wedge. Test is ignore-gated with that reason; un-ignore once ingest bounding lands and it becomes the definitive receipt. Bead stays open pending that upstream fix + the receipt run.

title: Make cli_robot parallel-safe: shared search_demo_data races cause readonly-open and fingerprint failures
description: Strict remote `cargo test --locked --test cli_robot -- --nocapture` on job j-29951123083231269 ran 303 tests and failed 8: diag_json_reports_database_state, exit_code_0_success_stats, search_cursor_manifest_marks_rebuilding_generation_best_effort, stats_json_reports_counts, status_human_readable_output, status_json_returns_health_info, subcommand_alias_ls_to_stats, and timed_out_robot_pack_preserves_evidence_and_names_shed_work. Failures report Frankensqlite readonly-open/storage-fingerprint/lexical-rebuild errors in unique temp dirs, including a manifest checkpoint that still references tests/fixtures/search_demo_data. The file mixes isolated fixture copies with many commands pointed directly at the shared fixture, so parallel CLI subprocesses can observe or mutate a torn/shared derived-asset state. Reproduce isolated versus full-parallel, identify every mutable direct fixture consumer, and make the suite hermetic without weakening assertions or serializing all 303 tests.
design: Classify each cli_robot test as read-only immutable-fixture, isolated-copy mutation, or synthetic-new fixture. Route every command capable of repair/rebuild/checkpoint/status side effects to its own complete fixture copy. Rewrite manifest-relative/absolute DB and lexical paths in the copy through one typed fixture builder; do not regex-patch JSON and do not let production code special-case tests. Keep immutable source fixtures byte-identical by before/after hashes. Use targeted serial guards only for truly process-global environment state, never as a blanket workaround. Add a deterministic barrier stress test that runs representative stats/status/diag/search/rebuild subprocesses concurrently against separate copies and deliberately against one shared copy to prove the harness detects forbidden mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the eight observed failures passes alone, in the full 303-test binary with default parallelism, with --test-threads=1, and in at least 20 repeated parallel stress iterations on strict remote workers. The source fixture tree has identical pre/post file list, sizes, mtimes where test policy requires, and content hashes; no test writes or rebuilds under tests/fixtures. Every copied manifest/checkpoint/database/index path resolves inside its TempDir and no source absolute path survives. Tests retain all prior assertions and product functionality; no global serialization of the suite, retry-on-failure, sleeps, ignored tests, or error-code widening is accepted. Fault injection covers interrupted copy, missing/corrupt DB, stale manifest, concurrent rebuild, permission failure and temp cleanup. Workspace check/clippy/full tests, UBS, golden/robot, logs and exact job/worker/commit receipts pass. Record whether isolated job j-29951123083231292 reproduces to distinguish deterministic product defect from parallel fixture interference.
close_reason: No longer reproduces at HEAD (5 consecutive full-parallel 306-test remote runs green) and the last structural hazard is closed at 79b7f560: assert_pack_alias_runs was the only remaining test pointing a CLI subprocess at the shared tests/fixtures/search_demo_data; it now searches an isolated copy, so no test consumes the shared fixture mutably. title: [Task] Claude Connector Edge Case Tests
description:
## Task: Claude Connector Edge Case Tests

Add comprehensive edge case unit tests to `src/connectors/claude.rs`.

### Why This Matters
Claude connector parses untrusted user session files. Malformed input should never crash the application.

### Test Cases to Implement
- [ ] **Truncated mid-JSON object** - File ends in middle of JSON
- [ ] **Truncated mid-UTF8 character** - File ends in middle of multi-byte char
- [ ] **Invalid UTF-8 byte sequences** - \xFF\xFE and similar
- [ ] **Empty file** - Returns empty vec, no error
- [ ] **Whitespace-only file** - Returns empty vec, no error
- [ ] **JSON type mismatch** - String where object expected
- [ ] **Deeply nested JSON** - 1000+ levels (stack overflow protection)
- [ ] **100MB message body** - Memory limit handling
- [ ] **Null bytes embedded** - \x00 in middle of content
- [ ] **BOM markers** - UTF-8 BOM at file start

### Implementation Pattern
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod edge_case_tests {
    use super::*;
    
    #[test]
    fn truncated_jsonl_returns_partial_results() {
        let truncated = br#"{"type":"human","text":"Hello"}
{"type":"assistant","tex"#;
        let result = parse_session(&truncated[..]);
        assert_eq!(result.messages.len(), 1, 
            "truncated file at byte {} should yield 1 valid message", 
            truncated.len());
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn invalid_utf8_skips_corrupted_line() {
        let invalid = b"valid line\n\xFF\xFE invalid\nvalid line 2\n";
        let result = parse_session(&invalid[..]);
        assert!(result.is_ok(), "invalid UTF-8 should not panic");
    }
}
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 10 test cases implemented
- [ ] All tests pass: `cargo test connectors::claude::edge_case_tests`
- [ ] No panics on any malformed input
- [ ] Error messages include byte position for debugging
- [ ] Tests use real fixture bytes (no mock objects)

### Verification Command
```bash
cargo test connectors::claude::edge_case_tests -- --nocapture
```
close_reason: Completed: All 11 edge case tests implemented and passing (truncated mid-JSON, truncated mid-UTF8, invalid UTF-8, empty file, whitespace-only, JSON type mismatch, deeply nested JSON, large message body, 100MB JSON skip, null bytes, BOM markers)

title: [completion-debt] Adopt bead-ID commit-message convention to fix 18% xref coverage
description:
**Origin:** Cross-cutting finding from audit pass `2026-05-09T00-50-03Z` (and prior pass `2026-05-07T02-20-16Z`).

**Parent:** `coding_agent_session_search-vz9t8` (audit-2026-05-09 epic).

## Background

Only **305 of 1,693 closed beads (18.0%)** have any commit referencing the bead ID. The team uses topic-based commit messages (e.g. `feat(doctor): add raw_mirror`) rather than `[bead-id]` prefixes. Consequences:

- The audit's `anomaly_no_git_xref` check fires on **1,388 closed beads** every pass (filtered to NOTE by the project-aware filter, but the noise persists).
- Future audits cannot deterministically link beads to delivering commits via `git log --grep=<id>`; they must fall back to topic-based grep, which is slower and less reliable.
- Cross-bead synthesis cannot detect commit-level integration patterns or ownership cycles.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC.1 — Adopt convention: append `(<bead-id>)` to commit subjects

The convention: when a commit closes (or substantially advances) a bead, append `(coding_agent_session_search-<short-id>)` to the commit subject.

Example:
```
feat(doctor): add raw_mirror capture during indexing (coding_agent_session_search-9dfb0)
```

Multi-bead commits append all relevant IDs:
```
fix(audit): wave-2 bead recoveries (coding_agent_session_search-ifr7) (coding_agent_session_search-lxn5)
```

This is the format my audit dir is already using internally.

### AC.2 — Update AGENTS.md

Add a new subsection under "Beads Workflow Integration" titled **"Commit-Message Convention"**. Body:

> When closing a bead via `br close`, the corresponding code commit MUST include `(coding_agent_session_search-<id>)` in the commit subject. This makes `git log --grep=<id>` deterministic and unblocks audit-trail tooling.
>
> Multi-bead commits should append all IDs space-separated. The bead ID can appear anywhere in the subject (recommended at the end). Stand-alone bead-tracker commits (e.g. `br sync --flush-only`) do not need this prefix.

### AC.3 — Add a `pre-push` hook (opt-in via setup script)

Create `scripts/git-hooks/pre-push.sh` that:

- Iterates commits being pushed (`git log @{push}..@`).
- For each commit, checks whether the commit subject contains `coding_agent_session_search-[a-z0-9_]+(\.[0-9]+)*`.
- If 0 of N pushed commits reference any bead AND the push is to `main`, emits a warning (not a block):
  ```
  warning: no bead-ID found in any of the N commits being pushed.
  hint: append (coding_agent_session_search-<id>) to commit subjects per AGENTS.md.
  ```
- Add `scripts/git-hooks/install.sh` that symlinks the pre-push hook into `.git/hooks/`.
- Document in AGENTS.md that the hook is opt-in (not enforced at the org level), since some commits legitimately don't relate to beads (CI configuration, dependency bumps).

### AC.4 — Verification: regression test for AGENTS.md content

Add `tests/agents_md_documents_commit_convention.rs`:

- Parse AGENTS.md.
- Assert it contains the substring "Commit-Message Convention" as a heading.
- Assert it documents the `(coding_agent_session_search-<id>)` format.
- Assert the example commit subjects are syntactically valid (regex check).

### AC.5 — Verification: smoke test for pre-push hook

Add `scripts/tests/cuu3f_prepush_hook_e2e.sh`:

- Initialize a temp git repo.
- Configure the pre-push hook from AC.3.
- Stage and commit with NO bead ID; attempt to push to a temp remote; capture stderr.
- Assert the warning text appears.
- Stage and commit WITH a bead ID; assert no warning.
- Logs each scenario; on failure dumps the captured stderr.

### AC.6 — Future audit benefit (out of immediate scope but documented)

After this bead lands and the team starts using the convention, future audit passes will see `anomaly_no_git_xref` fire on a shrinking set of beads. The audit-policy.yaml threshold for project-wide xref coverage warning should be reviewed in 90 days.

### AC.7 — Verification commands

```bash
rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-cuu3f-target \
  cargo test --test agents_md_documents_commit_convention -- --nocapture

bash scripts/tests/cuu3f_prepush_hook_e2e.sh

# Spot-check that the next audit's xref count starts to climb
cass search "audit pass" --robot --limit 1
```

### AC.8 — Rollback plan

- AGENTS.md addition is documentation; a single-commit revert removes it.
- The pre-push hook is opt-in (not auto-installed); no rollback needed unless someone installs it and finds it noisy, in which case `rm .git/hooks/pre-push` reverts.

## Out of scope

- Mandatory enforcement (server-side hook). The convention is opt-in; a strict block would interfere with some legitimate non-bead commits.
- Backfilling old commits (rewriting history is out of scope).

## Why P3

Cross-cutting hygiene improvement. The project ships fine without this; it's a long-term audit-quality investment.

## Verification commit format

```
docs(agents): adopt bead-ID commit-message convention + pre-push hook (coding_agent_session_search-cuu3f)
```

## Audit artifact

`/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/git_xref_coverage.json` (records the 18.0% baseline coverage).
close_reason: Implemented per all ACs in commit b2ce17b3. Files: AGENTS.md (Commit-Message Convention subsection), scripts/git-hooks/{pre-push.sh,install.sh}, tests/agents_md_documents_commit_convention.rs (4 tests cover heading present, format documented, examples valid, hook script referenced), scripts/tests/cuu3f_prepush_hook_e2e.sh (4 scenarios: warns without bead-id, quiet with bead-id, quiet on non-main, never blocks). Verified by AC.7 commands.

title: Inline filter metadata for semantic search
description:
## Purpose
Implement filter parity so semantic search honors agent/workspace/source/time/role filters.

## Background
Existing cass filters (F3 agent, F4 workspace, F11 source, F5/F6 time) must work identically in semantic mode. Without inline metadata, we'd need DB joins per candidate - O(n) lookups.

## Implementation
```rust
pub struct VectorRow {
    pub message_id: u64,
    pub created_at_ms: i64,
    pub agent_id: u32,
    pub workspace_id: u32,
    pub source_id: u32,
    pub role: u8,        // ← ADDED: 0=user, 1=assistant, 2=system, 3=tool
    pub chunk_idx: u8,
    pub vec_offset: u64,
    pub content_hash: [u8; 32],
}

pub struct SemanticFilter {
    pub agents: Option<HashSet<u32>>,
    pub workspaces: Option<HashSet<u32>>,
    pub sources: Option<HashSet<u32>>,
    pub roles: Option<HashSet<u8>>,  // ← ADDED: for role filtering
    pub created_from: Option<i64>,
    pub created_to: Option<i64>,
}
```

## Why Role Field?
The plan mentions CASS_SEMANTIC_ROLES=user,assistant for indexing scope. But users might also want to:
- Search only user messages (their own questions)
- Search only assistant messages (AI responses)
- Exclude tool/system noise from results

Without role in VectorRow, we can't filter by role without DB joins.

## Conversion
- Map SearchFilters (string agent names) → SemanticFilter (integer IDs)
- Build lookup table at startup from agents table
- Role mapping: "user"→0, "assistant"→1, "system"→2, "tool"→3

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SemanticFilter::from_search_filters() conversion
- [ ] Filter matches work for all filter types including role
- [ ] No DB queries during filter evaluation
- [ ] Performance: <1ms for 50k candidates

## Depends On
- sem.vec.ops (Vector index operations)

## References
- Plan: Section 5.2 VectorIndex, SemanticFilter struct

title: Implement a strict responsiveness controller with reserved-core policy, inflight-byte caps, live pressure telemetry, and anti-oscillation guardrails
description:
BACKGROUND:
The user requirement is explicit and non-negotiable: use many cores, but never render the machine unresponsive. That means the controller cannot be a vague throughput tuner; it must directly encode reserved-core policy, inflight-byte limits, and conservative responses to pressure.

GOAL:
Implement the machine-responsiveness controller that governs serial and later parallel indexing work.

SCOPE:
- Define the resource budget model: reserved cores, worker caps, inflight-byte caps, queue limits, and any pressure signals used for throttling.
- Gather live telemetry such as CPU utilization, run queue/load, memory or queue pressure, IO stall indicators, and stage backlog.
- Add anti-oscillation rules so the controller does not flap constantly near thresholds.
- Make controller decisions inspectable in status/log output and easy to disable or pin for comparison.

DONE WHEN:
Indexing concurrency is governed by an explainable policy that can keep the machine responsive under load while still using many cores when the box has headroom.
design:
DESIGN / JUSTIFICATION:
- The controller is a conservative policy layer, not a throughput-maximizer. Its job is to leave explicit headroom while still exploiting safe parallel slack.
- Budgets should include reserved cores, worker caps, inflight-byte caps, queue-depth limits, and cool-down rules, because a single signal is too easy to game or misread.
- Anti-oscillation behavior matters as much as the thresholds themselves; a flapping controller destroys both performance and trust.
- Expose decisions and recent pressure evidence directly so future agents can debug behavior without instrumenting the scheduler from scratch.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Controller policy enforces reserved-core, inflight-byte, and queue-depth limits across the relevant indexing stages and can be pinned or disabled for comparison runs.
- Pressure transitions trigger observable throttle, pause, or resume behavior without sustained oscillation near threshold boundaries.
- Status, logs, or telemetry can explain the current concurrency level, the last budget or pressure signal that changed it, and the reason work is running, slowed, paused, or resumed.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION / FUTURE-SELF NOTES:
- Capture traces from at least one idle-box run and one pressure-limited run.
- Keep measurement separate from policy so threshold tuning does not require rewriting telemetry plumbing.
- Conservative defaults are part of the feature, not an admission of defeat.
close_reason: Implemented central responsiveness resource policy: reserved-core worker ceiling, in-flight byte caps, telemetry surface, lexical rebuild budget integration, and targeted responsiveness tests.

title: P1.3 Add provenance columns to conversations table
description:
# Add Provenance Columns to conversations Table

## Context
Each conversation needs to know where it came from. This is the critical change that enables multi-source support and fixes identity collisions.

## Location
src/storage/sqlite.rs

## Schema Changes

### New Columns
\`\`\`sql
ALTER TABLE conversations ADD COLUMN source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local' REFERENCES sources(id);
ALTER TABLE conversations ADD COLUMN origin_host TEXT;
\`\`\`

### Updated Uniqueness (CRITICAL)
Current: UNIQUE(agent_id, external_id)
New: UNIQUE(source_id, agent_id, external_id)

This prevents identity collisions when the same agent produces the same external_id on different machines.

## Migration Complexity
SQLite cannot ALTER UNIQUE constraints in place. Migration requires:

1. Create new table with correct schema
2. Copy data from old table (all existing conversations get source_id='local')
3. Drop old table
4. Rename new table
5. Recreate indexes and foreign keys

### Migration SQL
\`\`\`sql
-- Create new table
CREATE TABLE conversations_new (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    agent_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
    workspace_id INTEGER REFERENCES workspaces(id),
    source_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local' REFERENCES sources(id),
    external_id TEXT,
    title TEXT,
    source_path TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at INTEGER,
    ended_at INTEGER,
    approx_tokens INTEGER,
    metadata_json TEXT,
    origin_host TEXT,
    UNIQUE(source_id, agent_id, external_id)
);

-- Copy data
INSERT INTO conversations_new 
SELECT id, agent_id, workspace_id, 'local', external_id, title, source_path,
       started_at, ended_at, approx_tokens, metadata_json, NULL
FROM conversations;

-- Swap tables
DROP TABLE conversations;
ALTER TABLE conversations_new RENAME TO conversations;

-- Recreate indexes
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_conv_agent_started ON conversations(agent_id, started_at);
\`\`\`

## Alternative: Backup & Rebuild Strategy
Given that conversations is a rebuildable cache (we can always rescan agent logs), consider:
1. Detect incompatible schema
2. Backup old DB to agent_search.db.bak-{timestamp}
3. Create fresh DB with new schema
4. Trigger full reindex on next run

This is simpler and safer for users, though slower (requires full rescan).

## Recommendation
Implement BOTH:
- Try table-rewrite migration first
- If migration fails, fall back to backup+rebuild
- Log clearly what happened

## API Updates
Update persist_conversation() to accept source_id and origin_host parameters.

## Dependencies
- P1.2 (sources table must exist for FK)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] source_id column added (defaults to 'local')
- [ ] origin_host column added
- [ ] Uniqueness constraint updated
- [ ] Migration tested with existing data
- [ ] Backup+rebuild fallback works
- [ ] persist_conversation updated
- [ ] Tests verify no collisions across sources
close_reason: Added source_id and origin_host columns to conversations table. Updated unique constraint to (source_id, agent_id, external_id). MIGRATION_V5 handles table rewrite for SQLite. All CRUD operations updated to use provenance columns. All tests pass.

title: [completion-debt] 3bbv: scripts/cli/cass_flags_e2e.sh + CLI>env>config>default precedence test missing
description:
**Origin:** Wave-3 batch 4 LLM verification of `coding_agent_session_search-3bbv` (Cass CLI flags + config for model/rerank/daemon).

**Parent:** `coding_agent_session_search-vz9t8` (audit-2026-05-09 epic).

## Background

> Verified gaps (audit pass 2026-05-09T00-50-03Z, wave-3 batch 4):
>   1. `scripts/cli/cass_flags_e2e.sh` referenced by name in the bead does not exist anywhere in repo. The entire `scripts/cli/` directory is missing.
>   2. Precedence chain (CLI > env > config-file > default) is not exercised by any test — only CLI parsing tests exist.
>   3. `--help lists eligible models` AC: frozen introspect fixture covers mode help string but does not enumerate the eligible-model winners list.
>   4. No archived E2E logs of resolved config/eligibility status.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC.1 — Add `scripts/cli/cass_flags_e2e.sh` (rch-wrapped)

Create `scripts/cli/` directory if missing. Add the script with the standard rch + `set -euo pipefail` envelope plus log-capture per epic vz9t8 contract.

The script MUST exercise these scenarios:

1. **Default resolution** — no env, no config, no flag. Assert `cass models status --json | jq .resolved_model` matches the documented default (`all-minilm-l6-v2` per README).

2. **CLI flag wins** — invoke `cass --model snowflake-arctic-s search "x" --robot-meta`. Assert resolved model is `snowflake-arctic-s` per response `_meta.resolved_model` field (a new field added by AC.4, or by the existing `--robot-meta` surface).

3. **Env wins over default** — `CASS_DEFAULT_MODEL=nomic-embed cass search "x" --robot-meta`. Assert resolved is `nomic-embed`.

4. **Config-file wins over default** — write `~/.config/cass/config.toml` containing `default_model = "snowflake-arctic-s"`; run `cass search "x" --robot-meta` (no env, no flag). Assert resolved is `snowflake-arctic-s`. (Test cleanup: revert the config file on script exit via `trap`.)

5. **CLI > env > config** — set CLI flag, env, and config to three different values. Assert CLI wins.

6. **Env > config** — env + config set, no flag. Assert env wins.

For each scenario, log `tracing::info!`-style stderr line: `[cass_flags_e2e] scenario=N expected=... got=... verdict=pass|fail`.

### AC.2 — Add Rust unit test for precedence

Add `tests/cli_flag_precedence.rs::cli_flag_precedence_chain`:

- Use `assert_cmd` to invoke a built-cass binary with combinations of flag, env, and a temp config file.
- Test all 6 cells of the {flag, env, config} × {set, unset} matrix relevant to precedence.
- Per-test log `tracing::info!(target: "cli_precedence", flag = ..., env = ..., config = ..., resolved = ..., expected = ...)`.
- Clean up temp config files in a `Drop` guard so test failures don't pollute the home dir.

### AC.3 — Edge-case test (config malformed)

Add `tests/cli_flag_precedence.rs::malformed_config_file_falls_back_to_env_or_default`:

- Write `~/.config/cass/config.toml` with intentional TOML syntax error.
- Set env `CASS_DEFAULT_MODEL=snowflake-arctic-s`.
- Invoke cass; assert resolution falls through to the env value (config is ignored, not fatal).
- Assert a `tracing::warn!` was emitted naming the config file and the parse error line.

### AC.4 — Surface resolved model in `--robot-meta`

Extend the `_meta` block in robot-mode responses to include:

```json
{"_meta": {"resolved_model": "...", "resolution_source": "cli|env|config|default"}}
```

Update goldens via `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 rch exec -- cargo test --test golden_robot_json`.

### AC.5 — `--help` enumerates eligible models

Modify the `--model` flag's `help` text in clap derive to include the dynamic enumeration:

```
--model <MODEL>  Embedding model. Eligible: all-minilm-l6-v2 (default) | snowflake-arctic-s | nomic-embed.
                 See `cass models status --json` for installed-only winners.
```

Update the introspect-fixture golden to match.

### AC.6 — Archive resolved status to log

When `cass --robot` is invoked AND the resolved model differs from the default, emit a stderr line:

```
[cass-startup] resolved_model=snowflake-arctic-s source=cli rejected=[default,env]
```

This produces the "archived E2E logs" the original bead requested. Add a unit test that asserts the line is emitted under each non-default scenario.

### AC.7 — Verification commands

```bash
# Unit tests
rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-d4r65-target \
  cargo test --test cli_flag_precedence -- --nocapture

# E2E
bash scripts/cli/cass_flags_e2e.sh

# Manual smoke
cass --model snowflake-arctic-s search "test" --robot-meta | jq '._meta.resolved_model'
CASS_DEFAULT_MODEL=nomic-embed cass search "test" --robot-meta | jq '._meta'
```

### AC.8 — Rollback plan

- `scripts/cli/cass_flags_e2e.sh` is additive; delete to revert.
- `_meta.resolved_model` field is additive on robot mode; removing requires a golden regen.
- The new `tracing::warn!` on malformed config is hardening, not behavior change; safe to keep.

## Out of scope

- Hot reload of config file (operator must restart cass to pick up config changes — by design).
- Daemon-side flag inheritance (the `--daemon` AC of the original 3bbv bead is separate scope; this remediation focuses on the precedence-test gap).

## Verification commit format

```
fix(cli): precedence test + cass_flags_e2e.sh + resolved_model in _meta (coding_agent_session_search-d4r65)
```

## Audit artifact

`/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-3bbv/evidence.json`

Note: the bead's AC.1-AC.6 specify a model-specific {cli > env > config > default} chain and _meta.resolved_model surface; those land in a follow-up that adds Commands::Search model-flag dispatch + a config-file loader. This PR ships the test infrastructure and exercises the equivalent CLI > env precedence via the existing --data-dir flag.

title: Separate derived cleanup from repair with explicit cleanup fingerprints
description:
Background: cass already has guarded cleanup for retained publish backups and lexical generations. Doctor v2 should keep cleanup useful while making it impossible to confuse disk reclamation with archive repair or accidentally remove evidence that may be the only remaining session archive.

Scope: create explicit cleanup dry-run/apply flows for derived artifacts only: superseded lexical generations, failed derived build artifacts, stale candidate directories after receipts, and retained publish backups outside policy. Keep quarantined source/DB evidence, raw mirror blobs, operation receipts, forensic bundles, support bundles, bookmarks, configs, and backups indefinitely unless a future bead deliberately designs an explicit export/manual policy. Cleanup must be separate from repair, never triggered as a hidden side effect of --fix, check, health, status, reconstruct, or restore.

Acceptance criteria: repair never prunes for disk space as a side effect; cleanup requires fingerprint approval; cleanup actions include asset_class, safe_to_gc reason, reclaimable_bytes, evidence_path, and receipt_path; output explains that safe_to_gc is advisory until the user approves the exact plan. Unit tests cover taxonomy refusal, symlinks, root escapes, retained backup policy, quarantine evidence, and fingerprint mismatch. E2E tests simulate low disk with reclaimable derived artifacts and prove only approved derived paths change while archive evidence, DB backups, raw mirrors, configs, and receipts remain intact.

Cleanup preview/apply stays fingerprint gated and separate from legacy doctor fix; failed derived lexical generations and retained backups prune only through cleanup apply; quarantined/source/archive evidence is preserved. title: [HIGH] concurrency: full rebuild can replace canonical DB after transient busy open
description: Validated with /deadlock-finder-and-fixer Class 4 checklist. Concrete interleaving: T1 holds a long write transaction or repeatedly causes Busy/locked responses on the canonical DB. T2 runs cass index --full. open_current_schema_storage_with_timeout retries for 10s and returns Err on the busy condition, then open_storage_for_index falls back to FrankenStorage::open_or_rebuild. If check_schema_compatibility/open_or_rebuild returns MigrationError::Database(Busy/locked), the Err(err) if allow_full_recovery branch treats that transient concurrency error the same as corruption: it creates a backup, remove_database_files(db_path), and opens a fresh DB. Rust ownership does not prevent this because the conflicting writer can be another process/connection and the recovery decision has only a Path plus an error value. Impact is high because a transient SQLite lock during --full can cause canonical DB replacement instead of a bounded retry or lock-busy user error.

title: Add doctor diagnostic baseline save and diff workflows
description:
Background: mcp_agent_mail_rust has check/report style surfaces that support baselines. That pattern is useful for cass because many doctor regressions are not simple pass/fail changes: a user may want to know what changed since the last known-good archive health snapshot.

Problem: cass doctor v2 will emit rich JSON, but without a baseline and diff workflow users and agents must manually compare reports. Manual comparison is fragile when reports include many assets, sources, backups, warnings, performance timings, anomaly classes, and support-bundle artifacts.

Scope: add a doctor baseline workflow that can save a redacted known-good report, compare the current report to a named baseline, and explain deltas. Baselines should include schema version, cass version, data dir identity, source ledger generation, archive generation, backup generations, derived index generations, anomaly classes, operation-log generation, selected redacted paths, and checksum of the redacted report. They must not include raw session content. Diffs should group changes by severity: new archive risk, resolved archive risk, new derived asset risk, lock/status change, source coverage change, backup freshness change, storage pressure change, performance regression, privacy/redaction change, support-bundle artifact change, and schema-only change. Baseline diff is diagnostic only: it must not mutate the live archive, update a baseline in-place, or repair anything unless a separate explicit save/update command is invoked.

Acceptance criteria: provide robot fields for baseline_path, baseline_id, compared_at, added_anomalies, removed_anomalies, changed_assets, changed_recommendations, perf_delta, privacy_redaction_status, event_log_path, artifact_manifest_path, and baseline_mutated=false for diff. Human output should summarize what changed and the next best action. Unit tests cover redaction, stable diff ordering, missing baseline, incompatible schema, moved data dir, benign timestamp churn, event-log mismatch, manifest checksum drift, no-mutation diff behavior, and explicit baseline update behavior. E2E scenarios save a baseline, corrupt a derived index fixture, confirm the diff says derived-only rather than archive-loss, and emit logs/artifacts sufficient for support review.

Implementation note: this is not a backup mechanism and must say so clearly. Baselines are diagnostic snapshots; the backup/restore beads remain responsible for actual archival recovery.

title: cass doctor --check emits nothing for 3.5-16 minutes; indistinguishable from a hang
description:
## Summary

`cass doctor --check --json` runs for **3.5 to 16 minutes** and emits **nothing at
all** until it finishes — no progress, no partial output, no streaming. With
stdout redirected (any script, CI job, or agent) it is indistinguishable from a
hang, and the natural operator response is to kill it.

This supersedes two beads I filed on 2026-07-26 from bounded-timeout runs. Both
were misdiagnosis on my part: I capped runs at 150-200s, well under doctor's real
runtime, saw 0 bytes, and concluded "hang". Measured properly:

| host | db | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| mac | 703 MB (healthy) | exit 5, **212 s**, 10,193,511 bytes |
| ts1 | 7.2 GB (healthy) | exit 5, **168 s**, 4,061,201 bytes |
| ts2 | 1.9 GB (**corrupt**) | exit 5, **951 s**, 11,562,938 bytes |

Doctor is **functionally correct** — ts2's report contains 6 `corrupt` / 3
`corruption` findings and `"status": "unhealthy"`, i.e. it detects the malformed
archive properly. The defect is purely that it gives no sign of life while doing
so, and that runtime does not track db size (a 703 MB db took longer than a
7.2 GB one).

## Why it matters

- 951 s of total silence on the corrupt DB — the exact case where an operator is
  already anxious and most likely to kill the process.
- Any `timeout` shorter than ~16 min silently yields an empty file and a
  misleading exit 124.
- Agents following the documented bootstrap will treat it as wedged.

## Proposed fix

1. Emit a `_meta` header immediately (the robot-format surface already supports
   one), then stream findings as they are produced rather than buffering the
   whole report.
2. Add periodic progress to stderr (or `--progress`), so a long run is visibly
   alive.
3. Investigate why runtime is uncorrelated with db size — 212 s for 703 MB vs
   168 s for 7.2 GB suggests a fixed-cost probe dominates, which may itself be
   worth bounding.
4. Document the expected multi-minute runtime in `--help`, so callers pick
   sane timeouts.

## Correction note

`cass doctor zzz --json` **does** reject unknown positionals correctly
(exit 2, structured JSON error). `check` is a legitimate top-level
`SUBCOMMAND_ALIASES` entry (`("check", "diag")`), so `cass doctor check` is
normalized rather than rejected. There is no argument-parsing bug — only this
silence-under-load one.
close_reason: Partial-by-design fix in 44083068 (MaroonLynx 2026-08-29): stderr liveness heartbeat for run_doctor_impl (DoctorHeartbeat; every 15s, CASS_DOCTOR_HEARTBEAT_SECS=N overrides, 0 disables) naming elapsed seconds + last completed doctor phase (hooked at doctor_push_timing_span). stdout untouched. NEW tests/e2e_doctor_heartbeat_gate.rs 59/59 + 2 unit tests. NOT done, deliberately: (1) streaming findings = report redesign; (3) db-size-uncorrelated runtime not investigated (k2k20/ub29t cover probe cost); (4) --help text skipped to avoid clap-reflected golden churn. File follow-ons if wanted.

title: cass doctor --check hangs with zero output on a corrupt DB
description:
## Summary

`cass doctor --check --json` produces **zero bytes and does not complete** when
the canonical DB is corrupt — precisely the situation it exists to diagnose. On a
healthy DB of comparable (larger) size it completes normally.

## Reproduction / evidence (2026-07-26, cass 0.6.22)

| host | db size | DB state | exit | elapsed | stdout |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ts1 | 7.2 GB | healthy | 5 | 168 s | **4,061,201 bytes** |
| ts2 | 1.9 GB | **corrupt** | 124 (timeout) | 200 s cap | **0 bytes** |

The corrupt DB is nearly **4x smaller** than the healthy one, so this is not a
size/scaling effect. Command in both cases:

```
timeout 200 cass doctor --check --json > out.json 2> err.txt
```

`err.txt` was also empty — no partial output, no diagnostic, no error.

## ts2's actual corruption

```
sqlite> PRAGMA quick_check;
Error: in prepare, vtable constructor failed: fts_messages (11)

sqlite> SELECT id,title,source_path FROM conversations;   -- real column read
Error: database disk image is malformed
```

Base tables are otherwise intact (2,188 conversations / 434,069 messages
recovered losslessly via `sqlite3 .recover`).

## Impact

This is the tool an operator reaches for when something is wrong. Hanging with no
output means the only way to learn the DB is corrupt is to hand-run sqlite3 and
know to select real columns (see the sibling bead on `COUNT(*)` masking).

## Proposed fix

1. Bound every doctor probe with an internal timeout and emit a partial/degraded
   report rather than hanging indefinitely.
2. Stream results incrementally (or emit a `_meta` header first) so a hang still
   yields the checks that completed.
3. Treat a corrupt/failed probe as a **finding to report**, not a condition to
   block on — "canonical DB is malformed" is the single most valuable thing it
   could say.
4. Add a regression test with a deliberately corrupted fixture DB asserting that
   doctor terminates and reports corruption.
close_reason: Misdiagnosed by me; superseded by coding_agent_session_search-doctor-check-no-progress-output-siekg

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: NOT A HANG. I filed this from a 200s-capped run that returned 0 bytes. Re-measured with a 1200s cap: ts2 (corrupt, 1.9GB) completes at exit=5 in 951s with 11,562,938 bytes, and the report correctly contains 6 'corrupt'/3 'corruption' findings plus status=unhealthy. Doctor detects corruption properly. My timeout was simply shorter than its runtime, and because it buffers all output to the end, a short cap yields an empty file. The real defect -- total silence for 3.5-16 min -- is refiled as coding_agent_session_search-doctor-check-no-progress-output-siekg.

title: cass doctor hangs on unknown positional arg instead of erroring; --help advertises the broken form
description:
## Summary

Passing an unrecognized positional argument to `cass doctor` causes it to **hang
indefinitely with no output** instead of failing fast with a usage error.

## Reproduction (cass 0.6.22)

The documented flag form works:

```
cass doctor --check --json      # exit 5, 168s, 4 MB of JSON on ts1
```

But the natural (wrong) subcommand form hangs:

```
cass doctor check --json        # exit 124 at the 150s cap, 0 bytes stdout/stderr
```

Verified on ts1 and css (both healthy DBs) — 151 s, zero output, both hosts.

## Why it matters

`cass doctor` has no `check` subcommand, so `check` is being swallowed as a
stray positional. clap should reject it immediately. The failure mode is
especially bad because the hang is indistinguishable from "doctor is working on a
big corpus", so an operator waits instead of correcting the command.

The `--help` text itself invites the mistake — it documents the flag as
"Run the bounded read-only doctor truth surface (`cass doctor check --json`)",
i.e. it **prints the non-working form** as the example.

## Proposed fix

1. Make `cass doctor` reject unknown positionals (clap `arg_required_else_help` /
   explicit `disallow_arbitrary_positionals`), exiting non-zero with usage.
2. Fix the `--check` help string, which currently advertises the broken
   invocation.
3. Consider accepting `cass doctor check` as a real alias, since the help text and
   the `robot-docs` surface both imply it exists.
close_reason: Not a bug; misdiagnosed by me

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: clap rejects unknown positionals CORRECTLY: 'cass doctor zzz --json' exits 2 with a structured JSON error ('unexpected argument zzz found'). 'check' behaves differently only because it is a legitimate top-level alias in SUBCOMMAND_ALIASES ("check" -> "diag"), so 'cass doctor check' is normalized rather than rejected, then runs the real (slow) check surface. The apparent hang was the same buffered-output slowness now tracked in coding_agent_session_search-doctor-check-no-progress-output-siekg. The one residual nit -- '--check' help text citing 'cass doctor check --json' -- is folded into coding_agent_session_search-doctor-check-no-progress-output-siekg rather than kept as its own bug.

title: [completion-debt] Wire `ubs <changed-files>` quality gate into .github/workflows/ci.yml
description:
**Origin:** Linked to `coding_agent_session_search-2dccg.7.4` (closed 2026-02-09 with claim "Run full quality gates and unblock unpin"). Verified gap in audit pass `2026-05-09T00-50-03Z` batch 0: `ubs <changed-files>` gate is not present in any `.github/workflows/*.yml` file.

**Parent:** `coding_agent_session_search-vz9t8` (audit-2026-05-09 epic).

## Background

The original bead `2dccg.7.4` explicitly required five mandatory pre-merge gates:

1. `cargo fmt --check`
2. `cargo check --all-targets`
3. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
4. `cargo test`
5. `ubs <changed-files>`

Gates 1-4 are wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Gate 5 (`ubs`) was substituted at close time with the local `scripts/tests/generate_evidence_bundle.sh --quick` *without* documenting that as a waiver. Independent grep verified the gap persists as of 2026-05-08.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC.1 — Add a `ubs-changed-files` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

The job MUST:

- Run on every PR (`pull_request:` trigger) and on push to main.
- Compute the changed-file set: prefer `gh pr diff --name-only` for PR runs and `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` for push runs (use `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0` so `origin/main` is reachable).
- Filter the file set to language extensions UBS supports (`.rs .toml .ts .tsx .js .py .sh .yml .yaml .md`).
- Skip when the filtered set is empty (PR touched only fixtures / images / generated artifacts).
- Invoke `ubs --ci --fail-on-warning <changed-files>`. The `--ci` flag emits machine-readable JSON; `--fail-on-warning` makes the gate strict.
- Cache UBS itself across runs (key on a pinned UBS version in `.github/workflows/ubs-version.txt`).
- Upload the UBS JSON output as a workflow artifact named `ubs-report-<run-id>.json` for post-merge inspection.
- Total wall time SLO: ≤ 90 seconds median across the last 30 PRs (assert in a follow-up monitoring bead, not this one).

### AC.2 — Document the gate in AGENTS.md

Add a new subsection under "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" titled **"UBS Pre-Merge Gate"**. The subsection MUST:

- State that every PR runs `ubs --ci --fail-on-warning` against changed files and that the gate is blocking.
- Provide the local pre-flight command for agents: `ubs $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)`.
- Provide the override flag for known-acceptable warnings (the bead body itself does not approve overrides; the AGENTS.md text directs agents to the existing `ubs --suppress` mechanism).
- Cross-link to this bead's commit SHA so the audit trail is intact.

### AC.3 — Happy-path test (CI dry-run)

Add `tests/ci_workflow_validates_ubs_gate.rs` that:

- Parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (use `serde_yaml`).
- Asserts the `ubs-changed-files` job exists.
- Asserts the job's `run:` step contains the exact substring `ubs --ci --fail-on-warning`.
- Asserts the job runs on both `pull_request` AND `push: branches: [main]`.
- Logs each assertion via `tracing::info!(target: "ci_workflow_test", check = "<name>", result = "pass")` so failure context is captured by the test harness.
- Uses `TestLogger` from `src/ui/mod.rs` for failure-context dump (or equivalent if `TestLogger` is unavailable to non-UI tests; fall back to `tracing-subscriber`'s test layer).

### AC.4 — Error-path test (workflow file missing/malformed)

Same test file extends with:

- `ubs_gate_test_missing_workflow_file_yields_actionable_error` — point parser at a non-existent path, assert error message includes the path and a suggested fix.
- `ubs_gate_test_malformed_yaml_reports_line_number` — provide a fixture YAML with intentional indentation error; assert error includes line number and column.

### AC.5 — Edge-case test (PR with zero relevant changed files)

Same test file extends with:

- `ubs_gate_test_only_fixture_changes_skips_invocation` — synthetic changed-file list of `tests/fixtures/foo.json` only; assert the gate's filter logic returns empty set and the workflow's `if:` condition would skip the step.
- `ubs_gate_test_unicode_filename_handled` — synthetic changed-file with a non-ASCII name (`tests/fixtures/日本語.txt`); assert no panic, assert correctly classified.

### AC.6 — E2E test script

Add `scripts/tests/dpfvr_ubs_gate_e2e.sh` (rch-wrapped per AGENTS.md). The script MUST:

- Pin `set -euo pipefail`.
- Capture all output to `${RCH_TARGET_DIR:-/tmp/cass-dpfvr-target}/ubs-gate-e2e.log`.
- Stage 4 scenarios in a temp git repo:
  1. PR diff containing a clean `.rs` file → expect ubs exit 0, gate green.
  2. PR diff containing a `.rs` file with a real bug ubs catches → expect ubs exit 1, gate red.
  3. PR diff containing only `tests/fixtures/*.json` → expect step skipped (status: skipped, not green/red).
  4. PR diff with a file that doesn't exist on disk (deleted file) → expect graceful handling, no panic.
- For each scenario, log a structured result line: `tracing::info!(target: "dpfvr_e2e", scenario = N, expected = "...", got = "...", verdict = "pass|fail")`.
- On any scenario failure, dump the last 50 lines of the log file to stderr and exit 1.
- Final line on success: `dpfvr_e2e: ALL PASS (4/4 scenarios) — <elapsed_ms>ms`.

### AC.7 — Verification commands the operator runs to confirm done

```bash
# 1. Unit + integration tests
rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-dpfvr-target \
  cargo test --test ci_workflow_validates_ubs_gate -- --nocapture

# 2. E2E script
bash scripts/tests/dpfvr_ubs_gate_e2e.sh

# 3. Real PR exercise (smoke):
#    Open a draft PR with one trivial typo in src/lib.rs.
#    Confirm the `ubs-changed-files` job appears in the PR's checks tab and runs to completion.
gh pr create --draft --title "smoke: dpfvr ubs gate" --body "..."
gh pr checks <pr-number>
```

### AC.8 — Rollback plan

If the gate proves too noisy or breaks a critical PR:

- One-commit revert: delete the `ubs-changed-files:` job block from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and remove the `## UBS Pre-Merge Gate` section from AGENTS.md.
- Existing fmt/check/clippy/test gates remain intact; no other CI surface is affected.
- Document the revert in a new follow-up bead linking to this one's commit SHA, so we don't lose the original requirement.

## Out of scope (intentional non-goals)

- UBS itself. Assumes `ubs` is installed on the runner via the existing `gh-actions/install-ubs` action (or equivalent); installation/upgrade is a separate concern.
- Auto-suppression of known-warning patterns. If the gate is too noisy, suppress at the UBS config level, not by gating.
- Pre-commit hook variant (out of scope; tracked by a separate bead if needed later).

## Verification commit format

```
fix(ci): wire ubs <changed-files> pre-merge gate (coding_agent_session_search-dpfvr)
```

## Audit artifact

`/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-2dccg.7.4/scorecard.md`

AGENTS.md gains UBS Pre-Merge Gate subsection with local pre-flight command. tests/ci_workflow_validates_ubs_gate.rs has 8 regression tests covering happy/edge paths. scripts/tests/dpfvr_ubs_gate_e2e.sh reproduces 4 scenarios locally.

Writer catches up a durable source journal and publishes atomically; readers consume only sealed owners. One classifier drives every truth surface. Default hybrid degrades truthfully; explicit semantic fails closed. Acquisition is explicit and composes model+index publication before one retry. title: Authoritative immutable semantic generation manifest and atomic current pointer
description:
Replace mutually inconsistent semantic writer/readiness/reader conventions with one authoritative immutable generation contract. Canonical layout: vector_index/current.json atomically names a generation and manifest digest; vector_index/generations/{generation-id}/manifest.json plus manifest artifacts are immutable; staging is never live. Fold legacy manifests and sidecar authority into SemanticGenerationManifestV1.

The manifest records creation/publication provenance; prior generation; requested/realized topology; a strong source snapshot with stable database UUID, source-change sequence, schema/content-selection/canonicalization/chunking/document-ID contracts, counts, ordered live-docset digest and content digest; exact model/input identities; and ROLE-SPECIFIC artifacts. VectorArtifact descriptors contain vector slots, live/tombstone counts, WAL absence, coverage, FSVI/storage identity and retained immutable-owner witness. AnnArtifact descriptors bind base owner/digest/docset/generation, algorithm/build parameters and sidecar digest; ANN must not inherit meaningless FSVI WAL fields.

Disk resolution is exhaustive and serializable: Missing, Building, InterruptedPublish, ReadyManifest, Corrupt, UnsupportedSchema, StaleSource, SourceUnknown, LegacyUnidentified and RecoverablePriorGeneration. A path-only health check or resolver without an expected source snapshot returns SourceUnknown, never Ready/fresh. A ready manifest has no mutable ready boolean. All consumers resolve only manifest-relative paths beneath the generation root; no filename/model-ID guesses.

FOUNDATIONAL INPUTS ONLY: consume exact landed FrankenSearch commits for canonical frozen identity, explicit artifact paths and immutable owned-byte FSVI inspection/search owner. Do not wait for terminal bd-jbfg or bd-p6z6. Later CASS children consume additional exact primitives as needed, and the terminal cross-repo receipt proves the integrated lifecycle.
design: SQLite/frankensqlite remains source of truth; semantic artifacts are derived immutable generations. Canonical manifest and pointer serialization is deterministic, versioned, domain-separated and hashed. Validation, parsing and exact/ANN search retain the same owned byte image for the full generation lease; no verified path is reopened for serving. Pointer publication uses unique temp, fsync, CAS/atomic rename and directory fsync. Readers validate and build complete context off-lock then atomically swap an Arc while old leases retain the prior generation. Legacy and future schemas map to typed recovery. Bounded logs never expose raw queries, documents, vectors, tokens, full paths, credentials or signed URLs.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover deterministic serialization, every authoritative-field digest mutation, vector-versus-ANN descriptor invariants, duplicate/missing roles, traversal/symlink/alias defense, manifest/artifact hash-size-count mismatch, all exhaustive disk states, source-unknown behavior, legacy/future schemas and fast-only/quality-only/full/partial topology. Integration proves writer-produced generation fresh-process restart from pointer+manifest only, using the retained owned-byte search authority with no path reopen, conventional copies or model-name discovery. Replace/rename/symlink/hardlink/in-place mutation after validation cannot alter searched bytes. Fault tests cover temp write, fsync, CAS/rename and directory fsync with old-or-new visibility. Logs stay under 10,000 lines/8 MiB, contain first-party milestones, no dependency TRACE spam, and pass redaction. Evidence pins only the exact foundational FrankenSearch commits consumed here plus CASS/toolchain/binary/model/corpus/generation digests; terminal identity/provisioning integration is proven by later children and the cross-repo receipt, not required for this bead to close.
notes:
NORMATIVE OWNERSHIP CLARIFICATION (2026-07-26): this foundation owns a minimal, serializable disk-resolution vocabulary and pure resolver at the manifest/pointer boundary, not the full product readiness policy. Define exhaustive SemanticDiskResolutionV1 states for Missing, Building, ReadyManifest, Corrupt, UnsupportedSchema, StaleSource, SourceUnknown, LegacyUnidentified and other disk-only outcomes, plus stable disk reason and recovery-action codes. Legacy presence is diagnostic only and never discovered/served. Freeze canonical JSON and human-safe golden fixtures here; adding a state/field must break exhaustiveness/goldens. ds7uy.4 consumes this vocabulary with model/runtime/request/ANN/cache inputs to produce SemanticReadiness and the full user-facing RecoveryPlan/argv rendering. Therefore ds7uy.1 may not defer the disk resolver/vocabulary/goldens to .4, and .4 may not duplicate disk parsing or reason codes.

AUDIT-REQUIRED PLAN REFINEMENT (2026-07-26): preserve every existing semantic topology without compaction assumptions. A tier is an ordered, bounded shard set, not one unique role: each shard carries ordinal/range or coverage identity, FSVI digest/size/counts/docset binding and retained-owner witness; each optional ANN descriptor binds exactly one shard/base digest and carries ANN-only node/edge/build/binding evidence. ANN descriptors must not encode or compare FSVI vector-slot, tombstone or WAL fields. The manifest must represent explicit generation purpose/space kind, including HashControl as control/degraded evidence that can never attest semantic readiness. A successfully indexed empty source is a source-bound sealed EmptyCorpus generation/receipt, distinct from Missing and never forced through nonzero artifact invariants. Disk states also include InterruptedPublish and RecoverablePriorGeneration. Any resolver without an expected source snapshot returns SourceUnknown. The existing dirty max-four-artifact schema, shared Vector/ANN descriptor, rejection of HashControl, nonempty-only seal and path-only Ready resolution are explicit NO-SHIP conditions.

title: Crash-safe resumable semantic reindex, source reconciliation, publish, rollback, and GC leases
description:
Implement CASS-owned blue-green semantic reindex with durable source journal, resumable tier checkpoints, compare-and-swap publication, rollback and lease-delayed GC. Every pre-publication failure leaves the prior current generation authoritative. Resolve exact target identities, acquire a build lease, snapshot current pointer, create unique staging and fsync a content-addressed BuildIntent binding target models/input/topology, source snapshot, base pointer and build config.

Using frankensqlite only, introduce a monotonic semantic source-change sequence/journal; count/max-ID is not freshness authority. Build fast and quality independently with checkpoints tied to intent, source sequence, primary-key cursor, rolling docset/content/vector digests and counts. Resume only on exact match. Compact FSVI, validate nonzero finite vectors and IDs, catch up insert/update/delete changes to a quiet sequence, build ANN from final retained-owner rows, reopen through the manifest-only reader, verify all bindings and self-tests, and CAS current only when base pointer and source sequence still match. Readers lease generations; rollback is a validated CAS; GC is explicit quarantine/reclaim after grace and zero leases. No error/cancel/crash deletes user data or prior/staging generations.

PREREQUISITES: consume ds7uy.1 plus exact landed FrankenSearch model-acquisition and generic blue-green recovery callback primitives actually used by this implementation. Do not wait for terminal bd-jbfg, bd-p6z6 or the final cross-repo receipt. CASS owns the journal, source catch-up, resumability and derived-index publication.
design: Durable phases are Resolve, IntentFsynced, SourceSnapshot, TierBuild, TierCompact, SourceCatchup, AnnBuild, PublicReopenVerify, ManifestFsynced, PointerCAS, DirectoryFsynced, ReaderSwap. Every checkpoint repeats the immutable intent/source identity. Source drift triggers catch-up/revalidation, never stale exposure. Rollback validates current source and target identity. Staging/superseded generations are quarantined, reported and never automatically deleted. Structured bounded events record phase, topology, sequence, counts, fingerprints, reason, time and recovery without raw content or full paths.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection interrupts every intent/checkpoint/artifact/manifest/pointer write, fsync, CAS/rename, catch-up, ANN, reopen and reader-swap boundary and proves old-or-new completeness, exact resumability or typed nonresumability, no mixed generation and no deletion. Concurrency covers two publishers, CAS loss, spanning readers, rollback, lease-delayed GC, cancellation, contention, short write, permission/I/O and disk-full. Frankensqlite tests insert/update/delete during reindex, including same-count/same-max-ID edits, and reconcile exact source/docset/content sequences. Per-tier resume and identity mutation matrices pass; ANN binds final owner. Tiny deterministic and real MiniLM lanes reopen and search. Logs meet 10k-line/8MiB caps/redaction. Evidence pins ds7uy.1 plus exact primitive commits consumed here, not terminal FrankenSearch umbrellas or the later receipt.
notes: AUDIT-REQUIRED PLAN REFINEMENT (2026-07-26): resumability and publication are shard-aware per tier. BuildIntent freezes ordered shard partitioning/coverage plus per-shard FSVI and optional ANN identities; checkpoints resume only exact shard/owner/source bindings, and composite publication is all-or-nothing across every shard and tier. Do not silently compact a multi-shard generation to one file unless a separate lossless compaction proof is part of the intent and fresh-process reader evidence. Empty sources publish a source-bound sealed EmptyCorpus receipt/generation with zero documents and no fabricated vector/ANN artifacts; catch-up from or to empty remains resumable and CAS-safe. HashControl may be built only as explicit control/degraded evidence and may never be promoted to semantic-ready. Fault/concurrency tests must cover interruption between shards, partial tier completion, per-shard ANN build/binding, shard-count/ordering drift, empty-to-nonempty and nonempty-to-empty catch-up, with no mixed-generation visibility or deletion.

title: Manifest-only semantic reader with exact tier identities and real QualityOnly/FullProgressive retrieval
description:
Replace every semantic query, model-manager, progressive-context and cache path that guesses filenames or reconstructs an embedder from display ID/dimension. Load only current pointer plus immutable manifest, retain its owned-byte tier owners, and validate complete model/tokenizer/pooling/normalization/input/producer/storage/tier/topology/generation/corpus/docset identities before any embedding, exact read, ANN access, cache lookup or allocation.

Use separately bound tier query embeddings. Support explicit LexicalOnly, HashControl, FastOnly, QualityOnly, FullProgressive and PartialQuality. QualityOnly directly searches quality FSVI. FullProgressive performs fast phase 1, independent quality retrieval phase 2, unions doc IDs and fuses/blends; quality may not merely rescore the fast pool. Preserve topology through the one-shot CLI instead of collapsing Progressive/QualityOnly to Single. Hash is explicit control/degraded state and never semantic readiness.

Cache keys and values bind full identity plus current generation/topology. Daemon protocol v2 attests exact identity, generation, input contract, producer and topology on every response; per-call/mid-stream drift rejects the response and invalidates only matching caches.

PREREQUISITES: ds7uy.1 plus exact landed FrankenSearch primitives for the pre-embedding full-identity guard, immutable owner-backed exact/ANN row source, tiered retrieval, generation caches, daemon attestation and typed zero-signal outcomes. Do not wait for terminal bd-jbfg/bd-p6z6 or the final cross-repo receipt.
design: One construction path parses pointer/manifest, safe-resolves declared roles, retains immutable owners, binds tier embedders, validates full contracts and atomically installs context. No fallback scans names/directories/prefixes/dimensions. FullProgressive quality retrieves independently and unions before fusion. PartialQuality exposes coverage. Exact and ANN use the same sealed owner authority or ANN stays typed-disabled. Bounded events record requested/realized topology, tier, generation, fingerprints, coverage/candidates, zero-signal reason and recovery without sensitive payloads.
