title: Progressive semantic query must consume the authoritative FSVI path, never fixed filenames
description: Observed contract break in every served semantic lane: the CASS writer publishes vector_index/index-<embedder>.fsvi, while legacy progressive readers discard the exact artifact already selected and opened, then guess vector.fast.idx, vector.idx, or vector.quality.idx. Exact and ANN serving must share one authoritative selected artifact. This bounded child repairs exact serving and optional native-ANN admission by carrying a retained SemanticIndexArtifact owner through CASS. It deliberately does not enable any FrankenSearch progressive or in-memory two-tier constructor that reopens a pathname: even the retained path may be atomically replaced after validation, so those modes fail closed with owner_backed_reader_required until coding_agent_session_search-cass-fsvi-semantic-witness-xbq0b and an owner-consuming FrankenSearch API remove the reopen race. Pointer-selected immutable generations remain fail closed for the same reason.
design: Represent every selected exact semantic source as one constructor-owned SemanticIndexArtifact with private fields that opens and retains its own VectorIndex plus the frozen path used for that open. Carry artifacts, never parallel reader/path vectors, through SemanticContext and SearchClient. Reject final-component FSVI symlinks and unreadable or invalid exact FSVI fail closed. Preserve an explicitly selected ANN candidate even when missing, a directory, broken/final-component symlink, hard-link alias, corrupt, stale, or non-native so it reaches bounded rejection rather than being mislabeled absent. At query time call FrankenSearch HnswIndex::try_load_native against the already-opened exact FSVI; accept only Some(native), map None to ann_sidecar_not_native, and map open/admission errors to ann_sidecar_open_failed. Never rebuild, convert, write, or substitute a graph. Cache the admitted graph or typed fallback reason per semantic context and warn once. Multiple exact shards use the existing exact merge and report multiple_exact_shards for ANN. Exact and FastOnly requests remain live from the retained exact owner when progressive construction is unavailable. Every progressive, QualityOnly, and path-based in-memory two-tier attempt whose reader would reopen a pathname returns owner_backed_reader_required before path discovery or open; readiness and serving expose the same reason. Keep the dormant path-based construction code unreachable until a distinct owner-backed capability can be set only by a future owner-consuming API.
acceptance_criteria: Mock-free restart/search E2E builds through the real CASS writer at vector_index/index-<embedder>.fsvi and creates no conventional copies. Corrupt fixed-name decoys prove no serving lane uses basename discovery. Unit and fresh-process E2E cover native ANN, absent ANN, corrupt metadata, non-regular candidates, final-component and broken symlinks, FSVI/ANN same-file alias, stale same-doc-id but different-vector ANN, missing/corrupt/wrong-identity FSVI, exact fast-only, explicit fast-plus-quality topology, multiple shards, and pointer-selected owner_backed_reader_required. Native ANN returns expected winners with ann_stats and no fallback reason. Every rejected or absent ANN succeeds through the retained exact FSVI, returns the exact winner, emits no ann_stats, and exposes one stable bounded reason in human and robot diagnostics. Atomic selected-path replacement must prove a newly reopened path produces a different winner while the installed SearchClient keeps the original exact winner; FastOnly falls back to that retained owner; progressive and two-tier APIs return owner_backed_reader_required; serving and diagnostics preserve bytes, mtimes, permissions, and directory inventory without rebuild or mutation. Readiness and execution must agree across monolithic, prototype-shard, and pointer-selected sources. Run strict-remote focused units, every fresh-process E2E in isolation plus the full semantic E2E target, workspace check, workspace clippy with warnings denied, explicit rustfmt check, git diff check, and UBS on every changed file. Record exact FrankenSearch and CASS SHAs plus remote job and worker receipts before close.

title: Daemon protocol v2 must bind and verify complete typed embedding identity per response
description: Replace every daemon request/response path that sends or accepts a display model name, dimension-only vector, or unbound raw embedding with one versioned typed protocol. The request binds the selected immutable generation, tier, topology, source/corpus/docset identity, input contract, producer, model revision, tokenizer, pooling, normalization, storage representation, dimension and distance contract. The response attests the same identity and binds the produced vector or result to one request nonce and generation. Fast and quality tiers are independently bound; a vector from one space can never be reused for the other. Per-call and mid-stream drift, replay, truncation, unknown fields/versions and same-dimension wrong-space substitutions fail closed before cache insertion or search. Explicit Semantic remains a typed failure; Hybrid may fall open only with requested/realized mode and bounded reason preserved.
design: Use one canonical identity value shared with the manifest reader and typed query-vector APIs, serialized in a strict versioned daemon envelope. Negotiate exactly one supported protocol rather than retaining a permissive compatibility shim. Bind request nonce, selected CURRENT generation, tier and topology at admission; the daemon signs or hashes the complete response envelope, and the client revalidates before allocation into result/cache state. Streaming responses repeat or chain the binding so a generation switch cannot splice chunks. Rejection produces stable machine reason codes and bounded redacted events without query text, vector bytes, secrets or full paths.
acceptance_criteria: Mutation tests change every identity field independently, including same dimension/different producer, model revision, tokenizer, pooling, normalization, input, distance/storage, tier, topology, source, corpus, docset and generation; each rejects before vector search, cache insertion or result emission. Unit and fresh-process daemon/client E2E cover compatible FastOnly, QualityOnly and FullProgressive requests, independent tier embeddings, reconnect/restart, nonce replay, cross-request substitution, truncated/duplicated/reordered frames, unknown protocol version, per-call drift and mid-stream CURRENT drift. Explicit Semantic never reports lexical success; Hybrid fallback is typed and truthfully reports requested/realized modes. Cache keys include complete identity and generation. Optimized strict-remote tests, workspace check/clippy/fmt and changed-file UBS run with under 10k lines/8MiB, redacted structured logs and exact binary/protocol/generation receipts.

title: Production semantic search must execute native ANN across every authoritative shard
description: Wire native HNSW into the production manifest-only reader for every ordered FSVI shard in each selected tier. Admit each sidecar only against the exact retained immutable base-shard owner and complete embedding/generation/source identity; path existence, basename, doc count and dimension are never readiness. Search all admitted shards, merge deterministic global top-k with stable tie rules, apply tombstones/filters, and preserve FastOnly, QualityOnly, FullProgressive and PartialQuality semantics. A rejected or absent ANN sidecar falls back to exact search for that same retained shard with a typed reason; it may never silently drop a shard, mix generations, use conventional filenames or claim ANN statistics for exact work.
design: Resolve CURRENT and its immutable manifest once, retain every exact shard owner, and derive a shard execution plan whose ANN member is optional only after exact native admission. Query vectors are typed and tier-specific. Execute per-shard ANN or exact fallback under one cancellation-aware bounded plan; resolve IDs from the bound base shard, then perform one deterministic global merge and provenance projection. Recheck no mutable path after admission. Readiness and query diagnostics consume the same per-shard admission outcome and stable reason taxonomy. Native ANN persistence, receipt binding and tombstone behavior must be production paths rather than test-only schemas.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover one and many shards, cross-shard winners, ties, k=0/1/10/100, empty corpus, zero live rows, tombstoned/filtered winners, partial quality coverage and deterministic rebuild/restart. Fresh-process no-mock E2E covers all FastOnly/QualityOnly/FullProgressive/PartialQuality topologies and proves a quality-only winner outside the fast pool is found. For each shard, corrupt/truncated/missing/stale/wrong-source/same-count-wrong-vector/wrong-identity/wrong-generation/symlink/cross-role sidecars are rejected and exact fallback returns parity without ANN stats; an admitted native sidecar reports bound ANN receipts and maintains required recall against exhaustive exact search. Omitted, duplicate, overlapping, gapped or reordered manifest coverage rejects before embedding. Logs are bounded/redacted; strict-remote unit/E2E/workspace check/clippy/fmt and changed-file UBS pin exact CASS and FrankenSearch receipt identities.

title: One semantic readiness and RecoveryPlan state machine across all truth surfaces
description:
Replace drifting readiness implementations in asset state, semantic readiness, model manager, manifest progress, query/daemon setup, TUI, status, health, doctor, answer packs and robot metadata with one pure typed classifier and one RecoveryPlan renderer. Consume ds7uy.1 disk states and ds7uy.3 runtime/query facts; no adapter reparses JSON, filenames or reason strings.

Inputs cover request/policy; model absent/partial/verifying/verified/unloadable/daemon-mismatched; exhaustive disk/source state; topology and per-tier coverage; full identity; vector/zero-signal; ANN; cache; runtime warm/cold; building/interrupted operation; lock contention; permission/I/O/no-space; cancellation; retry exhaustion. Outputs are versioned Ready, ReadyDegraded, NeedsProvisioning, NeedsReindex, Building, Unavailable, Corrupt or UpgradeRequired with stable reason and structured RecoveryPlan. Explicit semantic fails closed. Hybrid lexical fallback reports requested/realized mode, coverage, reason/action. FastTierRefined is a genuine semantic contribution even when quality is unavailable; it must not be mislabeled lexical-only. Stale/hash/model-only are never ready.

PREREQUISITES: ds7uy.1/.3 plus exact landed FrankenSearch disk-state, RecoveryPlan and zero-signal schemas actually consumed. Do not wait for terminal bd-jbfg/bd-p6z6 or the final receipt.
design: One serializable input snapshot and total pure classify function own policy. RecoveryPlan has structured action, argv, prerequisites, destructive flag, expected network/disk/time and retry permission; human output derives from it. Every argv must parse against the real CLI, so nonexistent forms such as models install --json cannot enter goldens. Adapters only gather and render. One bounded transition event emits on state change, never each poll.
acceptance_criteria: Exhaustive table/property tests cover policy, model, every disk/source state, topology, identity, signal, ANN, cache, warm/cold, contention, permission/I/O/no-space, cancellation, interrupted operation and retry exhaustion. Determinism, totality, serialization and fail-closed invariants hold. FastTierRefined remains semantic with exact coverage; partial quality is not lexical-only. Cross-surface goldens inject each state once and prove status/health/doctor/query/answer-pack/daemon/TUI/JSON/human outputs agree, and every RecoveryPlan argv parses and executes in a bounded fixture. Zero-signal exact/ANN parity and real MiniLM Ready/drift lanes pass. Logs stay under 10k lines/8MiB with no raw query/path/dependency TRACE. title: Bind each semantic execution to a truthful machine-readable provenance receipt
description: Make every shipped search surface emit one execution-bound receipt derived from the same immutable resolution and runtime facts that actually drove the query. The receipt must distinguish requested and realized mode/topology, semantic contribution by tier, exact versus native ANN per shard, selected generation and complete bounded identity fingerprints, source/docset witness, cache state, zero-signal state, coverage/candidate counts, fallback or failure reason and RecoveryPlan reference. design: Create the receipt at the execution boundary from typed manifest resolution, bound query-vector identities, per-shard search outcomes and the total readiness classifier; pass that owned value to all renderers. Use a versioned, bounded, privacy-safe schema with stable reason codes and fingerprint fields, never raw vectors, queries, content, secrets or full paths. Distinguish planned/readiness facts from observed execution facts. Receipt serialization is deterministic and tied to a request ID, exact binary identity and selected CURRENT witness. title: Explicit semantic ensure-ready provisioning: atomic acquire, blue-green reindex, and one-shot command retry
description:
Implement explicit CASS ensure-ready orchestration without surprise networking. Library code never prompts/downloads. Default hybrid performs zero surprise acquisition and may continue lexically with typed RecoveryPlan. Interactive explicit semantic may offer one consent prompt with exact model/revision/license/source/size/hash/destination plus document count, index disk/time and blue-green consequences. Consent authorizes one immutable model-generation acquisition, load self-test, ds7uy.2 reindex, ds7uy.4 readiness recheck and exactly one structured retry preserving query, filters, output, limit, topology/mode and robot flags.

Non-TTY never prompts and requires explicit ensure/provision; offline immediately emits a valid --from-file plan. QualityOnly MiniLM does not force a fast model. Network and from-file use unique staging under cross-process lock, streaming verification, load test, fsync and atomic immutable publication. Model selection and index selection publish as one compatible composite queryable generation; a marker-less or preseeded directory is never trusted merely because bytes exist. models install reports acquired-needs-reindex until a compatible index is published. Warm ready runs zero network; builds never acquire.

PREREQUISITES: ds7uy.2/.4 plus exact landed FrankenSearch acquisition and pure policy/RecoveryPlan primitives actually consumed. Do not wait for terminal bd-p6z6/bd-jbfg or the final receipt; this CASS child is what later produces that receipt.
design: One state machine: Classify, Plan, OptionalConsent, Lock, AcquireUniqueStaging, Verify, AtomicModelGenerationPublish, LoadSelfTest, BlueGreenReindex, CompositeSelectionCAS, ReadinessRecheck, RetryOriginalOnce. CLI alone owns TTY/prompt. Consent is exact and one-shot. Retry retains a typed request and guard. Acquisition/network/from-file share code and immutable receipts. Bounded events carry fingerprints, bytes, phase, consent, action, timing and request counts without queries/content/full paths/secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover library/TTY/non-TTY/default-hybrid/explicit/offline/already-ready, prompt details, accept/decline/EOF/cancel, cross-process lock races, unique staging, network/from-file parity, corrupt/partial/marker-interrupted artifacts, revision/hash/license mismatch and exact request preservation. Fault injection at every copy/download/write/fsync/rename/load/reindex/composite-CAS/readiness/retry boundary preserves prior model/index pair and never retries twice. Machine output freezes valid parseable argv, requested/realized mode, phase, acquired-versus-ready and zero-network warm count. Optimized no-mock real-MiniLM Treasure E2E proves empty -> refusal/plan -> authorization -> acquire -> quality-only blue-green index -> restart -> semantic/hybrid ground truth beating hash -> warm zero-network -> corrupt/missing/wrong/legacy/hash recovery -> one retry. Logs meet 10k-line/8MiB and redaction. Evidence pins ds7uy.2/.4 plus exact primitive commits consumed, not terminal umbrellas.
notes: AUDIT-REQUIRED PLAN REFINEMENT (2026-07-26): ensure-ready consumes shard-capable composite generations and EmptyCorpus without losing functionality. EmptyCorpus requires no model download or reindex loop and retries the original request once to an explicit empty semantic result. Any transition to a nonempty source builds/publishes the complete ordered shard/tier composite before readiness. HashControl may be provisioned only by explicit control/test intent and never satisfies semantic readiness. The retry must preserve robot budget and explicit Semantic versus Hybrid policy so budget pressure cannot silently turn Semantic into lexical. All rendered installation/recovery argv are produced by the ds7uy.4 typed plan, parser-tested against the real binary, and exercised; the invalid `models install --json` form is forbidden. Add multi-shard acquisition/reindex/restart, empty-to-nonempty, concurrent ensure, mid-build source drift, and exact request-preservation E2E lanes alongside the real MiniLM Treasure Island lifecycle.

title: secret_scan: entropy-span shadowing makes detects_generic_api_key and hex_entropy_detection unsatisfiable (2 red integration tests at HEAD)
description: Two tests in tests/secret_scan.rs fail at HEAD and appear UNSATISFIABLE under current mechanics (exposed once the test target compiles again; see the compile-repair commit). Mechanics: ENTROPY_BASE64_RE is [A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{20,} — '=' and '_' inside the class merge whole key=value assignments into ONE span ('api_key=abcdefgh12345678', 24 chars, shannon 4.42 >= threshold 4.0) -> high_entropy_base64 (Medium). push_finding's overlap dedup keeps one finding per overlapping span and lets higher severity REPLACE the kind, so generic_api_key (Low) is always shadowed. Same for hex: the base64 loop runs before the hex loop, its charset is a superset of hex, so any >=20-char hex with entropy >=4.0 becomes high_entropy_base64 and high_entropy_hex (Low) can never surface (the fixture's 64-char hex has entropy exactly 4.0). Options for the owner: (a) exclude '=' mid-token (base64 padding is terminal: [A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{20,}={0,2}) so assignments split at '=' — fixes the generic case; (b) scope dedup to IDENTICAL spans or keep kind-specific findings alongside the entropy finding; (c) run pattern findings at higher precedence than generic entropy for the same span; (d) declare shadowing intended and rewrite the two tests. Probe evidence: the failing assertion now prints the found kinds — got [(high_entropy_base64, Medium)] for the generic fixture. Repro: cargo test --test secret_scan detects_generic_api_key / hex_entropy_detection_for_long_hex_strings.
close_reason: Entropy shadowing fixed at e9a4d898/a06d3899: terminal-only base64 padding + pure-hex deferral; both red gates (detects_generic_api_key, hex_entropy_detection_for_long_hex_strings) green; full secret_scan 56/56.

(2) The base64 entropy loop defers pure-hex candidates >=32 chars to the hex classifier so high_entropy_hex surfaces. title: [MEDIUM] concurrency: non-watch indexing can leave WAL uncheckpointed after disabling autocheckpoint
description: Validated with /deadlock-finder-and-fixer Class 4 checklist. Concrete interleaving/sequence: T1 runs a non-watch index path, so run_index sets defer_checkpoints = !opts.watch, persist::apply_index_writer_checkpoint_policy stores PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 on the long-lived handle and with_ephemeral_writer applies the same to each short-lived writer. T1 then persists many batches. At successful close, close_storage_after_index calls close_without_checkpoint, explicitly suppressing the final checkpoint. No Rust ownership constraint prevents this because the WAL/checkpoint state is process/database state, not protected by the &FrankenStorage references; short-lived writers reopen by path and readers/search can run in other processes. Impact: large or long-running bulk index paths can leave WAL growth/replay work unbounded and can starve checkpoint progress rather than deferring it to a safe explicit checkpoint.
close_reason: Fixed close_storage_after_index to restore checkpoint policy, close the indexing handle, then run a post-close TRUNCATE checkpoint; added regression coverage for the restored policy and absence of backfillable WAL frames after close.

title: False-positive OOM quarantine on --watch batch ingest: VDBE bounded-guard NoMem misclassified as real OOM (gh #298)
description:
Follow-up to gh #290/#291 (both shipped). On the --watch batch path, small/medium conversations (2.8-6 MB files, 20-93 KB indexed text) are OOM-quarantined under batch load even though the SAME file ingests cleanly solo into a fresh data-dir. Quarantine reasons: index-ingest-out-of-memory (231) + watch-ingest-out-of-memory (92). These are nowhere near a real 24 GB host OOM.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): frankensqlite's bounded internal-allocation guards — notably the VDBE frame/register caps at crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/frame.rs:191,193,236 (also pager/page_buf/page_cache, vfs/memory) — emit the bare typed FrankenError::OutOfMemory (ErrorCode::NoMem) when a per-statement BOUNDED limit is exceeded, NOT when the OS is out of memory. cass's error_is_out_of_memory() (src/indexer/mod.rs:20887) downcasts to FrankenError::OutOfMemory and treats ANY such error as real OOM -> OOM-bisect -> per-conversation quarantine (src/indexer/mod.rs ~20505-20650 non-watch, ~20690-20840 watch). Bisect-to-single still trips because the single retry runs in the same loaded batch context (not truly isolated like the fresh-data-dir solo run).

FIX OPTION A (correct, source-level) — reclassify the spurious bounded-guard NoMem in frankensqlite to a distinct non-OOM error (e.g. a StatementLimit/Internal variant), so cass no longer misreads it as OOM. BLOCKED THIS SESSION: cass pins frankensqlite =0.1.9 from crates.io (local [patch] override is commented out per Cargo.toml), so any frankensqlite change needs a version bump + crates.io republish + AGENTS.md pin update. Also touches SQLite-compat surface (NoMem==SQLITE_NOMEM) and needs care to not regress real OOM mapping for other consumers.

FIX OPTION B (cass-side, self-contained) — gate the OOM->quarantine decision so a single conversation is only OOM-quarantined when a real-OOM is plausible (materialized bytes over a generous threshold AND/OR a real process/system memory-pressure signal). For sub-threshold conversations, retry the single conversation in a TRULY ISOLATED storage context (fresh connection / committed+reset txn — mirroring the fresh-data-dir solo success that the reporter proved works) BEFORE any quarantine; only quarantine if the isolated retry also fails.
  RISK: a naive 'skip quarantine for small convs' WITHOUT a successful isolated retry would either tight-loop (no progress) or silently drop (current code quarantines AND advances watch progress to avoid wedge). Mis-tuned gating could also MASK real OOMs — directly relevant to the wedge issues gh #296/#301. So Option B MUST include the isolated-retry success path, not just a size gate.

RECOMMENDED: Option B with an explicit isolated single-conversation retry + size/pressure gate, fully tested with a solo-vs-batch --watch-once differential (reporter offered to attach the watch log + per-conversation breakdowns). Possibly-related incidental noise: 'frankensqlite FTS batch insert failed ... table not found: fts_messages_data' (Tantivy authoritative; may be separate).

PRACTICAL IMPACT: low for the reporter (periodic one-shot 'cass index' avoids the batch path) but quarantines a few hundred indexable conversations on the default --watch daemon over a real ~12.4k-conv corpus. Relates to epic coding_agent_session_search-cass-fleet-resilience-20260608-uojcg.3 and follow-on xaztn.
close_reason: Cass-side Option B landed (bd7be1d0 + 3b048dcc): (1) watch path — solo isolate-retry now re-enters in SoloIsolatedRetry mode so a repeated OOM propagates to the Standard-mode caller's pressure/size gate instead of quarantining behind its back (the gate was production-dead code before; the 'ingested cleanly solo' log could lie); (2) NEW deferred_conversations plumbing preserves the watch watermark on defer so a deferred conversation is never silently dropped; (3) non-watch path gained the same plausibility gate before record_index_poison (231 of the field quarantines were index-ingest-out-of-memory); (4) deterministic tests for both defer paths (pressure reserve pinned to 0). fsqlite 0.1.13 still returns bare OutOfMemory from bounded guards (frame.rs) so Option A remains upstream.

title: [P2] Opt 5: Wildcard Regex Caching (LRU Cache for RegexQuery)
description:
# Optimization 5: Wildcard Regex Caching

## Problem Statement

Profiling shows meaningful CPU time spent in regex query construction for wildcard searches:

### CPU Profile Evidence (from perf)
```
1.16% tantivy_fst::regex::dfa::Dfa::add
0.86% tantivy::query::regex_query::RegexQuery::from_pattern
```

For TUI interactive search where users type incrementally (e.g., `*error*` → `*error*handling*`), the same regex patterns may be built repeatedly.

### Wildcard Benchmark Results
| Pattern Type | Latency |
|-------------|---------|
| `wildcard_exact_match` | 445 µs |
| `wildcard_prefix_pattern` | 614 µs |
| `wildcard_suffix_pattern` | 14 µs |
| `wildcard_substring_pattern` | 15 µs |
| `wildcard_large_dataset/suffix` | 3.2 ms |
| `wildcard_large_dataset/substring` | 7.5 ms |

The disparity suggests regex/DFA construction is significant for some patterns.

## Proposed Solution

LRU cache of `(<field>, <pattern>) -> Arc<RegexQuery>` to reuse compiled queries.

### Implementation Location
- File: `src/search/query.rs`
- Add thread-local or shared LRU cache

### Code Sketch
```rust
use lru::LruCache;
use std::sync::Mutex;

lazy_static! {
    static ref REGEX_CACHE: Mutex<LruCache<(String, String), Arc<RegexQuery>>> =
        Mutex::new(LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(64).unwrap()));
}

fn get_or_build_regex_query(field: &str, pattern: &str) -> Arc<RegexQuery> {
    let key = (field.to_string(), pattern.to_string());
    
    let mut cache = REGEX_CACHE.lock().unwrap();
    if let Some(cached) = cache.get(&key) {
        return Arc::clone(cached);
    }
    
    // Build the RegexQuery (expensive)
    let query = Arc::new(RegexQuery::from_pattern(pattern, field)?);
    cache.put(key, Arc::clone(&query));
    query
}
```

### Cache Configuration
- **Size**: 64 entries (covers typical interactive session diversity)
- **Eviction**: LRU (least recently used)
- **Key**: (field_name, pattern_string) tuple
- **Value**: Arc<RegexQuery> for cheap cloning

## Isomorphism Proof

Caching must not change which patterns are built or their semantics:
1. **Same key → same query**: Pattern string uniquely determines RegexQuery behavior
2. **Deterministic construction**: `RegexQuery::from_pattern` is pure for same inputs
3. **Arc sharing is safe**: RegexQuery is immutable after construction

## Expected Impact

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| First query | Full regex build | Full regex build |
| Repeated query | Full regex build | Cache hit (< 1µs) |
| TUI incremental | N × build cost | 1 × build cost |

Most impactful for:
- TUI interactive search (users refine queries)
- Robot mode with repeated similar patterns
- Test suites running many similar queries

## Cache Key Design Considerations

### Why (field, pattern) tuple?
- Same pattern on different fields produces different queries
- Field-specific optimizations in Tantivy

### Why String keys (not &str)?
- Cache outlives individual query lifetimes
- String allocation is negligible vs regex compilation cost

### Why Arc<RegexQuery>?
- Allows multiple concurrent searches to share the same compiled query
- Cheap clone for cache hits

## Memory Impact

- 64 entries × ~1KB per compiled query ≈ 64KB worst case
- Negligible compared to vector index memory

## Thread Safety

Options:
1. **Mutex<LruCache>**: Simple, low contention for typical usage
2. **RwLock<LruCache>**: Better for read-heavy workloads
3. **Thread-local caches**: No contention, but no sharing between threads

Recommendation: Start with Mutex. Profile if contention becomes an issue.

## Verification Plan

1. **Fixed-index test**: Repeated wildcard queries produce identical hits
2. **Cache hit test**: Second query returns cached result (verify via counter)
3. **Benchmark**: Compare repeated query latency with/without cache

## Rollback Strategy

Environment variable `CASS_REGEX_CACHE=0` to:
- Disable caching
- Build fresh RegexQuery for every query
- Useful for debugging cache-related issues

## Dependencies

- May need `lru` crate (or use `std::collections::HashMap` with manual eviction)
- Independent of vector search optimizations

## Cargo.toml Addition
```toml
[dependencies]
lru = "*"  # LRU cache implementation
```

Note: AGENTS.md specifies wildcard constraints (`*`) for all crates.

title: [MEDIUM] strategic-review: health/fast-surface <50ms latency claim has no regression gate
description:
Multi-perspective review finding (fast-vs-deep axis). README line 14 + cass health --help advertise health as "Minimal health check (<50ms). Exit 0=healthy, 1=unhealthy. For agent pre-flight checks." The golden tests pin envelope SHAPE (health_shape.json.golden, +1 instance + 2 semantic variants) but NO test measures wall-clock latency. A regression that adds a DB query, an fs::canonicalize loop, or a synchronous embedder probe to the health path would break the <50ms contract and agents would see pre-flight checks silently balloon to hundreds of milliseconds before anyone noticed.

Evidence of similar risk in adjacent commands:
- status_shape.json.golden (21 KB) was just added (q931h) — status emits nested index/db/semantic/rebuild/quarantine blocks that COULD grow arbitrarily.
- capabilities/api-version are simpler but also unbounded.
- diag is deliberately heavy (quarantine inventory walk) — not on the fast-surface list but sometimes confused for one.

Fix direction: add tests/latency_fast_surfaces.rs with per-command wall-clock budgets (p50 over 20 warmed runs, tolerant of CI jitter). Suggested budgets from README + robot-docs:
  health --json      : p50 < 50ms,  p99 < 150ms
  status --json      : p50 < 100ms, p99 < 300ms
  capabilities --json: p50 < 50ms,  p99 < 150ms
  api-version --json : p50 < 30ms,  p99 < 100ms

Rationale: agents run these as pre-flight checks every command; a 500ms regression on health is a user-visible taxonomy shift from "cheap probe" to "something we avoid". The latency gate would catch regressions at CI time instead of via user reports.

Note on flake mitigation: run-to-run variance on CI runners makes p99 caps prone to noise. Use a percentile over repeated invocations within the same test process (not p99 across separate runs), and set budgets at 3× the measured median on a warmed tempdir so expected noise stays well inside the gate.
close_reason: Shipped (commit). Latency regression test health_json_large_seeded_db_p50_stays_under_50ms exists at tests/e2e_health.rs:491 (peer-shipped, pane 4 validated). This commit formalises the CI-hard-gate contract via doc comment pointing at .github/workflows/ci.yml:227 where the e2e_*.rs glob auto-includes the test in every CI run. Asserts warmed p50 < 50ms over 11 measured samples after 5 warmup runs on a large seeded DB; 3× headroom over typical sub-20ms measurement absorbs CI jitter. Regression that pushes p50 above 50ms (new sync DB query, canonicalize loop, embedder probe) fails CI loudly.

title: Task 6.5: Create Test Fixtures for All Agent Formats
description:
# Objective
Create realistic test fixture files for all supported agent formats to enable unit and E2E testing.

## Fixture Location
tests/fixtures/

## Required Fixtures

### 1. claude_session.jsonl
Real Claude Code JSONL format:
```jsonl
{"type":"user","timestamp":1706400000000,"message":{"role":"user","content":"Read the README file"}}
{"type":"assistant","timestamp":1706400001000,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll read that for you."},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_abc123","name":"Read","input":{"file_path":"/README.md"}}]}}
{"type":"user","timestamp":1706400002000,"message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_abc123","content":"# Project Title\n\nDescription here."}]}}
{"type":"assistant","timestamp":1706400003000,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"The README contains the project title and description."}}
```

Content requirements:
- 1 user message
- 1 assistant message with 3 tool calls (Read, Bash, Glob)
- 3 tool results with mix of success/error
- 1 user follow-up
- 1 final assistant response
- Total: ~10 messages → should become 4 groups

### 2. codex_session.jsonl
Codex CLI format with function_call structure:
```jsonl
{"role":"user","content":"List files"}
{"role":"assistant","content":null,"function_call":{"name":"shell","arguments":"{\"command\":\"ls -la\"}"}}
{"role":"function","name":"shell","content":"file1.txt\nfile2.txt"}
{"role":"assistant","content":"There are 2 files."}
```

### 3. cursor_session.jsonl
Cursor format (research actual structure).

### 4. opencode_session.jsonl
OpenCode format with its specific message structure.

### 5. edge_cases.jsonl
Special cases:
- Empty messages
- Orphan tool results
- Tool calls without results
- Very long content
- Unicode content
- Nested JSON in tool input

## Fixture Validation Script
Create scripts/validate_fixtures.sh:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Validate all fixture files are valid JSONL
for f in tests/fixtures/*.jsonl; do
  echo "Validating $f..."
  jq -e . < "$f" > /dev/null || { echo "INVALID: $f"; exit 1; }
done
echo "All fixtures valid!"
```

## Documentation
Create tests/fixtures/README.md:
- Explain each fixture's purpose
- Document expected group counts
- Describe edge cases covered

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] claude_session.jsonl created with real format
- [ ] codex_session.jsonl created
- [ ] cursor_session.jsonl created
- [ ] opencode_session.jsonl created  
- [ ] edge_cases.jsonl created
- [ ] All fixtures are valid JSONL
- [ ] Each fixture has documented expected output
- [ ] Validation script passes

title: [LOW] strategic-review: no runtime check that introspect response_schemas match actual emitted JSON shape
description:
Multi-perspective review finding (symbolic-vs-runtime axis). cass introspect --json ships a response_schemas block (12 entries pre-0h4cx, 16 post-fix) that agents use to drive schema-aware parsing. The schemas are HAND-WRITTEN JSON Schema in src/lib.rs::build_response_schemas (lines 17293+). Nothing asserts that those hand-written schemas actually describe the JSON each corresponding command emits at runtime.

Concrete regression path: a future commit adds a new top-level field to cass health --json output (e.g., `fleet_id: i64`) but forgets to update the `health` entry in response_schemas. Agents using the schema to validate / filter fields silently drop the new field. Goldens catch the health.json.golden drift, but NOT the introspect↔runtime divergence.

Fix direction: add tests/metamorphic_introspect_schema.rs with one test per surface:
  for each surface in response_schemas keys:
      1. invoke `cass <surface> --json` against a fresh empty data_dir
      2. use json_value_schema(actual) to derive the runtime shape
      3. assert runtime keys ⊆ schema keys (schema may document optional-absent fields)
      4. assert runtime types match schema types for shared keys

Severity LOW because the goldens already pin shape + an agent reading introspect today gets a stale-but-benign view. Upgrading to the metamorphic cross-check turns introspect into a load-bearing contract instead of documentation.
close_reason: Implemented runtime introspect schema validation in tests/metamorphic_introspect_schema.rs and updated stale response_schemas for top-level runtime fields; verified focused test, clippy, and check.

title: [MEDIUM] mock-finder: src/indexer/refresh_ledger.rs module registered as pub mod but has zero callers outside itself
description:
Mock-code-finder finding: orphaned module.

## Location
\`src/indexer/mod.rs:5\`:

\`\`\`rust
pub mod refresh_ledger;
\`\`\`

The module defines a complete ledger API (PhaseRecord, RefreshLedger,
EquivalenceArtifacts, RefreshReadinessMilestones, readiness_milestones(),
phase_timing helpers, etc.) — but grep across the entire \`src/\` tree
confirms NOTHING outside refresh_ledger.rs imports or uses these types:

\`\`\`
\$ rg -rn 'RefreshLedger|PhaseRecord' src/ | grep -v refresh_ledger
(no output)

\$ rg -rn 'use.*refresh_ledger|pub use.*refresh_ledger' src/
(no output)
\`\`\`

The module is declared, compiled, and carries its own ~900 lines
of implementation + ~400 lines of unit tests, but no production
code-path records a phase, reads a milestone, or serializes a
ledger.

## Why this matters
Bead ibuuh.24 ("Deliver a world-class stale-index refresh architecture")
appears to have introduced this module as the evidence ledger for the
stale-refresh pipeline (per the module's own doc comment: "timings,
counters, and correctness artifacts for each phase"). Several
\`[ibuuh.24]\` commits (5579e562, 6474da3d, 9f3d49f2) touched it. But
the actual indexer/rebuild code in \`src/indexer/mod.rs\` and
\`src/indexer/semantic.rs\` does NOT call these APIs — they log via
\`tracing::info!\` directly.

Without callers, the ledger's contract is unverified against real
refresh behavior: its fields may not match what the refresh path
actually produces, its readiness_milestones() derivation may not
reflect the path's actual phase order, and its serialization shape
(the \`HashMap<String, u64> counters\` field I flagged earlier in
R2 review as non-deterministic under serde_json default iteration)
hasn't been exercised.

## Two hazards
1. **Drift**: the ledger APIs and the real rebuild path evolve
   independently; by the time someone wires the two together,
   the ledger's contract may no longer describe what the rebuild
   actually does.
2. **Latent non-determinism**: \`PhaseRecord.counters: HashMap<...>\`
   and \`RefreshLedger.tags: HashMap<...>\` serialize in random order
   (serde_json with preserve_order enabled preserves HashMap iter
   order, which is random per process). If the ledger ever gets
   written to a golden-tested file or compared byte-for-byte,
   the goldens flake. (Same class of bug as
   coding_agent_session_search-8sl73 fixed for IntrospectResponse.)

## Suggested completion
Three options — same decision tree as y0dto (ensure_cass_origin
dead-code bead):

1. **Wire it in**. Route the stale-refresh path (rebuild_tantivy_from_db
   and siblings in src/indexer/mod.rs) through RefreshLedger::new()
   + phase_start/phase_complete/counter_inc. Add a test that proves
   the ledger's readiness_milestones() match the user-visible
   time_to_search_ready_ms / time_to_lexical_ready_ms reported by
   \`cass health --json\`. Once wired, swap the HashMap fields to
   BTreeMap to make the serialized form byte-deterministic (prevents
   the latent-drift hazard).

2. **Delete the module**. If the ibuuh.24 architecture has chosen a
   different observability surface (e.g., the tracing-event stream
   + stall watchdog from ae411287), this module is vestigial. Remove
   \`pub mod refresh_ledger;\` from indexer/mod.rs and delete the
   file. ~900 LOC of unused code gone; commit message should
   explicitly cite which alternative replaced it so future agents
   don't try to re-introduce it.

3. **Park it with a beacon**. If the module is intentionally pre-
   landed for a specific future slice, add a top-of-module comment
   naming the target bead ID + expected wire-in deadline, AND swap
   HashMap → BTreeMap preemptively so the contract it locks in is
   deterministic when the wire-in lands.

## Severity
MEDIUM. Not a functional bug TODAY (no caller → no regression).
But 900 LOC of unwired scaffolding + a known non-determinism trap
in its serialization shape is exactly the mock-finder signal this
sweep is designed to surface.

Labels: indexer, refresh, lifecycle, cleanup, mock-finder.

title: P6.3: Performance Testing & Large Archive Profiling
P1.4a: Verify Command for CI Pipelines
description:
# P1.4a: Verify Command for CI Pipelines

## Goal
Provide `cass pages --verify` to validate an existing export bundle for CI/CD. The verifier must confirm correct structure, config schema, payload integrity, and the absence of secrets in site/.

## CLI Interface

```
cass pages --verify <PATH>

OPTIONS:
  --json         Output machine-readable JSON
  -v, --verbose  Include detailed check results
```

`PATH` may be either the export root (containing site/) or the site/ directory itself. Verify resolves to the site/ directory.

## Verification Checks

### 1) Required Files
- index.html
- config.json
- sw.js
- viewer.js
- auth.js
- styles.css
- robots.txt
- .nojekyll
- payload/ (with chunk files)
- integrity.json (if present, must validate)

### 2) config.json Schema
Validate required fields and types:
- version, export_id (base64, 16 bytes), base_nonce (base64, 12 bytes)
- algorithm == aes-256-gcm
- compression in {deflate, zstd, none}
- payload.chunk_size <= 32 MiB (default 8 MiB), payload.chunk_count > 0
- payload.files list length == chunk_count
- key_slots[] with slot_type, kdf, salt, nonce, wrapped_dek
- no human labels or PII fields in public config

### 3) Payload Manifest and Size Limits
- payload/chunk-00000.bin ... payload/chunk-N.bin exist and are contiguous
- each chunk file <= 100 MB (GitHub Pages hard limit)
- total site size computed and reported

### 4) integrity.json (if present)
- recompute sha256 for each site/ file
- compare with integrity.json entries
- fail on mismatch; report missing/extra files

### 5) Secret Leakage Checks
- ensure site/ does not contain recovery-secret.txt, qr-code.*, master-key.json, or private/
- ensure config.json does not include secret material (no plaintext passwords, no labels)

### 6) Optional blobs/
- if blobs/ exists, each filename must be sha256-*.bin
- blobs are included in integrity.json

## JSON Output (example)
```json
{
  "status": "valid",
  "checks": {
    "required_files": true,
    "config_schema": true,
    "payload_manifest": true,
    "size_limits": true,
    "integrity": true,
    "no_secrets_in_site": true
  },
  "warnings": [],
  "site_size_bytes": 25678901
}
```

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests
- Missing required files -> failure
- Invalid config.json fields -> failure
- Chunk count mismatch -> failure
- integrity.json mismatch -> failure

### Integration Tests
- Verify a known-good fixture export passes
- Verify a fixture with private files in site/ fails

### E2E Script
- Build export -> bundle -> cass pages --verify --json
- Log each check clearly with PASS/FAIL and timing

## Files to Create/Modify
- src/pages/verify.rs
- src/cli/pages.rs (add --verify)
- tests/pages_verify.rs
- tests/fixtures/pages_verify/

## Exit Criteria
1. Verify passes on valid bundles and fails on invalid ones
2. JSON output is stable for CI parsing
3. Clear error messages in verbose mode

# P3.5b: Deep Links & Hash-based Router

**Parent Phase:** Phase 3: Web Viewer

## Goal
Support direct URLs to specific conversations, messages, search results, and app panels, enabling shareability and browser history navigation on static hosting.

```

#/search?q=auth+bug      -> search query
#/c/12345                -> conversation 12345
```

title: Query Suggestions (did-you-mean)
description:
# Query Suggestions (did-you-mean)

## Problem Statement
When a search returns 0 results, agents have no guidance on what to try next:
- Was it a typo? ("git comit" → "git commit")
- Too specific? (suggest removing terms)
- Wrong field? (content vs title)

## Proposed Solution
Add suggestions to empty/sparse result sets:
```bash
cass search "git comit" --json
```

Output:
```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "hits": [],
  "suggestions": {
    "did_you_mean": ["git commit", "git comment"],
    "similar_terms": ["commit", "git"],
    "try_broader": ["git"],
    "popular_queries": ["git push", "git merge"]
  }
}
```

## Design Decisions

### When to Suggest
- Always when count=0
- Optionally when count < threshold (sparse results)
- Can be disabled with `--no-suggestions` for performance

### Suggestion Types
1. **did_you_mean**: Levenshtein-based typo corrections
2. **similar_terms**: Terms that appear in the index that are similar
3. **try_broader**: Subsets of the query to try
4. **popular_queries**: Common queries in similar domains (optional)

### Implementation Complexity
Requires:
- Index term enumeration (for did_you_mean)
- Edit distance calculation
- Query history tracking (for popular_queries, optional)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zero-result searches include `suggestions` object
- [ ] `did_you_mean` provides typo corrections
- [ ] `similar_terms` finds related indexed terms
- [ ] `try_broader` suggests query simplifications
- [ ] `--no-suggestions` disables for performance
- [ ] Suggestions are ranked by relevance

## Effort Estimate
Medium-High - 4-6 hours. Requires index term access and string similarity logic.

## Future Enhancement
Could integrate with LLM for semantic suggestions, but that's a separate feature.

title: ibuuh.10.12: e2e_large_dataset timeout-with-diagnostic wrapper for subprocess hangs
description: Sub-bead of coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.10 (test infrastructure). e2e_large_dataset.rs invokes cass as a subprocess via assert_cmd's .assert().success() which blocks forever if cass hangs. When pane 5 surfaced a hang in this suite, the signal was a silent stall — no diagnostic dump, no indication of what phase was stuck. This bead adds tests/util/timeout.rs::spawn_with_timeout_or_diag that wraps std::process::Command, polls try_wait with a bounded deadline, and on timeout dumps structured diagnostics (label, data_dir file listing, child PID, elapsed time, stderr-so-far) before killing the child and panicking. Includes a self-validation test that proves the wrapper fires on an intentionally-hung  command. Retrofit of the 16 e2e_large_dataset tests to use the wrapper is deferred to a follow-up bead — this bead lands the infra primitive.
close_reason: Shipped tests/util/timeout.rs with spawn_with_timeout_or_diag helper + 4 self-tests. Helper spawns std::process::Command, polls try_wait with a bounded deadline, on timeout kills the child + drains stdout/stderr tails + emits structured diag dump (label, pid, elapsed, data_dir listing, stream tails) + panics. Bug found DURING authoring (captured in source comment): shell-wrapped hang probes (/bin/sh -c 'sleep 30') orphan the inner sleep on SIGKILL and block drain_pipe_tail's read_to_end for the full 30s. Switched to direct /bin/sleep and the timeout test now runs in 0.30s. Also reordered kill-before-drain so read_to_end hits EOF once the child's write-end of the pipe closes. Retrofit of the 16 e2e_large_dataset tests to use the wrapper is deferred — infra primitive is now available for follow-up. Verified: cargo test --test e2e_large_dataset util::timeout::tests:: passes 4/4 in 0.30s on /data/rch_target_cass_p3.

title: [MEDIUM] reality-check: README semantic model-install claims contradict reality
description:
## Claim (README.md:203)
> **Manual install**: Place model files under your data directory (see below); cass will not auto-download.

## Reality (README.md:2453-2455 and actual CLI help)
\`cass models install\` DOES auto-download the model (~90 MB) from Hugging Face:

\`\`\`
\$ cass models install --help
Download and install the semantic search model
  --mirror <MIRROR>      Custom HTTP(S) mirror base URL for downloading
  --from-file <FROM_FILE> Install from local model directory (for air-gapped environments)
  -y, --yes              Skip confirmation prompt
\`\`\`

README line 2454 also describes the download path explicitly: \`cass models install # → Downloads from Hugging Face, verifies checksum\`.

Line 203 and line 2454 directly contradict each other.

## Secondary claim on same page
\`\`\`
cass models status --json
# → { \"installed\": true, \"model\": \"all-MiniLM-L6-v2\", \"size_bytes\": 91234567 }
\`\`\`

But the actual output has a completely different schema:
\`\`\`json
{
  \"model_id\": \"all-minilm-l6-v2\",
  \"model_dir\": \"...\",
  \"installed\": false,
  \"state\": \"not_acquired\",
  \"state_detail\": \"...\",
  \"next_step\": \"...\",
  \"lexical_fail_open\": true,
  \"revision\": \"c9745ed1...\",
  \"license\": \"Apache-2.0\",
  \"total_size_bytes\": 90872535,
  \"installed_size_bytes\": 0,
  \"observed_file_bytes\": 0,
  \"policy_source\": \"semantic_policy\",
  \"cache_lifecycle\": {...},
  \"files\": [...]
}
\`\`\`

No field named \`model\` or \`size_bytes\`. Users copy-pasting the example JSON shape for their automation will break.

## Minimal repro
\`\`\`bash
# Contradiction 1:
grep -n 'not auto-download\|downloads ~90MB' README.md
# Output shows lines 203 (\"not auto-download\") and 2454 (\"downloads ~90MB\")

# Contradiction 2:
cass models status --json | jq 'keys'
# Output does NOT include \"model\" or \"size_bytes\"; includes \"model_id\", \"total_size_bytes\", etc.
\`\`\`

## Suggested fix
Rewrite README §201-210 to match reality:

\`\`\`markdown
### 🧠 Optional Semantic Search (Local, No Network at Query Time)
- **Opt-in install**: \`cass models install\` downloads the MiniLM model (~90 MB) from Hugging Face once. At query time no network is used.
- **Air-gapped install**: \`cass models install --from-file <dir>\` accepts a pre-downloaded model directory.
- **Required files** (all must be present after install; \`cass models verify\` checks):

title: Bump fsqlite pin to revert pass-20 orphan-fk query-shape workaround
description:
Pass-20 (cass commit 1f20bd57, 'fix(storage): avoid fragile frankensqlite query shapes') worked around a correlated NOT EXISTS planner bug in frankensqlite c8ce64fd (cass's currently pinned revision). The workaround rewrites the orphan-FK probe in src/storage/sqlite.rs (ORPHAN_DIRECT_CHILD_TABLES + ORPHAN_MESSAGE_DEPENDENT_TABLES) from the natural correlated form to a non-correlated NOT IN form, and also rewrites delete_rows_by_i64_chunks from a chunked IN(?,?,?...) DELETE into a per-id loop.

## Status of the underlying bug

- Bug A (correlated NOT EXISTS returning false-positive orphans): REAL, confirmed reproducible on fsqlite c8ce64fd. Fixed in fsqlite HEAD.
- Bug B (dynamic IN(?,?,?...) DELETE row-count mismatch): NOT a real fsqlite bug — the chunked-IN DELETE shape worked correctly even on c8ce64fd. The per-id loop in delete_rows_by_i64_chunks was defensive over-engineering, but harmless.

## Evidence

Regression tests pinned in fsqlite at /data/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite/tests/cass_orphan_fk_repros.rs (commit 4bbac9b2 on fsqlite main). They reproduce both shapes against the cass orphan-cleanup schema replica. On HEAD they pass. On c8ce64fd, the three correlated_not_exists_* tests fail with 'left: [1..N], right: []' (the planner is dropping the correlation predicate and returning every metric row).

Verified locally by:
1. Reverting cass commit 1f20bd57 in a worktree.
2. Re-running cargo test --lib cleanup_orphan_fk_rows against cass's pinned fsqlite c8ce64fd: both tests fail (left=518, right=259) and (left=0, right=1).
3. Same revert, but with the [patch] override in cass Cargo.toml pointing at local fsqlite HEAD: both tests pass.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Bump fsqlite pin in Cargo.toml from c8ce64fd to a revision >= the commit that fixes the correlated NOT EXISTS planner bug. The fix is somewhere in the ~1700 commits between c8ce64fd and HEAD; bisecting fsqlite to find the exact fix commit is optional — picking a recent stable rev is fine.
2. Revert the SQL-shape changes in commit 1f20bd57:
   - Restore ORPHAN_DIRECT_CHILD_TABLES.orphan_id_sql to the correlated NOT EXISTS form.
   - Restore delete_rows_by_i64_chunks to the chunked IN(?,?,?...) shape (the per-id loop is the workaround for the non-bug; reverting is fine but optional).
   - Restore the sql_placeholders helper.
3. Re-run cargo test --lib cleanup_orphan_fk_rows and confirm both tests pass.
4. Also re-run the pages-cluster fixes (src/pages/size.rs SizeEstimate::from_database, src/pages/summary.rs get_date_histogram) — those were not workarounds for fsqlite bugs but for query-planner cosmetics, evaluate whether they still need to stand.
5. Update sibling-dependency contract table in README.md / AGENTS.md with the new pin and rev hash.

## References

- pass-20 commit: 1f20bd57 (fix(storage): avoid fragile frankensqlite query shapes)
- fsqlite regression test: crates/fsqlite/tests/cass_orphan_fk_repros.rs (commit 4bbac9b2)
- downstream cass tests: storage::sqlite::tests::cleanup_orphan_fk_rows_{removes_orphans_and_is_noop_on_clean_db, handles_more_than_one_delete_chunk}

title: GH#426: resumable per-source ingest ledger for interrupted incremental indexing
description: Committed conversations survive interruption, but source scan progress does not: retries re-read and re-parse the full modified corpus, active sessions can freeze connector watermarks, and the legacy non-streaming timer can advance before persistence. Implement a per-source observation ledger and graceful batch-boundary termination without timestamp shortcuts that can silently skip unpersisted files.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger identity binds connector, provenance/source id, normalized source path, observed size, and observed mtime; a source is skippable only when that exact observation was committed atomically with every canonical conversation derived from it. Files changed during parse, active/skipped files, parse failures, empty/multi-conversation sources, configured remote roots, and path exclusions never receive a false completed observation. Streaming and non-streaming modes remove unsafe mid-ingest watermark advancement. SIGTERM/SIGINT or a bounded-run control stops after an in-flight batch, persists safe ledger/watermark progress, performs a bounded checkpoint, releases index-run.lock, and exits nonzero. Focused kill/resume tests prove the second run stats all sources but parses only the remainder, produces no missing/duplicate conversations or lexical gap, and does not grow the rescan window while another session stays active.

What the seam provides: Connector::supports_source_boundaries() + scan_with_source_boundaries(ctx, &mut SourceScanHooks, on_conversation). SourceScanHooks carries (a) should_scan_source(&DiscoveredSourceFile)->bool — cheap pre-parse skip whose identity (provider slug, scan root, origin, canonical path, size, mtime) matches discover_source_files() exactly, observed BEFORE parsing; (b) on_source_complete(&SourceCompletion) — fired ONLY after every conversation derived from that source was delivered; never on parse failure, callback failure/cancellation, zero conversations, or when the source changed during parse (fs_metadata_changed re-stat guard). SourceCompletion.required_sidecars names the reconstruction set (e.g. Shelley WAL) whose fingerprints authorize a future skip. Default impl is a truthful no-boundary fallback (delegates to scan_with_callback, never invokes hooks) so cass keeps conservative behavior per connector.

Implemented so far: claude_code (per-file) and shelley (many-conversations-per-database — the case that made naive per-conversation completion unsafe). Conformance tests: completion-after-all-conversations ordering, cancellation-between-conversations withholds completion, skip predicate suppresses parse+completion, ledger-driven resume parses nothing on unchanged sources, identity equality with discovery. title: JUnit XML Test Reports for CI Integration
description:
# JUnit XML Test Reports for CI Integration

## What
Generate JUnit XML test reports for CI dashboards (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.)
that provide:
- Per-test pass/fail status
- Timing information
- Failure details with stack traces
- Test suite grouping

## Why
CI systems need structured test output to:
- Display test results in PR checks
- Track test flakiness over time
- Send notifications on failures
- Generate trend reports

## Technical Design

### Using cargo-nextest
`cargo-nextest` is a modern test runner that provides JUnit XML output natively.

```bash
# Install
cargo install cargo-nextest

# Run tests with JUnit output
cargo nextest run --profile ci
```

### Nextest Configuration
```toml
# .config/nextest.toml

[profile.default]
# Default profile for local development
fail-fast = true
retries = 0

[profile.ci]
# CI profile with JUnit output
fail-fast = false
retries = 2
slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 2 }

[profile.ci.junit]
path = "target/nextest/ci/junit.xml"
report-time = true

# Store failure output
store-success-output = false
store-failure-output = true
```

### GitHub Actions Integration
```yaml
# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        
      - name: Install nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
        
      - name: Run tests
        run: cargo nextest run --profile ci
        
      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: target/nextest/ci/junit.xml
          
      - name: Test Report
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: Cargo Tests
          path: target/nextest/ci/junit.xml
          reporter: java-junit
```

### Test Summary Script
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/test-summary.sh
# Parse JUnit XML and print summary

JUNIT_FILE=${1:-"target/nextest/ci/junit.xml"}

if [[ \! -f "$JUNIT_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "JUnit file not found: $JUNIT_FILE"
    exit 1
fi

# Extract counts using xmlstarlet
tests=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "//testsuite/@tests" "$JUNIT_FILE" 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1}END{print s}')
failures=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "//testsuite/@failures" "$JUNIT_FILE" 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1}END{print s}')
errors=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "//testsuite/@errors" "$JUNIT_FILE" 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1}END{print s}')
time=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "//testsuite/@time" "$JUNIT_FILE" 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1}END{printf "%.2f", s}')

echo "==============================================="
echo "                TEST SUMMARY                   "
echo "==============================================="
echo "Total tests:  $tests"
echo "Passed:       $((tests - failures - errors))"
echo "Failed:       $failures"
echo "Errors:       $errors"
echo "Time:         ${time}s"
echo "==============================================="

if [[ $failures -gt 0 ]] || [[ $errors -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo ""
    echo "FAILED TESTS:"
    xmlstarlet sel -t -m "//testcase[failure|error]" -v "@name" -n "$JUNIT_FILE"
    exit 1
fi

echo "✓ All tests passed\!"
```

### Nextest Filter Configuration
```toml
# .config/nextest.toml (continued)

[test-groups]
# Group tests for reporting
integration = { max-threads = 1, slow-timeout = { period = "120s" } }
unit = { max-threads = "num-cpus" }

[[profile.ci.overrides]]
filter = "test(e2e_)"
test-group = "integration"

[[profile.ci.overrides]]
filter = "not test(e2e_)"
test-group = "unit"
```

### Alternative: cargo2junit
For existing cargo test output:
```bash
# Install
cargo install cargo2junit

# Use with cargo test
cargo test -- -Z unstable-options --format json 2>&1 | cargo2junit > junit.xml
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cargo-nextest installed and configured
- [ ] JUnit XML generated for all test runs
- [ ] GitHub Actions displays test results
- [ ] Failed tests show in PR checks
- [ ] Test timing tracked
- [ ] Retry flaky tests (2 retries)
- [ ] scripts/test-summary.sh parses JUnit

## Dependencies
- cargo-nextest
- xmlstarlet (for summary script)
- dorny/test-reporter GitHub Action

## Considerations
- nextest is faster than cargo test (parallel execution)
- JUnit XML is industry standard, works everywhere
- Test groups help separate unit from integration
- Retry mechanism reduces flakiness impact

title: [Task] Opt 2.4: Benchmark SIMD dot product (expect 2-4x speedup)
description:
# Task: Benchmark SIMD Dot Product

## Objective

Measure the performance improvement from explicit SIMD dot product and document results.

## Benchmark Protocol

### 1. Baseline (Post-F16 Pre-Convert, SIMD Disabled)
```bash
export CASS_SIMD_DOT=0
cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- vector_index_search_50k --save-baseline simd_disabled
```

### 2. With SIMD Enabled
```bash
unset CASS_SIMD_DOT
cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- vector_index_search_50k --save-baseline simd_enabled
```

### 3. Compare Results
```bash
critcmp simd_disabled simd_enabled
```

## Expected Results

| Metric | Before (post-Opt1) | After SIMD | Change |
|--------|-------------------|------------|--------|
| `vector_index_search_50k` | ~30 ms | 10-15 ms | -50% to -66% |

The 2-4x speedup comes from:
- Processing 8 floats per instruction (AVX2)
- Better cache utilization
- Reduced instruction count

## Micro-Benchmark: Isolated Dot Product

Add a focused benchmark for just the dot product function:
```rust
// In benches/runtime_perf.rs
fn bench_dot_product(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let a: Vec<f32> = (0..384).map(|i| i as f32 * 0.001).collect();
    let b: Vec<f32> = (0..384).map(|i| i as f32 * 0.002).collect();
    
    c.bench_function("dot_product_scalar", |bencher| {
        bencher.iter(|| dot_product_scalar(black_box(&a), black_box(&b)))
    });
    
    c.bench_function("dot_product_simd", |bencher| {
        bencher.iter(|| dot_product_simd(black_box(&a), black_box(&b)))
    });
}
```

## Assembly Verification

Confirm SIMD instructions are being used:
```bash
cargo asm coding_agent_search::search::vector_index::dot_product_simd | grep -E "vmulps|vaddps|vfmadd"
```

## Documentation Updates

After benchmarking, update:
1. PLAN_FOR_ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS_ROUND_1__OPUS.md with actual results
2. Code comments documenting expected performance
3. Consider adding benchmark results to README.md

## Validation Checklist

- [ ] Baseline measured (SIMD disabled)
- [ ] SIMD enabled measured
- [ ] critcmp comparison shows 2-4x improvement
- [ ] Micro-benchmark confirms isolated speedup
- [ ] Assembly shows SIMD instructions
- [ ] Documentation updated

## Dependencies

- Requires completion of Opt 2.3 (tests passing)

title: [Task] Special Character Query Tests
description:
## Task: Special Character Query Tests

Test query parsing with special characters that could cause issues.

### Test Cases
- [ ] **Unbalanced quotes** - `"hello world` (no closing quote)
- [ ] **Escaped quotes** - `\"test\"` and `"test \"inner\" test"`
- [ ] **Backslash sequences** - `C:\Users\test`, `\\server\share`
- [ ] **Regex metacharacters** - `foo.*bar`, `[a-z]+`, `^start$`
- [ ] **SQL injection patterns** - `'OR 1=1--`, `; DROP TABLE`
- [ ] **Shell injection patterns** - `$(cmd)`, `` `cmd` ``, `| rm -rf`
- [ ] **Null bytes** - `test\x00hidden`
- [ ] **Control characters** - `\n\r\t` in query
- [ ] **HTML/XML entities** - `<script>`, `<`
- [ ] **URL encoding** - `%20`, `%2F`, `%00`

### Implementation
```rust
#[test]
fn unbalanced_quotes_handled_gracefully() {
    // Should not panic, should have defined behavior
    let q = QueryParser::parse(r#""hello world"#);
    assert\!(q.terms.len() >= 1, "unbalanced quote should still parse");
}

#[test]
fn sql_injection_treated_as_literal() {
    let q = QueryParser::parse("'OR 1=1--");
    // Verify it's treated as literal search, not executed
    assert\!(q.terms.iter().all(|t| \!t.text.contains(";")));
}
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 10 special character cases tested
- [ ] No panics on any input
- [ ] Injection patterns treated as literal text
- [ ] Tests pass: `cargo test search::query::tests::special_char`

### Verification
```bash
cargo test search::query::tests --test-threads=1 -- special --nocapture
```

title: [MEDIUM] audit: robot-docs commands + --robot-help advertise only ~10/31 actual subcommands
description:
cass --help enumerates 31 top-level subcommands (analytics, api-version, capabilities, completions, context, daemon, diag, doctor, expand, export, export-html, health, help, import, index, introspect, man, models, pages, resume, robot-docs, search, sessions, sources, state, stats, status, timeline, tui, view).

cass robot-docs commands (src/lib.rs:6893 RobotTopic::Commands) hardcodes only 10 entries: search, stats, status, diag, sessions, view, index, tui, capabilities, robot-docs. cass --robot-help is worse (5 subcommands surfaced).

Agents relying on robot-docs commands / --robot-help as the authoritative enumeration of the CLI surface (the documented pattern — README line 1017 directs agents at robot-docs <topic> for machine-readable docs) silently miss ~20 subcommands:

- Diagnostic JSON surfaces: health, doctor, introspect, api-version
- Model management: models (install / status / verify / check-update)
- Static export: pages, export-html, export
- Session navigation: expand, resume, timeline, context
- Remote sync: sources (list / sync / setup)
- Analytics: analytics (tokens / tools / models / rebuild / validate)
- Import path: import, completions, man

Consequence: an agent discovering cass via robot-docs commands cannot find the truth surfaces for health/doctor/models, and has no way to know expand/resume/timeline exist. Agents silently use less of the API than cass intends.

Fix direction: extend RobotTopic::Commands in src/lib.rs:6893 with a one-liner per missing subcommand (name + --json suffix where applicable + 1-line summary). Keep the existing search/index expansions; just fill in the gaps. Similar treatment for --robot-help enumeration.

Severity MEDIUM because it does not BREAK any user workflow, but it hides a large fraction of the advertised surface from the primary automation-discovery path.

title: Identify and Fill Unit Test Coverage Gaps
Add doctor failure-context capture and one-command reproduce tooling
description:
Background: mcp_agent_mail_rust has flake-triage and failure-context tooling that captures enough detail to reproduce failures instead of leaving operators with a vague failing log. Cass doctor needs that because repair, reconstruct, backup, and cleanup failures can be environment-sensitive: locks, disk pressure, platform rename semantics, permissions, fixture seeds, and source-pruning state all matter.

Problem: the existing cass doctor plan has e2e scripts and artifact capture, but it also needs a compact failure_context artifact and a one-command repro path. Without that, future failures in doctor e2e or user support cases will require manual archaeology through logs and temp dirs.

Scope: when a doctor e2e scenario, repair run, or verification phase fails, write a failure_context.json artifact with command, argv, env allowlist, cass version, git revision when available, platform, temp/data dir paths, fixture seed, scenario id, operation id, active locks, selected authority, rejected authorities, plan fingerprint, failed phase, failed check, recent operation events, stdout/stderr paths, receipt path, and artifact manifest path. The repro command must avoid destructive behavior by default and should target the captured fixture or copied candidate, not the users live archive unless the operator explicitly points it there. Include a scrubbed shell-safe repro script or command JSON, not only prose.

Acceptance criteria: e2e runner artifacts always include failure_context.json on failure. The artifact is redacted by default and has a schema/golden. Unit tests cover redaction, stable ordering, missing optional fields, command quoting, safe repro command construction, refusal to target live archives by default, and attachment to support bundles. E2E tests intentionally fail a post-repair probe and a lock-contention scenario, then prove the failure context points at the fixture copy, includes enough event-log context, and excludes raw session text. Robot-docs explain how agents should attach the failure context to bug reports.

Implementation note: this complements, not replaces, operation receipts. Receipts describe what doctor did; failure_context describes how to reproduce and debug the failure safely.

Verified focused e2e/unit/golden coverage plus cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked --all-targets, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, and git diff --check for touched files. The downstream scrubbed support-bundle packaging work remains in coding_agent_session_search-wjjqg, which is now unblocked by the failure_context artifact contract.

title: [Task] Opt 8.1: Design streaming indexing architecture
description:
# Task: Design Streaming Indexing Architecture

## Objective

Before implementing streaming backpressure, design the architecture and address ordering concerns.

## From PLAN Section 8.8

**Current**: Collect all `pending_batches` across connectors before ingesting
**Proposed**: Stream per-connector with bounded channel to single ingest worker

**Risk**: Ordering/tie-breaking could change if ingestion becomes interleaved differently.

## Architecture Design

```
┌───────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐
│ Claude Conn.  │────▶│               │     │               │
├───────────────┤     │   Bounded     │────▶│   Ingest      │
│ Cursor Conn.  │────▶│   Channel     │     │   Worker      │
├───────────────┤     │   (N=100)     │     │               │
│ Gemini Conn.  │────▶│               │     │               │
└───────────────┘     └───────────────┘     └───────────────┘
     Producers             Buffer              Consumer
```

## Design Decisions Required

### 1. Channel Capacity
- What buffer size? (PLAN suggests N=100)
- Too small: Producers block frequently
- Too large: Defeats backpressure purpose

### 2. Ordering Semantics
- Do we guarantee ordering within a connector?
- Do we guarantee ordering across connectors?
- How does interleaving affect search results?

### 3. Error Handling
- What if ingest worker fails mid-batch?
- How to recover from partial indexing?
- Transaction boundaries?

### 4. Progress Reporting
- How to show progress with async ingestion?
- Accurate counts during streaming?

### 5. Cancellation
- Ctrl-C during indexing?
- Clean shutdown without corruption?

## Expected Memory Impact

From PLAN:
- Current peak RSS: 295 MB
- Target: ~100-150 MB (50% reduction)

## Isomorphism Consideration (Relaxed)

From PLAN:
> This optimization has **weaker** guarantees than others:
> - Same **set** of indexed content
> - Potentially different **ordering** of inserts
> - Same **search results** (hit set, not necessarily order for tied scores)

Property to preserve:
```
∀ query: set(search(query).hits.message_id) ≡ set(search_streaming(query).hits.message_id)
```

Note: This is **set equality**, not sequence equality.

## Deliverables

1. Architecture diagram
2. Decision document for each design question
3. Risk assessment
4. Implementation plan with phases
5. Rollback strategy

## Complexity Warning

From PLAN:
> This is rated **HIGH effort** because:
> 1. Significant architectural change to indexing flow
> 2. Need to handle errors in worker thread
> 3. Progress reporting becomes async
> 4. Cancellation handling
> 5. Testing concurrent code

## Validation

Design is complete when:
- [ ] Architecture diagram finalized
- [ ] All design decisions documented
- [ ] Ordering semantics clearly defined
- [ ] Error handling strategy defined
- [ ] Risk assessment complete

title: canonical FTS dry-run is O(shadow) content-faulting on large partial shadows (GH #345)
description:
GH #345: canonical FTS dry-run (`doctor --rebuild-canonical-fts --dry-run`) is expensive (>22 min, ~18 GiB RSS, ~110 GiB logical reads) on a large partial shadow (~1.4M-row shadow in a 2M-message / 22 GB archive).

## Root cause (confirmed)
`inspect_search_fallback_fts_parity` (src/storage/sqlite.rs:11144) computes the exact canonical/FTS intersection via `count_fts_indexed_canonical_intersection` (:11116), which runs `FTS_INDEXED_CANONICAL_INTERSECTION_SQL` (:1153): `SELECT m.conversation_id FROM fts_messages_docsize f INNER JOIN messages m ON m.id = f.id`. This point-seeks the `messages` rowid b-tree once per shadow row; because `messages` is `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` with `content/extra_json/extra_bin` on the SAME leaf pages, every seek faults a full message-content leaf (+overflow). O(shadow) random content reads = the reported RSS/IO.

The classifier only needs `(has_missing, has_excess)` + the two cheap counts (indexable via the autoindex, indexed via docsize), not the exact intersection magnitude.

## Why the obvious fix does NOT work (empirically verified)
The natural index-only fix — load the indexable message-id set from the `(conversation_id, idx)` autoindex (which carries the rowid) and stream `fts_messages_docsize` ids testing membership — was implemented and its query plan asserted. **frankensqlite table-scans `messages` for `SELECT id FROM messages INDEXED BY sqlite_autoindex_messages_1 WHERE conversation_id IN (...)`** (EXPLAIN shows `OpenRead <messages>` + `Column 1`, not an index-only rowid projection), so it still faults content — AND a full scan regresses the small-partial-shadow case the current code deliberately optimizes (39k point-seeks vs a 2M-row scan). Reverted; not shipped.

## The real fix requires one of (a design decision):
1. **frankensqlite: index-only rowid projection** — support reading the rowid from the `(conversation_id, idx)` autoindex without a table seek (covering read / IdxRowid), so the indexable id-set can be loaded content-free. Then the index-only set-membership intersection works. This is the clean fix but is a frankensqlite planner enhancement.
2. **cass: counts-only / capped dry-run classification** — have the DRY-RUN report the three cheap counts + a "needs apply for exact parity" status, and cap or defer the exact intersection scan (bound it to the first N shadow rows with short-circuit on divergence). The APPLY (--yes) keeps the exact check. Trades dry-run precision (can't always distinguish Partial from Divergent cheaply) for bounded cost; touches the doctor dry-run envelope contract + goldens.

Both are real; neither is a clean drop-in. Recommend (1) bundled with the other frankensqlite FTS work (the #369 multi-leaf branch), or (2) as a deliberate doctor-dry-run redesign.

title: base-schema migration OOMs on legacy internal-content fts_messages; needs frankensqlite bounded WITHOUT-ROWID teardown (GH #349)
description:
GH #349: on a legacy (0.2.0) archive holding a large *internal-content* FTS5 `fts_messages` (WITHOUT ROWID shadow tables, multi-GB), `cass index --full` and `cass doctor` OOM.

## Root cause (confirmed)
`transition_from_meta_version` backfills `_schema_migrations` only through v13 for meta versions 10-12 (src/storage/sqlite.rs:~5865), so `MIGRATION_V14` = `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS fts_messages` (src/storage/sqlite.rs:~3593) runs on the existing archive. Executing that DROP invokes frankensqlite's FTS5 vtable teardown, which must hydrate the populated WITHOUT ROWID shadow tables (`fts_messages_data/_content/_docsize/_config/_idx`) into the compat MemDatabase — a multi-GB unbounded load that OOMs. `open()` deliberately uses the bounded `open_existing_schema_only` lane so ordinary opens stay pager-backed, but `run_migrations()` runs right after and the DROP forces the hydration that lane avoids.

Doctor's second OOM path: `open_readonly` (src/storage/sqlite.rs:4404) uses the generic `open_franken_with_flags(..., READ_ONLY)` lane — NOT the bounded `open_existing_schema_only` — so `cass doctor check` hydrates the whole DB (incl. the FTS shadow) and OOMs before it can diagnose.

## Why it's frankensqlite-blocked (same class as #368 defect 3)
frankensqlite explicitly does not support loading/reloading a populated WITHOUT ROWID FTS shadow: the in-tree classifier `error_message_indicates_populated_fts_shadow_without_rowid_reload` (src/storage/sqlite.rs:4033) matches "loading populated WITHOUT ROWID table fts_messages_... is not yet supported". So the DROP (and any per-row DELETE / individual backing-table DROP) either OOMs hydrating or errors "not yet supported" — you cannot bounded-tear-down the legacy shadow from cass alone. Removing it the way a stock sqlite would (writable_schema surgery on sqlite_master) is also unavailable: frankensqlite does not support `PRAGMA writable_schema` writes (AGENTS.md; storage/sqlite.rs:18662-65). Same underlying gap as #368 d3.

## Fix requires frankensqlite support (the real fix)
A bounded WITHOUT-ROWID teardown primitive: drop/empty a populated WITHOUT ROWID FTS shadow (or its backing tables) on the pager-backed lane WITHOUT hydrating it into MemDatabase — mirroring the deferred-FTS-validation open needed for #368 d3. Then `MIGRATION_V14`'s DROP (and `doctor --rebuild-canonical-fts`) can migrate/repair legacy internal-content archives.

## cass-side mitigations (possible follow-ups, each partial)
1. **Bounded doctor open:** add a bounded READ-ONLY frankensqlite lane (schema-only, pager-backed) and route `cass doctor check`'s `open_readonly` through it so doctor can at least DIAGNOSE the archive (report "legacy internal-content fts_messages present; needs migration") instead of OOMing. Blocked on a bounded read-only lane (open_existing_schema_only is a writable lane; 36 open_readonly callers make a global switch risky).
2. **Graceful migration error:** wrap `run_migrations()` so a populated-WITHOUT-ROWID / OOM failure of the base migration becomes a CLEAR, actionable error (this frankensqlite version cannot migrate a legacy internal-content fts_messages; recover a fresh native archive via `cass doctor --recover-from-archive <DIR>`) instead of a bare OOM exit 5. Diagnostic-only; does not complete the migration.

Both mitigations improve the operator experience but do not fix the migration; that needs the frankensqlite bounded WITHOUT-ROWID teardown. Recommend bundling with the ongoing frankensqlite FTS engine work (the #369 multi-leaf branch / #368 d3).
