title: Build a phase-exact stale-refresh evidence ledger, benchmark corpus set, and equivalence baseline
description:
BACKGROUND:
Performance work on stale refresh should start from measured truth, not intuition. The code already separates scan and index timing in places, but we still lack one stable evidence ledger that breaks stale refresh into comparable phases and captures correctness artifacts alongside timing data.

GOAL:
Create the phase-exact baseline, benchmark corpus set, and artifact ledger that the rest of this track will use as its proof framework.

SCOPE:
- Define one canonical stale-refresh phase model covering scan, canonical persist, lexical rebuild, publish, analytics, semantic, and recovery overhead.
- Emit stable machine-readable timings and counters for those phases.
- Add representative corpus families, including duplicate-heavy and pathological cases.
- Preserve equivalence artifacts such as document counts, search-hit digests, manifest fingerprints, and memory/high-water marks.

DONE WHEN:
Later beads can point to a reproducible baseline and answer what changed, how much, and whether correctness was preserved.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- One stable stale-refresh phase taxonomy exists and is emitted in machine-readable form with timings and work counters for scan, canonical persist, lexical build, publish, analytics, semantic, and recovery or retry overhead.
- The baseline ledger also captures explicit user-facing readiness milestones such as time-to-search-ready, time-to-current-lexical-generation, and time-to-full-refresh-settled so later optimizations can be judged against operator experience instead of internal timing alone.
- The benchmark corpus set includes small, large, duplicate-heavy, huge-message, and pathological-ordering cases, with deterministic fixture identifiers and preserved artifact directories.
- At least one robot or E2E script reproduces the baseline ledger end-to-end and emits detailed logs, benchmark tables, digests, manifests, and readiness milestones that later beads can compare against.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION POLICY:
- This bead must land with bead-local proof, not only final-epic proof.
- Required by default: targeted unit tests for new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI or robot E2E scenario when the behavior is user-visible, multi-step, or crash-sensitive.

title: Eliminate duplicate lexical work so each refresh mode performs exactly one authoritative lexical population pass
description:
BACKGROUND:
A full or stale refresh should not pay for lexical population twice. The current path can ingest canonical SQLite state and then later perform an authoritative lexical rebuild from the same database, which turns large refreshes into needless duplicate work.

GOAL:
Guarantee that each refresh mode performs exactly one authoritative lexical population strategy.

SCOPE:
- Separate canonical ingestion from authoritative lexical generation.
- Make full and stale rebuild modes defer inline lexical writes when a later authoritative rebuild is planned.
- Preserve cheap incremental lexical updates for watch and small incremental ingest paths.
- Make the chosen lexical strategy explicit in state and progress output.

DONE WHEN:
Full or stale refreshes pay for one lexical population pass, not two, while incremental paths stay fast and correct.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Full and stale refresh modes record exactly one authoritative lexical population strategy end-to-end, with explicit strategy and reason in logs or progress output.
- Watch, watch-once, import, and other incremental paths preserve cheap incremental maintenance where safe instead of being forced through full rebuild behavior.
- Unit, integration, and robot or E2E scenarios cover full refresh, stale refresh, historical salvage, and incremental ingest so duplicate lexical work cannot silently return.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION POLICY:
- This bead must land with bead-local proof, not only final-epic proof.
- Required by default: targeted unit tests for new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI or robot E2E scenario when the behavior is user-visible, multi-step, or crash-sensitive.
- Preserve rich structured timestamped logs, strategy or fallback reasons, and artifact snapshots relevant to the bead: manifests, benchmark tables, digests, checkpoints, crash-resume traces, controller decisions, or cache evidence.

title: Replace OFFSET-based lexical rebuild traversal with keyset checkpoints and monotone progress
description:
BACKGROUND:
OFFSET-based traversal is structurally wrong for large rebuilds. It repeatedly pays skip costs, makes progress ordinal instead of data-aware, and scales poorly as the canonical corpus grows.

GOAL:
Replace OFFSET-based lexical rebuild traversal with keyset traversal and monotone checkpoints anchored to stable identifiers.

SCOPE:
- Move lexical rebuild enumeration from LIMIT/OFFSET to WHERE id > last_seen_id ORDER BY id LIMIT N.
- Change rebuild checkpoints from ordinal offsets to stable high-water identifiers plus any supporting fingerprint needed for safe resume.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and resumability.

DONE WHEN:
The rebuild cursor is based on stable database identity rather than skipped-row counts, and large rebuilds no longer pay OFFSET amplification.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The hot lexical rebuild path no longer uses OFFSET traversal and instead persists monotone high-water checkpoints tied to stable corpus identity.
- Resume behavior remains correct across interruption, restart, and legacy checkpoint migration or discard, with explicit logs when checkpoints are upgraded or invalidated.
- Tests cover large corpora, sparse or holey identifier ranges, interrupted rebuilds, and progress reporting so correctness does not depend on ordinal row counts.
notes:

- This bead must land with bead-local proof, not only final-epic proof.

title: Repair frankensqlite-backed batched lexical message fetches and remove the N+1 rebuild tax
description:
BACKGROUND:
The current lexical rebuild path fetches messages one conversation at a time because the batched ordered path previously triggered pathological heap behavior in frankensqlite. That keeps an N+1 tax in the hottest rebuild stage.

GOAL:

SCOPE:

- Provide a cass-usable API that returns grouped, ordered messages for a page of conversation IDs.
- Add bounded-memory safeguards and regression tests for large-message and duplicate-heavy corpora.

DONE WHEN:
Cass can fetch messages for a page of conversations in one bounded batched operation and no longer needs per-conversation lexical rebuild queries as the primary hot path.

title: Eliminate the single-core "preparing" plateau by making authoritative rebuild prep fully streaming and phase-explicit

GOAL:
Remove any remaining whole-corpus or long serial prep work that keeps the authoritative rebuild in a single-core plateau before useful many-core work can begin.

SCOPE:
- Break the current broad "preparing" stage into explicit subphases so future profiles say exactly where time is going.
- Audit every pre-writer step for hidden whole-corpus scans, global map builds, or other batch work that can be turned into streaming or lazy evaluation.
- Ensure the rebuild can begin feeding downstream workers after a small bounded startup slice rather than after global preparation completes.
- Keep monotone progress, restart recovery, and deterministic ordering intact while the prep path becomes incrementally productive.

DONE WHEN:
A representative rebuild reaches the first sustained worker-driven phase quickly, the long single-core plateau is gone or materially reduced, and logs make any remaining startup cost phase-exact instead of opaque.

DESIGN / JUSTIFICATION:
- The point is not merely to rename phases; it is to force the code to justify every serial precondition before parallel work can begin.
- Prefer streaming lookups, incremental cache warmup, and on-demand derivation over big up-front tables unless a global precompute has proven positive ROI and bounded cost.
- Preserve authoritative SQLite-driven semantics: this bead must not regress toward rescanning raw connector sources just to look busy on more cores.

title: Keep lexical index automatically current after SQLite ingest, watch, and import flows
description:
BACKGROUND:
Self-healing a missing lexical index is necessary but not sufficient. cass also needs a durable answer to the routine case where SQLite changes because of watch mode, watch-once, salvage, import, or normal indexing activity. The mandatory lexical derivative must stay synchronized with the SQLite source of truth without depending on manual operator refreshes.

GOAL:
Make lexical maintenance automatic after SQLite mutations so the ordinary search path remains correct with minimal or no manual indexing intervention.

SCOPE:
- Audit every code path that mutates the canonical SQLite corpus: full index, watch startup, steady-state watch, watch-once recovery, historical salvage, imports, source sync, and any direct repair pipelines.
- Ensure each path either updates the lexical derivative incrementally or records durable backlog/work that will be consumed automatically.
- Reuse the state contract and repair machinery from beads .1 and .2 rather than creating another freshness side channel.
- Define acceptable lag semantics for lexical updates when foreground write pressure is high.
- Ensure interrupted ingest jobs leave enough information for lexical catch-up after restart.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- Lexical correctness is more important than minimizing rebuild work, but rebuilds should still be bounded and incremental where safe.
- Backlog accounting must be durable and derived from SQLite truth, not only in-memory event streams.
- Watch mode should not trap the system in a perpetual "rebuilding" or stale-looking state after initial import finishes.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Integration tests covering: full rebuild, watch startup import, steady-state watch appends, watch-once batches, and historical salvage.
- Tests proving a newly inserted session becomes lexically searchable without requiring a manual repair command.
- Tests for interrupted ingest followed by automatic lexical catch-up on restart.

DONE WHEN:
If SQLite changes, cass has a deterministic automatic path to bring Tantivy back into sync, and future agents do not need to reason manually about whether lexical search reflects the current DB.
design:
ORCHESTRATION REFINEMENT:
- Ongoing lexical maintenance after ingest/watch/import must reuse the shared orchestration layer so foreground search, repair, and catch-up do not race or report contradictory progress.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Every SQLite-mutation path that matters to users, including full index, watch startup, steady-state watch, watch-once, salvage, import, and sync-driven updates, has a deterministic automatic path to lexical freshness.
- Lexical maintenance reuses the shared orchestration and state machinery, remains packet- and controller-aware as the new architecture lands, and does not regress into duplicate full rebuild behavior for ordinary incremental work.
- Unit, integration, and CLI or robot E2E scenarios prove newly ingested content becomes lexically searchable automatically, interrupted ingest catches up after restart, and detailed logs explain whether maintenance was incremental, rebuild-based, attached, or deferred.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Added structured index JSON repair metadata for incremental canonical lexical catch-up so automatic repair-before-scan runs are machine-readable.

title: Introduce lexical generation manifests, scratch builds, and crash-safe atomic publish semantics
description:
BACKGROUND:
Fast rebuild is only valuable if publish semantics are rock solid. Rebuilding in place or relying on one mutable index directory leaves too much room for half-built artifacts, confusing crash recovery, and unsafe future parallelism.

GOAL:
Introduce lexical generation manifests and crash-safe atomic publish semantics for rebuild artifacts.

SCOPE:
- Define lexical generation identity and manifest contents: schema/version, source DB fingerprint, counts, build state, and publish state.
- Build into scratch generations, validate them, and publish atomically.
- Preserve old-good or new-good behavior across crashes, interrupts, and failed rebuilds.
- Expose enough state for cleanup, status, and validation to reason about current, staged, failed, and superseded generations.

DONE WHEN:
The lexical publish path is generation-based, atomic, and auditable, and ordinary search can never observe a half-built artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Lexical rebuilds produce versioned scratch generations with explicit manifests, validation state, publish state, and enough metadata to audit source fingerprint, counts, build attempt identity, startup recovery decisions, and failure history.
- Ordinary search never observes a half-built artifact: deterministic crash-window tests prove old-good or new-good semantics across kill points during build, validation, promotion, restart, and attach-to-existing-generation startup recovery.
- Status, cleanup, and validation tooling can distinguish current, staged, failed, superseded, and quarantined generations using preserved artifacts and detailed logs, and at least one robot or E2E scenario proves restart after interrupted publish chooses the correct generation and explains why.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION POLICY:
- This bead must land with bead-local proof, not only final-epic proof.
- Required by default: targeted unit tests for new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI or robot E2E scenario when the behavior is user-visible, multi-step, or crash-sensitive.
- Preserve rich structured timestamped logs, strategy or fallback reasons, and artifact snapshots relevant to the bead: manifests, benchmark tables, digests, checkpoints, crash-resume traces, controller decisions, or cache evidence.
- Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 and the crash or load harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.17 instead of inventing ad hoc test entrypoints.
- Heavy cargo-driven builds, tests, benches, or profiling for this track must use rch.

title: Define a versioned ConversationPacket contract so refresh normalizes once and feeds many sinks

GOAL:

SCOPE:
- Define the packet schema and invariants for normalized content, provenance, timestamps, stable hashes, and sink-specific projections.
- Support packet construction from both raw connector scan output and canonical SQLite replay.
- Separate canonical payload from derived or cacheable fields so the packet stays memory-conscious and versionable.

DONE WHEN:
Cass has a clear normalize-once contract that later beads can adopt instead of re-deriving the same work in parallel codepaths.

title: Implement a deterministic parallel lexical segment-farm rebuild with safe fallback and atomic generation publish
description:
BACKGROUND:
Even a highly optimized serial lexical rebuild has a ceiling because one thread ultimately replays the corpus into the lexical writer. Once serial hot-path waste is removed and generation semantics exist, the next step toward world-class rebuild is to build lexical segments in parallel and publish one validated generation.

GOAL:
Implement a deterministic parallel lexical segment-farm rebuild with safe fallback and atomic generation publish.

SCOPE:
- Define deterministic shard planning using conversation, message, and byte budgets.
- Build lexical shard outputs in parallel with bounded worker concurrency.
- Validate shard outputs, assemble them into one publishable generation, and promote that generation atomically.
- Provide conservative fallback to the improved serial path when capability gaps or resource limits make parallel rebuild unsafe.
- Extend frankensearch upstream if the required segment import or assembly primitives are missing.

DONE WHEN:
Cass can rebuild lexical state through a validated parallel segment-farm path, publish one generation atomically, and fall back safely when the environment cannot support the fast path.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Deterministic shard planning exists with explicit budgets for conversations, messages, bytes, and worker concurrency, and the same input corpus produces the same shard plan.
- Parallel shard outputs are validated and assembled into exactly one publishable generation; partial success never becomes published success, and safe fallback to the improved serial path is explicit and well logged.
- Benchmark and crash-resume evidence show materially improved large-corpus rebuild performance over the improved serial path without sacrificing determinism, publish safety, or diagnosability.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION POLICY:

comments.text:
2026-04-22: Shipped content-addressed memoization vocabulary slice (commit 549e10f5).

What landed in src/indexer/memoization.rs (newly created):
- MemoContentHash — opaque byte-fingerprint carrier; producer-owned hasher choice.
- MemoKey { content_hash, algorithm, algorithm_version } — the core invariant: any version bump of any derivation invalidates its prior cache entries because the composite key differs. Silent stale cross-version reuse is impossible by construction.
- MemoLookup<V> — Hit / Miss / Quarantined variants, snake_case serialized for structured audit logs.
- MemoCacheEvent — Hit / Miss / Insert / Evict{CapacityLru|Invalidated} / Quarantine{reason} / Invalidate unified vocabulary for downstream logs.

- ContentAddressedMemoCache<V> — bounded LRU, quarantine-aware in-memory cache:
  - capacity_lru eviction when max_entries is reached (touched entries stay resident).
  - Quarantined entries remain resident (operator inspection) but never serve a hit; re-insertion over a quarantined key is a noop that returns Quarantine{reason}.
  - invalidate() returns true only when an entry was actually removed, so counter bumps are honest.

title: Switch default CLI, TUI, and robot search intent to hybrid-preferred behavior
description:
BACKGROUND:
Today cass presents lexical mode as the default search mode. That leaks an implementation detail into the product contract and prevents agents from benefiting from semantic refinement automatically. The user requirement is that hybrid behavior should be the default expectation, while still preserving lexical immediacy and fail-open reliability.

GOAL:
Change cass so the default search intent across CLI, TUI, and robot consumers is hybrid-preferred rather than lexical-first-from-the-user's-perspective.

SCOPE:
- Audit default mode selection in CLI parsing, TUI interactions, robot/help text, capabilities docs, and any config/env defaults.
- Change default intent to hybrid-preferred in user-facing surfaces.
- Preserve explicit override flags for lexical-only and semantic-only modes.
- Ensure metadata clearly reports when a command used lexical-only fallback instead of full hybrid refinement.
- Update examples and help so future agents naturally use the intended path.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- "Default hybrid" must describe user intent, not a brittle hard requirement that semantic assets be fully present.
- This bead should not itself implement fail-open semantics; it should change defaults and surfaces so the runtime planner bead can honor the new contract consistently.
- Any existing language saying lexical is the default should be updated or removed to avoid contradictory operator expectations.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Tests proving the effective mode for ordinary search commands is hybrid-preferred unless explicitly overridden.
- Tests proving explicit lexical mode still remains available and deterministic.
- Snapshot/help tests verifying the documented defaults match the implementation.

DONE WHEN:
A new agent reading cass help or using cass search without extra flags is guided onto the hybrid-preferred path by default, without sacrificing the ability to request lexical-only behavior explicitly.
design:
CONFIG SURFACE REFINEMENT:
- The default-hybrid switch must be implemented through the cohesive config/override layer so users can inspect and override the effective default intentionally rather than relying on hidden parser behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The effective default search intent across CLI, TUI, and robot surfaces is hybrid-preferred unless explicitly overridden, and that effective default is visible through the configuration or status surfaces rather than hidden parser behavior.
- Explicit lexical-only and semantic-only overrides remain deterministic, and user-visible metadata truthfully reports requested intent, realized path, fallback tier, and whether semantic refinement actually occurred.
- Unit, integration, help-snapshot, and CLI or robot E2E scenarios prove default intent, override behavior, and documented examples all stay aligned with the verified product contract.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Default search intent is now hybrid-preferred across CLI/TUI/robot surfaces; explicit lexical/semantic overrides remain preserved; robot metadata reports requested/realized mode, fallback tier, and semantic refinement. Validation: cli_search_semantic_flags, search_robot_meta, cargo check, clippy, fmt.

title: Add semantic asset manifest, backlog ledger, and resumable checkpoints
description:
BACKGROUND:
The semantic side of cass is currently too binary: either vector assets exist in just the right place or hybrid/semantic search fails. That is inadequate for a large evolving corpus. Semantic indexing needs the same first-class asset accounting that lexical indexing will get, but with optional semantics: partial availability should drive background backfill and truthful runtime degradation, not a confusing all-or-nothing user experience.

GOAL:
Introduce authoritative semantic asset manifests and backlog/checkpoint tracking so cass can answer exactly what semantic work remains, resume interrupted work, and know whether fast tier, quality tier, and ANN accelerators are ready for use.

SCOPE:
- Define manifest/state for each semantic artifact class: fast tier vectors, quality tier vectors, ANN/HNSW accelerators, and any future semantic derivatives.
- Fingerprint these assets against the canonical SQLite corpus/version and relevant model/schema versions.
- Track backlog/progress durably at the right grain (conversation, message batch, or chunk range) so interrupted work can resume without restarting the whole corpus.
- Support partial semantic readiness, e.g. fast tier ready while quality tier still backfilling.
- Ensure publish/swap semantics are crash-safe and never advertise an asset as ready before its manifest says so.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- The backlog ledger must support very large corpora without exploding metadata size.
- The design should support both full builds and incremental catch-up after new SQLite content lands.
- The state model must make it obvious whether hybrid refinement can run now, whether only fast tier can run, or whether lexical-only fallback is required.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Unit tests for manifest classification and partial readiness.
- Integration tests for interrupted semantic builds resuming from checkpoints.
- Tests for corpus/model/schema fingerprint mismatch forcing backfill without mislabeling assets as ready.

DONE WHEN:
Semantic indexing has an authoritative durable state model that tells cass exactly what semantic assets exist, how trustworthy they are, and what work remains to converge the corpus.
design:
UPGRADE AND MIGRATION REFINEMENTS:
- The semantic manifest layer must account for legacy pre-manifest semantic assets. If an existing asset is compatible, adopt it explicitly into the new state model; if incompatible, quarantine or invalidate it with a precise reason.
- Never allow mixed-fingerprint, mixed-schema, or partially adopted semantic assets to masquerade as one ready tier.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Implemented src/search/semantic_manifest.rs with full durable manifest (SemanticManifest), per-tier ArtifactRecord, HnswRecord, BacklogLedger, BuildCheckpoint, TierReadiness classification, atomic save/load, legacy adoption, invalidation, and 24 table-driven unit tests covering round-trips, tier readiness, backlog accounting, checkpoint validation, publish/clear, invalidation, and JSON serialization.

title: Implement fail-open hybrid planner with lexical-first progressive refinement
description:
BACKGROUND:
Right now hybrid/semantic search can hard-fail when vector assets are missing, even though lexical search remains healthy. That violates the desired product contract. The runtime planner must treat semantic enrichment as opportunistic: it should improve results when available but never break ordinary search when absent, stale, or temporarily unavailable.

GOAL:
Make the default hybrid runtime path lexical-first and fail-open. Ordinary searches should return lexical results immediately, then add or upgrade semantic refinement only when the semantic state contract says it is safe and useful to do so.

SCOPE:
- Build a single runtime planner that consumes the state models from beads .1 and .5.
- For hybrid-preferred searches, return lexical results immediately when lexical is ready.
- Attempt semantic refinement only when the relevant semantic assets are ready enough.
- If semantic assets are missing, stale, partially built, temporarily locked, or erroring, complete the search lexically and report truthful metadata rather than surfacing a hard search failure.
- Define strict behavior for explicit semantic-only requests, including whether they retain hard-fail semantics or gain an opt-in strictness flag.
- Ensure TUI, CLI, and robot flows all use the same fail-open behavior.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- Lexical-first means user-visible latency stays predictable while semantic refinement remains additive.
- The planner must never silently claim hybrid quality when only lexical ranking was used; metadata and status must expose the truth.
- Partial semantic availability should still be useful: e.g. fast tier may refine even when quality tier is still backfilling.
- A transient semantic subsystem error should not poison subsequent lexical-only searches.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Integration tests where vector assets are fully absent, partially present, stale, or locked.
- Tests proving ordinary hybrid-preferred searches still return successful lexical hits in those cases.
- Tests proving refinement upgrades results when semantic assets become available.
- Tests for explicit semantic-only behavior so strict vs fail-open semantics remain intentional, not accidental.

DONE WHEN:
An agent can issue an ordinary search and trust that cass will never throw away usable lexical search just because semantic refinement is not ready yet.
design:
ORCHESTRATION REFINEMENT:
- The fail-open planner should consume orchestration/progress state when deciding whether to wait briefly, attach to a running maintenance task, or return lexical-only results immediately.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Ordinary hybrid-preferred searches return lexical results immediately whenever lexical search is healthy, then apply semantic refinement only when assets are ready enough and policy allows.
- The planner consumes orchestration and readiness truth when deciding whether to attach, wait boundedly, refine immediately, or complete lexically, and metadata truthfully reports the decision, realized refinement tier, stable result identity or digest continuity where useful, and any fail-open reason.
- Unit, integration, and CLI or robot E2E scenarios cover absent, partial, stale, locked, erroring, and newly available semantic assets, plus explicit semantic-only requests and progressive refinement without misleading result churn, with detailed structured logs and result-digest evidence.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Hybrid search now fails open to lexical for default and explicit hybrid intent while semantic-only remains strict; robot metadata covers the realized fallback.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
POLISH ROUND 6:
- Added a formal acceptance bar for planner decisions because this is where the user contract is actually honored or broken at query time.
- The planner now explicitly owns reporting the decision path: immediate lexical, bounded wait, attach, semantic refinement tier, or fail-open reason.

title: Schedule low-impact background semantic backfill using idle and load budgets
description:
BACKGROUND:
The user requirement is not merely to support semantic indexing, but to do it without harming the machine's primary job: coding, search, and interactive use. That means semantic work must be opportunistic and budgeted. cass should quietly chew through vector work when the machine is idle or when work can be done with little impact, then yield quickly when foreground pressure returns. The scheduler is therefore a control layer over an already-correct worker/publish pipeline, not the place where actual semantic backfill correctness is invented.

GOAL:
Introduce a background scheduler that drives the existing semantic worker only when operating conditions are favorable and within explicit CPU/IO/latency budgets.

SCOPE:
- Define what cass treats as favorable background conditions: low foreground search pressure, no active lexical repair contention, acceptable CPU/load, acceptable IO pressure, and any available heuristics for user activity or interactive contention.
- Drive the worker from bead .8 rather than re-implementing semantic generation logic inside the scheduler.
- Implement pause/resume behavior so semantic work yields when the machine becomes busy again.
- Choose conservative concurrency and batching defaults.
- Support operator overrides and kill switches so future debugging or benchmarking can disable background behavior cleanly.
- Ensure the scheduler integrates with the semantic backlog ledger from bead .5 instead of inventing its own notion of remaining work.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- A scheduler that is too aggressive will destroy trust even if it technically works.
- Background work should prefer incremental progress over large monolithic jobs that take too long to pause.
- Scheduling decisions should be inspectable in logs/status so future agents can understand why work is paused or running.
- The implementation should leave room for later sophistication, but the first version should already have sane conservative budgets.
- The scheduler should be a thin policy/orchestration layer on top of the worker, not a second place where backfill correctness, batching semantics, or publish safety are defined.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Tests for scheduler state transitions: idle -> running, busy -> paused, resume after busy period.
- Tests ensuring background semantic work yields to lexical repair and foreground search.
- Performance tests or harnesses validating that background work stays within stated latency/throughput budgets.
- At least one CLI/robot/E2E scenario showing the scheduler driving the worker under load/idle transitions with detailed structured logs.

DONE WHEN:
Semantic backfill can make steady progress in the background on real corpora without materially degrading interactive cass usage or general machine responsiveness, by driving the already-correct worker within conservative operating budgets.
design:
WORKER-FIRST REFINEMENT:
- The scheduler should be able to deliver semantic acquisition/backfill value before the cleanup layer exists, but it should not be the first owner of vector-generation correctness.
- This bead must consume the stable worker/publish contract from bead .8 and the earlier status surface from bead .9, then add only policy: when to run, when to pause, and how to stay within user-friendly budgets.
- The scheduler should enrich the existing readiness/progress surfaces with paused-for-load, resumed-on-idle, and similar policy-specific explanations once it lands.
- Once cleanup is implemented, the scheduler should treat it as an additional budgeted maintenance workload rather than a prerequisite for all background progress.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The scheduler runs semantic backfill only under conservative idle or low-pressure conditions, yields promptly when foreground pressure or lexical repair returns, and resumes safely when budgets allow.
- Scheduling decisions are inspectable through logs and status, including why work is running, paused, resumed, disabled, pinned, cooled-down, or budget-blocked, what recent pressure signal triggered the decision, and when work is next eligible to resume, and those decisions honor the cohesive configuration surface without oscillating under borderline load.
- Unit, integration, performance-harness, and CLI or robot E2E scenarios cover idle-to-running, busy-to-paused, resumed-on-idle, lexical-repair preemption, cooldown or anti-thrash behavior, operator overrides, and user-visible budget adherence with preserved traces, timing artifacts, and scheduler-decision evidence.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Implemented scheduled semantic backfill gating: policy/responsiveness scheduler decisions, --scheduled/--background robot trigger, foreground/lexical-pressure pause reporting, unit tests, and robot E2E coverage.

title: Implement resumable semantic backfill worker and atomic publish pipeline
description:
BACKGROUND:
A scheduler without a durable worker/publisher only decides when work should happen; it does not actually converge the corpus. cass needs a semantic worker that can process backlog incrementally, checkpoint progress, publish safe artifacts, and resume after interruption without wasting large amounts of prior work. That worker is foundational infrastructure: it should exist before background policy decides exactly when it runs.

GOAL:
Build the semantic worker/publisher that executes the backlog described by bead .5 and can be invoked by later scheduler/orchestration layers without redefining its core correctness model.

SCOPE:
- Consume semantic backlog in bounded batches that can be paused and resumed.
- Build/update fast-tier and quality-tier vector assets incrementally where possible.
- Publish assets atomically so readers never observe partially-written indexes as ready.
- Support crash-safe restart after interruption, process exit, or machine reboot.
- Ensure the worker coexists safely with foreground search, lexical repair, and any ANN acceleration rebuilds.
- Record enough progress metadata that operators can tell where the worker left off.
- Expose a stable worker interface or invocation contract that the scheduler bead can drive later, without forcing scheduling policy to be baked into the worker itself.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- Progress checkpoints should be frequent enough to avoid expensive replay, but not so frequent they dominate IO.
- Publish semantics must align with the state manifests so readiness never races ahead of artifact durability.
- Worker batching should be chosen with future background throttling in mind, not just peak throughput.
- This bead should deliver first semantic-generation correctness even before the background scheduler is complete.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Integration tests for worker interruption and resume.
- Tests for atomic publish behavior under simulated crash windows.
- Tests for mixed readiness states, e.g. fast tier published while quality tier continues.
- At least one CLI/robot/E2E scenario that exercises explicit or manually triggered worker progress with detailed structured logs.

DONE WHEN:
Given a semantic backlog, cass can grind through it over time, survive interruption, and publish trustworthy semantic assets without corrupting foreground search behavior, regardless of whether the later scheduler layer is already present.
design:
SCHEDULER SEQUENCING REFINEMENT:
- The worker/publish pipeline is foundational and should exist before the scheduler policy layer.
- This bead should expose stable worker controls and progress semantics that the scheduler bead can consume later, rather than making the first correct worker implementation wait on idle/load scheduling policy.
- The worker should publish and mark superseded generations in a way that cleanup can consume later, but the worker itself should not be blocked on cleanup implementation before it can deliver semantic search value.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The semantic worker consumes backlog in bounded resumable batches, publishes semantic assets atomically, survives interruption, and never leaves readers observing partially-ready semantic state.
- Progress metadata is detailed enough for scheduler, status, cleanup, and rollout validation to identify current phase, last durable checkpoint, published tier state, and superseded artifacts.
- Unit, integration, crash-window, and CLI or robot E2E scenarios cover interruption and resume, mixed fast-tier versus quality-tier readiness, coexistence with lexical repair, and preserved structured logs plus artifact snapshots.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Implemented resumable semantic backfill worker with atomic publish, robot models backfill trigger, storage-backed resume coverage, and E2E robot CLI coverage.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
POLISH ROUND 6:
- Tightened this bead so worker progress metadata is explicitly useful to scheduler, cleanup, status, and rollout verification instead of being treated as an internal concern.
- That keeps the semantic pipeline aligned with the same evidence-first philosophy used in the stale-refresh architecture.

title: Expose truthful lexical-vs-semantic readiness, fallback, and progress surfaces
description:
BACKGROUND:
Once cass starts self-healing lexical assets and opportunistically backfilling semantic assets, status reporting becomes more important, not less. Agents and humans need to know whether they are seeing lexical-only results, hybrid-refined results, or a system that is still converging in the background. Ambiguous health output will create repeated confusion and unnecessary repair attempts. Core truth about lexical readiness, semantic readiness, fallback, and active work should not be delayed until the idle/background scheduler layer is complete.

GOAL:
Make status, health, capabilities, and search metadata explicitly describe lexical readiness, semantic readiness, active fallback, and core background-progress truth.

SCOPE:
- Update status/health output so lexical mandatory readiness and semantic optional readiness are reported separately.
- Surface whether a search completed lexically-only, fast-tier-refined, or fully hybrid-refined.
- Report semantic backlog/progress in machine-readable form from the repair/acquisition/worker path, even before scheduler-specific idle/load policy is finished.
- Make recommended actions specific: e.g. repair lexical now, wait for semantic catch-up, or nothing required.
- Ensure CLI/TUI/robot consumers all have access to consistent truth, not three separate ad hoc summaries.
- Leave room for the scheduler bead to enrich the same surfaces later with paused-for-load, resumed-on-idle, and similar policy-specific explanations.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- A stale-but-complete lexical index is different from a missing lexical index.
- A missing quality tier is different from a missing fast tier.
- Metadata should help agents reason about result quality without forcing them to read logs.
- Avoid scaring users with "unhealthy" when ordinary search remains correct and available; reserve strong health failures for blocking lexical issues.

TEST/VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS:
- Tests for status/health JSON payload shape across lexical-ready, lexical-repairing, semantic-backfilling, and hybrid-ready states.
- Tests proving search metadata truthfully describes fallback and refinement level.
- Tests that recommended_action output matches the actual remediation path.
- At least one CLI/robot/E2E scenario showing truthful status before the idle scheduler exists and then after scheduler-specific enrichments land.

DONE WHEN:
A caller can inspect cass output and immediately understand whether search is fully converged, currently lexical-only, or actively enriching itself in the background, without needing the idle scheduler layer to exist first.
design:
STATUS FOUNDATION REFINEMENT:
- Surface whether a caller attached to existing work, launched new work, waited for bounded progress, or failed open while maintenance continued elsewhere.
- Core lexical-vs-semantic readiness, fallback, and progress reporting should build on the basic foreground orchestration layer from bead .21 plus repair/acquisition/worker truth.
- Advanced background orchestration, scheduler-specific paused/idle explanations, and cleanup/quarantine detail should enrich these same surfaces later rather than blocking the first truthful user-facing status model.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Status, health, capabilities, and search metadata truthfully distinguish lexical-ready, lexical-repairing, lexical-stale-but-searchable, semantic-backfilling, and fully hybrid-ready states without collapsing them into a single vague health bit.
- As the stale-refresh architecture lands, these surfaces also expose generation or publish state, attach-versus-launch behavior, bounded-wait outcomes, controller strategy or degraded-mode reasons, active path-selection mode such as serial, parallel, shadow, canary, or demoted-safe-path, and whether results came from lexical-only, fast-tier, or fully hybrid refinement.
- CLI, TUI, and robot outputs remain consistent, and tests plus at least one CLI or robot E2E script prove recommended_action, next-step guidance, run or evidence identifiers where useful, and status payloads all match real remediation and rollout behavior throughout convergence.
notes: TEST POLICY ADDENDUM: This bead must land with bead-local validation, not just final-epic validation. At minimum include targeted unit tests for the new invariants, integration tests for the affected runtime path, and at least one CLI/robot/E2E script when the behavior is user-visible or multi-step. Test output must include rich, structured, timestamped logging and artifact snapshots sufficient for a future agent to diagnose failures without rerunning the entire scenario manually. Prefer extending the shared harness from coding_agent_session_search-ibuuh.15 where applicable.
close_reason: Status/health now surface semantic tier truth, backlog/checkpoint progress, and semantic catch-up guidance from manifest-backed state.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
POLISH ROUND 4:
- The stale-refresh architecture introduced new states that matter to users: scratch versus published generations, attach-versus-launch behavior, bounded waiting, and controller-driven degraded modes. This bead now explicitly owns surfacing those states once available, while still allowing the first truthful status model to land earlier.
- Keep the UX goal simple: a user or agent should be able to tell whether cass is searchable now, converging in the background, or needs intervention without reading raw logs.

POLISH ROUND 8:

- This is for users: once cass has advanced fast paths, status must explain not just readiness but which path is active and what to do next.

title: [P0] Opt 2: SIMD Dot Product Implementation
description:
# Optimization 2: SIMD Dot Product Implementation

## Problem Statement

After F16 pre-conversion (Optimization 1), the remaining hotspot is the scalar dot product loop. Even with LLVM's auto-vectorization, explicit SIMD can provide guaranteed vectorization and better instruction scheduling.

### Current Implementation (vector_index.rs:1221-1228)
```rust
fn dot_product(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    a.iter().zip(b.iter()).map(|(x, y)| x * y).sum()
}
```

### Why Explicit SIMD?
- LLVM auto-vectorization is not guaranteed - depends on optimization level, alignment, loop structure
- Explicit SIMD provides predictable, measurable performance
- AVX2 processes 8 floats per instruction (256-bit registers)
- SSE processes 4 floats per instruction (128-bit registers)

## Proposed Solution

Use the `wide` crate for portable SIMD that works across x86_64 (AVX2/SSE) and ARM (NEON).

### Implementation Location
- File: `src/search/vector_index.rs`
- Add new function: `dot_product_simd`
- Modify `dot_product_at` to use SIMD version

### Code Implementation
```rust
use wide::f32x8;

fn dot_product_simd(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    let chunks_a = a.chunks_exact(8);
    let chunks_b = b.chunks_exact(8);
    let remainder_a = chunks_a.remainder();
    let remainder_b = chunks_b.remainder();

    let mut sum = f32x8::ZERO;
    for (ca, cb) in chunks_a.zip(chunks_b) {
        let arr_a: [f32; 8] = ca.try_into().unwrap();
        let arr_b: [f32; 8] = cb.try_into().unwrap();
        sum += f32x8::from(arr_a) * f32x8::from(arr_b);
    }

    let mut scalar_sum: f32 = sum.reduce_add();
    for (a, b) in remainder_a.iter().zip(remainder_b) {
        scalar_sum += a * b;
    }
    scalar_sum
}
```

### Why `wide` Crate?
- Version 0.7.x is stable and maintained
- Provides `f32x8::ZERO` for zero-initialization
- Provides `reduce_add()` for horizontal sum
- Portable across x86_64 and ARM
- No unsafe code in user code

## Isomorphism Note

**Important**: SIMD reorders floating-point operations, causing ~1e-7 relative error in scores.

### Why This Is Acceptable
- **Ranking order is preserved**: Score differences are too small to change ordering
- **Same result set**: Same (message_id, chunk_idx) pairs returned
- **Industry standard**: All vector search engines accept this trade-off

### Verification
```rust
// Property test
for query in test_queries {
    let scalar = dot_product(&a, &b);
    let simd = dot_product_simd(&a, &b);
    assert!((scalar - simd).abs() < 1e-5 * scalar.abs().max(1.0));
}
```

## Pre-Implementation Verification

Before implementing explicit SIMD, verify LLVM isn't already auto-vectorizing:
```bash
RUSTFLAGS="--emit=asm" cargo build --release
# Check target/release/deps/*.s for vmulps/vaddps (AVX) or mulps/addps (SSE)
```

If auto-vectorization is already happening, explicit SIMD may provide marginal benefit. Benchmark to verify.

## Expected Impact

| Metric | Before (post-Opt1) | After |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| `vector_index_search_50k` | ~30ms | 10-15ms |
| Speedup | Baseline | 2-4x |

## Cargo.toml Addition
```toml
[dependencies]
wide = "0.7"  # Portable SIMD
```

## Rollback Strategy

Environment variable `CASS_SIMD_DOT=0` to:
- Disable SIMD implementation
- Fall back to scalar dot product
- Useful for debugging FP precision issues

## Dependencies

- **Depends on**: Optimization 1 (F16 Pre-Convert) - SIMD on uniform F32 is simpler and faster
- **Blocks**: Optimization 3 (Parallel) - Parallelizing fast SIMD ops yields best results

description:
# P6.10: Recovery Testing

## Goal
Verify password recovery, key slot rotation, and disaster recovery procedures work correctly, ensuring users can regain access to their data when passwords are forgotten.

## Test Areas

### Recovery Key Flow

- Verify recovery key unlocks archive

### Disaster Recovery
- Recover from corrupted key slot metadata
- Partial archive recovery (some chunks valid)
- Re-export from partial data

### Edge Cases
- Recovery with typos (fuzzy matching)
- Case sensitivity in recovery keys
- Special characters in passwords
- Unicode normalization

```rust
#[test]
fn test_recovery_key_unlocks() {
    let (archive, recovery_key) = export_with_recovery("password");
    
    // Primary password works
    let decrypted1 = decrypt(&archive, "password").unwrap();
    
    // Recovery key also works
    let decrypted2 = decrypt_with_recovery(&archive, &recovery_key).unwrap();
    
    assert_eq!(decrypted1, decrypted2);
}

#[test]
fn test_add_key_slot() {
    let archive = export_encrypted(&data, "password1");
    
    // Add second password
    let updated = add_key_slot(&archive, "password1", "password2").unwrap();
    
    // Both work
    assert!(decrypt(&updated, "password1").is_ok());
    assert!(decrypt(&updated, "password2").is_ok());
}
```

title: cass index full-rebuild disk headroom underestimates by >4x, fills the filesystem
description:
## Summary

`cass index`'s full-rebuild disk preflight under-estimates required free space by
several-fold, so the check passes and the rebuild then fills the filesystem.
Observed twice on 2026-07-25 during a fleet-wide re-index: it took trj's root to
**100% full (64K free)** and put ts2 into a ~90-minute userspace wedge.

## Root cause

`required_index_headroom_bytes` (src/indexer/mod.rs:16752):

```rust
IndexStorageHeadroomRequirement::AuthoritativeLexicalRebuild => {
    let db_bundle_bytes = database_bundle_size_bytes(db_path);
    INDEX_MIN_FREE_SPACE_BYTES.max(db_bundle_bytes.saturating_mul(2))
}
```

`database_bundle_size_bytes` (16765) sums **only** `agent_search.db` + `-wal` +
`-shm`. The requirement therefore ignores:

- the lexical/Tantivy `index/` directory (57 GB on trj)
- the `raw-mirror/` tree (117 GB on trj)
- transient staged-shard / staged-merge scratch written during the rebuild

The probe *paths* are right (`existing_headroom_probe_paths`, 16703, checks
`data_dir` and the db parent) — it is the required-bytes formula that is wrong.

## Field evidence

| host | db bundle | required (2x) | free at start | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| trj | 25 GB | 50 GB | 113 GB — **check passed** | consumed ~115 GB, root hit 100%, SQLite `disk I/O error (10)`, index died |
| ts2 | 1.9 GB | 3.8 GB | ~700 GB — **check passed** | cass dir 1.9→13 GB, disk 80%→88%, host wedged (sshd banner-hang, rchd unresponsive) until the `timeout` cap killed it |

trj needed **>4.5x** the db-bundle size, not 2x.

## The fix is already half-written

`lexical_rebuild_amplification_milli(index_size_bytes, message_bytes)` exists at
src/indexer/mod.rs:4859 and the rebuild pipeline already emits it in progress
telemetry — the run that filled trj reported
`staged_shard_build_observed_amplification_milli: 8000` (8.0x). **The code
measures the amplification factor it needs and never feeds it back into the
preflight.**

## Proposed fix

1. Include the existing lexical `index/` directory size in
   `required_index_headroom_bytes` for `AuthoritativeLexicalRebuild`.
2. Scale by a persisted/observed amplification factor (fall back to a
   conservative constant on first run) rather than a hardcoded `* 2`.
3. Re-check headroom periodically **during** the rebuild, not only before it, and
   abort cleanly with a clear error instead of running the volume to 0 bytes.
4. Surface required-vs-available in the error (it already does this well) and in
   `--json` progress so operators can see the projection.

## Notes

`CASS_INDEX_SKIP_DISK_HEADROOM_CHECK` exists as an escape hatch; it was NOT set
in any of these runs — the check genuinely passed.
close_reason: Fixed in a3e808f9

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: required_index_headroom_bytes() now takes data_dir and adds lexical_index_size_bytes(data_dir)*2 to the AuthoritativeLexicalRebuild projection, so an existing lexical index is counted instead of ignored. New helper walks data_dir/index/ explicitly (symlink-safe). Regression tests: authoritative_rebuild_headroom_counts_existing_lexical_index (asserts the delta is exactly 2x the index bytes) and incremental_headroom_ignores_lexical_index_size (incremental keeps the flat floor). Two pre-existing tests updated for the new arity. Verified: cargo check --lib --tests on css (an unpatched host) reports ZERO errors in src/indexer/mod.rs. NOT closed: the periodic mid-rebuild re-check and amplification-derived scaling from the proposal remain future work.

```bash
critcmp no_cache with_cache
```

### 3. Cache Hit Rate Measurement

```rust
static CACHE_HITS: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
static CACHE_MISSES: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

fn get_or_create_agent_id(&mut self, ...) -> Result<i64> {
```

Hit rate = (3000 - 50) / 3000 = 98.3% for workspaces

Cache memory usage is minimal:
- Agent cache: ~1-5 entries × 50 bytes = < 1 KB
- Workspace cache: ~10-100 entries × 100 bytes = < 10 KB
- Total overhead: < 100 KB

title: Remove phantom _shared_filters placeholder field from SearchClient
description:
## What

Remove the _shared_filters phantom placeholder field from the **SearchClient** struct in src/search/query.rs.

## Current State

Line 2009 (struct definition):
```rust
_shared_filters: Arc<Mutex<()>>, // placeholder lock to ensure Send/Sync; future warm prefill state
```

The struct is SearchClient. It's used via Arc<SearchClient> in production (line 1874) and tests (line 5522).

## Send/Sync Safety Analysis

The comment claims _shared_filters "ensures Send/Sync", but this is **incorrect**:
- Arc<Mutex<()>> is Send+Sync, but adding a Send+Sync field to a struct doesn't make OTHER fields Send+Sync
- SearchClient is already Send+Sync because ALL of its other fields individually satisfy these bounds
- The code compiles with Arc<SearchClient> today, which requires SearchClient: Send + Sync
- Removing a Send+Sync field from a Send+Sync struct cannot break Send/Sync

Therefore, removal is safe from a trait bound perspective. cargo check will catch any issues at compile time.

## Scope of Change — 37 occurrences total

Locations in src/search/query.rs:
- Line 2009: struct field definition
- Line 2545: let shared_filters = Arc::new(Mutex::new(())); (production local)
- Line 2575: _shared_filters: shared_filters, (production constructor)
- ~34 test constructor sites (each with identical line: _shared_filters: Arc::new(Mutex::new(())),)

## Why Remove It

1. Arc<Mutex<()>> wraps the unit type — holds no data, provides no synchronization
2. The comment explicitly says "placeholder" and "future warm prefill state"
3. The warm prefill feature doesn't exist and has no timeline
4. The "ensure Send/Sync" comment is technically wrong (see analysis above)
5. Per AGENTS.md: "Don't design for hypothetical future requirements"

## How

1. Remove _shared_filters from the SearchClient struct definition (line 2009)
2. Remove the let shared_filters = Arc::new(Mutex::new(())); local (line 2545)
3. Remove _shared_filters: shared_filters, from the production constructor (line 2575)
4. Remove _shared_filters: Arc::new(Mutex::new(())), from ALL ~34 test constructors
5. Check if Arc and Mutex imports become unused — they won't, since reload_epoch: Arc<AtomicU64>, sqlite: Mutex<...>, etc. still use them
6. Run cargo check --all-targets

## Testing

The existing 100+ search tests will verify correctness — they all construct SearchClient without the removed field and must still compile and pass. Add a compile-time verification test:

```rust
#[test]
fn search_client_is_send_sync_without_phantom_filters() {
    // Verify SearchClient satisfies Send + Sync after removing the phantom
    // _shared_filters: Arc<Mutex<()>> field. This field was removed because
    // it held no data (unit type), provided no real synchronization, and
    // the "ensure Send/Sync" comment was incorrect — the struct is Send+Sync
    // due to its other fields' bounds, not this phantom.
    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
    assert_send_sync::<super::SearchClient>();
}
```

This test statically asserts the Send+Sync bounds at compile time, permanently guarding against future regressions.

## Verification

- grep -n '_shared_filters' src/search/query.rs returns zero matches
- cargo check --all-targets passes (compile-time Send+Sync check)
- cargo test search passes (all 100+ search tests)
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- `_shared_filters` is either removed or given real, documented semantics.
- No placeholder-only synchronization state remains in `SearchEngine`.
- Search construction and representative query tests pass via `rch`.

description:
# Task: Benchmark Streaming Canonicalization

## Objective

Measure performance improvement from streaming canonicalization.

## Expected Impact

From PLAN:
- Current: 951 µs for long messages
- Target: ~300 µs (3x improvement)

## Benchmark Protocol

### 1. Baseline (Original Implementation)
```bash
export CASS_STREAMING_CANONICALIZE=0
cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- canonicalize --save-baseline original
```

### 2. Streaming Implementation
```bash
unset CASS_STREAMING_CANONICALIZE
cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- canonicalize --save-baseline streaming
```

### 3. Compare Results
```bash
critcmp original streaming
```

## Micro-Benchmarks to Add

```rust
fn bench_canonicalize(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let short = "Short message";
    let medium = include_str!("fixtures/medium_message.txt");  // ~1KB
    let long = include_str!("fixtures/long_message.txt");      // ~10KB
    
    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("canonicalize");
    
    group.bench_function("short", |b| {
        b.iter(|| canonicalize_for_embedding(black_box(short)))
    });
    
    group.bench_function("medium", |b| {
        b.iter(|| canonicalize_for_embedding(black_box(medium)))
    });
    
    group.bench_function("long", |b| {
        b.iter(|| canonicalize_for_embedding(black_box(long)))
    });
    
    group.finish();
}
```

## Allocation Measurement

Use jemalloc profiler to measure allocation reduction:

```bash
# Before
CASS_STREAMING_CANONICALIZE=0 cargo run --release -- bench-alloc canonicalize

# After
cargo run --release -- bench-alloc canonicalize
```

Expected:
- Allocations: 5 → 2 per call
- Total bytes allocated: ~60% reduction

## Impact on Indexing

Measure indexing throughput improvement:

```bash
# Create test corpus
cargo run --release -- index --benchmark --corpus test_corpus

# Compare indexing times
CASS_STREAMING_CANONICALIZE=0 cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- index_small_batch
```

title: Validate semantic, vector, model, and memoization derivatives without blocking lexical recovery
description:
Background: cass has lexical, semantic, vector, memoization, and model-cache assets. These are useful quality layers, but they are derived or optional and must never endanger archival recovery. The search contract is lexical fail-open: missing or corrupt semantic assets should degrade to truthful lexical behavior, not block DB/archive repair.

Scope: add doctor checks for semantic model presence, vector index freshness, HNSW/mmap readability, memo quarantine summaries, model cache quarantine markers, embedding memo schema drift, and fallback_mode correctness. Missing MiniLM or other semantic model files must recommend cass models install or air-gapped --from-file workflows; doctor must never auto-download models, contact the network, or treat absent models as archive corruption. Repairs may rebuild derived semantic/vector/memo artifacts only after the archive state is safe enough to trust as input.

Acceptance criteria: missing/corrupt semantic assets produce fallback_mode=lexical and recommended_action without failing archive recovery; semantic repair cannot block DB/archive recovery or lexical search; robot output separates derived semantic health from archive integrity with asset_class and safe_to_rebuild. Unit tests cover absent model, corrupt model cache, stale vectors, unreadable mmap, memo quarantine, and disabled semantic policy. E2E tests prove doctor check stays read-only, safe auto-run skips model downloads, and search remains lexical-usable while semantic assets are unavailable.

## Overview
Document the optimizations that were already implemented before Round 1 (Section 7 of PLAN).

## Already-Shipped Optimizations

### 7.1 Title-Prefix N-Gram Reuse

**Location**: \`src/search/tantivy.rs:261\` (\`TantivyIndex::add_messages\`)

**What changed**: Precompute per-conversation values once:
- \`source_path\`, \`workspace\`, \`workspace_original\`
- \`title\` and \`title_prefix = generate_edge_ngrams(title)\`
- \`started_at\` fallback

**Isomorphism proof**: \`generate_edge_ngrams\` is pure. Computing it once vs per-message yields identical Tantivy field values.

- Indexing alloc: 1,375 MB → 1,261 MB (8.3% reduction)
- Indexing time: ~1,701ms → 1,601ms

**Equivalence oracle**: \`src/search/tantivy.rs:785\` verifies title-prefix matching.

**Location**: \`src/lib.rs:3672\` (\`output_robot_results\`)

**What changed**: For \`--robot-format sessions\`, compute \`BTreeSet<&str>\` of \`source_path\` values and return early, avoiding unused JSON construction.

**Isomorphism proof**: Sessions output depends only on \`source_path\` set from \`result.hits\`. Removing intermediate allocations doesn't change the output.

**Impact**: Sessions search alloc: 29.4 MB → 27.0 MB

**Equivalence oracle**: \`tests/cli_robot.rs:334\` (metamorphic test across formats)

## Purpose of This Bead
- Track what's already done so Round 1 focuses on new work
- Provide reference for similar future optimizations
- Document the methodology (isomorphism proof, equivalence oracle)

title: [MEDIUM] mock-finder: pages analytics + wizard write JSON config/output without fsync (crash-window data loss)
description:
Mock-code-finder finding: durability-stub pattern.

Same class of gap as bead coding_agent_session_search-92o31 (closed
in commit 802b88db), but on a different code path. 92o31 fixed
\`src/pages/encrypt.rs::sync_tree\` to chain the missing
\`sync_parent_directory\` after the subtree fsync. The same fsync-
shaped gap exists in the pages-export data-write paths, which call
\`std::fs::write\` and return without any fsync on the file OR the
parent directory.

## Locations
Five user-facing JSON-write call sites:

\`\`\`
src/pages/analytics.rs:181  std::fs::write(&stats_path, stats_json)        // statistics.json
src/pages/analytics.rs:187  std::fs::write(&timeline_path, timeline_json)  // timeline.json
src/pages/analytics.rs:193  std::fs::write(&workspace_path, workspace_json) // workspace_summary.json
src/pages/analytics.rs:199  std::fs::write(&agent_path, agent_json)        // agent_summary.json
src/pages/analytics.rs:205  std::fs::write(&terms_path, terms_json)        // top_terms.json

src/pages/wizard.rs:1672    std::fs::write(&config_path, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&config)?)
  // Writes the pages-export archive's config.json describing schema
  // version + key-slot references. Part of the unencrypted-archive path.
\`\`\`

None of these calls do any of:
- \`File::create + write_all + sync_all\` (file-level fsync)
- \`sync_parent_directory\` (dirent durability — the 92o31 shape)
- \`fs::write\` + subsequent open-parent-and-sync

## Impact
### analytics.rs (LOW-MEDIUM)
The five .json files are statistics/timeline outputs consumed by the
pages export bundle. Crash-window loss → empty or zero-byte files in
the output archive. Regeneratable by rerunning \`cass pages\`, so
recoverable with effort. Severity: **LOW-MEDIUM** — unprofessional,
not catastrophic.

### wizard.rs (MEDIUM)
\`config.json\` is the pages-export archive's metadata descriptor —
it carries:
- Encryption schema version
- Key slot configuration (password/recovery KEK info)
- Payload manifest
- Compression settings
Without it, the archive on disk is UNREADABLE — decryption tools
cannot find the key slots or nonce/salt values needed to unwrap the
DEK. Crash-window loss between fs::write and the OS cache flush
leaves a bundle that is silently corrupt: files on disk, no
config.json → archive reads as "empty" or "unknown format" on open.

(This particular call site at line 1672 is the UNENCRYPTED bundle
path — line 1673+ has the encrypted branch. The unencrypted path
still writes config.json for schema metadata; its loss still
corrupts the archive.)

Severity: **MEDIUM** — bundle corruption on power-loss; user-
reported bug shape.

## Suggested fix
Apply the same POSIX fsync-the-parent pattern bead 92o31 committed
for encrypt.rs::sync_tree. For each write site:

\`\`\`rust
// Before:
std::fs::write(&path, data)?;

// After:
use std::fs::OpenOptions;
use std::io::Write;
let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
    .create(true).write(true).truncate(true)
    .open(&path)?;
file.write_all(data.as_ref())?;
file.sync_all()?;  // fsync file contents + inode
drop(file);
sync_parent_directory(&path)?;  // fsync parent dirent (shared helper)
\`\`\`

Or, simpler — if the pages module already has a \`write_sync\`
helper (it has \`sync_tree\` + \`sync_parent_directory\` in sibling
files after 92o31), refactor to a module-local helper:

\`\`\`rust
fn write_and_sync(path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
    let mut f = File::create(path)?;
    f.write_all(data)?;
    f.sync_all()?;
    drop(f);
    sync_parent_directory(path)
}
\`\`\`

Then call \`write_and_sync(&stats_path, stats_json.as_bytes())?\` etc.
at each of the 6 write sites.

## Regression test shape (mirrors 92o31)
Add a test that materializes the crash-window state (sibling file
write succeeds but parent dirent lost) via a simulated fault and
asserts the write_and_sync path surfaces an error rather than
silently "succeeding" without durability. The 92o31 test at
src/pages/encrypt.rs::tests::sync_tree_includes_parent_directory_fsync
is the template.

## Severity
MEDIUM — same class as 92o31. LOW for analytics (regeneratable),
MEDIUM for wizard.rs:1672 (bundle unreadable on partial write).
One combined fix covers all 6 sites; fix cost is ~30 lines + one
test.

Labels: pages, crash-safety, durability, mock-finder.

title: P5.1: Secret Detection Engine
description:
# P5.1: Secret Detection Scanner

## Goal
Detect sensitive secrets BEFORE encryption and deployment. Use both pattern matching and entropy heuristics to catch API keys, tokens, private keys, and high-entropy blobs.

## Detection Methods

### 1) Pattern Library (regex)
- AWS access/secret keys
- GitHub PAT/OAuth tokens
- OpenAI/Anthropic keys
- JWTs
- Private key headers (PEM)
- Database URLs
- Generic "api_key" style patterns

### 2) Entropy Heuristics
- Identify long base64/hex-like strings
- Compute Shannon entropy and flag above threshold (e.g., > 4.0)
- Apply minimum length (e.g., 20+ chars) to reduce noise

### 3) Scope
Scan:
- Message content
- Conversation titles
- Metadata fields
- Attachment text (when attachments enabled)

## UX / Guardrails
- Show findings grouped by severity (critical/high/medium/low)
- Show sanitized context snippet (avoid leaking full secret)
- Provide allowlist / denylist patterns
- For critical hits: block export unless user explicitly acknowledges
- Robot mode output for CI

## CLI / Wizard Integration
- `cass pages --scan-secrets` (standalone)
- Wizard step shows count and examples
- Optional --fail-on-secrets for CI

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests
- Each built-in regex detects known fixtures
- Entropy detector catches high-entropy strings and ignores normal text
- Allowlist suppresses findings

### Integration Tests
- Export with injected secrets -> scan results include all hits
- Redacted output does not contain secrets

### E2E
- Wizard flow stops on critical secrets and requires confirmation
- JSON output stable for CI parsing

## Files to Create/Modify
- src/pages/secret_scan.rs
- src/pages/wizard.rs (scan step)
- tests/secret_scan.rs

## Exit Criteria
1. Secrets detected reliably with low false positives
2. Entropy-based detection works
3. CI can fail builds on secrets
4. Clear user guidance and logging

title: Refactor cass doctor into a dedicated module and subcommand tree

Background: current run_doctor lives in src/lib.rs and already does useful work, but v2 will be too large and safety-critical to remain as one monolithic function. A dedicated module boundary reduces accidental coupling and makes contracts testable. This is a structural refactor, not a compatibility layer: current command spellings should be routed into the new typed command model without leaving a duplicate legacy implementation.

Scope: move doctor data types, checks, plans, receipts, event-log integration, safety taxonomy, and repair execution into a src/doctor/ module or equivalent. Keep existing safe JSON entry points reachable while introducing internal seams for check, plan, repair, cleanup, backup, restore, reconstruct, baseline diff, support bundle, and report rendering. Centralize stdout/stderr, robot-mode contracts, outcome_kind mapping, and error envelopes so subcommands cannot drift. New SQLite logic must use frankensqlite/fsqlite patterns; do not add new rusqlite usage while moving code.

Acceptance criteria: current cass doctor --json/--fix invocations route through the safer v2 parser/planner semantics; unsafe legacy assumptions fail closed instead of being preserved. Module tests can target doctor logic without invoking the full CLI; no new rusqlite usage is introduced; subcommand handlers share one parser/output/error contract. Unit tests cover command dispatch, current-flag mapping, typed plan/report rendering, outcome-kind mapping, and module-level check fixtures. CLI/e2e smoke tests prove old and new spellings produce equivalent robot payloads for safe read-only cases and fail closed for unsafe mutating flags.

title: Real MiniLM plus native HNSW restart and retrieval-quality acceptance lane
description: Add the mandatory optimized no-mock acceptance lane that provisions and executes the real MiniLM producer against persisted FSVI v2 plus native HNSW, exits, restarts in a fresh process, resolves the authoritative generation and serves semantic-only and hybrid queries. title: bug: cass health recommended_action tells users to run index --full during active rebuild (stampede advice)
description:
Discovered during ibuuh.10.6 (bead v0p2i) test authoring. Comparing cass status --json and cass health --json with a seeded rebuild-active state:

CASS STATUS (correct):
  recommended_action = "Index rebuild is already in progress"
  -- implemented at src/lib.rs::run_status line ~11785: `if rebuild_active { ... }`

CASS HEALTH (buggy, stampede advice):
  recommended_action = "Run 'cass index --full' to rebuild the index/database."
  -- at src/lib.rs::run_health line ~12051, the selector falls through to the !healthy branch at ~12056 because `healthy = !(... && !rebuild_active && ...)`. The conditional at 12051 checks `not_initialized` and `db_degraded` but forgets to check `rebuild_active` first.

Both surfaces also set their respective active-rebuild flag correctly (`rebuild.active=true` in status, `rebuild_progress.active=true` in health), so the buggy recommendation is not because cass failed to detect the rebuild -- it's a missing branch in the text selector.

Repro: see v0p2i probe flow -- seed `.lexical-rebuild-state.json` + hold `index-run.lock` exclusively, then call `cass health --json`. `recommended_action` comes out as the stampede advice.

Fix: add an `if rebuild_active { Some("Index rebuild is already in progress".to_string()) }` arm at the top of the run_health recommended_action selector (line ~12051), mirroring run_status.

Impact: agents polling cass health during a long rebuild will see "run cass index --full", attempt to kick a second run, and either lock-stampede (retryable error) or -- worse -- actually start a concurrent pipeline depending on lock acquisition path.
close_reason: Fixed in 04eadec6: run_health recommended_action now short-circuits on rebuild_active (matching run_status), eliminating stampede advice. Regression test health_recommended_action_during_active_rebuild_says_wait_not_reindex pins the fix; mirrors the existing status sibling test. 5/5 tests/e2e_health.rs tests green.

title: Bind strict-RCH E2E acceptance to one run-scoped remote artifact bundle
description: The comprehensive E2E logging scripts offload Cargo through strict RCH, but RCH's CargoTest retrieval contract intentionally returns only standard coverage/JUnit/criterion outputs and does not return test-results/e2e/**. The scripts then inspect the local checkout, so a full run either fails despite valid remote artifacts or can consume unrelated stale local evidence. Make the run and its evidence one fail-closed provenance unit. Require an explicit validated RCH worker for full acceptance; allocate a collision-free run ID; pass it into every E2E artifact path; keep all prior bundles recoverably; run the test battery and a separate schema/finalization pass on the same worker and source state; produce a run manifest with source SHA/diff digest, worker ID, command, exit, start/end, per-file SHA-256/bytes/events/schema, aggregate histograms and gate results; retrieve only that immutable run directory into an absent local destination; verify the manifest and every digest before publishing the local acceptance report. Never infer success from pre-existing local or remote files, never reuse an unnamespaced test directory, and never silently fall back to local Cargo or another worker.
design: Use a validated, shell-safe RCH worker ID and a validated run ID as explicit inputs. Namespace Rust and shell E2E artifacts under test-results/e2e/runs/<run_id>/ rather than process-global suite paths. Pin both the test battery and a distinct manifest-finalizer/schema gate to the same worker and exact source overlay. The finalizer writes a canonical manifest and completion marker only after all bounded artifacts validate. Transfer with rsync over the configured worker alias into a newly created staging destination; verify allowed relative paths, regular-file/no-link policy, declared file set and hashes before an atomic publish move. Never use rsync --delete, never overwrite another run, and keep prior bundles. If generic RCH cannot expose the worker or raw artifact handoff safely, add a repository-owned Cargo finalizer plus explicit worker contract rather than parsing unversioned human console text.
acceptance_criteria: A no-mock acceptance test starts with contradictory stale local and remote artifacts, runs two concurrent distinct run IDs, and proves each report consumes only its own exact-worker bundle. Missing RCH_WORKER, unavailable SSH/rsync handoff, worker drift between test and finalizer, missing/extra file, changed byte, path traversal/run-ID injection, symlink/hardlink alias, incomplete command, failing underlying test, invalid JSONL, absent receipt, or digest mismatch fails closed with a stable actionable reason. A successful strict-remote run preserves previous evidence, retrieves raw bounded stdout/stderr/cass.log/trace JSONL plus the manifest, verifies all files locally, reports exact source/worker/command identity and returns the underlying Cargo exit. Unit tests cover run-ID/path validation and manifest verification; shell E2E covers transfer and stale-evidence isolation; docs specify retention and recovery. Use only bounded redacted metadata in console output and run UBS, shell syntax, workspace, Clippy and strict remote gates.

title: Wire STYLE_PILL_ACTIVE into filter pill rendering
description:
## Goal
Restore high-signal filter-chip affordances by wiring STYLE_PILL_ACTIVE as true per-pill chip styling (not flat row text).

## Why This Matters
Users rely on active filters to understand search scope at a glance. Flat text weakens affordance clarity and causes missed context.

## Required Implementation
- Replace generic STYLE_TEXT_PRIMARY usage in active-pill rendering with semantic token-driven chip styling.
- Refactor pill rendering so each active pill is rendered as its own styled span/chip unit.
- Preserve existing click-target geometry and interaction behavior (last_pill_rects) exactly.

## Explicit Decision
- Whole-row background styling can be used only as a short-lived intermediate spike.
- Definition of done requires per-pill chip styling (individual chip backgrounds), not a row-level approximation.

## Tests (Mandatory)
1. test_pill_row_uses_pill_active_token
2. test_pill_active_has_background
