title: Prove end-to-end many-core utilization and machine responsiveness with phase-by-phase benchmarks, crash tests, and rollout gates
description:
BACKGROUND:
The entire point of this track is to stop claiming progress based on micro-optimizations while the real end-to-end process still spends long periods on one core or makes the machine feel bad. The verification bead must therefore prove both throughput and responsiveness, phase by phase, from start to finish.

GOAL:
Build the final evidence pack and rollout gates for end-to-end many-core indexing.

SCOPE:
- Measure phase-by-phase core utilization, queue behavior, search-ready time, fully-settled time, and user-facing responsiveness under representative corpora.
- Compare the old path, improved serial path, and segment-farm path where applicable.
- Include crash/restart, attach-to-progress, and degraded-mode scenarios so throughput gains do not hide safety regressions.
- Encode rollout gates that require both materially better core utilization and preserved responsiveness.

DONE WHEN:
Future agents can answer, with artifacts rather than anecdotes, whether cass now uses many cores end-to-end and whether it does so without freezing the machine.
design:
DESIGN / JUSTIFICATION:
- This verification bead exists to stop wishful thinking. Improvements only count if phase-by-phase evidence shows many-core use from start to finish while responsiveness remains within stated limits.
- Compare baseline, improved-serial, and parallel or shard-farm paths where available so future agents can see which architectural moves actually paid off.
- Treat crash, restart, attach, and degraded-mode behavior as first-class rollout criteria because performance wins that break reliability are not wins.
- Encode rollout gates explicitly so release decisions do not depend on oral history from this session.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Artifact-backed benchmark and profiling results exist for representative corpora, including phase timings, CPU-core utilization by phase, queue behavior, search-ready time, fully-settled time, and user-visible responsiveness metrics.
- Crash, restart, attach-to-progress, degraded-mode, and controller-limited scenarios are exercised and documented well enough to support rollout decisions.
- Rollout gates explicitly state what counts as success, what regressions block rollout, and how future agents should rerun or extend the evidence pack.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION / FUTURE-SELF NOTES:
- Preserve the corpus definitions, machine assumptions, controller settings, and measurement commands alongside the evidence so future comparisons stay honest.
- Prefer before-and-after artifacts that can be re-read quickly over one-off anecdotal observations in chat history.
- If a future release note cannot answer "does indexing now use many cores end-to-end without making the machine feel bad?" from these artifacts, this bead is incomplete.
close_reason: Added an artifact-backed many-core rollout gate row that preserves phase utilization, search-ready improvement, foreground responsiveness, controller-limited settling, and pass/fail verdict snapshots.

Evidence should include truthful status or health or robot output, shadow or compare or demotion behavior from the late controller path, and clear explanation of why cass chose the active strategy.
- Required validation should include comprehensive unit and integration coverage plus multiple CLI or robot E2E scripts that capture search-ready versus fully-settled timing, interactive latency under load, attach-to-progress behavior, rollback or old-good fallback evidence, and preserved structured logs or artifacts sufficient for release gating.

- Final rollout proof should now also cover artifact-retention and disk-safety behavior for the shard-farm architecture: scratch generations, quarantined shards, superseded generations, and deferred compaction debt must remain inspectable and reclaimable without threatening the current good index.
- Required evidence should include disk-footprint snapshots, dry-run cleanup or reclaimability output where applicable, and release-gate artifacts showing that the many-core design improves throughput without turning storage management into a user hazard.

- Final rollout proof should explicitly exercise effective-setting introspection and override precedence for the many-core path: if a run was pinned to serial, allowed to go parallel, demoted for safety, or placed in shadow mode, the evidence pack should show both the realized behavior and the effective-setting source that authorized it.
- This matters for trust: users need to be able to explain whether cass behaved conservatively because of defaults, environment overrides, CLI flags, or persisted policy.

title: [MEDIUM] mock-finder: pages include_pwa config flag accepted but no PWA artifacts generated
description:
Mock-code-finder finding — same shape as the recently-closed bead
coding_agent_session_search-adyyt (include_attachments).

## The mock surface
\`src/pages/config_input.rs\` exposes \`include_pwa: bool\` in three
places (BundleConfig field + ResolvedBundle field + Default init)
and includes it in the docstring example JSON + the
\`example_config()\` output. The value flows from JSON config into
\`to_resolved\`:

\`\`\`rust
// src/pages/config_input.rs:574
bundle: ResolvedBundle {
    title: self.bundle.title.clone(),
    description: self.bundle.description.clone(),
    include_pwa: self.bundle.include_pwa,    // ← set here
    hide_metadata: self.bundle.hide_metadata,
},
\`\`\`

That is the ONLY place \`include_pwa\` is written beyond the Default
initializer. Grep for consumers:

\`\`\`bash
\$ rg -n '\\.include_pwa\\b|bundle\\.include_pwa' src/
src/pages/config_input.rs:574:                include_pwa: self.bundle.include_pwa,
# (no other hits)
\`\`\`

The resolved field is never read. No code path checks
\`resolved.bundle.include_pwa\` or \`bundle.include_pwa\` to decide
whether to emit a service worker, write a \`manifest.json\`, inject
a \`<link rel=\"manifest\">\` tag, or anything else PWA-related.

## Verification that PWA output is NOT generated
\`\`\`bash
\$ rg -n 'service.worker|service_worker|sw\\.js|\"manifest.json\"|PWA|ProgressiveWeb' src/pages/ src/html_export/
# no hits
\`\`\`

No \`manifest.webmanifest\`/\`sw.js\`/\`<link rel=\"manifest\">\` ever
appears in the generated HTML archive. Setting
\`include_pwa: true\` in the JSON config has ZERO observable effect
on the output.

## Why this is a mock
The name \`include_pwa\` is a user-facing promise: PWA support would
mean the exported HTML is installable as a Progressive Web App
(offline cache, home-screen install, etc.). Operators setting it
to \`true\` will reasonably expect those artifacts. They don't
get them. No error, no warning — just silent no-op.

Same textbook mock pattern as \`include_attachments\` (closed in
bead adyyt, commit 1ebf2709): config field is accepted, serialized,
propagated through layers, and then dropped on the floor.

## Impact
MEDIUM. Unlike adyyt which also had a hard rejection at runtime,
this one is more insidious: the export succeeds with the flag set,
the JSON output validates, and operators may ship archives
believing they're PWA-installable when they aren't. No error
surface ever tells them otherwise.

## Suggested completion
Same two-option playbook as adyyt:

### Option 1 — Remove (recommended, narrow scope)
Delete the field end-to-end, same pattern as adyyt (commit 1ebf2709,
7 files, +16/-200). Surface to cull:
- \`src/pages/config_input.rs\`: ResolvedBundle field + BundleConfig
  field + Default init + to_resolved mapping + docstring example +
  example_config JSON
- Any tests/fixtures that set \`include_pwa\`: tests/pages_wizard.rs,
  tests/pages_pipeline_e2e.rs, tests/e2e_pages.rs (quick check
  shows include_pwa appears in the fixtures the same way
  include_attachments did; confirm and remove in the same pass)
- Any docs / example configs in README.md / docs/ that mention the
  field

### Option 2 — Implement PWA support
Much larger: add a service-worker template (cache-first for the
exported HTML + assets, fall-through for navigation), a
\`manifest.webmanifest\` generator (name / short_name / icons /
start_url / display), inject \`<link rel=\"manifest\">\` and
\`<script>navigator.serviceWorker.register(...)</script>\` into the
exported HTML when \`resolved.bundle.include_pwa=true\`. Add tests
that scrape the output HTML for these markers.

Option 1 ships in ~45 min. Option 2 is a multi-day feature.

## Severity
MEDIUM — silent no-op on a user-visible flag. Fix is mechanical
(option 1). Future PWA feature work can re-introduce the flag
with end-to-end tests at that time.

title: Add cass doctor backups list, verify, and restore commands
description:
Background: repair without visible backups is not trustworthy. Users need to inspect what backups exist, verify their checksums and sidecars, rehearse restores safely, and restore intentionally if a repair or external event goes wrong. The safest restore UX is to prove a backup in an isolated candidate directory before touching the live archive.

Scope: define backup root layout, backup metadata, DB/WAL/SHM bundle capture, config/bookmark inclusion rules, checksum manifests, list output, verify output, restore rehearsal, and restore command semantics. Rehearsal must rebuild into a temp/candidate dir, verify manifests/checksums, open the DB through frankensqlite, run read-only queries plus rollback-only probes when safe, and emit logs proving the live archive was untouched. Live restore must be explicit, fingerprinted, and must create a backup of the pre-restore current state.

Acceptance criteria: backups list shows age, coverage, asset classes, and verification status; verify detects missing sidecars/checksum drift; rehearsal is the easy safe default and produces detailed artifact logs; live restore refuses unsafe targets and records a receipt; no backup is deleted by restore. Unit tests cover manifest validation, sidecar mismatch, path traversal, restore target refusal, frankensqlite open/probe behavior, and checksum drift. E2E scripts cover list, verify, rehearsal, failed rehearsal, and fingerprint-approved restore against fixture data only.

title: Expose provider source-discovery callback for raw-mirror preparse capture
description:
Background: coding_agent_session_search-9dfb0 now captures explicit file roots before parser execution and has a safe Codex directory-root preflight, but the remaining cross-provider gap cannot be honestly closed from CASS alone. franken-agent-detection is currently pinned as a git dependency (Cargo.toml rev b0c44f23...), and its Connector trait exposes parsed conversations but not an authoritative pre-parse list of source files. Without such a callback, CASS can only mirror non-Codex directory-root files after parse succeeds, which defeats the sole-copy protection goal for parser failures.

Goal: add an authoritative provider source-discovery contract to the FAD/CASS boundary so CASS can mirror every raw source file a connector is about to parse before parser code can drop, skip, or fail on it. This must cover local detected roots, configured local/remote roots, streaming index, batch index, and watch reindex paths.

Design direction: prefer adding an upstream FAD API such as Connector::discover_source_files(&ScanContext) -> Result<Vec<DiscoveredSourceFile>> or a scan_with_source_callback variant that emits source-file events before parse. The event payload should include provider slug, scan root identity, source path, source role/type (primary session log, message shard, metadata sidecar, sqlite/db file, attachment/part file if required), origin/source metadata if available, mtime/size when cheaply known, and whether the file is required for reconstructing the conversation. CASS should consume this event stream and call raw_mirror::capture_source_file before invoking parse. If the upstream dependency remains git-pinned, this bead must include updating Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock to the new reviewed rev and documenting the rev boundary.

Safety constraints: do not add broad catch-all home-directory mirroring. Each connector must enumerate only files it actually treats as session evidence. Enumeration must not follow symlinks, must surface unreadable/deleted files as diagnostics without writing partial manifests, must respect since_ts filtering where the connector scan would, and must preserve current connector identity/external-id behavior. Multi-file connectors such as OpenCode/Cline/Cursor-like sources need explicit modeling of the file set needed for reconstruction instead of pretending a single parsed conversation source_path is enough.

title: [Task] Opt 8.3: Benchmark streaming indexing memory usage
description:
# Task: Benchmark Streaming Indexing Memory Usage

## Objective

Measure peak RSS reduction from streaming backpressure indexing.

## Expected Impact

From PLAN:
- Current peak RSS: 295 MB
- Target: ~100-150 MB
- Reduction: 50%+

## Benchmark Protocol

### 1. Peak RSS Measurement

Use `/usr/bin/time -v` to measure peak RSS:

```bash
# Batch mode
CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=0 /usr/bin/time -v cass index --full 2>&1 | grep "Maximum resident"

# Streaming mode
CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=1 /usr/bin/time -v cass index --full 2>&1 | grep "Maximum resident"
```

### 2. Memory Profile Over Time

Use `memory_profiler` or similar to track memory over indexing:

```bash
# Record memory profile
heaptrack cass index --full
heaptrack_print heaptrack.cass.*.gz > profile.txt
```

### 3. Large Corpus Stress Test

Create large test corpus to stress memory:

```bash
# Generate 10,000 conversations
cargo run --release -- generate-test-corpus --size 10000

# Index with batch mode
CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=0 /usr/bin/time -v cass index --corpus test_corpus

# Index with streaming mode
CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=1 /usr/bin/time -v cass index --corpus test_corpus
```

### 4. Indexing Throughput Comparison

Streaming may have slight overhead:

```bash
# Batch mode throughput
CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=0 cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- index

# Streaming mode throughput
CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=1 cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- index
```

Acceptable overhead: < 10% slower throughput for 50%+ memory reduction.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Peak RSS reduced by > 40%
- [ ] Memory stays bounded during indexing
- [ ] Throughput overhead < 10%
- [ ] Large corpus (10k+ convs) doesn't OOM
- [ ] Documentation updated with results

## Note on Priority

From PLAN:
> This is P3 (low priority) because:
> - Current memory usage (295 MB) is acceptable
> - Higher complexity and risk
> - Other optimizations provide more immediate value
> - Consider only for memory-constrained environments

title: Extend doctor coverage to multi-machine sources and sync gaps
description:
Background: cass supports multi-machine search and sources.toml, so archive safety is not only local ~/.codex or ~/.claude state. A user may have remote source paths, stale sync state, unreachable SSH hosts, ambiguous remote identities, or mirrored local copies that are now the only surviving evidence. Doctor v2 should make those cases explicit instead of treating them as generic source errors.

Scope: extend source inventory, coverage ledger, health/status fields, and doctor reports to classify local sources, configured remote sources, last successful sync, missing remote source files, unreachable hosts, stale remote indexes, local archive ahead of remote, remote copy ahead with verified checksums, ambiguous remote identity, and local mirror-only coverage. Keep remote operations read-only unless the existing sources flow explicitly performs sync. Provide recommended actions that distinguish run sources sync, inspect remote, reconstruct from mirror, verify remote identity, and no action needed.

Acceptance criteria: doctor check and status can report multi-machine coverage risk without blocking local archive recovery; robot JSON exposes remote_source_state and sync_staleness where known; docs explain that cass-owned mirror and DB evidence remain precious even when remotes disappear. Unit tests cover remote state classification and authority/refusal decisions. E2E fixtures or integration scripts cover remote source present/local mirror missing, local archive ahead of remote, remote copy ahead with verified checksums, ambiguous remote identity, SSH/source unavailable, stale sync, remote source pruned, and local mirror preserved states. Logs identify which machine/source is authoritative, which evidence was rejected, and why no live remote data was mutated.

title: P4.2: GitHub Pages Deployment
description:
# GitHub Pages Deployment

**Parent Phase:** Phase 4: Wizard & Deployment
**Depends On:** P4.1 (Interactive Wizard)
**Duration:** 2-3 days

## Goal

Implement deployment to GitHub Pages via gh CLI, including repository creation and Pages configuration.

## Technical Approach

### New Module: src/pages/deploy_github.rs

### Deployment Flow

1. Check Prerequisites
   - gh CLI installed
   - gh auth status passes
   - Network connectivity

2. Create Repository (if needed)
   gh repo create <name> --public --description "..."

3. Clone to Temp Directory
   git clone <repo-url> temp-dir

4. Copy Bundle Contents
   - Clear existing files
   - Copy site/ directory contents
   - Create .nojekyll file
   - Add robots.txt

5. Commit and Push (Orphan Branch)
   git checkout --orphan gh-pages
   git add -A
   git commit -m "Deploy cass archive"
   git push -f origin gh-pages

6. Enable GitHub Pages
   gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -X POST \
      -f source.branch=gh-pages -f source.path=/

7. Return URL
   https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>

### Prerequisites Struct

struct Prerequisites {
    gh_cli: Option<String>,        // Version if installed
    gh_authenticated: bool,
    disk_space_mb: u64,
    estimated_size_mb: u64,
}

### Error Handling

- gh not installed: Provide install instructions
- Not authenticated: Prompt to run gh auth login
- Network error: Retry with exponential backoff
- Repo exists: Ask to overwrite or use different name

### GitHub Pages Limits

- Site size: Max 1 GB
- Per-file: Max 100 MiB (warn at 50 MiB)
- Bandwidth: 100 GB/month soft limit

### Exit Criteria

1. Repository created successfully
2. Files pushed to gh-pages branch
3. Pages enabled via API
4. URL returned and accessible
5. Error messages helpful
6. Prerequisites checked first
close_reason: Implemented GitHubDeployer with: prerequisites checking (gh/git CLI), size validation (1GB limit, 100MiB per file), repository creation, git clone/push to gh-pages branch, Pages API enable. Includes 5 unit tests.

title: Short-circuit redact_text with RegexSet pre-check in indexer/redact_secrets.rs
description:
FILE: src/indexer/redact_secrets.rs (lines 89-98)

CURRENT COST:
```rust
pub fn redact_text(input: &str) -> String {
    let mut output = input.to_string();          // unconditional allocation
    for pat in SECRET_PATTERNS.iter() {          // 12 patterns
        output = pat.regex.replace_all(&output, REDACTED).into_owned();
    }
    output
}
```

Called on every message content string (and recursively via redact_json on every string in tool-result JSON) during indexing (`map_to_internal`). The overwhelming majority of messages contain NO secrets, but we still:
  1. Always allocate `input.to_string()` up front.
  2. Run all 12 regex scans sequentially over the full text.
  3. Each `replace_all(...).into_owned()` allocates a new String on every iteration, even when no match.

At scale this is called once per message across hundreds of thousands of messages.

PROPOSED CHANGE:
1. Build a `Lazy<RegexSet>` matching the same 12 patterns as `SECRET_PATTERNS`. RegexSet compiles to a single Aho-Corasick-like scan over all patterns and returns which (if any) matched in one pass. See `regex::RegexSet`.
2. In redact_text, first call `SECRET_SET.matches(input)`. If `matched_any()` is false (the common case), return `Cow::Borrowed(input)` — no allocation, no scans.
3. If some patterns matched, only run `replace_all` for the subset of SECRET_PATTERNS whose indices are in `matches.iter()`. This reuses the existing regex instances.
4. Change the return type to `Cow<'_, str>` (or keep `String` and call `.into_owned()` on callers — trivial since most callers already convert).

EXPECTED WIN:
For message content WITHOUT secrets (95%+ of indexed content), eliminate 12 full regex scans + 12 String allocations per message. On a corpus of 500k messages that is a meaningful indexing throughput improvement — potentially 5-10x speedup in the redaction step, which becomes the bottleneck in tight indexing loops.

VERIFICATION:
1. Existing tests in src/indexer/redact_secrets.rs must all pass unchanged (behavior is identical, only allocation pattern changes).
2. Add a micro-benchmark to `benches/index_perf.rs` comparing `redact_text("harmless content")` before and after — should drop from ~O(12 scans) to ~O(1 set scan).
3. Spot-check: pick a fixture with known secrets and verify the output is byte-identical to the current implementation.
close_reason: Optimized redact_text with RegexSet pre-check, Cow no-allocation harmless path, matched-subset replacement, and benchmark coverage.

title: P4.1d: robots.txt & SEO Prevention Files
description:
# P4.1d: robots.txt & SEO Prevention Files

**Parent Phase:** Phase 4: Wizard & Deployment
**Section Reference:** Plan Document Section 10, line 2511
**Depends On:** P4.1a (Bundle Builder)

## Goal

Generate SEO prevention files to discourage search engine indexing of encrypted archives.

## Why This Matters

Even though archives are encrypted:
- Search engines may index the auth page URL
- Auth pages leak metadata (title, fingerprint)
- Best practice is to discourage crawling

## Files to Generate

### robots.txt

```
# cass archive - encrypted content, indexing not useful
User-agent: *
Disallow: /
```

### Meta Tags (already in index.html)

```html
<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">
```

### X-Robots-Tag Header (via Service Worker)

```javascript
// In sw.js addSecurityHeaders()
headers.set('X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex, nofollow');
```

## Implementation

```rust
// In src/pages/bundle.rs

fn generate_robots_txt(site_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    let content = r#"# cass archive - encrypted content
# Indexing is not useful and may expose metadata
User-agent: *
Disallow: /
"#;
    
    fs::write(site_dir.join("robots.txt"), content)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## Test Cases

1. robots.txt created in site/ directory
2. Content disallows all crawlers
3. Service Worker adds X-Robots-Tag header
4. Meta tag present in index.html

## Files to Modify

- `src/pages/bundle.rs` (add robots.txt generation)
- `web/public/sw.js` (add X-Robots-Tag header)

## Exit Criteria

1. robots.txt generated with correct content
2. All three layers of SEO prevention active
3. No leakage of sensitive metadata to search engines
close_reason: All 3 layers of SEO prevention are now active: 1) robots.txt generated by bundle.rs, 2) meta robots tag in index.html, 3) X-Robots-Tag header added to sw.js addSecurityHeaders() function

title: Build interactive host selection UI
description:
# Build interactive host selection UI

## What
Create a terminal-based interactive UI for users to select which SSH hosts to 
configure as remote sources. Must handle rich multi-line display, filtering,
and various host states.

## Why
The core UX principle of this feature is "opt-in selection." Users should:
1. See all available hosts with rich context at a glance
2. Understand the state of each host before selecting
3. Quickly find hosts in large lists (10+ hosts)
4. Have full control over what gets configured

A well-designed selection UI is the difference between "configuration wizard" 
and "annoying automation."

## Visual Design

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Select hosts to configure as remote sources                                │
│  ↑/↓ navigate • Space toggle • / search • a all • n none • Enter confirm   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  [x] css                                                    ✓ Ready to sync │
│      209.145.54.164 • ubuntu 22.04 • 45GB free                              │
│      ✓ cass v0.1.50 • 1,234 sessions indexed                                │
│      Claude ✓  Codex ✓  Cursor ✓  Gemini ✓                                  │
│                                                                             │
│  [x] csd                                                    ✓ Ready to sync │
│      144.126.137.164 • ubuntu 22.04 • 32GB free                             │
│      ✓ cass v0.1.49 • 567 sessions indexed                                  │
│      Claude ✓  Codex ✓  Cursor ✗  Gemini ✓                                  │
│                                                                             │
│  [ ] trj                                                    ⚠ Needs install │
│      100.91.120.17 • ubuntu 20.04 • 128GB free                              │
│      ✗ cass not installed (will install via cargo)                          │
│      Claude ✓  Codex ✗  Cursor ✗  Gemini ✗                                  │
│                                                                             │
│  [ ] yto                                                    ⚠ Needs install │
│      37.187.75.150 • ubuntu 22.04 • 89GB free                               │
│      ✗ cass not installed (will install via cargo)                          │
│      Claude ✓  Codex ✗  Cursor ✗  Gemini ✗                                  │
│                                                                             │
│  [─] fmd                                                    ✗ Unreachable   │
│      51.222.245.56 • connection timed out                                   │
│      Cannot probe - check SSH configuration                                  │
│                                                                             │
│  [=] work-laptop                                            ═ Already setup │
│      192.168.1.50 • already configured in sources.toml                      │
│      Use 'cass sources edit' to modify                                       │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  3 selected: 2 ready to sync, 1 needs install (~3 min)
  Press Enter to continue or Esc to cancel
```

## Host States & Display

### State Legend
| Symbol | State | Selectable | Pre-selected |
|--------|-------|------------|--------------|
| `[x]` / `[ ]` | Selectable host | Yes | Based on status |
| `[─]` | Unreachable | No | N/A |
| `[=]` | Already configured | No | N/A |

### Pre-selection Logic
- Hosts with cass indexed AND agent data: **pre-selected** (ready to sync)
- Hosts with cass not indexed: **pre-selected** (quick to index)
- Hosts without cass: **not pre-selected** (requires install confirmation)
- Unreachable/already-configured: **not selectable**

### Status Badges (right-aligned)
- `✓ Ready to sync` - cass installed + indexed
- `⚡ Needs indexing` - cass installed, index empty/missing
- `⚠ Needs install` - cass not found
- `✗ Unreachable` - SSH connection failed
- `═ Already setup` - in sources.toml already

## Keyboard Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| ↑/↓ or j/k | Navigate up/down |
| Space | Toggle selection on current item |
| Enter | Confirm selection |
| Esc or q | Cancel |
| a | Select all (selectable hosts) |
| n | Deselect all |
| / | Start search/filter mode |
| Esc (in search) | Exit search mode |

### Search/Filter Mode
For users with many hosts, pressing `/` enters filter mode:
```
┌─ Filter: css_ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Showing 2 of 12 hosts matching "css"                                      │
│                                                                             │
│  [x] css                                                    ✓ Ready to sync │
│      ...                                                                    │
│  [ ] css-staging                                            ⚠ Needs install │
│      ...                                                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Implementation

### Data Structures
```rust
pub struct SelectableHost {
    pub probe_result: HostProbeResult,
    pub state: HostState,
    pub selected: bool,
    pub display_lines: Vec<String>,  // Pre-rendered ANSI lines
}

pub enum HostState {
    ReadyToSync,      // cass installed + indexed
    NeedsIndexing,    // cass installed, needs index
    NeedsInstall,     // cass not found
    Unreachable,      // SSH failed
    AlreadyConfigured, // in sources.toml
}

pub struct HostSelectionResult {
    pub selected_hosts: Vec<HostProbeResult>,
    pub hosts_needing_install: Vec<HostProbeResult>,
    pub hosts_needing_index: Vec<HostProbeResult>,
    pub estimated_install_time_secs: u64,
    pub cancelled: bool,
}
```

### Selection UI Function
```rust
pub fn run_host_selection(
    probed_hosts: &[HostProbeResult],
    already_configured: &HashSet<String>,
) -> Result<HostSelectionResult, CliError> {
    // 1. Build selectable items with pre-computed display
    let items = build_selectable_hosts(probed_hosts, already_configured);
    
    // 2. Apply pre-selection logic
    let items = apply_preselection(items);
    
    // 3. Run interactive selection
    let selected_indices = run_multiselect(&items)?;
    
    // 4. Build result
    build_selection_result(&items, &selected_indices)
}
```

### Terminal Width Handling
- Minimum width: 60 chars (truncate hostnames)
- Optimal width: 80+ chars (full display)
- Very narrow: fall back to compact single-line mode

### Non-TTY Fallback
If stdin is not a TTY, provide helpful error:
```
Error: Interactive selection requires a terminal.

For non-interactive use:
  cass sources setup --hosts css,csd,yto
  cass sources setup --non-interactive  # select all reachable
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shows all discovered hosts with probe results
- [ ] Multi-line rich display per host (4 lines)
- [ ] Right-aligned status badges
- [ ] Clear visual distinction between host states
- [ ] Pre-selects appropriate hosts based on status
- [ ] Unreachable/already-configured hosts shown but not selectable
- [ ] Space toggles selection
- [ ] Enter confirms, Esc cancels
- [ ] 'a' selects all selectable, 'n' deselects all
- [ ] '/' enables search/filter for large host lists
- [ ] Summary footer updates in real-time
- [ ] Estimated install time shown when applicable
- [ ] Handles terminal resize gracefully
- [ ] Non-TTY gives helpful error message

## Dependencies
- Requires: TUI library (coding_agent_session_search-tlk6)
- Requires: SSH probing (coding_agent_session_search-vxe2)

## Testing
- Test with 1, 5, 20 hosts
- Test narrow terminal (60 chars)
- Test various host state combinations
- Test search with partial matches
- Test non-TTY detection
close_reason: Implemented HostState enum, status badges, probe conversion, run_host_selection(), multi-line display, pre-selection logic, TTY detection. Search/filter deferred. Commit 84ad6dc

title: API Contract Clarity: Predictable, Documented Behavior
description:
# API Contract Clarity

## The Problem
Agents need **certainty** about API behavior:
- What fields will always be present?
- What types are returned?
- What features are available?
- Will the API change?

Current documentation is informal and incomplete.

## The Solution
Make the API **self-documenting** and **introspectable**:
1. Full schema introspection command
2. Capabilities discovery
3. Version negotiation

## Subtasks
1. **rob.api.intro** - Full schema introspection
2. **rob.api.caps** - Capabilities endpoint
3. **rob.api.version** - API versioning

## Value for Agents
- Confidence: Know exactly what to expect
- Adaptation: Discover available features
- Stability: Understand version compatibility

title: Capabilities Endpoint (cass capabilities)
description:
# Capabilities Endpoint (cass capabilities)

## Problem Statement
Agents need to know what features are available:
- Does this version support --fields?
- Is aggregation available?
- What connectors are supported?

## Proposed Solution
Add `cass capabilities` command:
```bash
cass capabilities --json
```

Output:
```json
{
  "crate_version": "0.1.30",
  "api_version": 1,
  "contract_version": "1",
  "features": [
    "json_output",
    "jsonl_output",
    "robot_meta",
    "time_filters",
    "field_selection",
    "aggregations",
    "cursor_pagination"
  ],
  "connectors": [
    "codex", "claude_code", "gemini", "opencode", "amp", "cline"
  ],
  "limits": {
    "max_limit": 1000,
    "max_content_length": 100000,
    "max_fields": 20
  },
  "documentation_url": "https://github.com/..."
}
```

## Design Decisions

### Feature Flags
List individual features so agents can check availability:
```python
if "field_selection" in capabilities["features"]:
    cmd += " --fields source_path,line_number"
```

### Version Numbers
- `crate_version`: Semantic version of the binary
- `api_version`: Integer version of the API contract (bump on breaking changes)
- `contract_version`: Existing robot-docs contract version

### Limits
Expose operational limits so agents don't exceed them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `cass capabilities --json` returns feature list
- [ ] Features list accurately reflects available functionality
- [ ] Version numbers included
- [ ] Limits documented
- [ ] Human-readable output without --json

## Effort Estimate
Low - 1-2 hours. Static information assembly.

title: Full Schema Introspection (cass introspect)
API Versioning Strategy
description:
# API Versioning Strategy

## Problem Statement
As the CLI evolves, agents need to understand compatibility:
- Will my scripts break with the next update?
- How do I handle version differences?
- When are breaking changes introduced?

## Proposed Solution
Formalize versioning strategy:

### API Version Number
Simple integer that increments on breaking changes:
- v1: Current stable API
- v2: Future breaking changes

### Compatibility Promise
- Minor/patch releases: No breaking changes to JSON output
- New fields may be added (additive changes OK)
- Field removal or type changes require version bump

### Version Negotiation
```bash
cass search "query" --json --api-version 1
# If api-version is incompatible, return error with supported versions
```

### Deprecation Warnings
When using deprecated features:
```json
{
  "_warnings": ["--robot flag is deprecated; use --json instead"],
  "hits": [...]
}
```

## Documentation
Add CHANGELOG section specifically for API changes:
- Breaking changes clearly marked
- Migration guides for version transitions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] api_version number in capabilities output
- [ ] Deprecation warnings in JSON output
- [ ] CHANGELOG tracks API changes
- [ ] `--api-version` flag for version negotiation (optional)

## Effort Estimate
Low - 1-2 hours. Mostly documentation and version tracking.

title: Context Window Management: Minimizing Token Consumption
description:
# Context Window Management

## The Problem
AI agents have **limited context windows**. Every token matters. Current search output includes:
- Full message content (often 1000+ chars per hit)
- Verbose snippets with markdown formatting
- Fields the agent may not need (workspace, title when empty)

A typical 10-result search can produce 50KB of JSON. An agent working on a complex task might need to run 5-10 searches, quickly consuming 500KB of context just for search results.

## The Solution
Give agents **precise control** over what fields are returned and how much content is included.

## Impact Analysis
| Scenario | Current Size | With Optimization | Reduction |
|----------|-------------|-------------------|----------|
| 10 hits, full content | ~50KB | ~2KB (paths only) | 96% |
| 10 hits, truncated | ~50KB | ~5KB (200 char limit) | 90% |
| 20 hits, aggregated | ~100KB | ~1KB (counts only) | 99% |

## Subtasks
1. **rob.ctx.fields** - Field selection (--fields) - HIGHEST PRIORITY
2. **rob.ctx.trunc** - Content truncation (--max-content-length)
3. **rob.ctx.tokens** - Token budget (--max-tokens)
4. **rob.ctx.quiet** - Auto-quiet in robot mode

## Implementation Order
1. Auto-quiet (trivial, immediate value)
2. Field selection (high impact, moderate effort)
3. Content truncation (high impact, low effort)
4. Token budget (medium impact, higher effort)

title: Field Selection (--fields flag)
description:
# Field Selection (--fields flag)

## Problem Statement
Current search output includes ALL fields for every hit:
```json
{"score": 4.2, "agent": "claude_code", "workspace": "/long/path", 
 "source_path": "/very/long/path/to/session.jsonl", "snippet": "...",
 "content": "<potentially 10KB of text>", "title": "...", 
 "created_at": 1234567890, "line_number": 42, "match_type": "exact"}
```

Often an agent only needs 2-3 fields:
- Just paths and line numbers to open files
- Just scores to rank results
- Just agents to understand distribution

## Proposed Solution
Add `--fields` flag to select specific fields:
```bash
cass search "error" --json --fields source_path,line_number,score
```

Output:
```json
{"count": 10, "hits": [
  {"source_path": "/path/to/file.jsonl", "line_number": 42, "score": 4.2},
  ...
]}
```

## Design Decisions

### Field Naming
Use exact field names from current schema:
- `score`, `agent`, `workspace`, `source_path`, `snippet`, `content`, `title`, `created_at`, `line_number`, `match_type`

### Special Fields
- `*` or `all` - include all fields (default behavior)
- `minimal` - shorthand for `source_path,line_number,agent`
- `summary` - shorthand for `source_path,line_number,agent,title,score`

### Metadata Fields
Top-level fields (`count`, `limit`, `offset`, `query`) always included. `--fields` only affects `hits` array contents.

### Invalid Fields
Unknown field names produce a warning on stderr but don't fail the command (graceful degradation).

## Implementation Approach

```rust
// In search command args:
#[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',')]
fields: Option<Vec<String>>,

// In output_robot_results():
fn filter_hit_fields(hit: &SearchHit, fields: &Option<Vec<String>>) -> serde_json::Value {
    let all_fields = serde_json::to_value(hit).unwrap();
    match fields {
        None => all_fields,
        Some(field_list) => {
            let mut filtered = serde_json::Map::new();
            for field in field_list {
                if let Some(value) = all_fields.get(field) {
                    filtered.insert(field.clone(), value.clone());
                }
            }
            serde_json::Value::Object(filtered)
        }
    }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--fields source_path` returns only source_path in each hit
- [ ] `--fields source_path,line_number,score` returns exactly those 3 fields
- [ ] `--fields minimal` expands to predefined set
- [ ] `--fields summary` expands to predefined set
- [ ] Unknown fields logged as warning, don't fail command
- [ ] Works with all robot formats (json, jsonl, compact)
- [ ] Update robot-docs schemas to document --fields
- [ ] Add tests for field filtering

## Context Savings Estimate
| Fields Requested | Typical Hit Size | Reduction |
|-----------------|------------------|----------|
| All (default) | ~5KB | 0% |
| source_path,line_number | ~200 bytes | 96% |
| summary preset | ~500 bytes | 90% |

## Effort Estimate
Medium - 2-3 hours. Requires:
- CLI arg parsing
- Field filtering logic
- Preset expansion
- Tests
- Documentation updates

title: Auto-Quiet in Robot Mode
description:
# Auto-Quiet in Robot Mode

## Problem Statement
When using `--json` or `--robot` flags, INFO log messages still appear on stderr:
```
2025-11-30T23:24:37.912929Z  INFO search_start backend="sqlite" query="hello"
{"count": 2, "hits": [...]}
```

While logs go to stderr (correct), many subprocess libraries combine stdout+stderr by default. This means agents using common patterns like Python's `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)` or Node's `execSync` will see logs mixed with JSON.

## Current Workaround
Agents must remember to add `--quiet` flag:
```bash
cass --quiet search "query" --json
```

This is an unnecessary tax on every robot invocation.

## Proposed Solution
When `--json`, `--robot`, or `--robot-format` is specified, automatically suppress INFO-level logs (equivalent to `--quiet`). Only WARN and ERROR logs should appear on stderr in robot mode.

## Implementation
```rust
// In lib.rs, after parsing CLI args:
let effective_quiet = cli.quiet || is_robot_mode(&command);

fn is_robot_mode(cmd: &Commands) -> bool {
    match cmd {
        Commands::Search { json, robot_format, .. } => *json || robot_format.is_some(),
        Commands::Stats { json, .. } => *json,
        Commands::Diag { json, .. } => *json,
        Commands::Index { json, .. } => *json,
        Commands::View { json, .. } => *json,
        _ => false,
    }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `cass search "q" --json 2>&1` produces clean JSON with no log lines
- [ ] `cass search "q" --robot-format jsonl 2>&1` produces clean JSONL
- [ ] WARN/ERROR logs still appear on stderr (for debugging)
- [ ] Explicit `--verbose` overrides auto-quiet
- [ ] Update robot-docs contracts to reflect new behavior
- [ ] Add test: `robot_mode_suppresses_info_logs`

## Effort Estimate
Trivial - 30 minutes. Change is ~10 lines of code.

## Risk Assessment
Low risk. This is purely additive behavior that matches user expectations.

title: Token Budget (--max-tokens)
description:
# Token Budget (--max-tokens)

## Problem Statement
Agents have specific token budgets for tool outputs. Rather than guessing how many results to request or what content length to use, agents should be able to say "give me as much as fits in N tokens."

## Proposed Solution
Add `--max-tokens N` flag for intelligent output limiting:
```bash
cass search "error" --json --max-tokens 2000
```

Output:
```json
{
  "count": 47,
  "returned": 12,
  "truncated": true,
  "token_estimate": 1987,
  "hits": [...]
}
```

## Design Decisions

### Token Estimation
Use simple heuristic: ~4 characters per token (conservative for English text with JSON overhead). Could use tiktoken for accuracy but adds dependency.

### Truncation Strategy
1. Start with all requested hits
2. Estimate total tokens
3. If over budget, progressively:
   a. Truncate content fields
   b. Reduce number of hits
   c. Remove optional fields

### Metadata Preservation
Always include: count, returned, truncated, token_estimate. These don't count against budget.

## Implementation Complexity
This is more complex than simple field selection because it requires:
- Token estimation logic
- Iterative trimming strategy
- Priority ordering of what to cut

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--max-tokens 1000` produces output estimating <1000 tokens
- [ ] `truncated: true` when output was limited
- [ ] `returned` field shows actual hits returned vs total matches
- [ ] `token_estimate` field shows estimated tokens in response
- [ ] Graceful degradation (fewer hits rather than error)

## Effort Estimate
Medium-High - 4-6 hours. Requires token estimation and iterative trimming logic.

## Alternative Considered
Could use external tokenizer (tiktoken) for accuracy, but:
- Adds Python dependency or Rust port
- Simple heuristic is good enough for budgeting
- Can refine estimation later if needed

title: Content Truncation (--max-content-length)
description:
# Content Truncation (--max-content-length)

## Problem Statement
The `content` and `snippet` fields can contain very long text (10KB+ for detailed conversations). Even when an agent wants content, they often only need the first few hundred characters to understand context.

## Proposed Solution
Add `--max-content-length N` flag to truncate text fields:
```bash
cass search "error" --json --max-content-length 200
```

Output:
```json
{"content": "First 200 chars of content...", "content_truncated": true, ...}
```

## Design Decisions

### Which Fields Are Affected
- `content` - main message content
- `snippet` - highlighted excerpt
- `title` - usually short, but truncate if needed

### Truncation Indicator
Add `_truncated` suffix field when content is truncated:
```json
{"content": "truncated...", "content_truncated": true}
```

### UTF-8 Safety
Truncate at character boundaries, not byte boundaries. Ensure valid UTF-8 output.

### Ellipsis
Append `...` when truncating to indicate incompleteness.

## Implementation
```rust
fn truncate_content(s: &str, max_len: usize) -> (String, bool) {
    if s.chars().count() <= max_len {
        (s.to_string(), false)
    } else {
        let truncated: String = s.chars().take(max_len.saturating_sub(3)).collect();
        (format!("{}...", truncated), true)
    }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--max-content-length 100` truncates content to ~100 chars
- [ ] Truncated fields have `_truncated: true` sibling field
- [ ] UTF-8 boundaries respected (no broken characters)
- [ ] Works with `--fields` (truncation applied to selected fields)
- [ ] Ellipsis appended to truncated content
- [ ] Test: various Unicode content truncation

## Effort Estimate
Low - 1-2 hours. Simple string truncation with UTF-8 awareness.

description:
# Workflow Optimization

## The Problem
Agent workflows often follow patterns:
1. Search for something
2. Examine results
3. Refine search or dig deeper
4. Take action on findings

Current CLI requires verbose command sequences with manual state management.

## The Solution
Optimize common workflow patterns:
1. **Aggregations**: Get overview without full results
2. **Context**: Find related sessions
3. **Correlation**: Track multi-step operations
4. **Pagination**: Reliable cursor-based navigation

## Subtasks
1. **rob.flow.agg** - Aggregation mode
2. **rob.flow.context** - Session context command
3. **rob.flow.reqid** - Request ID correlation
4. **rob.flow.cursor** - Cursor-based pagination

## Value for Agents
- Efficiency: Get answers with fewer commands
- Context: Understand relationships between results
- Traceability: Track operations across steps

title: Aggregation Mode (--aggregate)
description:
# Aggregation Mode (--aggregate)

## Problem Statement
Agents often want overview statistics without full results:
- How many errors per agent?
- What workspaces have the most activity?
- What's the time distribution?

Currently requires fetching all results and aggregating client-side, wasting tokens.

## Proposed Solution
Add `--aggregate` flag for server-side aggregation:
```bash
cass search "error" --json --aggregate agent,workspace
```

Output:
```json
{
  "total_matches": 147,
  "aggregations": {
    "agent": {
      "buckets": [
        {"key": "claude_code", "count": 89},
        {"key": "codex", "count": 45},
        {"key": "gemini", "count": 13}
      ]
    },
    "workspace": {
      "buckets": [
        {"key": "/project-a", "count": 50},
        {"key": "/project-b", "count": 40},
        {"key": "<other>", "count": 57}
      ]
    }
  },
  "hits": []  // Empty when aggregating only
}
```

## Design Decisions

### Aggregatable Fields
- `agent` - Group by agent type
- `workspace` - Group by workspace path
- `date` - Group by day/week/month
- `match_type` - Group by exact/wildcard/fuzzy

### Bucket Limits
Default to top 10 buckets per field. Use `<other>` for remainder.

### Combining with Results
- `--aggregate` alone: Only aggregations, no hits
- `--aggregate` with `--limit N`: Both aggregations and N hits

### Performance
Aggregations should be efficient:
- Use SQL GROUP BY where possible
- Cache aggregation results

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--aggregate agent` groups by agent
- [ ] `--aggregate agent,workspace` groups by both
- [ ] Aggregation-only mode returns empty hits array
- [ ] Can combine with --limit for both aggs and hits
- [ ] Top 10 buckets with <other> for overflow
- [ ] Performance: <200ms for aggregation queries

## Context Savings
Aggregation response: ~500 bytes vs ~50KB for full results. **99% reduction!**

## Effort Estimate
Medium - 3-4 hours. Requires SQL GROUP BY queries and result formatting.

title: Session Context Command (cass context)
description:
# Session Context Command (cass context)

## Problem Statement
When an agent finds an interesting result, they often want:
- Other sessions in the same workspace
- Sessions from the same time period
- Related conversations by topic

Currently requires multiple manual searches.

## Proposed Solution
Add `cass context` command to find related sessions:
```bash
cass context /path/to/session.jsonl --json
```

Output:
```json
{
  "source": {
    "path": "/path/to/session.jsonl",
    "agent": "claude_code",
    "workspace": "/myproject",
    "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z"
  },
  "related": {
    "same_workspace": [
      {"path": "...", "title": "...", "created_at": "...", "relevance": 0.9}
    ],
    "same_day": [...],
    "same_agent": [...],
    "similar_content": [...]  // If semantic search available
  }
}
```

## Design Decisions

### Relation Types
1. **same_workspace**: Sessions in same workspace directory
2. **same_day**: Sessions within 24 hours
3. **same_agent**: Sessions from same agent type
4. **similar_content**: Content-based similarity (future)

### Limits
Return top 5 per relation type by default. Configurable with `--limit`.

### Input Flexibility
Accept:
- Full path to session file
- Session ID from search results
- Line number reference (source_path:line)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `cass context <path>` finds related sessions
- [ ] Returns same_workspace, same_day, same_agent relations
- [ ] Relevance scores for ranking
- [ ] Configurable limits per relation type
- [ ] JSON output for automation

## Effort Estimate
Medium - 3-4 hours. Requires relational queries across session metadata.

title: Request ID Correlation (--request-id)
description:
# Request ID Correlation (--request-id)

## Problem Statement
Agents run multi-step workflows:
1. Search for errors
2. Analyze top result
3. Search for related fixes
4. Compile summary

Tracking which response corresponds to which request is error-prone.

## Proposed Solution
Add `--request-id` flag for correlation:
```bash
cass search "error" --json --request-id "step-1-find-errors"
```

Output:
```json
{
  "request_id": "step-1-find-errors",
  "count": 10,
  "hits": [...]
}
```

## Design Decisions

### ID Format
Accept any string. Agent's responsibility to ensure uniqueness.

### Trace Integration
If `--trace-file` is used, include request_id in trace entries for audit correlation.

### No Server State
Request ID is purely for response labeling. No server-side tracking.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--request-id "foo"` includes `request_id: "foo"` in response
- [ ] Works with all output formats
- [ ] Included in trace file entries
- [ ] No validation on ID format (any string)

## Effort Estimate
Trivial - 30 minutes. Pass-through from CLI arg to response.

title: Query Intelligence: Understanding and Improving Queries
description:
# Query Intelligence

## The Problem
Agents often struggle with queries:
1. **Why did this return 0 results?** - Was the query malformed? Too specific?
2. **How was my query interpreted?** - Did it understand my intent?
3. **What would work better?** - Suggestions for improvement

## The Solution
Make the query engine transparent and helpful:
- Explain how queries are parsed and executed
- Suggest alternatives when queries fail
- Allow dry-run validation

## Subtasks
1. **rob.query.explain** - Query explanation (--explain)
2. **rob.query.suggest** - Suggestions and did-you-mean
3. **rob.query.dry** - Dry-run mode (--dry-run)

title: Reliability & Safety: Robust Operation
description:
# Reliability & Safety

## The Problem
Agents need to handle failures gracefully:
- Should I retry this error?
- Will retrying cause duplicate work?
- How long should I wait?

Current error handling provides basic information but lacks recovery guidance.

## The Solution
Enhance error handling with:
1. Idempotency support for safe retries
2. Retry hints in error responses
3. Timeout configuration

## Subtasks
1. **rob.safe.idemp** - Idempotency keys
2. **rob.safe.retry** - Retry hints in errors
3. **rob.safe.timeout** - Timeout configuration

## Value for Agents
- Resilience: Automatic recovery from transient failures
- Safety: No duplicate work from retries
- Predictability: Clear timeout behavior

title: Idempotency Keys
description:
# Idempotency Keys

## Problem Statement
For long-running operations like indexing, agents may need to retry after failures. But retrying could cause duplicate work or inconsistent state.

## Proposed Solution
Add `--idempotency-key` flag for safe retries:
```bash
cass index --full --idempotency-key "idx-2025-01-30-001" --json
```

Behavior:
1. First call: Execute operation, store result with key
2. Subsequent calls with same key: Return cached result
3. Key expiration: 24 hours

Output:
```json
{
  "idempotency_key": "idx-2025-01-30-001",
  "cached": true,
  "original_timestamp": "2025-01-30T10:00:00Z",
  "result": {...}
}
```

## Design Decisions

### Scope
Only for mutating operations:
- `cass index` - Indexing operations
- NOT for reads (search, stats, view)

### Storage
Store idempotency keys in SQLite meta table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE idempotency_keys (
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  result_json TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER,
  expires_at INTEGER
);
```

### Collision Handling
If same key used with different parameters, return error (not cached result).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--idempotency-key` parameter for index command
- [ ] Repeated calls return cached result
- [ ] `cached: true` indicates cached response
- [ ] Keys expire after 24 hours
- [ ] Parameter mismatch returns error

## Effort Estimate
Medium - 2-3 hours. Requires key storage and result caching.

title: Retry Hints in Errors
description:
# Retry Hints in Errors

## Problem Statement
Current error format includes `retryable: bool` but lacks guidance:
- How long to wait before retry?
- How many retries are reasonable?
- What should change between retries?

## Proposed Solution
Enhance error response with retry guidance:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 7,
    "kind": "lock-busy",
    "message": "Database locked by another process",
    "retryable": true,
    "retry_after_ms": 1000,
    "max_retries": 3,
    "retry_hint": "Wait for other process to complete"
  }
}
```

## New Fields

### retry_after_ms
Suggested delay before retry in milliseconds.
- Lock errors: 1000ms
- Rate limits: 5000ms
- Transient failures: 500ms

### max_retries
Recommended maximum retry attempts.
- Lock errors: 3
- Network errors: 5
- Permanent errors: 0 (not retryable)

### retry_hint
Human/agent-readable suggestion for recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `retry_after_ms` in retryable errors
- [ ] `max_retries` recommendation
- [ ] `retry_hint` with actionable guidance
- [ ] Values appropriate per error type
- [ ] Update robot-docs error schema

## Effort Estimate
Low - 1-2 hours. Enhance existing error construction.

title: Timeout Configuration
description:
# Timeout Configuration

## Problem Statement
Agents need predictable timing:
- How long will this command take?
- Can I set a maximum wait time?
- What happens on timeout?

## Proposed Solution
Add `--timeout` flag for time-bounded operations:
```bash
cass search "query" --json --timeout 5000  # 5 second timeout
```

On timeout:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 10,
    "kind": "timeout",
    "message": "Operation timed out after 5000ms",
    "retryable": true,
    "partial_results": true
  },
  "hits": [...]  // Partial results if available
}
```

## Design Decisions

### Timeout Scope
- Search: Query execution time
- Index: Per-session processing time
- View: File read time

### Partial Results
Where possible, return partial results gathered before timeout.

### Default
No default timeout (backward compatible). Agents opt-in.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--timeout N` parameter in milliseconds
- [ ] Timeout error with code 10
- [ ] Partial results when available
- [ ] Works for search, index, view commands

## Effort Estimate
Medium - 2-3 hours. Requires async timeout handling.

title: State Awareness: Knowing System Status
description:
# State Awareness

## The Problem
Agents operate blind:
- Is the index up-to-date or stale?
- When was the last indexing run?
- Are there pending sessions to index?
- Is the cache warm?

Without this information, agents might:
- Search stale data and miss recent conversations
- Unnecessarily re-index when not needed
- Not know when to retry operations

## The Solution
Expose system state through:
1. Dedicated status command
2. Freshness metadata in search responses
3. Health check endpoint for quick validation

## Subtasks
1. **rob.state.status** - Status command
2. **rob.state.meta** - Index freshness in robot-meta
3. **rob.state.health** - Health check endpoint

## Value for Agents
- Confidence: Know when to trust search results
- Efficiency: Only index when needed
- Debugging: Understand why results might be incomplete

title: [HIGH] session-review of gi4oy: skip_db_open masks corrupt-DB scenario when path is a directory
description: Session-wide deep review finding. Regression introduced by gi4oy (f3dcce6d): skip_db_open optimistic path branched on (skip_db_open + db_exists). exists() returns true for BOTH regular files AND directories. tests/cli_robot.rs:2725::health_json_reports_open_error_for_unopenable_db_path creates a DIRECTORY at the DB path and asserts db.opened=false / open_error / healthy=false / status=degraded. Post-gi4oy that test FAILS — skip branch synthesized opened=true regardless. A directory-at-DB-path reported healthy=true through cass health. Fix: capture db_metadata once, derive .len() AND .is_file(), guard the skip-open branch with db_is_regular_file. If DB path exists but is not a regular file, fall through to probe_state_db which surfaces opened=false + open_error. Preserves gi4oy perf for normal DB files; restores integrity contract for corrupt scenarios.

title: OMP XDG classifier vs resume test: custom XDG_DATA_HOME stores are undetectable; two lib tests red with full root-cause
description: Two deterministic lib reds share one design conflict plus one lifecycle question, root-caused 2026-08-25 (MossyBridge). (1) cli_read_db_tests::resume_preserves_omp_xdg_session_root (authored b637c479) writes <tmp>/xdg/omp/sessions/-projects-cass/<ts>_id.jsonl and expects agent=omp, but has_xdg_omp_layout_marker (hardened later in the profile-provenance wave) only matches the literal .local/share/omp/{sessions,profiles/<name>} windows, so ANY custom XDG_DATA_HOME (which is user-configurable) makes an OMP store undetectable to resume — the test's premise is right for real users, the classifier's strictness comment only argued against bare .omp-substring theft in mirror names. Proposed narrow loosening that preserves the anti-theft rule: also accept windows [omp, sessions, <dash-prefixed sanitized cwd>] and [omp, profiles, <valid profile name>] — requires the store-internal chain, not a stray ancestor; pi precedence in owner() is unaffected (pi markers are checked first). Not landed unilaterally because the strict form carries a deliberate design comment from the hardening wave. (2) storage::sqlite::tests::legacy_remote_omp_reclassification_rejects_non_mirror_lookalikes fails EARLIER than its reclassification assertions: assert_eq!(old_lookup_exists, 1) at sqlite.rs:30750 sees 0 — conversation_external_lookup is no longer populated inline at insert for the remote fixture (fails in isolation, so not the ambient-defer race fixed in 8023e92d). Either the lookup lifecycle became lazy/rehydrating in the storage wave and the expectation is stale, or inline population regressed; whoever owns the external-lookup lifecycle should decide which.

Item 2 (conversation_external_lookup no longer populated inline at insert; lookalike test fails at its precondition) remains open for the external-lookup lifecycle owner.

The lookalike test's precondition asserted the retired table and failed before its real refusal assertions; it now reads the live tail table. With this the full cass lib suite is green.

title: [EPIC] Performance Optimization Round 1: Semantic Search 20-30x Speedup
description:
# Performance Optimization Round 1: Semantic Search Pipeline

## Overview

This epic tracks the implementation of high-impact performance optimizations identified through rigorous profiling and analysis. The primary goal is achieving a **20-30x speedup** on semantic (vector) search while preserving exact search semantics.

## Strategic Context

CASS (Coding Agent Session Search) indexes conversations from Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, Gemini, Aider, and other coding agents into a unified, searchable index. Performance is critical for:
- Interactive TUI responsiveness (target: <50ms for any search)
- Robot mode for AI agents consuming search results programmatically
- Batch operations like multi-machine sync and bulk indexing

## The Problem: 56ms Vector Search Latency

Profiling revealed the **semantic search path is the primary bottleneck**:
- `vector_index_search_50k`: **56.1ms** (vs 10.5µs for lexical search)
- Root cause: O(n×d) linear scan over 50k vectors with 384 dimensions each
- Additional overhead: F16→F32 conversion per dot product element

## The Solution: Three-Stage Optimization Chain

By combining three complementary optimizations, we achieve multiplicative speedups:

1. **F16 Pre-Convert** (56ms → 30ms): Eliminate per-query F16→F32 conversion by pre-converting at load time
2. **SIMD Dot Product** (30ms → 10-15ms): Explicit AVX2/SSE vectorization using `wide` crate
3. **Parallel Search** (10-15ms → 2-3ms): Rayon parallel scan with thread-local heaps

## Hard Constraints (from AGENTS.md)

All implementations MUST follow these non-negotiables:
- NO FILE DELETION without explicit permission
- Cargo only; Rust edition 2024 nightly
- After substantive changes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`
- One lever per change; no unrelated refactors
- Include rollback guidance (env vars for each optimization)

## Equivalence Oracle

For optimization verification, outputs must match:
1. **Vector search**: Same (message_id, chunk_idx) set returned. Scores may differ by ~1e-7 relative error due to FP reordering with SIMD - acceptable for ranking.
2. **RRF fusion**: Deterministic tie-breaking by SearchHitKey ordering (already implemented).
3. **Canonicalization**: Byte-for-byte identical output (test with content_hash).

## Success Metrics

| Metric | Before | After | Validation |
|--------|--------|-------|------------|
| `vector_index_search_50k` | 56.1ms | 2-3ms | `cargo bench --bench vector_perf` |
| Memory (50k F16 vectors) | 38.4 MB | 76.8 MB | Acceptable 2x for 20x speedup |
| Search results | Baseline | Identical | Equivalence oracle tests |

## Rollback Strategy

Each optimization has an env var to disable:
- `CASS_F16_PRECONVERT=0`: Keep F16 storage, convert per-query
- `CASS_SIMD_DOT=0`: Fall back to scalar dot product
- `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH=0`: Use sequential scan
- `CASS_LAZY_FIELDS=0`: Hydrate all fields regardless of request
- `CASS_REGEX_CACHE=0`: Disable wildcard regex caching
- `CASS_STREAMING_CANONICALIZE=0`: Use original canonicalize function
- `CASS_SQLITE_CACHE=0`: Disable ID caching

## Dependencies and Ordering

The P0 optimizations form a critical dependency chain:
- SIMD dot product benefits most AFTER F16 pre-convert (same data type throughout)
- Parallel search benefits most AFTER SIMD (parallelizing already-fast operation)

P1/P2/P3 optimizations are largely independent and can proceed in parallel.

title: P4.1a: Bundle Builder & Static Site Generator
description:
# P4.1a: Bundle Builder & Static Site Generator

## Goal
Build the deployable static site bundle (site/) plus the private offline artifacts (private/) from an encrypted export. Output must match the chunked AEAD format and be safe for public hosting (GitHub Pages / Cloudflare Pages) with no secrets in site/.

## Output Structure (Split Output)

```
cass-pages-export/
├── site/                       # DEPLOY THIS (public)
│   ├── index.html              # Auth UI + app shell (no inline scripts)
│   ├── .nojekyll               # Disable Jekyll
│   ├── robots.txt              # Disallow crawling
│   ├── config.json             # Public params + payload manifest (no secrets)
│   ├── integrity.json          # sha256 + size for each public file
│   ├── payload/                # Chunked AEAD ciphertext (ALWAYS used)
│   │   ├── chunk-00000.bin
│   │   ├── chunk-00001.bin
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── blobs/                  # Optional encrypted attachment blobs
│   │   ├── sha256-abc123.bin
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── sw.js                   # COOP/COEP service worker
│   ├── viewer.js               # Main app logic
│   ├── auth.js                 # Auth flow
│   ├── search.js               # Search UI
│   ├── conversation.js         # Conversation rendering
│   ├── styles.css              # Tailwind-based styles
│   ├── vendor/
│   │   ├── sqlite3.js
│   │   ├── sqlite3.wasm
│   │   ├── sqlite3-opfs.js
│   │   ├── argon2-wasm.js
│   │   ├── argon2-wasm.wasm
│   │   ├── fflate.min.js
│   │   ├── marked.min.js
│   │   ├── prism.min.js
│   │   ├── dompurify.min.js
│   │   └── html5-qrcode.min.js
│   ├── assets/
│   │   ├── logo.svg
│   │   └── icons.svg
│   └── README.md               # Public archive description (no secrets)
└── private/                    # NEVER DEPLOY (offline storage only)
    ├── recovery-secret.txt
    ├── qr-code.png
    ├── qr-code.svg
    ├── integrity-fingerprint.txt
    └── master-key.json         # Optional encrypted DEK backup
```

Notes:
- No archive.enc or encrypted.bin. All exports use chunked AEAD in payload/.
- config.json is public and contains only parameters (no secrets or labels).
- index.html must not inline config (CSP stays strict). Config is fetched.
- integrity.json is public; integrity-fingerprint.txt is a short summary hash for out-of-band verification.

## Builder Responsibilities

1. Create site/ and private/ directories.
2. Write config.json from encryption pipeline (version, export_id, base_nonce, compression, kdf defaults, payload manifest, key slots, exported_at, cass_version).
3. Write payload/chunk-*.bin files and optional blobs/ for attachments.
4. Copy web assets (HTML, JS, CSS, vendor, assets) from web/dist or pages_assets.
5. Generate integrity.json for all files in site/ and a private integrity-fingerprint.txt.
6. Write robots.txt and .nojekyll.
7. Write README.md (public) and private recovery artifacts.
8. Optional: generate PWA manifest if enabled.

## Security / CSP Requirements

- index.html uses CSP meta tag (no inline scripts, only 'self' and 'wasm-unsafe-eval').
- No secrets in site/ (no recovery secret, no QR images, no master-key backup).
- No inline config. All config is read from config.json via fetch.

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests
- config.json schema round-trip
- integrity.json includes all public files, correct hashes and sizes
- payload manifest count and file names match generated chunks

### Integration Tests
- Build a small export and assert exact directory tree
- Verify site/ has no private artifacts
- Verify optional blobs/ is included only when attachments enabled

### E2E Script
- Build export -> bundle -> cass pages --verify
- Optional: start preview server and load auth page
- Log each check with clear PASS/FAIL markers

## Files to Create/Modify

- src/pages/bundle.rs
- src/pages/integrity.rs
- src/pages/assets.rs (copy logic)
- tests/pages_bundle.rs
- tests/fixtures/pages_bundle/

## Exit Criteria

1. site/ deploys cleanly on GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages
2. All required files present and integrity.json validates
3. No secrets in site/
4. config.json matches encryption output
5. Chunked payload loads in web viewer
close_reason: Implemented BundleBuilder with full functionality: creates site/ and private/ directories, copies encrypted payload, embeds web assets, generates integrity.json with SHA256 hashes, writes robots.txt/.nojekyll, writes private recovery artifacts, integrated with wizard. All 12 integration tests pass.

title: Replace FNV-1a byte-loop stable_content_hash with xxhash or gxhash in search/query.rs
description:
FILE: src/search/query.rs (lines 1404-1453)

CURRENT COST:
`stable_content_hash` and its helper `hash_bytes` implement FNV-1a by byte, in a hand-rolled scalar loop:

```rust
fn hash_bytes(mut hash: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    const FNV_PRIME: u64 = 1099511628211;
    for byte in bytes {
        hash ^= u64::from(*byte);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);
    }
    hash
}
```

`stable_content_hash` is called on dedup/hash paths per hit (FusedHit construction, dedup key computation, content-hash-based dedup in `resolve_semantic_doc_ids_for_hits_distinguishes_same_source_path_line_by_content_hash`, etc.) — for search results with content up to 2000 chars this is a 2KB byte-by-byte mul chain with no SIMD, no vectorization, and sequential data dependencies. Modern machines can hash >10 GB/s with xxhash3 or gxhash vs FNV-1a at ~1 GB/s.

PROPOSED CHANGE:
Replace the body with `twox_hash::XxHash64` or the `gxhash` crate (both already transitive deps via frankensearch — verify with `cargo tree | grep -E 'xxhash|gxhash'`). Preserve the whitespace-invariant split semantics (iterate over split_whitespace tokens and feed them through the hasher with a space separator between tokens). Use a fixed seed (0) for deterministic cross-run output. The function is NOT on-disk format — grep confirms it feeds in-memory dedup HashMap keys and tests, so changing the hash value is safe (no schema migration).

EXPECTED WIN:
4-10x faster hashing for long content bodies (~1-2 KB typical tool outputs). Each search with 100 hits computes ~100 hashes, so the saved µs add up. Also used by stable_hit_hash which is even hotter.

VERIFICATION:
1. Before changing, run the full dedup test suite: `cargo test --lib -- resolve_semantic_doc_ids_for_hits_distinguishes`
2. After change, all of `cargo test --lib search::query::` must pass (includes the ~20 content_hash-consuming tests around lines 7835-11931).
3. Benchmark: add a criterion bench for `stable_content_hash` with 200/2000 char inputs if one doesn't exist, or measure via `search_perf::rrf_fusion_*` which consumes it transitively.
4. Update any test that hardcodes specific hash numeric output (`rg 'stable_content_hash\(' tests/`).

SAFETY NOTE:
Confirm stable_content_hash is not persisted to disk (message_docs / storage) — only used in-memory for dedup. grep src/storage and src/indexer before committing.
close_reason: Replaced FNV-1a byte-loop in stable_content_hash + stable_hit_hash with xxhash_rust::xxh3::Xxh3 (xxh3-64). Tokenization preserved (split_whitespace + 0x20 separator), dedup semantics byte-identical apart from the hash value itself (in-memory only, not persisted). Added xxhash-rust as direct dep with xxh3 feature. Landed in commit 88a647ff. rch cargo check --all-targets: green.

title: E2E Test Runner Script with Detailed Logging
description:
# E2E Test Runner Script with Detailed Logging

## What
Create a comprehensive shell script that runs all cass E2E tests with:
- Detailed, structured logging
- Colored human-readable output
- Timing information
- Phase separation (unit, integration, E2E)
- Failure diagnostics
- Summary report

## Why
Currently tests are run via `cargo test` which provides minimal output. Developers
and CI need:
- Clear visibility into what's being tested
- Timing data for performance regression detection
- Detailed failure context for debugging
- Structured output for CI parsing

## Technical Design

### Main Test Runner Script
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/test-all.sh
# Comprehensive test runner with detailed logging

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
LOG_DIR="${PROJECT_ROOT}/test-logs"
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/test_${TIMESTAMP}.log"

# Colors
RED='\\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\\033[0;34m'
CYAN='\\033[0;36m'
NC='\\033[0m' # No Color

# Verbosity
VERBOSE=${VERBOSE:-0}
PARALLEL=${PARALLEL:-1}
INCLUDE_SSH=${INCLUDE_SSH:-0}
INCLUDE_SLOW=${INCLUDE_SLOW:-0}

# =============================================================================
# Logging Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    local level=$1
    shift
    local msg="$*"
    local timestamp=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N")
    
    # Color based on level
    case $level in
        INFO)  color=$GREEN ;;
        WARN)  color=$YELLOW ;;
        ERROR) color=$RED ;;
        DEBUG) color=$CYAN ;;
        *)     color=$NC ;;
    esac
    
    # Console output (colored)
    echo -e "${color}[${timestamp}] [${level}]${NC} ${msg}"
    
    # Log file output (plain)
    echo "[${timestamp}] [${level}] ${msg}" >> "$LOG_FILE"
}

log_section() {
    local title=$1
    echo ""
    log INFO "=================================================================="
    log INFO "  $title"
    log INFO "=================================================================="
}

log_subsection() {
    local title=$1
    echo ""
    log INFO "--- $title ---"
}

# =============================================================================
# Timing Functions
# =============================================================================

declare -A TIMINGS

time_start() {
    local name=$1
    TIMINGS["${name}_start"]=$(date +%s.%N)
}

time_end() {
    local name=$1
    local start=${TIMINGS["${name}_start"]}
    local end=$(date +%s.%N)
    local duration=$(echo "$end - $start" | bc)
    TIMINGS["${name}_duration"]=$duration
    log INFO "⏱  $name completed in ${duration}s"
}

# =============================================================================
# Test Phases
# =============================================================================

run_unit_tests() {
    log_section "PHASE 1: Unit Tests (src/ modules)"
    time_start "unit_tests"
    
    local args=("--lib" "--color=always")
    [[ $PARALLEL -eq 1 ]] && args+=("--jobs" "$(nproc)")
    
    if cargo test "${args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; then
        log INFO "✓ Unit tests passed"
        UNIT_RESULT=0
    else
        log ERROR "✗ Unit tests failed"
        UNIT_RESULT=1
    fi
    
    time_end "unit_tests"
    return $UNIT_RESULT
}

run_connector_tests() {
    log_section "PHASE 2: Connector Tests (real fixtures)"
    time_start "connector_tests"
    
    local connectors=("claude" "codex" "gemini" "cline" "aider" "amp" "opencode" "pi_agent")
    local failed=0
    
    for conn in "${connectors[@]}"; do
        log_subsection "Testing connector: $conn"
        if cargo test --test "connector_${conn}" --color=always 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; then
            log INFO "  ✓ $conn connector passed"
        else

print_summary() {
    log_section "TEST SUMMARY"
    
    echo ""
    printf "%-30s %10s %10s\\n" "Phase" "Duration" "Status"
    printf "%-30s %10s %10s\\n" "-----" "--------" "------"
    
    for key in unit_tests connector_tests cli_tests ui_tests ssh_tests slow_tests; do
        local duration=${TIMINGS["${key}_duration"]:-"N/A"}
        local status
        
        case $key in
            unit_tests)      status=${UNIT_RESULT:-"?"};;
            connector_tests) status=${CONNECTOR_RESULT:-"?"};;
            cli_tests)       status=${CLI_RESULT:-"?"};;
            ui_tests)        status=${UI_RESULT:-"?"};;
            ssh_tests)       status=${SSH_RESULT:-"skipped"};;
            slow_tests)      status=${SLOW_RESULT:-"skipped"};;
        esac
        
        if [[ $status == "0" ]]; then
            printf "%-30s %10s ${GREEN}%10s${NC}\\n" "$key" "${duration}s" "PASS"
        elif [[ $status == "skipped" ]]; then
            printf "%-30s %10s ${YELLOW}%10s${NC}\\n" "$key" "-" "SKIP"
        else
            printf "%-30s %10s ${RED}%10s${NC}\\n" "$key" "${duration}s" "FAIL"
        fi
    done
    
    echo ""
    log INFO "Log file: $LOG_FILE"
}

# =============================================================================
# Main
# =============================================================================

main() {
    mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
    
    log_section "CASS TEST RUNNER"
    log INFO "Project root: $PROJECT_ROOT"
    log INFO "Log file: $LOG_FILE"
    log INFO "Timestamp: $TIMESTAMP"
    log INFO "Settings: PARALLEL=$PARALLEL INCLUDE_SSH=$INCLUDE_SSH INCLUDE_SLOW=$INCLUDE_SLOW"
    
    cd "$PROJECT_ROOT"
    
    # Run all phases, collecting results
    run_unit_tests && UNIT_RESULT=0 || UNIT_RESULT=1
    run_connector_tests && CONNECTOR_RESULT=0 || CONNECTOR_RESULT=1
    run_cli_tests && CLI_RESULT=0 || CLI_RESULT=1
    run_ui_tests && UI_RESULT=0 || UI_RESULT=1
    run_ssh_tests && SSH_RESULT=0 || SSH_RESULT=1
    run_slow_tests && SLOW_RESULT=0 || SLOW_RESULT=1
    
    print_summary
    
    # Exit with failure if any required phase failed
    if [[ ${UNIT_RESULT:-1} -ne 0 ]] || \
       [[ ${CONNECTOR_RESULT:-1} -ne 0 ]] || \
       [[ ${CLI_RESULT:-1} -ne 0 ]] || \
       [[ ${UI_RESULT:-1} -ne 0 ]]; then
        log ERROR "TESTS FAILED"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    log INFO "ALL TESTS PASSED"
    exit 0
}

# Parse arguments
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        -v|--verbose)   VERBOSE=1; shift ;;
        --no-parallel)  PARALLEL=0; shift ;;
        --include-ssh)  INCLUDE_SSH=1; shift ;;
        --include-slow) INCLUDE_SLOW=1; shift ;;
        --all)          INCLUDE_SSH=1; INCLUDE_SLOW=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help)
            echo "Usage: $0 [options]"
            echo "  -v, --verbose     Verbose output"
            echo "  --no-parallel     Run tests sequentially"
            echo "  --include-ssh     Include SSH integration tests (requires Docker)"
            echo "  --include-slow    Include slow/performance tests"
            echo "  --all             Include all optional tests"
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown option: $1"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

main
```
