title: Remove process-global environment mutation from the E2E command harness and restore safe parallelism
description:
Problem: PhaseTracker::trace_env_guard installs CASS_TRACE_FILE, CASS_TRACE_ID, CASS_TRACE_TEST_ID, CASS_TRACE_FILTER, CASS_TRACE_MAX_BYTES, and CASS_TRACE_MAX_EVENTS with process-global EnvGuard; semantic cases also replace process-global HOME and CODEX_HOME. Rust test threads share one process, so overlapping guards can cross-route a cass child to another test’s fixture or evidence artifact and can restore stale prior values out of order. The bounded-trace slice serializes the currently affected semantic and schema-validation cases as an immediate evidence-integrity boundary, but serialization lengthens real E2E lanes and leaves the unsafe helper available to every future caller.

Design: make subprocess environment explicit and immutable per test. Replace the guard API with an E2eCommandEnvironment value that applies HOME, CODEX_HOME when present, CASS_TRACE_FILE, CASS_TRACE_ID, CASS_TRACE_TEST_ID, CASS_TRACE_FILTER, CASS_TRACE_MAX_BYTES, and CASS_TRACE_MAX_EVENTS directly through Command::env/envs. Route assert_cmd::Command and std::process::Command construction through one typed helper so a caller cannot accidentally omit correlation or budgets. Do not set or remove process environment in the tracker. Convert all trace_env_guard call sites, prioritizing semantic and schema-validation targets, including helper-driven invalid-ANN cases. Preserve real subprocesses and artifacts; add no mocks or compatibility shim. Remove only serialization attributes made unnecessary by the completed conversion.

Acceptance: (1) a structural policy test fails if tests/util/e2e_log.rs or converted E2E targets invoke std::env::set_var/remove_var or trace_env_guard; (2) at least two deliberately overlapping cases with distinct HOME, CODEX_HOME, trace path, trace ID, and test ID run concurrently and each child reads only its own corpus and writes only its own cass-trace-v1 artifact; (3) the complete semantic and schema-validation targets pass under default parallel scheduling and --test-threads=1; (4) a repository-wide call-site inventory proves no trace_env_guard remains and documents any unrelated, separately tracked process-global mutation; (5) every trace record carries the owning test_id/trace_id and all artifacts pass scripts/validate-e2e-jsonl.sh; (6) no fixture, output protocol, ANN/FSVI behavior, phase event, or diagnostic field is lost; (7) workspace check, clippy -D warnings, rustfmt check, focused tests, full relevant E2E targets, and UBS pass or explicitly classify pre-existing findings; (8) record elapsed time and artifact identity before/after, reporting improvement only as harness throughput, never product performance.

title: [MEDIUM] security: ChatGPT AES key file loaded without permission check (mode > 0600 not refused)
description:
security-audit-for-saas sweep on ChatGPT connector encryption surface.

CLAIM (chatgpt.rs comment): 'ChatGPT desktop encrypts conversations using AES-256-GCM with a key stored in the [keychain]'. The connector loads that key from CHATGPT_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var OR from one of three key file paths.

FINDING (franken_agent_detection/src/connectors/chatgpt.rs:109-117): the key file load path uses fs::read() without ANY check on file permissions. A 32-byte AES-256 key file with mode 0644 (world-readable) or 0664 (group-readable) is loaded silently. SSH refuses to use a private key with mode > 0600 for exactly this reason (the key is as sensitive as a credit card number — it decrypts the user's entire ChatGPT history).

SECURITY RATIONALE:
- The key decrypts the operator's full ChatGPT conversation history (potentially years of personal/professional content). Treating it like an SSH key is the obvious bar.
- Three paths searched in priority order; first match wins. If a process can write ~/.config/cass/chatgpt_key.bin with mode 0644, the connector will accept it. A multi-user system (shared dev box, lab machine) where one user's HOME is readable to others leaks the key.
- No symlink check either — a key file pointing to /dev/null or /etc/passwd would have its first 32 bytes loaded as a key (mostly harmless, decryption fails, but defense-in-depth says reject).
- CHATGPT_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var path has the same key-material concerns but is process-scoped (not on-disk persistent), so the file path is the higher-risk surface.

ATTACK SHAPE: Local privilege escalation / cross-user key disclosure on shared systems. Severity MEDIUM (requires local read access to the key file's directory).

Fix scope (~20 min):
1. After fs::read() succeeds, call std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt::mode() on the file metadata, mask with 0o077 (group + other bits), refuse the load if any of those bits are set. Emit tracing::warn! pointing at the offending path and the offending mode bits.
2. Also tighten the load to check std::fs::symlink_metadata first and refuse symlinks (matches the ssh-key-loading discipline).
3. Test: fs::set_permissions to 0o644 on a tempfile key, attempt load, expect None + warn message containing 'mode' or 'permissions'.

Out of scope but worth a follow-up: zeroize the [u8; KEY_SIZE] field on Drop using the zeroize crate.

This finding is in franken_agent_detection (sibling crate), not src/ — but cass consumes it directly and ships it as a feature, so the fix lands in the FAD repo.
close_reason: Shipped in FAD repo (commit 11c7efc on franken_agent_detection main). chatgpt.rs::load_encryption_key now gates each key file path through chatgpt_key_file_mode_is_safe (refuses symlinks + refuses any group/other permission). 2 regression tests pin 0600/0400/0644/0660/symlink behaviors. Validated under rch from FAD repo, exit=0.

title: cass status cannot distinguish a corrupt DB from a merely stale one; COUNT(*) masks corruption
description:
## Summary

A corrupt canonical DB is reported by `cass status` as merely
`healthy:false, stale:true` — indistinguishable from "your index is just out of
date". There is no signal that the archive is **malformed**, so operators (and
agents following the documented bootstrap) run `cass index` to "fix staleness",
which is the worst possible action on a corrupt DB.

## Evidence (2026-07-26, cass 0.6.22)

ts2, whose DB genuinely cannot be read:

```
$ cass status --json
{"healthy":false,"stale":true,"rebuilding":false}

$ sqlite3 agent_search.db 'SELECT id,title FROM conversations'
Error: database disk image is malformed
```

Same output shape as an ordinary stale-but-fine host.

## The detection trap (worth encoding in cass itself)

**`SELECT COUNT(*)` does not detect this class of corruption.** SQLite answers
`COUNT(*)` from an index without reading table B-tree pages, so a corrupt DB
counts perfectly and only fails when real columns are read:

```
sqlite> SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations;    -- 2188      (succeeds!)
sqlite> SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages;         -- 434069    (succeeds!)
sqlite> SELECT id,title,source_path FROM conversations;
Error: database disk image is malformed
```

Any health check built on COUNT is therefore worthless. The reliable cheap probe
is a real column projection, e.g.
`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,title,source_path FROM conversations)`.

This cost two full failed merge runs before it was spotted, because both my
verification and the natural intuition ("counts match the source, so it copied
fine") are silently wrong.

## Prevalence

Not a one-off: **ts2 and csd were both malformed** on 2026-07-26, and ts2 was
*also* malformed in the 2026-05-19 consolidation run. Both recovered with
`sqlite3 .recover` (csd losslessly at 6,643 conversations; ts2 lost 11 of 2,188).

## Proposed fix

1. Add a cheap real-column probe to `cass status` / `cass health` and report a
   distinct `corrupt: true` (or a `db_integrity` field), separate from `stale`.
2. When corrupt, `status` should recommend `.recover`/`doctor`, and `cass index`
   should refuse to start a rebuild against a malformed DB rather than
   rewriting on top of it.
3. Never implement an internal integrity heuristic on `COUNT(*)`.
close_reason: Landed: (1) cass status now runs a BOUNDED real-column integrity probe (single-row projections at both B-tree edges of conversations+messages; O(1), runs even when counts are skipped for >256MB archives — the exact ts2 configuration that previously had no signal) and reports a DISTINCT database.integrity field (ok|corrupt|unknown) + integrity_detail + integrity_hint; corrupt forces status=unhealthy, healthy=false, a warning, and a recommended_action that says do-NOT-index / doctor+.recover first (staleness advice never shown for a corrupt archive). Classification is typed (DatabaseCorrupt/NotADatabase/WalCorrupt + malformed/disk-image message fallback); busy/transient errors report unknown, never a false corrupt. COUNT(*) is never used for integrity (the bead's trap is documented at the probe). (2) cass index REFUSES to start against a malformed canonical DB (all modes read it, incl. --force-rebuild's readonly authoritative rebuild) with recovery guidance; CASS_INDEX_ALLOW_MALFORMED_DB=1 is the explicit escape hatch. (3) health's <50ms d0rmo/gi4oy watermark contract untouched (probe never runs there; integrity stays unknown by design). Tests: healthy/missing-DB negative + smashed-table-pages positive (fixture checkpoints WAL into main then smashes both main pages and WAL frames — WAL replay otherwise silently masks main-page corruption, itself a finding worth this note). 2/2 green on trj; clippy -D warnings + fmt clean. Caveat recorded: the probe is a probe, not a proof — corruption confined to unprobed interior pages still needs cass doctor --check.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Strengthened by 2026-07-28 measurements. cass doctor --check DOES detect the corruption correctly (ts2 report: 6 'corrupt'/3 'corruption' findings, status=unhealthy) -- but it takes 951 SECONDS on that host to say so, and emits nothing until it finishes (see doctor-check-no-progress-output-siekg). So today the ONLY way to learn an archive is malformed is a ~16-minute run. That makes the cheap-probe ask here more valuable, not less: cass status/health should surface a distinct corrupt signal in milliseconds via a real column projection, instead of leaving 'healthy:false, stale:true' as the only fast signal -- which actively misleads toward running cass index on a corrupt DB.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CONFIRMED with the full status payload (my original evidence was a 3-field jq projection; this is the whole object). On ts2's malformed DB, cass status --json reports: opened=true, open_error=null, conversations=null, messages=null, counts_skipped=true. So the archive OPENS cleanly -- the corruption is in table B-tree pages, not the header/WAL -- open_error stays null, and counts are skipped by design. Nothing in the fast surface can see it. NOTE THE DESIGN CONTRACT: run_health carries an explicit comment citing beads d0rmo + gi4oy that health is the <50ms surface which force-skips both the COUNT(*) and the FrankenStorage open, delegating integrity to doctor. A fix must NOT silently reverse that. Contract-respecting proposal: a BOUNDED real-column probe (e.g. SELECT id,title,source_path FROM conversations LIMIT 1) is O(1) -- it touches one table page, costs microseconds, and would have caught this, unlike COUNT(*). Offer it as an explicit signal (integrity: ok|corrupt|unknown) rather than repurposing 'healthy', and gate it behind a flag if the <50ms budget is sacred. Caveat: LIMIT 1 is a probe, not a proof -- corruption on later pages still needs doctor.

close_reason: Live connector ingest diagnostics and provider hardening are wired and proven by focused unit, mixed-corpus E2E, and zero-warning new-file UBS gates.

title: A2: Query History Debouncing
description: Epic for fixing query history to only save final queries, not every intermediate keystroke.
notes:
**Problem** (tui.rs:3382-3389):
Currently after EVERY debounced search (60ms debounce at line 3294-3296), the query is saved to history:
```rust
if !query.trim().is_empty()
    && query_history.front().map(|q| q != &query).unwrap_or(true)
{
    query_history.push_front(query.clone());
}
```

So typing 'foobar' saves: 'f', 'fo', 'foo', 'foob', 'fooba', 'foobar' - 6 entries for one search!

**Root Cause**:
- Search debounce (60ms) is for responsive live search
- History save happens after each search, not after user 'commits' query

**Solution Options**:
1. **Separate history debounce**: Save to history only after longer pause (e.g., 2-3 seconds)
2. **Commit on Enter**: Only save when user presses Enter or navigates results
3. **Consolidation on save**: Dedupe history on exit by removing prefixes
4. **Hybrid**: Debounce + commit tracking

**Recommended**: Option 2 (commit on explicit action) - clearest user intent

title: A3: Full Wildcard Support
description: Epic for implementing full asterisk (*) wildcard support in search queries.
notes:
**Goal**: Support wildcards:
- `*foo` - prefix wildcard (find 'barfoo', 'bazfoo')
- `foo*` - suffix wildcard (find 'foobar', 'foobaz') - partially exists via prefix match mode
- `*foo*` - both (find anything containing 'foo')
- Explicit asterisks should override implicit behavior

**Current State**:
- Prefix match mode (F9) appends `*` to terms automatically (tui.rs:1148-1163)
- query.rs sanitize_query() likely strips `*` as non-alphanumeric
- Tantivy supports wildcards but may need WildcardQuery

**Implementation Approach**:
1. Preserve `*` in sanitize_query()
2. Parse wildcards before Tantivy query construction
3. Use appropriate Tantivy query types (WildcardQuery, PhraseQuery)
4. Track which terms used wildcards for ranking purposes

title: A3.3: Build Tantivy queries from wildcard patterns
description: Construct appropriate Tantivy query types based on parsed wildcard patterns.
notes:
**Tantivy Query Mapping**:
- `Exact` → TermQuery or edge-ngram prefix (existing behavior)
- `Prefix` → Use existing edge-ngram or PhrasePrefix
- `Suffix` → RegexQuery with `.*term$` or content_prefix ngram reversed
- `Contains` → RegexQuery with `.*term.*`

**Challenge**: Tantivy doesn't have native suffix/contains. Options:
1. RegexQuery (slow but works)
2. Reverse-indexed field (complex schema change)
3. Filter post-search using SQLite FTS5 (has `*term*` support)

**Recommended Approach**:
1. For `*foo*` (contains): Use FTS5 fallback which supports `*term*`
2. For `*foo` (suffix): Same FTS5 approach
3. For `foo*` (prefix): Use existing edge-ngram approach

title: A5: Smarter Ranking
description: Epic for improving search result ranking with recency, match quality, and configurable weighting.
notes:
**Current Ranking** (tui.rs:3321-3338):
```rust
let alpha = match ranking_mode {
    RankingMode::RecentHeavy => 1.0,
    RankingMode::Balanced => 0.4,
    RankingMode::RelevanceHeavy => 0.1,
};
let score_a = a.score + alpha * recency(a);
```

**Problems**:
1. Only considers Tantivy score + recency
2. No match quality factor (exact vs wildcard)
3. All wildcard matches treated equally

**Improved Ranking Formula**:
```
final_score = tantivy_score * match_quality_factor + alpha * recency

match_quality_factor:
  - Exact match: 1.0
  - Suffix wildcard only (foo*): 0.9
  - Prefix wildcard only (*foo): 0.8
  - Contains wildcard (*foo*): 0.7
  - Implicit wildcard fallback: 0.6
```

**User-Configurable**:
- F12 cycles: RecentHeavy / Balanced / RelevanceHeavy / MatchQualityHeavy

notes:

```rust

    RecentHeavy,

    RelevanceHeavy,

title: Epic: Swarm coordination intelligence and proof-debt control plane
description:
BACKGROUND:
The closed qhj9o campaign already covered many-core performance, cost planning, tail-latency evidence, topology budgets, remote indexing, semantic sharding, and repairable derived-asset evidence. The active oh96l cockpit already covers read-only status, stale advisories, evidence broker, source adapters, TUI surfacing, large fixtures, docs, and final schema freeze.

This epic is the next non-duplicative layer: turn status and evidence into safer assignment plans, coordination quality checks, proof-debt remediation, historical learning, and outcome analytics for large agent swarms. The default posture must stay read-only and advisory. It must not mutate Beads, Agent Mail, git state, reservations, source archives, or derived indexes without explicit operator action.

PHASE 2 30 TO 5 SUMMARY:
Best five ideas after winnowing: work-packet planner for scoped agent assignments; coordination protocol linter for Agent Mail and Beads hygiene; proof-debt ledger with remediation queue; session-mined regression and test suggester; workflow outcome analytics connecting skills, commands, proof gates, files, and bead closure quality.

PHASE 3 NEXT 10 SUMMARY:
Next ten ideas: worktree and reservation collision simulator; token-budgeted context-pack optimizer; verification playbook recommender from touched files and history; real-history swarm replay fixtures; operator incident timeline; stale-reservation arbitration assistant; CI failure triage pack; model and context budget forecaster; command-safety policy linter; retrospective generator for closed swarm campaigns.

OVERLAP CHECK:
Build on qhj9o, oh96l, uuwye answer packs, and z9fse analytics instead of duplicating them. Do not reimplement the swarm status aggregator, evidence broker, large-fixture perf gate, cass pack renderers, query/index cost planner, source health scheduler, or topology budget planner.

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
Future agents can ask cass for a safe work packet, see coordination/proof debt before closeout, get evidence-backed verification suggestions, and learn from prior swarm outcomes. Each slice needs robot JSON, deterministic fixtures, redaction rules, no-mutation tests, and artifact-backed proof. Passing unit tests alone is not enough.

title: Add verification-failed repair markers and repeated-repair refusal gates
description:
Background: beads_rust doctor protects users from repeated failed repair attempts by writing a verification-failed marker and refusing to repeat the risky rebuild path unless the operator explicitly opts in. That pattern is directly relevant to cass because a failed repair attempt can leave clues that should not be overwritten by another automated attempt.

Problem: cass doctor v2 already plans dry-run fingerprints, receipts, forensic bundles, and atomic promotion, but it does not yet require a durable failed-repair marker that changes future behavior. Without that marker, an impatient user or automation loop could run doctor --fix repeatedly against the same fragile archive, producing noise and potentially obscuring the first failure evidence.

Scope: introduce a repair failure marker stored in the cass doctor state area. It must record operation id, command line mode, plan fingerprint, affected artifacts, selected authority, rejected authorities, preflight checks, applied actions, verification checks, failed checks, forensic bundle path, candidate path, timestamps, cass version, platform, and whether any user data was ever modified. Subsequent mutating repair commands must detect the marker and refuse the same repair class by default. Provide an explicit override flag such as --allow-repeated-repair or a more cass-specific equivalent, and require the new attempt to create a new operation id and preserve the previous marker.

Acceptance criteria: robot output has stable fields: repair_previously_failed, failure_marker_path, repeat_refusal_reason, override_available, and override_used. Human output clearly says no further mutation was attempted. Unit tests cover marker creation, marker parsing, refusal, override, marker preservation, corrupt marker fallback, and multiple repair classes. E2E tests simulate a verification failure, rerun doctor --fix, prove it refuses by default, then prove an explicit override creates a second receipt without deleting the first marker.

Implementation note: this gate should run before any candidate promotion or cleanup apply. It is acceptable to still run read-only doctor checks while a marker exists, because read-only diagnostics help the user understand the failure.

title: Cache thread-local DefaultCanonicalizer in search/canonicalize.rs to avoid per-call allocation
description:
FILE: src/search/canonicalize.rs

CURRENT COST:
canonicalize_for_embedding() (line 36-38) constructs a fresh DefaultCanonicalizer via `DefaultCanonicalizer::default()` on every call. This function is called on every indexed message (src/indexer/semantic.rs:393, src/daemon/worker.rs:295), on every search hit that goes through semantic lookup (src/search/query.rs:3995, 4087, 7514), and once per query (src/search/query.rs:4656). DefaultCanonicalizer is a stateless struct with 3 usize fields (max_length, code_head_lines, code_tail_lines) — see /data/projects/frankensearch/crates/frankensearch-core/src/canonicalize.rs:58. No reason to allocate per call.

PROPOSED CHANGE:
Replace `DefaultCanonicalizer::default().canonicalize(text)` with a `std::thread_local! { static CANON: DefaultCanonicalizer = DefaultCanonicalizer::default(); }` (or `static CANON: OnceLock<DefaultCanonicalizer>` if DefaultCanonicalizer is Sync) and call `CANON.with(|c| c.canonicalize(text))`. Leaves the two mid-stream String allocations (`strip_markdown_and_code` internal buffer and whitespace pass) in place — those are the real cost — but removes the struct-construction overhead and keeps a clean injection point for future interning.

EXPECTED WIN:
Eliminates a per-call struct default construction (minor CPU, a few loads/stores). Main value is creating the cached instance pattern so a follow-up can add input-length short-circuiting (e.g. skip NFC+markdown stripping when input is pure-ASCII without markdown indicators, which covers a large share of tool-output messages).

VERIFICATION:
1. cargo test --lib search::canonicalize (14 existing tests must still pass).
2. Benchmark: rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_cass cargo bench --bench search_perf -- canonicalize
3. Compare before/after Criterion output under target/criterion/canonicalize_*. Target: eliminate the ~200ns of per-call Default::default overhead on short inputs; should not regress long-input cases.

PRIOR ART:
The 2026-01-25 extreme-software-optimization session flagged `canonicalize_long_message_streaming` as 35% slower than the legacy implementation and identified canonicalization as a top hotspot. This bead targets the low-hanging allocation portion, independent of the streaming question.
close_reason: Cached DefaultCanonicalizer in thread_local! static (src/search/canonicalize.rs). canonicalize_for_embedding now calls CANONICALIZER.with(|c| c.canonicalize(text)) instead of constructing DefaultCanonicalizer::default() per call. Landed in commit b295080c. rch cargo check --all-targets: green. Creates a clean injection point for follow-up input-length short-circuiting on ASCII-without-markdown inputs.

title: [Task] Opt 8: Implement streaming backpressure indexing
description:
# Task: Implement Streaming Backpressure Indexing

## Objective

Replace batch collection with streaming per-connector processing using bounded channels for memory control.

## Implementation Summary

### Key Changes

1. **Create StreamingIndexer**:
   ```rust
   struct StreamingIndexer {
       tx: SyncSender<ConversationBatch>,
       ingest_handle: thread::JoinHandle<Result<IndexStats>>,
   }
   
   impl StreamingIndexer {
       fn new(tantivy_index: TantivyIndex, sqlite_conn: Connection) -> Self {
           let (tx, rx) = sync_channel(100);  // Bounded buffer
           let ingest_handle = thread::spawn(move || {
               for batch in rx {
                   tantivy_index.add_conversation(&batch)?;
                   sqlite_conn.insert_conversation(&batch)?;
               }
               Ok(stats)
           });
           Self { tx, ingest_handle }
       }
       
       fn send_batch(&self, batch: ConversationBatch) -> Result<()> {
           self.tx.send(batch)?;  // Blocks if buffer full (backpressure!)
           Ok(())
       }
   }
   ```

2. **Modify connector flow** to use streaming indexer instead of collecting all batches

3. **Handle errors and progress reporting** in async context

### Env Var Toggle
`CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=1` to enable (disabled by default due to complexity)

## Detailed Implementation

See parent feature issue (coding_agent_session_search-1h0p) for:
- Architecture diagram
- Backpressure mechanism
- Ordering considerations
- Memory impact analysis
- Verification plan

## Implementation Complexity: HIGH

This is rated HIGH effort because:
- Significant architectural change
- Error handling in worker thread
- Progress reporting becomes async
- Cancellation handling
- Testing concurrent code

## Files to Modify

- `src/indexing/mod.rs` - StreamingIndexer
- Connector files - Use streaming instead of batch collection
- Progress reporting - Update for async

## Validation

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo check --all-targets
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test

# Memory test
/usr/bin/time -v cass index --full 2>&1 | grep "Maximum resident"
```

## Success Criteria

- [ ] StreamingIndexer implemented
- [ ] Bounded channel provides backpressure
- [ ] Peak RSS reduced by 50%+
- [ ] Same search results (set equality)
- [ ] Cancellation handled gracefully
- [ ] Env var toggle works

## Note on Priority

This is P3 (low priority) because:
- Current memory usage (295 MB) is acceptable
- Higher complexity and risk
- Other optimizations provide more immediate value
- Consider only for memory-constrained environments

title: Add post-repair write read-after-write probes for archive DB and derived assets
description:
Background: beads_rust doctor does not trust that a repair succeeded merely because the repair code returned Ok. It performs a rollback-only write/read probe after repair. Cass should copy that first-principles idea: the only useful repair is one that leaves the archive and derived surfaces actually usable.

Problem: cass doctor v2 currently has candidate verification and atomic promotion beads, but it does not explicitly require a post-repair probe that proves the promoted state can be opened, written, read, rolled back, and queried through the same pathways real cass commands use. A database can pass a superficial integrity check while still failing on writer locks, permissions, WAL behavior, migration state, or search hydration.

Scope: implement a post-repair probe suite that runs after any mutating doctor operation and before success is reported. For the SQLite archive, the probe should open through the production storage path, start a rollback-only transaction, insert or update a sentinel in a doctor-owned scratch/probe namespace, read it back, rollback, and verify no durable user-visible row was left behind. For derived lexical and semantic assets, probes should verify open, minimal query, generation identity, and consistency with the archive generation. For backups and candidates, probes should verify manifest checksums and restore-readability without promoting them.

Acceptance criteria: robot output includes post_repair_probes with per-probe status, duration, failure reason, and whether failure blocked promotion or merely blocked cleanup. Unit tests cover successful rollback, write denied, read after write mismatch, rollback failure, WAL/SHM sidecar issue, derived index open failure, and probe namespace isolation. E2E scripts must prove that doctor --fix reports failure when repair mutates but the post-repair probe fails, and that the original forensic bundle and failure marker remain available.

Implementation note: this bead should be wired into repair apply, reconstruct promotion, backup restore, and safe auto-run. The probe must never use rusqlite in new code; use the frankensqlite production path required by AGENTS.md.

title: Add privacy and redaction regression tests for doctor logs artifacts and mirror metadata
description:
Background: doctor v2 will intentionally preserve and log more evidence. That is correct for recovery, but it increases the risk of leaking absolute paths, secrets, prompts, tokens, private code snippets, or attachment references through stdout, JSON, receipts, event logs, e2e artifacts, or documentation examples.

Scope: add unit and e2e tests that seed fixtures with realistic sensitive values in source paths, environment variables, session text, config snippets, remote hostnames, and attachment references. Verify default human output, robot JSON, receipts, event logs, e2e manifests, and doctor artifacts redact or scope those values according to the privacy policy. Include verbose diagnostics tests that prove opt-in detailed output is explicit and still avoids secret-bearing fields where required.

Acceptance criteria: tests fail if default doctor output leaks seeded secrets or full sensitive paths; e2e artifacts include redaction reports; mirror metadata stores enough provenance for recovery without exposing sensitive paths unnecessarily in normal output; public Pages/export paths are not allowed to include raw mirror blobs or doctor forensic bundles by accident.
close_reason: Implemented and verified privacy/redaction regression coverage with required doctor e2e redaction reports, seeded support-bundle sentinel scenario, artifact tree leak assertions, raw mirror/public export policy verification, and full cargo gates.

title: v0.6.24 RELEASE BLOCKER: 3 cross-platform storage::sqlite defects in repair/recovery paths (planner under-plan, FTS content loss after legacy dedup, seed-canonical readonly CannotOpen) + 15 macOS-only engine-close failures
description:
RELEASE BLOCKER for v0.6.24 (found by the release test gate, 2026-08-11; full-workspace release-profile run on macOS arm64 + targeted Linux x86_64 cross-check on ts1 at HEAD 9fba135c): 3 storage::sqlite lib tests fail CROSS-PLATFORM and all three are REAL product defects in recovery/repair paths, not stale assertions. 15 additional failures are macOS-ONLY (they pass on Linux). Tagging was stopped; everything else for the release is staged and ready.

THE THREE CROSS-PLATFORM DEFECTS (each verified failing serially on both macOS and Linux):
1. storage::sqlite::tests::list_conversation_footprints_for_lexical_rebuild_raises_stale_low_tail_cache (assert at src/storage/sqlite.rs:24865): with a deliberately staled conversation_tail_state (last_message_idx=0 vs 3 real messages), list_conversation_footprints_for_lexical_rebuild returns message_count=1/4096 bytes instead of raising to 3/12288 — the lexical-rebuild PLANNER under-plans shards and will trip the doc>plan invariant downstream.
2. storage::sqlite::tests::rebuild_fts_via_rusqlite_cleans_duplicate_legacy_schema_rows (assert ~26867): after the legacy duplicate-fts_messages cleanup + rebuild flow, SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fts_messages via FrankenConnection returns 0 instead of 1 — the canonical message's FTS content is LOST after cleanup (silently unsearchable until some later full rebuild). The test's own comment documents the intended contract ("one canonical message bounds repair work" and one hydrated row).
3. storage::sqlite::tests::seed_canonical_from_best_historical_bundle_copies_data_and_resets_runtime_meta (unwrap at ~25196): after seed_canonical copies the historical bundle into place, the READ-ONLY reopen via open_franken_with_flags(SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY) fails CannotOpen. PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS (mechanism-consistent, not single-stepped): the pinned engine's 2026-07-21 wave makes read-only opens use ReadOnlyExisting semantics — "joins an existing generation WITHOUT creating namespace records; missing or malformed records fail closed" — and a freshly file-copied DB has NO -fsqlite-ns-use/-gate records, so the read-only open fails closed. If confirmed, EVERY copy/restore-then-readonly-open flow is affected in production, not just this test. Fix candidates: seed flow performs one writable open (or explicit namespace establishment) before the read-only verify; or the engine offers an establish-if-absent read-only mode for single-writer restore flows.

ATTRIBUTION CONSTRAINTS DISCOVERED: cass HEAD cannot compile against any pre-fts5-line engine rev (open_existing_schema_only_deferred_fts5 is load-bearing; also build.rs enforces the exact pin rev as a dependency source contract), so engine-swap bisection is impossible — HEAD and engine 2351c6c5 are inseparable. The fts5 line is NOT merged into frankensqlite main, and no pushed rev contains both the fts5/deferred-open work AND the GH#294 read-neutrality fixes.

MACOS-ONLY FAILURES (15, pass on Linux, persist under --test-threads=1 so not parallel interference): 10x indexer::persist::persist_internal_tests (all dying in "closing frankensqlite writer for begin-concurrent mode ... closing frankensqlite connection" on temp DBs) + 7x search::semantic_manifest accepted_* (subset overlaps count). Platform-specific engine close/lock behavior on darwin worth its own pass once the cross-platform three are fixed.

COUNTERVAILING FIELD EVIDENCE (why this is a targeted fix, not a crisis): the same HEAD binary has been running in production on this Mac all day — bounded 30 s opens, honest health, full 12 GB corpus rebuild, sub-second search — and stock sqlite3 opens the fsqlite-written corpus fine. The defects are in the REPAIR/RECOVERY flows (planner raise, legacy-dedup hydration, seed-canonical reopen), which is exactly why the test gate and not field use caught them.

RELEASE STATE, STAGED AND WAITING (repeat of what is DONE): version already 0.6.24; CHANGELOG entry cut and pushed (9fba135c); dsr registered (coding_agent_session_search; healthy hosts mmini darwin/arm64 + trj/ts1 linux/amd64; BOTH Windows hosts unhealthy — release will ship without windows assets, note in body); brew tap formula update plan ready (Formula/cass.rb: version + 3 sha256; linux-arm64 has no build host — keep that branch pinned to the v0.6.23 asset URL); asset contract = cass-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz + sha256 + SHA256SUMS + install.sh/ps1 + sbom. UNBLOCK = fix the three tests above, rerun the gate (macOS: full workspace; Linux: the storage/persist/manifest clusters), then tag v0.6.24 and run the dsr build/release + tap bump.
close_reason: All defects fixed, gates green both platforms, v0.6.24 released and fleet-verified. Detail in final comment.

title: [completion-debt] Add automated CI guard scanning scripts/*.sh and scripts/e2e/*.sh for bare cargo invocations
description:
**Origin:** Consolidates the audit-trail gap from three closed beads (audit pass `2026-05-09T00-50-03Z` batches 4 + 1):
- `coding_agent_session_search-vq9l5` (test-report.sh through rch)
- `coding_agent_session_search-yzh2t` (security_paths_e2e.sh through rch)
- `coding_agent_session_search-zlzpk` (validate_docs.sh through rch)

**Parent:** `coding_agent_session_search-vz9t8` (audit-2026-05-09 epic).

## Background

All three originator beads correctly rch-wrapped their target shell script and committed the diff cleanly. Independent grep verifies the rch wrapping landed. **However**, the existing CI guard `golden_regeneration_hints_do_not_use_bare_cargo` in `tests/golden_robot_json.rs` walks only:

- `tests/`
- `docs/`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `README.md`

`scripts/*.sh` and `scripts/e2e/*.sh` are outside its scan path. Future commits could silently revert the rch wrapping (or introduce new bare-`cargo` invocations) and the test suite would not catch it. The original audit caught these via one-shot `rg` scans, not committed regression tests.

This bead also subsumes `coding_agent_session_search-iaor8` (the zlzpk `set -e + ((CHECKS++))` polish), since extending the scan to detect that bash idiom is in scope here. (See AC.5 — if iaor8's owner closes it, link the closure to this bead's commit.)

## Acceptance criteria

### AC.1 — Add a `scripts_rch_compliance` guard test

Create `tests/scripts_rch_compliance.rs`. It MUST:

- Walk `scripts/**/*.sh` (recursive). Use the same exclude pattern AGENTS.md uses for `tests/` (skip `.gitignore`'d files, `node_modules`, `target`).
- For each file, scan for bare-`cargo` invocations using `regex` crate. Pattern set:
  - `\bcargo\s+(build|test|bench|clippy|run|check|fmt|update|install)\b` outside of comments AND outside of strings.
  - Comments: `^\s*#` (line-start) and trailing `# ...` after a `;`. Heredoc-bodies must also be scanned.
- For each match, classify as compliant or violating:
  - **Compliant:** preceded by `rch exec --`, OR appears inside a `run_cargo()` function body, OR appears inside a `$RCH_BIN exec --` substitution, OR the line itself defines a function named `*cargo*` (definitions, not invocations).
  - **Violating:** any other context.
- Emit `tracing::info!(target: "scripts_rch_compliance", file = path, line = N, snippet = "...", verdict = "compliant|violating")` for every match.
- Test fails on any violating match. Failure message includes file:line, the matched snippet, and a one-line hint pointing at `scripts/lib/run_cargo.sh` (which the project should provide; if it does not, this bead also creates it — see AC.2).

### AC.2 — Provide `scripts/lib/run_cargo.sh` helper (if not already present)

Centralizes the rch-wrap idiom so future scripts can `source` it instead of reinventing. Must export:

- `run_cargo()` function: thin wrapper around `rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${RCH_TARGET_DIR:-/tmp/cass-rch-target}" cargo "$@"`. Logs `tracing::info!`-style structured line to stderr on every invocation: `[run_cargo] cmd=... cwd=... target=... rch_bin=...`.
- `RCH_TARGET_DIR` defaulted to a stable per-script subdir.
- `RCH_BIN` resolution: `${RCH_BIN:-rch}` with a fallback to `~/.local/bin/rch`.

If the file already exists, AC.2 is satisfied and AC.1 should reference it.

### AC.3 — Add a `scripts_set_e_arithmetic_safety` guard test (subsumes iaor8)

Bash's `set -e` plus `((VAR++))` causes silent script abort whenever `VAR` is 0 (the `((CHECKS++))` expression evaluates to 0 itself, which `set -e` treats as failure). Real example: zlzpk's `validate_docs.sh` log_pass function aborted on its first call.

Same `tests/scripts_rch_compliance.rs` (or a sibling test file) extends to:

- Walk `scripts/**/*.sh` and `scripts/e2e/**/*.sh`.
- Match pattern `\(\(\s*\w+\+\+\s*\)\)` and `\(\(\s*\w+\-\-\s*\)\)`.
- For each match, check the file for `set -e` (or `set -euo pipefail`) earlier in the file.
- If `set -e` is present AND the increment idiom is present, fail with file:line and a hint suggesting `((VAR += 1))` or `((VAR++)) || true`.

### AC.4 — Happy-path test

Add fixture `tests/fixtures/scripts_rch_compliance/clean.sh` containing:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/run_cargo.sh"
run_cargo build --release
echo "done"
```

Test asserts the scanner reports zero violations on this fixture.

### AC.5 — Error-path test

Add fixture `tests/fixtures/scripts_rch_compliance/violating.sh` containing:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
cargo build  # bare cargo, should violate
((COUNT++))  # set -e + ++, should violate
```

Test asserts the scanner reports exactly 2 violations and that the failure message includes both file:line locations.

### AC.6 — Edge-case test

Add fixture `tests/fixtures/scripts_rch_compliance/comment_string_immune.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Don't use cargo build directly — wrap via run_cargo.
echo "the line 'cargo test' in this string should not trigger"
cat <<'EOF_INNER'
cargo build  # heredoc body — also should not trigger
EOF_INNER
```

Wait — heredocs CAN contain executable shell when used via `bash <<EOF` so the scanner SHOULD trigger on heredoc bodies executed via `eval`. Test: assert scanner is correctly conservative — flags heredoc that's evaluated, ignores heredoc that's just a string.

### AC.7 — E2E test script

Add `scripts/tests/tafss_compliance_scanner_e2e.sh` (rch-wrapped). Same logging+failure-capture contract as in epic vz9t8. Exercises the scanner against:

1. The real `scripts/` tree at HEAD — expect zero violations.
2. A synthetic violating script created in a tempdir — expect ≥1 violation, all reported to stdout.
3. A synthetic empty `scripts/` tree — expect zero violations, exit 0.

### AC.8 — Verification commands

```bash
# Unit/integration tests
rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-tafss-target \
  cargo test --test scripts_rch_compliance -- --nocapture

# E2E
bash scripts/tests/tafss_compliance_scanner_e2e.sh

# Real-world canary: the test should currently pass on HEAD
# (this bead's CI run against main verifies that)
```

### AC.9 — Rollback plan

If the scanner is too aggressive (e.g., flags a legitimate `cargo` invocation in a comment AND fails CI):

- One-commit revert: delete `tests/scripts_rch_compliance.rs`. The shell scripts themselves remain rch-wrapped (the scanner's job is to keep them so).
- Per-pattern suppression via a `tests/fixtures/scripts_rch_compliance/IGNORE.toml` allowlist (file:line patterns); tracked as a follow-up bead if needed.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring existing shell scripts — the originating beads already did that work. This bead only adds the regression test.
- Linting bash style (shellcheck integration). Useful but separate; tracked elsewhere.

## Verification commit format

```
fix(tests): scripts/**/*.sh rch-compliance + set-e arithmetic guard (coding_agent_session_search-tafss)
```

## Audit artifacts

- `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-vq9l5/`
- `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-yzh2t/`
- `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-zlzpk/`
close_reason: Implemented per all ACs in latest commit. tests/scripts_rch_compliance.rs has 8 tests: 3 live-fire (no_bare_cargo, no_set_e_arithmetic, helper_module_exists), 5 synthetic fixtures (violating script, clean script, set_e+inc, no_set_e+inc, safe-form, comment-immune). scripts/lib/run_cargo.sh provides the shared rch-wrapped cargo invocation helper. scripts/tests/tafss_compliance_scanner_e2e.sh orchestrates. iaor8 was closed-as-superseded by this scanner's set-e arithmetic guard.

title: Add doctor concurrency, lock ownership, and interrupted-repair state model
description:
Background: doctor must not race index rebuilds, watcher ingestion, another doctor repair, or manual cleanup. Existing cass has advisory index lock concepts, but v2 needs a unified recovery-state model so interrupted repair is observable and resumable instead of being mistaken for a clean or failed archive.

Scope: define lock files/state rows for doctor plans, candidate builds, restore, cleanup, backup verification, and promotion. Include owner pid/process metadata, command line or mode, heartbeat, started_at, stale-owner detection, read-only behavior while a repair is active, and explicit refusal rules for concurrent mutating doctors. Define interrupted-state classifications for abandoned candidates, incomplete receipts, missing event logs, stale verification-failed markers, and parked backups after partial promotion. The model should support safe inspection by doctor check without mutating state.

Acceptance criteria: doctor check reports active repair/rebuild state; repair refuses unsafe concurrency; interrupted candidate directories and receipts are classified without deletion; stale states produce specific next actions rather than generic failure. Unit tests simulate stale and active locks, heartbeat expiry, pid reuse ambiguity, missing owner metadata, interrupted candidate build, interrupted promotion, concurrent cleanup, and read-only check during active repair. E2E tests run two doctor processes against the same fixture and assert one blocks with lock-busy/repair-blocked JSON while artifacts show no live archive mutation.
close_reason: Implemented doctor operation_state concurrency model and mutation lock. cass doctor --fix now acquires doctor/locks/doctor-repair.lock before mutating, reports active index/watch/doctor owners, classifies interrupted doctor/tmp, receipt/event, raw-mirror tmp, legacy lock, and interrupted lexical publish backup artifacts without deletion, blocks mutating repair when locks or interrupted artifacts are present, and exposes repair-blocked/lock-busy JSON. Added unit, CLI, e2e-runner pointer, schema, and golden coverage; verified cargo test --lib doctor_asset_taxonomy_tests, cargo test --test cli_doctor, cargo test --test doctor_e2e_runner, golden tests, fmt, check, clippy, and diff check.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Plan-space review refinement: treat pid/owner metadata as advisory evidence, not authority. The state model should explicitly handle pid reuse, missing /proc access, clock skew, host reboot, remote-source locks, and stale heartbeats by producing unknown/needs-manual-review states rather than unsafe stale-lock cleanup. E2E lock tests should prove the recommended action stays non-destructive when ownership cannot be proven.

title: Add metamorphic pack field-mask projection tests
description:
Background: Queue is dry after closing docs-safety work. The recent pack field-mask implementation added dotted projection and mixed unknown-field behavior, but its focused tests assert examples rather than metamorphic invariants. Field-mask projection has predictable relations under input transformations: reordering requested fields and adding duplicate valid fields should not change the projected JSON payload.

title: Eliminate remaining process-global environment mutation from all Rust tests
description:
Problem: after do8r7 removes the E2E subprocess trace guard, 21 Rust test targets still contain roughly 207 EnvGuard::set or std::env::set_var/remove_var operations. The largest surfaces are tui_smoke (40), semantic_integration (28), connector_codex (28), connector_pi_agent (24), cli_index (19), regression_behavioral (11), and e2e_full_integration (10). These calls share one process across libtest threads; serialization only masks overlap, and a panic can strand a value for later tests. The immutable pre-change workspace control already demonstrated 62 failures under --test-threads=1, so this is correctness and evidence integrity, not cosmetic cleanup.

Design: split by dependency shape, not by file count. (A) Subprocess tests must construct children through E2eCommandEnvironment and pass all configuration directly with Command::env. (B) In-process connector/indexer tests must stop using environment as an API: add explicit configuration/context inputs or pure lookup-closure parsers, then test those values directly. (C) Tests of genuinely process-global facilities such as tracing subscriber installation must execute in a dedicated child test process with a typed fixture protocol, never mutate the shared libtest process. (D) Preserve every current fixture, protocol assertion, log field, and error branch; do not replace real behavior with mocks or broad serialization. Add child beads per A/B/C surface after graph review so agents can work on non-overlapping files.

Acceptance: repository-wide structural policy reports zero production-test EnvGuard::set and zero std::env::set_var/remove_var outside a narrowly documented child-process bootstrap module; all former environment parser cases have pure unit coverage; connector/indexer integrations pass under default parallel scheduling and --test-threads=1; deliberate overlapping tests prove disjoint values; panic-path tests prove no leakage to the next case; workspace check, clippy -D warnings, rustfmt, relevant E2E suites, and UBS pass; before/after elapsed time is reported only as harness throughput; no product-performance claim is inferred.

title: Migrate watch, import, salvage, and incremental entrypoints onto the same streaming packet pipeline with shadow-equivalence gates
description:
BACKGROUND:
A new many-core rebuild pipeline only solves part of the problem if watch mode, import flows, salvage, and other incremental mutation paths keep their own bespoke normalization and indexing logic. The architecture must converge on one shared streaming path or the project will re-accumulate serial hot spots and correctness drift.

GOAL:
Move all meaningful indexing entrypoints onto the same packet-driven streaming pipeline with guarded rollout and equivalence proof.

SCOPE:
- Audit full index, watch startup, steady-state watch, watch-once, import, salvage, and repair flows.
- Route each path through the shared packet and stage machinery rather than sink-specific bespoke loops.
- Add shadow or compare mode where needed so old/new behavior can be compared safely before removal of legacy paths.
- Preserve existing user-visible guarantees for targeted incremental work and automatic lexical freshness.

DONE WHEN:
All important indexing entrypoints use the shared streaming pipeline, or explicitly document why they remain legacy-only temporarily, with equivalence evidence for the migrated cases.
design:
DESIGN / JUSTIFICATION:
- The new packet pipeline only matters if it becomes the one path that real indexing entrypoints share; otherwise the codebase will keep re-growing bespoke serial loops and mismatched semantics.
- Migrate entrypoints in a guarded way: prefer shadow or compare mode first, capture semantic diffs, then flip the authoritative path only after equivalence is demonstrated.
- Keep user-facing guarantees boring: watch and incremental flows should still feel immediate and deterministic even if the internal pipeline is now staged and controller-aware.
- Allow temporary exemptions only when there is a written reason, an explicit owner, and a plan to converge later.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Full rebuild, watch startup, steady-state watch, watch-once, import, salvage, and repair are each either routed through the shared packet pipeline or explicitly tracked as a temporary exemption with rationale.
- Shadow-equivalence or compare-mode evidence exists for the migrated paths, proving packet content, lexical output, and checkpoint behavior match the intended source-of-truth semantics.
- Robot or integration coverage shows migrated incremental paths preserve automatic lexical freshness, deterministic progress reporting, and clear diagnostics about which pipeline path ran.
notes:
LOCAL VALIDATION / FUTURE-SELF NOTES:
- Preserve a migration matrix listing every indexing entrypoint, whether it is legacy, shadowed, or fully migrated, and what evidence was used to justify the state.
- Save at least one divergence artifact from compare mode so future agents know what a real mismatch looks like.
- Resist one-off fast paths unless they are encoded as reusable pipeline stages rather than bespoke loops.
close_reason: Added index --json entrypoint diagnostics so watch/incremental/full paths are machine-readable during the streaming-pipeline migration.

title: Add dialoguer crate for interactive TUI
description:
# Add dialoguer crate for interactive TUI

## What
Add the `dialoguer` crate (and evaluate alternatives) to enable interactive 
terminal UI components for the setup wizard.

## Why
The remote sources setup wizard needs rich interactive components:
- Multi-select checkbox list with multi-line item display
- Confirmation prompts before destructive operations  
- Search/filter for large host lists

## Critical Design Decision: Library Choice

### The Challenge
Our selection UI design (from rnjt) shows multi-line items:
```
[x] css
    209.145.54.164 • ubuntu
    ✓ cass v0.1.50 installed • 1,234 sessions
    Claude ✓  Codex ✓  Cursor ✓
```

Standard dialoguer MultiSelect shows single-line items only. We need to evaluate:

### Option 1: dialoguer with ANSI pre-formatting
```rust
let items: Vec<String> = hosts.iter().map(|h| {
    format!("{}\n    {} • {}\n    {} • {} sessions\n    {}",
        h.name.bold(),
        h.hostname.dimmed(),
        h.os.dimmed(),
        format_cass_status(&h.cass_status),
        h.session_count,
        format_agents(&h.detected_agents)
    )
}).collect();

MultiSelect::new().items(&items).interact()?
```
- **Pro**: We already use dialoguer patterns, consistent with indicatif
- **Con**: ANSI in items may cause display issues, no built-in search

### Option 2: inquire crate
```rust
use inquire::MultiSelect;

let items: Vec<HostItem> = hosts.iter().map(|h| HostItem::from(h)).collect();
MultiSelect::new("Select hosts:", items)
    .with_formatter(&|opts| format_selected(opts))
    .with_render_config(render_config())
    .prompt()?
```
- **Pro**: Better item formatting support, built-in filtering
- **Con**: Different API, another dependency

### Option 3: Custom with ratatui
Build custom selection widget using ratatui (tui-rs successor).
- **Pro**: Complete control, can match exact mockup
- **Con**: Significant implementation effort, heavy dependency

### Recommendation
Start with **Option 1 (dialoguer + ANSI)** for simplicity. If that proves 
insufficient, pivot to Option 2 (inquire). Document this decision.

## Implementation Steps
1. Add `dialoguer = "*"` to Cargo.toml
2. Add `console = "*"` if not present (dialoguer's styling backend)  
3. Create proof-of-concept MultiSelect with multi-line ANSI items
4. Test terminal compatibility (various terminals, sizes)
5. If PoC fails, evaluate inquire as fallback

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] dialoguer compiles without errors
- [ ] Proof-of-concept: MultiSelect with 3-4 line items displays correctly
- [ ] Test in: Terminal.app, iTerm2, VS Code terminal, basic Linux terminal
- [ ] ANSI colors render correctly in items
- [ ] Selection indices map correctly to multi-line items
- [ ] Document any limitations found

## Fallback Plan
If dialoguer multi-line items don't work well:
```toml
# Alternative
inquire = "*"
```
The inquire crate has native support for custom item rendering.

## Notes
- dialoguer integrates well with indicatif (already in use for progress bars)
- Both libraries are actively maintained
- Either choice should support our needs with different tradeoffs
close_reason: Implemented HostSelector with multi-line ANSI display, confirmation prompts, and 7 passing tests. Code committed in cbf1888.

title: Vector index operations (read/write/search)
description:
## Purpose
Implement vector index CRUD operations with crash safety and optimized search.

## Core Operations
1. **Create**: Build index from embeddings + metadata
2. **Load**: mmap from disk, validate header CRC32
3. **Save**: Atomic write (temp → fsync → rename)
4. **Search**: Brute-force dot product with inline filter

## Atomic Write Pattern
```rust
fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    let temp = path.with_extension("cvvi.tmp");
    let mut f = File::create(&temp)?;
    self.write_to(&mut f)?;
    f.sync_all()?;  // fsync file
    File::open(temp.parent().unwrap())?.sync_all()?;  // fsync dir
    std::fs::rename(&temp, path)?;  // atomic rename
}
```

## f16 Quantization
- Use half crate for f16 ↔ f32 conversion
- Quantize on write, dequantize on read
- Quality loss negligible for cosine similarity
- Memory: 50k vectors × 384 dim = 36MB (f16) vs 73MB (f32)

## SIMD-Optimized Search (Critical for Performance)
For 50k vectors, naive search could take 50-100ms. With SIMD, target <20ms.

**Optimization strategies**:
1. **Aligned allocation**: Ensure vector slab is 32-byte aligned for AVX
2. **Contiguous layout**: Store all vectors contiguously for cache efficiency
3. **Iterator patterns**: Use patterns that auto-vectorize well
4. **Consider explicit SIMD**: If auto-vectorization insufficient, use `std::simd` (nightly) or `wide` crate

```rust
// Good: Auto-vectorizes well
fn dot_product(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    a.iter().zip(b.iter()).map(|(x, y)| x * y).sum()
}

// Alternative: Explicit SIMD with wide crate
fn dot_product_simd(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
    use wide::f32x8;
    // ... 8-wide SIMD dot product
}
```

**Benchmarking required**: Test auto-vectorization vs explicit SIMD on target hardware.

## mmap Loading
For large indices (>100MB), use mmap to avoid loading entire file into RAM:
```rust
let mmap = unsafe { Mmap::map(&file)? };
let vectors = VectorSlab::from_mmap(&mmap, header.count, header.dimension);
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Roundtrip: save → load preserves all data
- [ ] Atomic: crash mid-write doesn't corrupt
- [ ] mmap loading for large indices
- [ ] f16 vs f32 rankings are equivalent
- [ ] Search 50k vectors < 20ms (benchmark!)
- [ ] Vector slab is properly aligned for SIMD

## Depends On
- sem.vec.fmt (CVVI format)
- sem.emb.hash (for testing)

## References
- Plan: Section 5.2-5.4

title: P3.7: Settings & Storage Controls
description:
# P3.7: Settings & Storage Controls

## Goal
Provide a settings panel at #/settings for security and storage controls, aligned with the OPFS opt-in design and session management guidance.

## Required Controls
- Session mode:
  - Memory-only (default)
  - SessionStorage (survive refresh, not new tab)
  - LocalStorage (explicit warning, least secure)
- OPFS persistence opt-in ("Remember on this device")
- Clear OPFS cache button (force re-decrypt)
- Clear Service Worker cache (re-fetch assets)
- Lock/Reset session (forget derived key)

## UX Requirements
- Clear warnings about security tradeoffs
- Show current cache state and approximate size
- Confirmations for destructive actions

## Implementation Notes
- Use storage abstraction (session storage, local storage, memory)
- OPFS cache metadata keyed by export_id
- Integrate with decrypt pipeline to honor opt-in

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests
- storage mode switching
- OPFS metadata read/write/clear

### Integration Tests
- enable OPFS -> refresh -> loads from cache
- clear cache -> forces decrypt

### E2E
- navigate to #/settings and toggle modes
- log clear action results

## Files to Create/Modify
- web/src/settings.js
- web/src/storage.js
- web/src/viewer.js (route integration)
- web/tests/settings.test.js

## Exit Criteria
1. OPFS opt-in and clear-cache flow works
2. Session storage modes behave as documented
3. Settings panel accessible and understandable
close_reason: Complete: settings.js has full implementation with storage mode selector (memory/session/local), OPFS opt-in toggle, clear OPFS/SW cache buttons, lock/reset session controls. Integrated into bundle.rs

title: [Task] Opt 3.1: Verify VectorRow is Send+Sync for Rayon
description:
# Task: Verify VectorRow is Send+Sync for Rayon

## Objective

Before implementing parallel search with Rayon, verify that `VectorRow` and related types implement `Send` and `Sync` traits, which are required for safe parallel iteration.

## Investigation Steps

### 1. Check VectorRow Definition
```bash
# Find VectorRow definition
rg "struct VectorRow" src/
```

### 2. Verify Trait Implementations
```rust
// Add to tests or run in playground
fn assert_send<T: Send>() {}
fn assert_sync<T: Sync>() {}

#[test]
fn vector_row_is_send_sync() {
    assert_send::<VectorRow>();
    assert_sync::<VectorRow>();
}
```

### 3. Check All Fields
VectorRow should only contain:
- Primitive types (u64, u32, f32, etc.) - inherently Send+Sync
- &str/String - Send+Sync
- No Rc, RefCell, raw pointers

### 4. Check VectorIndex Sharability
For parallel search, we need:
```rust
// VectorIndex must be sharable across threads
fn assert_sync<T: Sync>() {}
assert_sync::<VectorIndex>();  // Or &VectorIndex must be Send
```

## Expected Findings

VectorRow likely contains only:
- `message_id: u64`
- `chunk_idx: u32`
- `vec_offset: usize`

All primitive types = Send + Sync ✓

## Potential Issues

If VectorRow contains:
- `Rc<T>` → Not Send, need to use `Arc<T>`
- `RefCell<T>` → Not Sync, need different design
- Raw pointer → May need unsafe impl or wrapper

## Document Findings

1. List all fields in VectorRow
2. Confirm Send+Sync status
3. Note any required changes

## Validation Checklist

- [ ] VectorRow definition found
- [ ] All fields enumerated
- [ ] Send+Sync compile test passes
- [ ] VectorIndex sharability confirmed
- [ ] No blocking issues identified

## Dependencies

- Requires completion of Opt 2.4 (SIMD benchmarked)
- This is a prerequisite for Opt 3.2 (implementation)

title: Advanced Performance Optimizations Round 1 (OPUS Analysis)
description:
# Performance Optimization Epic

## Background
A deep, ultra-intensive code analysis was performed to identify provably-isomorphic optimizations
in the cass codebase. These optimizations maintain identical output while improving performance
through better algorithms, data structures, and memory access patterns.

## Scope
18 distinct optimization opportunities identified across 4 tiers:
- **Tier 1 (High Impact):** 5 optimizations with 15-60% improvement potential
- **Tier 2 (Medium Impact):** 5 optimizations with 5-20% improvement potential  
- **Tier 3 (Architectural):** 3 optimizations requiring structural changes
- **Tier 4 (Micro-optimizations):** 5 small targeted improvements

## Key Principles
1. **Isomorphic Changes Only:** All optimizations produce identical outputs
2. **Measurable Impact:** Each has benchmarkable before/after metrics
3. **No Over-Engineering:** Minimum complexity for maximum gain
4. **Hot Path Focus:** Changes target actual performance-critical code paths

## Files Analyzed
- src/search/vector_index.rs (CVVI format, SIMD dot products)
- src/search/query.rs (query execution, caching, RRF fusion)
- src/search/tantivy.rs (edge n-gram generation)
- src/search/canonicalize.rs (text normalization)
- src/storage/sqlite.rs (metadata parsing, schema)
- src/connectors/mod.rs (workspace path matching)
- src/indexer/mod.rs (parallel scanning, agent discovery)

title: Promote verified candidates with atomic swap and rollback receipts
description:
Background: once a candidate has passed integrity and coverage checks, promotion still needs filesystem safety. Readers should never see a half-swapped DB/index, and interrupted promotion should be recoverable. Promotion is not cleanup: prior live state remains evidence until a separate approved cleanup flow handles derived artifacts.

Scope: implement atomic promotion for DB bundle and derived indexes with parked backups, fsync/sync-tree where appropriate, rollback on failure, and receipt records. Handle DB/WAL/SHM sidecars as an indivisible bundle, and keep lexical/semantic derived assets consistent with the promoted DB generation. Readers should see old or new state, never a mixed generation. Keep prior live state under a verified backup path until explicitly reclaimed by the separate cleanup command and never delete source/mirror/config/bookmark evidence during promotion.

Acceptance criteria: promotion is all-or-nothing from the user perspective; crash/interruption tests leave either old or new usable state; rollback receipts point to exact backup paths; no source evidence is deleted. Unit tests cover generation markers, sidecar bundling, rollback path selection, fsync failure, rename fallback, reader-visible consistency, backup manifest checksums, and refusal when coverage/probe gates are stale. E2E/fault-injection scripts interrupt promotion at multiple phases and capture before/after inventories, DB open probes, search readiness, receipts, event logs, and rollback verification.
close_reason: Acceptance satisfied: atomic candidate DB/WAL/SHM promotion now has rollback receipts, failpoint interruption e2e coverage, post-repair DB/search probes, derived follow-up truth surfaces, and reader-visible old-or-new lock-window proof; semantic/vector model-depth work remains tracked separately in coding_agent_session_search-j17zv.

title: P1.3a: Dual FTS5 Strategy (Code vs Prose)
description:
# P1.3a: Dual FTS5 Strategy (Code vs Prose) **Parent Phase:** Phase 1: Core Export **Section Reference:** Plan Document Section 9.2, lines 1623-1658 **Depends On:** P1.3 (FTS5 Index Generation) ## Goal Implement dual FTS5 indexes optimized for different content types: one for natural language prose (with Porter stemming) and one for code/paths (with unicode tokenization). ## Why Two Indexes? | Content Type | Best Tokenizer | Example Query | Reason | |--------------|----------------|---------------|--------| | Prose/docs | porter unicode61 | "running tests" matches "run test" | Stemming finds word variants | | Code/paths | unicode61 tokenchars | "getUserId" exact match | Camel case, no stemming | ## Schema ```sql -- Index 1: Prose search (Porter stemmer for natural language) CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_fts USING fts5( content, title, tokenize = 'porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2' ); -- Index 2: Code/path search (unicode with extended tokenchars) CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE messages_code_fts USING fts5( content, source_path, tokenize = "unicode61 tokenchars '-_./\\:@#$%'" ); -- Populate both indexes INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, content, title) SELECT id, content, title FROM messages; INSERT INTO messages_code_fts(rowid, content, source_path) SELECT m.id, m.content, c.source_path FROM messages m JOIN conversations c ON m.conversation_id = c.id; ``` ## Query Strategy Selection ### Auto-Detection Heuristics ```javascript function detectQueryType(query) { // Code patterns const codePatterns = [ /[A-Z][a-z]+[A-Z]/, // camelCase /[a-z]+_[a-z]+/, // snake_case /\.[a-z]{2,4}$/, // file extensions /\/[a-z]+\//, // path segments /\.[a-zA-Z]+\(/, // method calls /^(def|fn|func|class|const|let|var)\s/, // keywords ]; const isCode = codePatterns.some(p => p.test(query)); // Prose indicators const proseIndicators = [ query.split(' ').length > 3, // Multi-word /^(how|what|why|when|where)\b/i.test(query), // Questions /\b(the|is|are|was|were)\b/i.test(query), // Articles ]; const isProse = proseIndicators.some(Boolean); if (isCode && !isProse) return 'code'; if (isProse && !isCode) return 'prose'; return 'both'; // Search both, merge results } ``` ### Search Execution ```javascript async function search(db, query, limit = 50) { const queryType = detectQueryType(query); const sanitizedQuery = sanitizeFtsQuery(query); if (queryType === 'prose') { return db.exec(` SELECT m.*, messages_fts.rank FROM messages_fts JOIN messages m ON messages_fts.rowid = m.id WHERE messages_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY rank LIMIT ? `, [sanitizedQuery, limit]); } if (queryType === 'code') { return db.exec(` SELECT m.*, messages_code_fts.rank FROM messages_code_fts JOIN messages m ON messages_code_fts.rowid = m.id WHERE messages_code_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY rank LIMIT ? `, [sanitizedQuery, limit]); } // Search both, merge and deduplicate const [proseResults, codeResults] = await Promise.all([ searchProse(db, sanitizedQuery, limit), searchCode(db, sanitizedQuery, limit), ]); return mergeAndRank(proseResults, codeResults, limit); } ``` ### Query Sanitization (FTS5 Injection Prevention) ```javascript function sanitizeFtsQuery(query) { // Escape FTS5 special characters return query .replace(/"/g, '""') // Escape quotes .replace(/\*/g, '') // Remove wildcards (or allow?) .replace(/\^/g, '') // Remove prefix operator .trim(); } // Wrap in quotes for exact phrase function exactPhrase(query) { return '"' + sanitizeFtsQuery(query) + '"'; } ``` ## UI Integration ### Search Mode Toggle ```html
``` ### Visual Indicator Show which index was used: ``` 🔍 Searching code index... (detected "getUserId" as code pattern) ``` ## Test Cases 1. "running tests" → prose index, finds "run test" 2. "getUserId" → code index, exact match 3. "src/main.rs" → code index, path match 4. "how does auth work" → prose index 5. Mixed query → both indexes, merged results 6. SQL injection attempt → sanitized, no error 7. Empty query → handled gracefully ## Files to Create/Modify - `src/pages/schema.sql` (add dual FTS tables) - `web/src/search.js` (query type detection) - `tests/fts_dual.rs` (new) - `web/tests/search.test.js` (new) ## Exit Criteria 1. Both FTS indexes created correctly 2. Auto-detection works for common patterns 3. Manual override available in UI 4. Results properly merged and ranked 5. No FTS5 injection vulnerabilities
close_reason: Already implemented: dual FTS tables + auto/override search mode + tests

title: Expose first-class doctor e2e and golden tooling commands
description:
Background: mcp_agent_mail_rust makes validation practical by exposing e2e list/run and golden capture/verify surfaces instead of hiding everything behind tribal scripts. Cass doctor already has beads for e2e scripts and golden tests, but the plan should require a discoverable developer interface so future agents can run the right subset without guessing.

Problem: doctor v2 will span read-only checks, repair, reconstruct, restore, cleanup, auto-run, privacy, fault injection, and cross-platform filesystem behavior. If validation is only a collection of ad hoc test names, agents will either run too little or waste time running the wrong heavy suites. Worse, they may accidentally run tests against live user archives if the interface is not opinionated.

Scope: add a first-class validation surface for doctor scenarios. This can be a cargo xtask, scripts/doctor-e2e wrapper, or cass-internal test harness command, whichever best fits the repo, but it must provide list, describe, run, filter/include, exclude, force-build when relevant, artifact-dir, update-goldens, verify-goldens, fail-fast, keep-temp, json output, and scenario-manifest validation. It should classify scenarios by speed/risk labels and print the exact safe command to rerun a failure. It must never run bare cass TUI. It must default to safe fixture data and refuse to mutate live user archives unless an explicit test-only fixture path is provided.

Acceptance criteria: agents can list doctor scenarios, inspect expected contracts, run one scenario, run a labeled group, capture artifacts, update reviewed goldens, and verify goldens using documented commands. The command output includes scenario id, fixture id, label set, expected mutation class, log paths, failure_context path on failure, and next suggested command. Unit tests or smoke tests cover CLI parsing, scenario discovery, manifest validation, refusal of unsafe live paths, and JSON output stability. E2E documentation includes example commands for common doctor development workflows and names which suites are quick enough for local use versus CI/release-only.

Implementation note: this bead is about making verification operational. It should depend on the e2e runner and golden contract beads and should block final release validation.
close_reason: Implemented and verified first-class doctor e2e/golden tooling command surface with safe fixture defaults, scenario discovery, filtering, artifact/run summaries, golden helpers, docs, and full cargo gates.

title: [P3] Opt 8: Streaming Backpressure for Indexing
description:
# Optimization 8: Streaming Backpressure for Indexing

## Problem Statement

Current indexing collects ALL `pending_batches` from ALL connectors before starting ingestion:

### Current Flow
```
1. Discover all sources (Claude, Cursor, Gemini, etc.)
2. For each source: scan filesystem, parse JSONLs, collect batches
3. Store ALL batches in memory
4. Ingest ALL batches into Tantivy + SQLite
```

### Memory Impact
- 3000 conversations × 12 messages = 36,000 messages in memory
- Peak RSS: 295 MB (from profiling)
- All data must fit in RAM before processing starts

### Allocation Profile Evidence
```
Indexing total allocated: ~1,375 MB for 36k messages
```

This is well above the 295 MB peak RSS because of:
- Batch collection → ingestion → deallocation cycle
- Rust's allocator holding onto freed pages

## Proposed Solution

Stream per-connector with bounded channel to single ingest worker.

### Architecture
```
┌───────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐
│ Claude Conn.  │────▶│               │     │               │
├───────────────┤     │   Bounded     │────▶│   Ingest      │
│ Cursor Conn.  │────▶│   Channel     │     │   Worker      │
├───────────────┤     │   (N=100)     │     │               │
│ Gemini Conn.  │────▶│               │     │               │
└───────────────┘     └───────────────┘     └───────────────┘
     Producers             Buffer              Consumer
```

### Implementation Location
- File: `src/indexing/mod.rs` (or wherever batch coordination happens)
- Modify connector → ingestion flow

### Code Sketch
```rust
use std::sync::mpsc::{sync_channel, SyncSender, Receiver};
use std::thread;

const BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 100;

struct StreamingIndexer {
    tx: SyncSender<ConversationBatch>,
    ingest_handle: thread::JoinHandle<Result<IndexStats>>,
}

impl StreamingIndexer {
    fn new(tantivy_index: TantivyIndex, sqlite_conn: Connection) -> Self {
        let (tx, rx) = sync_channel(BATCH_BUFFER_SIZE);
        
        let ingest_handle = thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut stats = IndexStats::default();
            for batch in rx {
                // Ingest one batch at a time
                tantivy_index.add_conversation(&batch)?;
                sqlite_conn.insert_conversation(&batch)?;
                stats.conversations += 1;
                stats.messages += batch.messages.len();
            }
            Ok(stats)
        });
        
        Self { tx, ingest_handle }
    }

    fn send_batch(&self, batch: ConversationBatch) -> Result<()> {
        // Blocks if channel is full (backpressure!)
        self.tx.send(batch)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn finish(self) -> Result<IndexStats> {
        drop(self.tx); // Signal completion
        self.ingest_handle.join().unwrap()
    }
}

// Usage in connector
for conversation in claude_connector.discover() {
    let batch = parse_conversation(conversation)?;
    streaming_indexer.send_batch(batch)?;  // Blocks if ingest is slow
}
```

### Backpressure Mechanism
- `sync_channel(100)` creates a bounded channel
- When buffer is full, `send()` blocks the producer
- This prevents memory from growing unboundedly
- Connectors automatically slow down when ingestion is the bottleneck

## Expected Impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Peak RSS | 295 MB | ~100-150 MB |
| Total alloc | 1,375 MB | ~same (but spread over time) |
| Memory spikes | Large | Controlled |
| Indexing latency | ~same | ~same (possibly +5% overhead) |

The main benefit is **predictable memory usage**, not speed improvement.

## Risk: Ordering Changes

### The Risk
If ingestion becomes interleaved differently (e.g., Claude batch 1, Cursor batch 1, Claude batch 2), the order of database inserts may change.

### Impact Analysis
- **Search results**: Unaffected (ordering by score, not insert order)
- **Message IDs**: May differ between runs (if auto-increment)
- **Tie-breaking**: If messages have same score and different IDs, order may change

### Mitigation
- Ensure stable sort with secondary key (e.g., source_path + timestamp)
- Document that message IDs are not stable across reindexing
- Add equivalence test comparing search results (not IDs)

## Isomorphism (Relaxed)

This optimization has **weaker** guarantees than others:
- Same **set** of indexed content
- Potentially different **ordering** of inserts
- Same **search results** (hit set, not necessarily order for tied scores)

### Property to Preserve
```
∀ query: set(search(query).hits.message_id) ≡ set(search_streaming(query).hits.message_id)
```

Note: This is set equality, not sequence equality.

## Implementation Complexity

This is rated **HIGH effort** because:
1. Significant architectural change to indexing flow
2. Need to handle errors in worker thread
3. Progress reporting becomes async
4. Cancellation handling
5. Testing concurrent code

## Verification Plan

1. **Metamorphic test**: Batch vs streaming indexing yield same search results
2. **Memory test**: Peak RSS stays below threshold during streaming
3. **Stress test**: Large corpus (100k messages) doesn't OOM
4. **Cancellation test**: Ctrl-C during indexing doesn't corrupt index

## Rollback Strategy

Feature flag `CASS_STREAMING_INDEX=0` (or `1` to enable) to:
- Revert to batch collection mode
- Useful if streaming introduces bugs

## Dependencies

- None technically, but should be implemented after P0/P1 optimizations are stable
- Lower priority because memory usage is acceptable currently (295 MB)
- Consider only if targeting memory-constrained environments

title: Duplicate conversations: full-rebuild vs watch ingest compute different external_id formats (projects/<rel> vs <rel>) (gh #302)
description: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED by code reading (Linux). Claude external_id is derived by the FAD connector as path.strip_prefix(scan_root). The two ingest paths use DIFFERENT scan roots for the same corpus: (1) full-rebuild via ScanContext::local_default -> source_roots -> projects_root_candidates() roots at ~/.claude/projects -> bare id '<rel>/<uuid>.jsonl'; (2) live --watch daemon via build_watch_roots uses detect_installed_agents root_paths which reports ~/.claude (FAD src/lib.rs maybe_push(&[".claude"])) -> prefixed id 'projects/<rel>/<uuid>.jsonl'. classify_paths (prefer_explicit_paths=false) sets scan_root.path=root.path (the ~/.claude dir, is_file()=false) so the connector strips ~/.claude leaving the projects/ prefix. Since dedup key is (source_id, agent_id, external_id), the two forms never match -> watcher inserts duplicate rows that accumulate. FIX SHIPPED (forward dedup): canonicalize_claude_external_id() at the prepare_conversation_for_ingest chokepoint strips a single leading 'projects/' for the claude connector so all paths agree on the bare form. REMAINING (this bead): a doctor command to collapse PRE-EXISTING duplicate rows (issue ask #2) for operators who already accumulated dupes -- keep one row + its messages, drop the projects/-prefixed twin.
