title: Define explicit no-op partial blocked and incomplete repair outcome contracts
description:
Background: beads_rust doctor has explicit no-op and incomplete-repair messaging. That is more than polish: it prevents operators and robots from mistaking skipped work for completed repair. Cass doctor needs the same precision because many safe behaviors intentionally refuse mutation.

Problem: archive-first doctor flows will often say no: no mutation because read-only mode, no promotion because coverage would shrink, no cleanup because artifact may still be evidence, no repeated repair because a verification-failed marker exists, or no automatic action because storage pressure is advisory. Those are successful safety decisions, but they are not the same as a fixed system.

Scope: define stable outcome states for each doctor operation: ok-no-action-needed, ok-read-only-diagnosed, fixed, partially-fixed, repair-blocked, repair-refused, repair-incomplete, verification-failed, cleanup-dry-run-only, cleanup-refused, auto-run-skipped, support-bundle-only, baseline-diff-only, and requires-manual-review. Each outcome must include reason, action_taken, action_not_taken, safe_to_retry, requires_override, data_loss_risk, next_command, artifact_manifest_path where relevant, and whether the process exit code should be success, health failure, usage error, lock busy, or repair failure.

Acceptance criteria: robot and human outputs distinguish no-op, partial, blocked, refused, and failed states without relying on free-form prose. Add unit tests for outcome-to-exit-code mapping and representative doctor commands in read-only, dry-run, --fix, --auto, support-bundle, baseline-diff, lock-busy, coverage-shrink, missing-authority, and marker-refusal scenarios. E2E scripts assert robots can branch on outcome.kind and recommended_action while human output remains clear. Update robot-docs to tell agents exactly how to branch on outcome.kind rather than numeric exit codes alone.

Implementation note: this bead should feed the stable schema, golden tests, human output copy, repair receipts, and safe auto-run orchestration. The goal is to make cautious refusal feel useful rather than broken.
close_reason: Implemented the stable DoctorOperationOutcomeKind contract across robot JSON, introspection schema, robot-docs, cleanup receipts, e2e pointer assertions, and human doctor output coverage. Verified unit, CLI, e2e, golden, fmt, check, and clippy gates.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Fresh-eyes graph correction: this outcome-contract bead should be upstream of the doctor module refactor, not blocked by it. The contract needs only the asset taxonomy, anomaly vocabulary, and repair-mode design; then the module refactor and all later command surfaces can implement one shared outcome model instead of inventing ad hoc blocked/refused/no-op states.

title: Profile-driven re-engineering of index-time secret redaction hot path
description: Operator verdict: index-time redaction is catastrophically slow on giant single conversations (60-90MB codex rollouts, ~40k messages ran 10+ min single-threaded in map_to_internal_with_redactor). Campaign: (1) measure with a bench over real fixtures (benches/redaction_perf.rs), (2) profile, (3) optimize the MemoizingRedactor/map path with byte-identical output proofs (frozen-reference property test + golden corpus + real-corpus output digest), (4) parallelize giant single conversations, (5) add documented operator switch CASS_INDEX_REDACTION=full|off (default full, legacy CASS_REDACT_SECRETS preserved). Threat model note: raw session files and cass raw-mirror blobs (encryption state none) already hold the same raw text on disk; index-time redaction protects queryable surfaces only.
close_reason: Campaign complete with measured proof. THREAT MODEL: index-time redaction protects only queryable surfaces (SQLite rows, FTS/lexical index, exports, robot output) — raw session files AND cass raw-mirror blobs (<data_dir>/raw-mirror/v1/, encryption state 'none', captured unconditionally in prepare_conversation_for_ingest) already hold the same raw text on disk. BASELINE (bench redaction_perf, real codex fixtures, medians): production memoized path ran at 17.3MB/s on a 21.8MB/20,902-msg midsize corpus (1.2592s) — 18.0x slower than the plain uncached path in the same run; profile showed O(capacity) VecDeque LRU MemoKey memcmp scans + blake3 keying + double copies dwarfing actual regex work ~17:1. ROUNDS (each with byte-identical output digests on all fixtures + 31/31 redact tests green): R1 f5f4d7ba prefilter-first cache bypass (clean strings skip all memo machinery): midsize 1.2592->0.0614s (20.5x), mixed 0.3711->0.0180s (20.6x), giant 0.1427->0.0145s (9.8x). R2 e4a15698 O(log n) recency-sequence LRU: candidate-dense worst case (12k distinct Bearer tokens) 0.2816->0.0763s (3.7x). R3 ec20b699 64KiB memoization byte-cap bounds worst-case cache memory to ~256MiB (was unbounded GBs — the swap-thrash regime of the original incident). FINAL: midsize 0.0563s (387MB/s, 22x), mixed 0.0144s (26x), giant single-conversation 0.0123s (12x), dense 0.0665s (4.2x); memoized==uncached ratio 18x->~1.0x. OPERATOR CONTROL (landed 21f095a3): CASS_INDEX_REDACTION=full|off, default full unchanged, legacy CASS_REDACT_SECRETS honored, precedence tested, README documents the honest trade. Proofs: frozen-reference proptest (512 cases), literal golden corpus incl. adversarial near-misses, blake3 output digests on 4 real/synthetic fixtures stable across all rounds. Caveats: host under swarm load (LA 12-85) — medians + same-run ratios used; giant 63MB rollout parses to only 2,427 msgs on current FAD (>=32MB extra compaction upstream already mitigates the original incident shape); pre-existing flaky begin-concurrent persist test filed as wp8i0; pre-existing storage/sqlite failures tracked separately (08c455fa).

title: [MEDIUM] cleanup_path_has_symlink_below_root fails open when walk exhausts parents past root
description: src/lib.rs::cleanup_path_has_symlink_below_root (added in 0a89a96a) returns false ("no symlink, safe") in two arms when the walk reaches the filesystem root without ever hitting the configured root: (a) symlink_metadata error and (b) parent==current. The bead's commit message states the walk "runs out of parents (fail closed)" but the current code returns false in those branches, which is the SAFE direction in the safety predicate, not fail-closed. Reachable via paths with .. segments that pass the upstream Path::starts_with check (which is component-based and does not canonicalize). Currently masked by the downstream canonicalize() check inside cleanup_target_path_is_safe — defense-in-depth catches it. A future refactor that removes or weakens the canonicalize check would expose the gap as a real symlink-escape vector. Fix: return true ("has symlink, unsafe") in the unreachable-root arms so the helper itself is fail-closed independent of downstream canonicalize. Add a regression test where path passes textual starts_with via .. but the symlink walk exhausts parents — pre-fix the helper returns false (caller would have to rely on canonicalize), post-fix it returns true.

title: [MEDIUM] mock-finder: ensure_cass_origin helper is dead code (no callers anywhere in src/)
description:
Mock-code-finder finding: orphaned helper.

## Location
\`src/lib.rs:11641-11642\`:

\`\`\`rust
#[allow(dead_code)]
fn ensure_cass_origin(
    metadata: &mut serde_json::Value,
    source_id: &str,
    kind: crate::sources::provenance::SourceKind,
    host: Option<&str>,
) {
    if !metadata.is_object() {
        *metadata = serde_json::json!({});
    }

    let Some(obj) = metadata.as_object_mut() else {
        return;
    };
    // ...
}
\`\`\`

The \`#[allow(dead_code)]\` attribute plus grep across the full src/
tree confirms this function has ZERO callers:

\`\`\`
\$ rg -n 'ensure_cass_origin' src/
src/lib.rs:11642:fn ensure_cass_origin(
\`\`\`

Single hit — the definition itself.

## What's incomplete
The function's signature suggests it was written to stamp cass
provenance fields (source_id, origin_kind, origin_host) onto a
\`serde_json::Value\` produced by a connector or export path —
probably part of an earlier provenance-enrichment slice that was
rolled back or refactored around. Now it sits as dead scaffolding
that takes up space and invites future drift: someone could
inadvertently re-enable it against a serialization contract that
has moved on.

## Suggested completion
Three options:

1. **Wire it in** — grep for places that build \`serde_json::Value\`
   containing session/conversation metadata and should stamp
   provenance (e.g., export-html JSON payloads, models status
   blocks with source references). If the function is still useful,
   remove \`#[allow(dead_code)]\` and add the call sites. Add a
   regression test proving the provenance fields appear in the
   stamped output.

2. **Delete it** — if provenance stamping has moved to a different
   code path (e.g., \`normalized_search_hit_source_id\` /
   \`normalized_search_hit_origin_kind\` which ARE used), this
   helper is obsolete. Remove the function + its
   \`use crate::sources::provenance::SourceKind\` import if that was
   pulled in only for this fn.

3. **Document why it's reserved** — if it's intentionally kept for
   a specific upcoming slice, replace the bare
   \`#[allow(dead_code)]\` with a doc comment naming the bead ID and
   expected wiring plan (similar to the
   \`LexicalRebuildFinalMergeArtifact.segments\` pattern at
   src/indexer/mod.rs:11215 which has a clear "kept for test
   assertions + future diagnostics" comment).

Option 2 is the minimal cleanup; option 1 restores intended
functionality if the provenance pipeline still needs it.

## Severity
MEDIUM. Not a functional bug, but dead code in a 28k-line prod
module is a mock-finder signal — either the feature was pulled
half-way or a newer impl exists elsewhere. Either way, carrying
both surfaces invites confusion.

Labels: cleanup, mock-finder, provenance.

title: [INFRA] Regression Guardrails and CI Benchmarking
description:
# Infrastructure: Regression Guardrails and CI Benchmarking

## Purpose

Ensure performance optimizations don't regress over time. This task sets up:
1. Automated benchmark comparison in CI
2. Performance thresholds that fail the build
3. Baseline tracking across commits

## Current State

### Existing Guardrails
- `tests/robot_perf.rs`: Latency thresholds for robot commands
- `tests/cli_robot.rs:334`: Sessions output metamorphic parity
- `src/search/tantivy.rs:785`: title_prefix matching test

These are correctness tests, not performance regression tests.

### Missing
- Automated benchmark comparison in CI
- Baseline storage and tracking
- Threshold-based failure for regressions

## Proposed Solution

### 1. GitHub Actions Workflow for Benchmarks

```yaml
# .github/workflows/perf.yml
name: Performance Benchmarks

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  bench:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Install Rust (nightly)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@nightly
        
      - name: Restore baseline
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: target/criterion
          key: bench-baseline-${{ github.base_ref }}
          
      - name: Run benchmarks
        run: cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- --save-baseline pr
        
      - name: Compare to baseline
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          cargo install critcmp
          critcmp main pr --threshold 10
          # Fails if any benchmark regresses by >10%
          
      - name: Save baseline (on merge to main)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: |
          cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- --save-baseline main
```

### 2. Critical Benchmark Thresholds

| Benchmark | Threshold | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| `search_latency` | < 50 µs | TUI responsiveness |
| `vector_index_search_50k` | < 10 ms (after opts) | Semantic search target |
| `index_small_batch` | < 20 ms | Indexing throughput |
| `canonicalize_long_message` | < 500 µs (after opt) | Index-time target |

### 3. Memory Regression Tests

```rust
// tests/perf_memory.rs
use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

struct TrackingAllocator;

static ALLOCATED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
static PEAK: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

#[global_allocator]
static ALLOC: TrackingAllocator = TrackingAllocator;

unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for TrackingAllocator {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let ptr = System.alloc(layout);
        if !ptr.is_null() {
            let current = ALLOCATED.fetch_add(layout.size(), Ordering::SeqCst) + layout.size();
            PEAK.fetch_max(current, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
        ptr
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        ALLOCATED.fetch_sub(layout.size(), Ordering::SeqCst);
        System.dealloc(ptr, layout)
    }
}

#[test]
fn indexing_peak_memory_regression() {
    // Index test corpus
    let _stats = index_test_corpus();
    
    let peak_mb = PEAK.load(Ordering::SeqCst) / 1_000_000;
    assert!(peak_mb < 350, "Peak memory {}MB exceeds 350MB threshold", peak_mb);
}
```

### 4. Benchmark Result Artifact Collection

```yaml
- name: Upload benchmark results
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: benchmark-results
    path: target/criterion/**/*.json
    retention-days: 30
```

This enables historical analysis and trend detection.

## Implementation Checklist

1. [ ] Create `.github/workflows/perf.yml`
2. [ ] Add `critcmp` comparison step
3. [ ] Set appropriate thresholds for each benchmark
4. [ ] Add memory tracking test
5. [ ] Configure artifact retention
6. [ ] Add PR comment bot for benchmark diffs (optional)
7. [ ] Document threshold rationale in README

## Validation Commands

After implementing, verify with:
```bash
# Run benchmarks locally
cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- --save-baseline before

# Make a change
# ...

# Compare
cargo bench --bench runtime_perf -- --save-baseline after
cargo install critcmp && critcmp before after
```

## Dependencies

- Should be set up BEFORE implementing P0 optimizations
- Provides baseline for measuring optimization impact
- Prevents future regressions from erasing gains

title: SQLite source-scan cap is applied before query filters
description: The bounded source-table fallback in src/search/query.rs selects the first SQLITE_MESSAGE_SCAN_FALLBACK_LIMIT messages by global m.id, then applies agent, workspace, created-range, source, and session-path filters in Rust. A selective filter whose valid rows begin after the global cap therefore returns a false empty or truncated page even when its filtered corpus is within the bounded scan budget. Push the existing filter semantics into the parameterized source SQL before ORDER BY/LIMIT while retaining post-hydration defense and the bounded text scan.

Fresh-eyes review also found the existing normalized_search_origin_kind_sql_expr was not a true twin: no-source/no-kind/no-host legacy rows were SQL-remote but Rust-local. FLAKY timing assertion. tests/e2e_large_dataset.rs::incremental_index_on_large_base at line 573-577:

    assert!(
        incremental_duration_ms < full_duration_ms,
        "Incremental index ({} ms) should be faster than full index ({} ms)",

3. Use deterministic timing instead of wall-clock — count work items processed or use tracing spans.

title: Phase 2: Encryption Engine
description:
# Phase 2: Encryption Engine

**Parent Epic:** coding_agent_session_search-zv6w
**Depends On:** coding_agent_session_search-6uo3 (Phase 1: Core Export)
**Estimated Duration:** 1-2 weeks

## Goal

Implement the cryptographic foundation: envelope encryption with Argon2id key derivation, AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption, and key slot management for multiple passwords/recovery secrets.

## Why Envelope Encryption

Unlike direct password-based encryption, envelope encryption separates the DEK (data encryption key) from user passwords:

- **DEK** (random 256-bit): Encrypts the actual payload
- **KEK** (key encryption key): Derived from password via Argon2id, wraps DEK
- **Key slots**: Multiple KEKs can wrap the same DEK

Benefits:
1. Password rotation without re-encrypting payload
2. Multiple passwords (like LUKS disk encryption)
3. Recovery secret independent from user password
4. AAD binding prevents chunk swapping attacks

## Cryptographic Parameters

### Key Derivation (Argon2id for passwords)
```
Memory:     64 MB (65536 KB)
Iterations: 3
Parallelism: 4
Salt:       16 bytes (random per slot)
Output:     32 bytes (256-bit KEK)
```

### Key Derivation (HKDF-SHA256 for recovery secrets)
```
Salt:   16 bytes (random per slot)
Output: 32 bytes (256-bit KEK)
```

### Payload Encryption (Chunked AEAD)
```
Algorithm:   AES-256-GCM
Key:         256-bit DEK (random per export)
Chunk size:  8 MiB default (max 32 MiB)
Nonce:       96-bit counter-based (prefix || counter)
AAD:         export_id || chunk_index || schema_version
Auth tag:    128 bits per chunk
```

### Key Wrapping
```
Algorithm:   AES-256-GCM
Key:         256-bit KEK
Nonce:       96 bits (random per slot)
AAD:         export_id || slot_id
```

## Streaming Encryption Pipeline

For large archives, encryption MUST stream: SQLite → compress → chunk → encrypt → write

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SQLite DB → deflate compress → 8MB chunks → AEAD encrypt   │
│                                              ↓              │
│                              payload/chunk-00000.bin        │
│                              payload/chunk-00001.bin        │
│                              ...                            │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

## New Rust Crate Dependencies

```toml
argon2 = "0.5"
aes-gcm = "0.10"
zeroize = "1.7"      # Secure memory clearing
flate2 = "1.0"       # Deflate compression
rand = "0.8"         # Cryptographic RNG
base64 = "0.22"      # For config.json encoding
```

## config.json Output Format

```json
{
    "version": 2,
    "export_id": "base64-16-bytes",
    "base_nonce": "base64-12-bytes",
    "compression": "deflate",
    "kdf_defaults": { "argon2id": {...} },
    "payload": {
        "chunk_size": 8388608,
        "chunk_count": 4,
        "files": ["payload/chunk-00000.bin", ...]
    },
    "key_slots": [
        { "id": 0, "slot_type": "password", "kdf": "argon2id", ... },
        { "id": 1, "slot_type": "recovery", "kdf": "hkdf-sha256", ... }
    ]
}
```

## Exit Criteria

1. Streaming encryption works for 1GB+ databases
2. Multiple key slots unlock same payload
3. Counter-based nonce derivation correct
4. AAD binding prevents chunk tampering
5. Memory usage bounded (O(1) with respect to DB size)
6. Zeroize clears secrets from memory

title: P3.4 Update robot-docs output format with provenance
description:
# P3.4 Update robot-docs output format with provenance

## Overview
Extend the robot-docs output format to include provenance information so AI agents
consuming CASS output can understand session origins.

## Implementation Details

### Robot Output Extension
The robot-docs format produces machine-readable search results. Extend it:

```markdown
# Search Results for "authentication bug"

## Result 1
- **Conversation ID**: conv_abc123
- **Agent**: claude-code
- **Workspace**: /Users/me/projects/myapp
- **Score**: 0.95
- **Timestamp**: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z
- **Source**: laptop.local (remote)
- **Synced At**: 2024-01-15T12:00:00Z

### Snippet
...code snippet here...
```

### Format Function Update
In the robot-docs formatting code:
```rust
fn format_robot_doc_result(hit: &SearchHit) -> String {
    let mut output = String::new();
    // ... existing fields
    
    // Add provenance
    let source_label = match (&hit.source_hostname, &hit.source_type) {
        (Some(host), SourceType::Remote) => format!("{} (remote)", host),
        (Some(host), SourceType::Local) => format!("{} (local)", host),
        (None, _) => "local".to_string(),
    };
    output.push_str(&format!("- **Source**: {}\n", source_label));
    
    if let Some(synced) = &hit.sync_timestamp {
        output.push_str(&format!("- **Synced At**: {}\n", synced.to_rfc3339()));
    }
    
    output
}
```

### JSON Output Extension
For `--format json`:
```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct RobotJsonResult {
    // ... existing
    source_hostname: Option<String>,
    source_type: String,
    sync_timestamp: Option<String>,
}
```

## Dependencies
- Requires P3.3 (SearchHit has provenance fields)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Robot markdown output includes Source line
- [ ] Robot JSON output includes provenance fields
- [ ] Format consistent with existing robot-docs style
- [ ] Backward compatible (old tools can ignore new fields)

description:
**Origin:** Wave-2 LLM evidence-gathering in audit pass `2026-05-09T00-50-03Z` batch 3. Linked to:
- `coding_agent_session_search-ifr7` (P0 SIMD Dot Product Implementation)
- `coding_agent_session_search-lxn5` (P1 Parallel Vector Search)

**Parent:** `coding_agent_session_search-vz9t8` (audit-2026-05-09 epic).

## Background

Both originator beads documented a "Rollback Strategy" with named env vars (`CASS_SIMD_DOT=0` for ifr7, `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH=0` for lxn5) that operators could flip to disable the optimization if it regressed. The core work — SIMD dot product (in path-dep `frankensearch`) and parallel rayon search (in `frankensearch-index/src/search.rs`) — is fully implemented. **However**, no source file in cass actually reads either env var to gate the optimization at runtime.

> Verified gap (audit pass 2026-05-09T00-50-03Z, wave-2 batch 3 LLM evidence-gatherer):
> "MISSING `CASS_SIMD_DOT=0` rollback env var — documented in `docs/perf/baseline_round1.md:146` and planning doc, but no source file actually reads the env var. The core SIMD work is fully implemented (in path-dep `frankensearch`); only the documented rollback escape hatch is missing."
> "MISSING `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH=0` rollback env var — same pattern as ifr7."

## Acceptance criteria

### AC.1 — Wire `CASS_SIMD_DOT` env var

Add a single config-loading point in `src/lib.rs` (or `src/search/policy.rs` if that file is the natural home) that reads `CASS_SIMD_DOT` via `dotenvy::var()` (per AGENTS.md "NEVER use `std::env::var()` directly"). The value MUST be parsed as bool with the following semantics:

- Unset, `1`, `true`, `on`, `yes` → SIMD enabled (default; no behavior change from current).
- `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` → SIMD disabled; query path falls back to scalar dot product.
- Any other value → log a `tracing::warn!` and treat as enabled.

The setting MUST be read once at startup (cached in a `OnceLock<bool>`), not per-query.

### AC.2 — Wire `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH` env var

Same shape as AC.1, but gates the rayon parallel search path. Disabled mode MUST fall through to the existing single-threaded path (no removal of the parallel code; only a runtime gate).

### AC.3 — Numeric equivalence test for `CASS_SIMD_DOT`

Add `tests/perf_e2e.rs::simd_dot_runtime_toggle_equivalence`. It MUST:

- Generate a deterministic 1024-dim query vector and 100 deterministic 1024-dim doc vectors (seeded RNG).
- Compute top-10 cosine similarity ranking with `CASS_SIMD_DOT=1`.
- Compute the same ranking with `CASS_SIMD_DOT=0`.
- Assert ranking identity for top-10 (not just element-wise score equality, since rounding could permute mid-tier ties).
- For score equality, assert max absolute deviation ≤ 1e-6 across all 100 docs.
- Log structured outcome: `tracing::info!(target: "simd_toggle", n_docs = 100, dim = 1024, max_deviation = ..., ranking_match = true)`.

### AC.4 — Numeric equivalence test for `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH`

Add `tests/perf_e2e.rs::parallel_search_runtime_toggle_equivalence`. Same shape as AC.3 but compares rayon parallel vs single-threaded result sets. Top-10 ranking MUST be identical and result-set length MUST match exactly.

### AC.5 — Error-path test (invalid env value)

Add `tests/perf_e2e.rs::invalid_env_value_emits_warning_and_defaults_to_enabled`. Set `CASS_SIMD_DOT=banana`; assert:

- The cached config resolves to `enabled = true`.
- A `tracing::warn!` was emitted (use `tracing-test::traced_test`).
- The query path runs without panic.

### AC.6 — Edge-case test (env var changed mid-run)

Add `tests/perf_e2e.rs::env_var_change_mid_run_does_not_affect_cached_config`. Set `CASS_SIMD_DOT=1`; run a query; set `CASS_SIMD_DOT=0`; run another query; assert both queries used the same SIMD path (the `OnceLock` cached the first read). This documents the deliberate startup-only semantics.

### AC.7 — E2E test script (status surface)

Add `scripts/tests/yvv7r_rollback_envvars_e2e.sh` (rch-wrapped). The script MUST:

- Build cass.
- Run `cass health --json` with each combination of (`CASS_SIMD_DOT={1,0}`, `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH={1,0}`) — 4 scenarios.
- For each scenario, parse `cass health --json` output and assert it includes the optimization status under a new field `runtime_optimizations` with shape:
  ```json
  {"runtime_optimizations": {"simd_dot": true|false, "parallel_search": true|false, "config_source": "env|default"}}
  ```
- Log each scenario's result with `tracing::info!`-style stderr line.
- On any scenario failure, dump the full `cass health` output to `${RCH_TARGET_DIR:-/tmp}/cass-yvv7r-e2e.log` and exit 1.

### AC.8 — Health-surface change

`cass health --json` MUST grow a new `runtime_optimizations` object as in AC.7. This makes the env-var state introspectable for operators and monitoring. Update the health golden test under `tests/golden_robot_json.rs` accordingly; regenerate goldens via `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 rch exec -- cargo test`.

### AC.9 — README update

`README.md` "Complete Environment Variable Reference" table grows two rows under a new **Performance / Search Toggles** subsection:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `CASS_SIMD_DOT` | enabled | Set to `0` to disable SIMD dot product (rollback escape hatch). Read once at startup. |
| `CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH` | enabled | Set to `0` to fall back to single-threaded vector search. Read once at startup. |

### AC.10 — Verification commands

```bash
# Unit + integration
rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cass-yvv7r-target \
  cargo test --test perf_e2e simd_dot_runtime_toggle parallel_search_runtime_toggle invalid_env_value env_var_change -- --nocapture

# E2E
bash scripts/tests/yvv7r_rollback_envvars_e2e.sh

# Manual smoke
CASS_SIMD_DOT=0 cass search "rust async" --robot --limit 5 | jq '.hits | length'
cass health --json | jq '.runtime_optimizations'
```

### AC.11 — Rollback plan

This bead's whole purpose is rollback infrastructure, so meta-rollback is trivial:

- The new `runtime_optimizations` health field is additive — removing it is a one-commit change.
- The env var read is gated by the `OnceLock`; if the read itself misbehaves, force the fallback path by setting the var explicitly to `0` (which is the rollback semantic by design).
- Tests are isolated to `tests/perf_e2e.rs` and `scripts/tests/yvv7r_*.sh`; both can be deleted in one commit if needed.

## Out of scope

- Per-query toggle. Startup-cached only by design (the env-var contract is "operator flips, restarts cass, measures"; per-query toggling adds complexity without rollback value).
- Auto-detection of CPU SIMD capability. Already handled by frankensearch at compile time; this bead only adds runtime DISABLE, not auto-fallback on missing CPU features.

## Verification commit format

```
fix(search): wire CASS_SIMD_DOT + CASS_PARALLEL_SEARCH rollback env vars (coding_agent_session_search-yvv7r)
```

## Why P2 (medium priority)

These are operational safety nets — without them, if SIMD or parallel search regresses (e.g., on an unusual CPU), there's no fast escape hatch. Current state is fine for happy path, but the documented rollback strategy is unimplemented. **Blocks `8tgic` (SIMD tests)** which depends on `CASS_SIMD_DOT` existing.

## Audit artifacts

- `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-ifr7/`
- `/data/projects/coding_agent_session_search/beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-05-09T00-50-03Z/beads/coding_agent_session_search-lxn5/`

title: [DEFERRED] Opt 9: Approximate NN (IVF/HNSW) - Future Consideration
description:
# Deferred Optimization: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search

## Status: DEFERRED

This optimization is intentionally deferred due to:
1. Low confidence in user acceptance
2. High implementation effort
3. Requires explicit opt-in semantics

## From PLAN Section 6: Opportunity Matrix

| # | Optimization | Impact | Confidence | Effort | Score |
|---|-------------|--------|------------|--------|-------|
| 9 | Approximate NN (IVF/HNSW) | O(n) → O(√n) | **LOW** | **HIGH** | 2.0 |

## Why Deferred

**CASS is a precision-focused code search tool.**

Users searching their coding agent conversations expect:
- **Exact results** - not "close enough" results
- **Complete recall** - no relevant results missed
- **Deterministic behavior** - same query always returns same results

Approximate search would:
- Potentially miss relevant results
- Return different results on repeated queries
- Confuse users expecting exact matching

## If Implemented (Future)

### Requirements
1. **Explicit opt-in**: `--approximate` or `--mode=approximate` flag
2. **Clear warning**: "Results may be incomplete (approximate mode)"
3. **Recall metric**: Show estimated recall percentage
4. **Fallback**: Easy switch back to exact mode

### Technical Approach (for reference)
- **IVF (Inverted File Index)**: Cluster vectors, search only relevant clusters
- **HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)**: Graph-based approximate search
- **PQ (Product Quantization)**: Compressed vector representations

### Libraries to Consider
- `hora` - Rust native ANN library
- `faiss` bindings - Industry standard
- `annoy` bindings - Spotify's ANN library

### Expected Impact (if implemented)
- O(n) → O(√n) or O(log n) search complexity
- 50k vectors: ~1-2ms (vs 2-3ms with exact SIMD+parallel)
- Marginal benefit given current performance targets

## Decision Criteria for Future

Consider implementing when:
1. Index size exceeds 1M vectors
2. Users explicitly request faster approximate search
3. Search latency becomes noticeable (>100ms)

## Current Status

With optimizations 1-3 (F16 pre-convert + SIMD + parallel), we achieve:
- 56ms → 2-3ms (20-30x speedup)
- This is fast enough for interactive use

**No action needed at this time.**

title: [P2] Opt 7: SQLite N+1 Caching (Agent/Workspace ID Cache)
description:
# Optimization 7: SQLite N+1 Caching

## Problem Statement

During indexing, `ensure_agent` and `ensure_workspace` are called per conversation, resulting in N+1 query patterns:

### Current Behavior
For each conversation:
1. `INSERT INTO agents ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (ensure agent exists)
2. `SELECT id FROM agents WHERE name = ?` (get agent ID)
3. `INSERT INTO workspaces ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (ensure workspace exists)
4. `SELECT id FROM workspaces WHERE path = ?` (get workspace ID)

### Scale
- 3000 conversations = 12,000 SQL queries just for agent/workspace lookups
- Most conversations share the same agent (e.g., "claude") and workspace

### Syscall Evidence (from strace)
```
Indexing syscalls (36k messages):
- futex: 22,689
- pwrite64: 31,443
- pread64: 9,109
```

The `pread64` calls include redundant agent/workspace lookups.

## Proposed Solution

Cache `HashMap<String, i64>` for agent IDs and workspace IDs per indexing batch.

### Implementation Location
- File: `src/storage/sqlite.rs` (or wherever indexing happens)
- Add batch-scoped caches

### Code Sketch
```rust
struct IndexingBatch {
    agent_cache: HashMap<String, i64>,
    workspace_cache: HashMap<String, i64>,
}

impl IndexingBatch {
    fn get_or_create_agent_id(&mut self, conn: &Connection, name: &str) -> Result<i64> {
        if let Some(&id) = self.agent_cache.get(name) {
            return Ok(id);
        }
        
        // Ensure agent exists
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO agents (name) VALUES (?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
            [name],
        )?;
        
        // Get ID (might be from existing row)
        let id: i64 = conn.query_row(
            "SELECT id FROM agents WHERE name = ?",
            [name],
            |row| row.get(0),
        )?;
        
        self.agent_cache.insert(name.to_string(), id);
        Ok(id)
    }

    fn get_or_create_workspace_id(&mut self, conn: &Connection, path: &str) -> Result<i64> {
        if let Some(&id) = self.workspace_cache.get(path) {
            return Ok(id);
        }
        
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO workspaces (path) VALUES (?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
            [path],
        )?;
        
        let id: i64 = conn.query_row(
            "SELECT id FROM workspaces WHERE path = ?",
            [path],
            |row| row.get(0),
        )?;
        
        self.workspace_cache.insert(path.to_string(), id);
        Ok(id)
    }
}
```

### Cache Lifetime
- Created at start of indexing batch
- Dropped at end of batch
- Not persisted across separate `cass index` invocations

## Expected Impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Agent lookups (3000 convs, 1 agent) | 6000 queries | 2 queries |
| Workspace lookups (3000 convs, 50 workspaces) | 6000 queries | 100 queries |
| Total SQL queries | 12000+ | ~200 |

Actual latency improvement depends on:
- SQLite query overhead (~10-50µs per query)
- Network latency (if using remote SQLite)
- Whether SQLite page cache is warm

## Isomorphism Proof

This caching is safe because:
1. **Resulting IDs are identical**: Same INSERT...ON CONFLICT + SELECT logic
2. **Transaction boundaries unchanged**: Cache is batch-scoped
3. **No state leakage**: Cache cleared between batches
4. **Deterministic mapping**: agent name → ID is deterministic within a batch

### Verification
```rust
#[test]
fn cached_vs_uncached_same_ids() {
    let corpus = test_corpus();
    
    // Index without cache
    let ids_uncached = index_without_cache(&corpus);
    
    // Index with cache
    let ids_cached = index_with_cache(&corpus);
    
    assert_eq!(ids_uncached, ids_cached);
}
```

## Edge Cases

### New Agent/Workspace Mid-Batch
Handled correctly: cache miss triggers INSERT...ON CONFLICT + SELECT.

### Concurrent Indexing
If multiple processes index simultaneously:
- INSERT...ON CONFLICT handles races correctly
- Cache is process-local, so no cross-process issues
- Worst case: redundant queries (correctness preserved)

### Database Schema Changes
If `agents` or `workspaces` tables are modified externally:
- Cache may have stale IDs
- Acceptable: rare scenario, batch-scoped cache means short staleness window
- Fix: Could add cache invalidation on batch start (query max ID)

## Verification Plan

1. **ID equivalence test**: Cached vs uncached produce same agent/workspace IDs
2. **SQL query count test**: Measure query reduction with `PRAGMA profile`
3. **Benchmark**: Index time with/without caching

## Rollback Strategy

Environment variable `CASS_SQLITE_CACHE=0` to:
- Disable ID caching
- Query database for every agent/workspace lookup
- Useful for debugging ID-related issues

## Dependencies

- None (independent of search path)
- Index-time only optimization

title: Golden-freeze cass export-html output (scrubbed HTML with embedded styles + script)
description:
'cass export-html' produces a self-contained HTML file (meta + embedded CSS + embedded JS + conversation payload). The encryption variant also embeds an AES-GCM wrapped payload. Today tests/pages_export.rs checks fragments (specific tags / selectors) but the COMPLETE HTML shape — DOCTYPE, meta encoding, Open Graph tags, syntax-highlight style block, embedded script structure, payload framing — is not byte-compared against a golden. Subtle regressions (e.g. a script tag moving outside head, a style rule dropped, a meta attribute rename) slip through all existing assertions.

GAP:
- tests/fixtures/golden/ only covers NormalizedConversation serialization, not the rendered HTML export.
- tests/pages_export.rs uses fragment checks ('contains the conversation title', 'contains the message content') — no full-output golden.

Add two golden HTML files under tests/golden/html_export/:
  - basic_export.html.golden (unencrypted, representative 3-message conversation)
  - encrypted_export.html.golden (password-derived key, deterministic salt via test-only override)

Use Pattern 5 (canonicalized golden) + Pattern 2 (scrubbed golden):
  - Canonicalize: normalize line endings, strip trailing whitespace per line
  - Scrub: ISO timestamps, duration strings, cass version string (-[VERSION]), any UUID-like ids, the encryption salt + IV bytes (require a test-only seed override, e.g. CASS_EXPORT_DETERMINISTIC_SEED=...), and absolute paths embedded as data-* attributes
  - Keep: DOCTYPE, meta tags, style block key selectors, script block structure, rendered message HTML

Because the export bundles syntax-highlight CSS, expect a large golden (~20-50KB). Keep it under 100KB per the skill's checklist; if larger, split into htmldoc_head.golden + htmldoc_body.golden. PROVENANCE records the fixture conversation, cass version, and regeneration command.

DONE WHEN:
- 2 scrubbed golden HTML files in tests/golden/html_export/ committed + human-reviewed
- tests pass under rch exec cargo test --test pages_export_golden
- Encryption test reproducibly generates the same ciphertext (deterministic salt/IV seeded via test-only env var)

# Master Plan: Comprehensive Analytics in cass (Tokens, Cost, Tool/Plan, Time-Series, UX)

## Why This Exists
AI coding agents leave behind high-signal logs (conversations, tool calls, model usage). Those logs already live in cass as the unified, local knowledge base. The missing piece is **first-class analytics** so that humans and other agents can answer:

- How many tokens did I spend per hour/day/week/month?
- Which agent(s) were responsible? Which project/workspace? Which machine/source?
- How much of that is **real provider usage** vs **content-length estimates**?
- What share of work is tool-heavy vs plan-heavy?
- What did this cost (USD) based on model pricing?
- Can I see these patterns as charts and drill down to the exact sessions/messages?

Design constraint: **local-only, privacy-respecting, derived-data rebuildable, and robot-first.**

## Definitions (Avoid Confusion)
### Two Token Notions
We must carry both throughout the system.

1. **API usage tokens** (cost/compute relevant)
   - Source: provider usage blocks when available
   - Example: Claude Code `message.usage` exposes input/output/cache/thinking tokens
   - Used for cost estimation and “benchmark per MM tokens” questions

2. **Content token estimate** (corpus/length relevant)
   - Source: message content itself (deterministic estimate)
   - Current heuristic: `content_chars / 4`
   - Applies to every connector uniformly, used for coverage + comparisons

### Data Quality / Coverage
Every aggregation must report:
- how many messages had real API usage
- how many used estimation fallback
- which connectors/models are missing token usage

This is not optional: analytics without coverage reporting becomes self-deception.

## Data Sources (Connector Reality)
- Claude Code: rich `usage` blocks (input/output/cache/thinking + model)
- Codex: token_count events exist, but must be wired to assistant turns (see `z9fse.5`)
- Cursor/OpenCode/Factory/Pi-Agent/Gemini: often provide model names; token usage varies
- Others: often no token usage, rely on estimates

## Storage: Current Reality (Two Analytics Tracks)
The SQLite schema currently contains two parallel analytics tracks:

### Track A: General Message Analytics
- `message_metrics` (fact table keyed by message_id)
- `usage_hourly` and `usage_daily` (rollups keyed by hour/day + agent/workspace/source)

This track supports:
- hour/day time series
- dimensions: agent_slug, workspace_id, source_id
- per-role counts for user/assistant (counts + content token est)
- tool_call_count (count only)
- has_plan + plan_message_count (count only)

### Track B: Token Ledger + Model/Cost (Legacy/Parallel)
- `token_usage` (per-message ledger with model fields)
- `token_daily_stats` (daily rollups by day + agent_slug + source_id + model_family)
- `model_pricing` (pattern-based pricing table)
- conversations table has token summary columns (total tokens, estimated_cost_usd, etc)

This track supports:
- model-family breakdown
- per-conversation summaries

### Critical Problem: Coherency
- Ingest currently populates BOTH Track A and Track B.
- Rebuild/backfill currently rebuilds ONLY Track A (`rebuild_analytics()` clears + repopulates message_metrics + usage_*).
- Cost estimation columns exist, but cost is not computed yet (estimated_cost_usd remains NULL/0).

This means it is possible for Track B to drift/stale. This must be fixed before analytics are exposed broadly.

## Desired End State
1. **Single coherent analytics contract** surfaced via CLI and UI.
2. All derived analytics tables are either:
   - fully rebuildable from SQLite `messages`/`conversations`, OR
   - clearly deprecated and not used.
3. CLI and FrankenTUI use the same internal query layer so results match.
4. Tests enforce invariants and keep performance regressions out.

## Query Semantics (Non-Negotiable)
- Buckets are UTC.
- Buckets are based on message created_at when available; fallback to conversation started_at.
- All commands must be robot-safe:
  - stdout = data only (JSON)
  - stderr = diagnostics
  - exit codes follow cass conventions

## UX Plan (FrankenTUI)
Analytics should be exposed as a dedicated **Analytics view** with:

- A “recent activity” default (last 24h/7d) so it renders fast.
- A top filter strip consistent with search:
  - time range
  - source filter (local/remote/host)
  - agent filter
  - workspace filter
- A main dashboard with:
  - tokens over time (line/area)
  - coverage overlay (API vs estimated)
  - breakdown tables (agents/workspaces/models)
  - heatmap (daily sessions/messages)

Everything must support drill-down:
- Select a bucket -> show the sessions/messages that contributed
- Jump back into the standard search/detail view

Also: analytics must never block interactive search. All heavy queries run async; UI shows skeletons + progress.

## Testing Pyramid (Must Be Real)
- Unit tests: extraction shapes, time bucket boundaries, plan detector corpus
- Integration tests: fact rows == rollups invariants on synthetic DB
- CLI e2e: stable JSON outputs + capture stderr diagnostics
- FrankenTUI: snapshot/golden tests + PTY e2e flows for analytics navigation/drilldown

## How This Maps to Beads
This master comment is the canonical background. Individual beads reference it conceptually but must remain self-contained for implementation.

Key areas:
- CLI contract + schemas
- Ledger coherency (rebuild covers all derived tables)
- Coverage improvements (Codex wiring)
- Model + cost estimation
- UI dashboards/charts/drilldown
- Tests and perf guardrails

title: Task: Analytics schema + migrations (message_metrics + rollups)
description:
## Goal
Add ultra-efficient SQLite storage for token and usage analytics.

## Tables
- message_metrics (fact table; 1 row per message_id)
- usage_hourly (rollup; hour_id x dims)
- usage_daily (rollup; day_id x dims)

## Hard Requirements
- Buckets MUST be based on message created_at (not conversation started_at).
- Integer bucket ids (hour_id, day_id) for compact keys and fast range scans.
- Narrow schema: ints + small text dims only. No JSON blobs in analytics tables.
- Indexes for fast queries by time + agent_slug + workspace_id + source_id.

## Rollup Fields (v1)
Rollups must include enough counters to compute the requested averages:
- message_count, user_message_count, assistant_message_count
- tool_call_count
- plan_message_count
- api_coverage_message_count
- content_tokens_est totals (total/user/assistant)
- api token totals (total/input/output/cache_read/cache_creation/thinking)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Migrations create all tables, primary keys, and required indexes.
- Migration smoke test asserts tables and indexes exist.

## Testing & Logging

title: Task: Cost estimation (USD) from model_pricing + coverage diagnostics
description:
## Goal
Compute *historical* estimated USD costs from token usage using the existing SQLite analytics schema:
- per-message ledger: `token_usage.estimated_cost_usd`
- daily rollups: `token_daily_stats.estimated_cost_usd`
- conversation summaries: `conversations.estimated_cost_usd` (and friends)
- pricing table: `model_pricing` (pattern match + effective_date)

This must be:
- correct across time (pricing changes)
- deterministic (stable pattern selection)
- coverage-aware (never “fake precision” when pricing/model is unknown)

## Context (Current Reality)
- Ingest currently inserts `token_usage` rows with token components + model_name/provider/etc.
- `model_pricing` is already seeded, but cost is not computed (cost column left NULL/0).
- `token_daily_stats` includes `estimated_cost_usd` but is not populated.

## Design Requirements
1. **Pricing selection** (deterministic)
   - Match: `token_usage.model_name LIKE model_pricing.model_pattern` (and provider match when available).
   - Effective date: pick the row with the greatest `effective_date` that is <= message timestamp date.
   - Specificity tie-break: prefer the most specific pattern (longest pattern, or an explicit `priority` column if we add one).

2. **Component costs**
   - input: `input_tokens * input_cost_per_mtok / 1_000_000`
   - output: `output_tokens * output_cost_per_mtok / 1_000_000`
   - cache_read: if price present, include; else flag missing.
   - cache_creation: if price present, include; else flag missing.
   - thinking tokens: only compute if/when providers price it (usually not priced separately).

3. **Coverage / “no fake precision”**
   - If no pricing row is found:
     - `estimated_cost_usd` must be NULL (not 0.0), and we must track pricing coverage counts in queries.
   - If only some components are priced:
     - Either (A) compute partial USD and flag partial coverage, OR (B) treat as NULL.
     - Choose one policy and document it in robot-docs; whichever we choose must be stable.

4. **Performance**
   - Ingest path: cost computation must be O(inserted_messages) and avoid per-row SQL lookups where possible.
   - Backfill path: must run chunked and be able to handle millions of rows.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Pricing lookup utility**
   - Add `pricing::lookup_model_price(model_name, provider, timestamp_ms)` that returns the chosen pricing row + diagnostics.
   - Add tests for ambiguous patterns and effective_date selection.

2. **Compute per-message USD**
   - During ingest (when building `TokenUsageEntry`), compute `estimated_cost_usd` using the lookup.
   - For backfill/rebuild (z9fse.13), recompute deterministically from messages -> token_usage.

3. **Roll up USD**
   - Update `TokenStatsAggregator` to sum `estimated_cost_usd` into `token_daily_stats.estimated_cost_usd`.
   - Update conversation summary updater (`update_conversation_token_summaries_in_tx`) to set `conversations.estimated_cost_usd` as SUM of non-null `token_usage.estimated_cost_usd`.

4. **Diagnostics**
   - Provide counts for:
     - priced vs unpriced messages
     - top unknown model names
     - partial pricing cases (if we allow partial USD)

## Acceptance Criteria
- token_usage rows created by ingest have correct `estimated_cost_usd` when pricing exists.
- token_daily_stats estimated_cost_usd equals SUM(token_usage.estimated_cost_usd) for that day/model_family slice.
- conversation estimated_cost_usd equals SUM(token_usage.estimated_cost_usd) for that conversation.
- Coverage diagnostics clearly report unknown models/pricing gaps.

## Testing & Logging
- Unit tests:
  - pricing selection (pattern specificity + effective_date)
  - arithmetic correctness and rounding
- Integration tests:
  - seed model_pricing + insert token_usage rows -> verify ledger + rollup + conversation summaries
- E2E scripts (extend z9fse.8):
  - index fixture -> `cass analytics cost --json` (once implemented) validates USD totals + coverage output
- Logging:
  - debug-level logs for pricing misses (sampled/throttled, not spammy)
close_reason: All acceptance criteria verified. Pricing lookup (PricingTable), cost computation (compute_cost), ingest integration, conversation summaries, daily rollups, analytics query layer, DerivedMetrics (cost_per_message, cost_per_1k_api_tokens), coverage diagnostics (PricingDiagnostics), and 8+10+4 unit tests all passing.

description:

title: Task: Analytics query library (shared by CLI + ftui dashboards)
description:
## Goal
Create a reusable analytics query layer (a small internal library) so we do NOT duplicate analytics logic across:
- `cass analytics ...` CLI (robot JSON)
- ftui analytics dashboards (interactive TUI)
- pages export analytics generator (optional future unification)

This is the “single source of truth” for bucket semantics, filters, week/month logic, derived metrics, and stable ordering.

## Why This Matters
If we implement analytics queries directly inside CLI handlers and then again inside the TUI, we will drift. Drift here is catastrophic because users will see different token totals depending on which view they use.

The query layer should be:
- fast: prefer rollups (`usage_hourly`/`usage_daily`, plus tool/model rollups when they exist)
- deterministic: stable ordering + stable rounding rules
- explicit about semantics: UTC boundaries, ISO week rules, coverage definition

## Proposed API (Rust)
Create `crate::analytics` with submodules:

1. `crate::analytics::types`
   - Filter structs: `AnalyticsFilter { since, until, agents[], workspaces[], sources[], roles[] }`
   - Grouping enum: `GroupBy { Hour, Day, Week, Month }`
   - Dimension enum: `Dim { Agent, Workspace, Source, Role, Model, Tool }`
   - Metric enum: `Metric { ApiTotal, ApiInput, ApiOutput, ContentEstTotal, ToolCalls, PlanCount, CoveragePct, UsdEstTotal, ... }`
   - Output structs for robot JSON (serde Serialize)

2. `crate::analytics::query`
   - `query_tokens_timeseries(conn, filter, group_by, metric_set) -> Timeseries`
   - `query_breakdown(conn, filter, dim, metric, limit) -> Vec<Row>`
   - `query_tools(conn, filter, group_by, metric_set, limit) -> ToolReport` (served from tool rollups when available)
   - `query_status(conn) -> AnalyticsStatus`

3. `crate::analytics::bucketing`
   - `hour_id_from_millis`, `day_id_from_millis` (already exist in storage)
   - helpers to map day_id -> iso_week_id and day_id -> month_id (UTC)

4. `crate::analytics::derive`
   - derived averages computed safely (divide-by-zero safe, explicit nulls)
   - token component composition (`api_total = in+out+cache_read+cache_creation+thinking`)

## Semantics (Must Be Written Down)
- All buckets are UTC.
- Weeks are ISO-8601 weeks (Mon start). Output key must include both `iso_year` and `iso_week`.
- Months are calendar months UTC (year + month).
- Coverage definition: `api_coverage_message_count / message_count` where “api coverage message” means `api_data_source == 'api'`.

## Implementation Constraints
- Prefer rollup tables:
  - hour queries read `usage_hourly`
  - day/week/month queries read `usage_daily` and aggregate (week/month)
  - tools queries read tool rollups (z9fse.6) when present
- If a request asks for a metric not representable from rollups, either:
  - explicitly reject with a clear error, OR
  - require `--deep` and use message_metrics scan with visible perf warning + `_meta.path="slow"`

## Acceptance Criteria
- CLI analytics commands (z9fse.3.*) call this module (no duplicated SQL in CLI handlers).
- ftui analytics views use the same module for DB-backed queries.
- Unit tests cover:
  - week/month boundary logic
  - derived metric math
  - ordering stability (bucket sorting)
- Integration tests seed rollup rows and verify query outputs exactly.

## Testing & Logging
- Unit: boundary tests for iso weeks (year transitions) and months.
- Integration: create a small in-memory SQLite DB with rollup rows and assert outputs.
- Logging: debug spans include query name, filters, rows scanned, elapsed_ms.
notes: DEFERRED: Build CLI commands directly first (z9fse.3.x). Extract shared query library only when the TUI dashboard (2noh9.4.18) actually needs it. Premature abstraction risk.
close_reason: done

title: Task: Make analytics tracks coherent (rebuild covers token_usage/token_daily_stats + summaries)
description:
## Goal
Eliminate drift between analytics **Track A** and **Track B** so any rebuild/backfill produces a coherent, deterministic analytics state.

## Current Reality (2026-02-06)
- **Track A (v11)**: `message_metrics` + `usage_hourly` + `usage_daily`.
  - `SqliteStorage::rebuild_analytics()` currently clears + rebuilds **only Track A**.
- **Track B (v10)**: `token_usage` + `token_daily_stats` + conversation token summary columns (`conversations.total_*`, `grand_total_tokens`, `estimated_cost_usd`, `primary_model`, etc.).
  - Live ingest currently populates Track B.
  - Rebuild/backfill does **not** rebuild Track B.

Result: after running rebuild/backfill, Track B can be stale/inconsistent with Track A.

## Decision (v1)
- Keep both tracks for now (Track A drives general time-series; Track B carries model/pricing/cost + per-conversation summaries).
- Make rebuild/backfill **explicit** about which tracks are rebuilt and provide an **all-tracks** option.
- Add drift detection + invariants so drift cannot regress silently.

## Deliverables
1. **Rebuild API with track selection**
   - Implement rebuild modes:
     - Track A only (existing)
     - Track B only
     - All tracks (A then B)
   - Implementation options:
     - extend `SqliteStorage::rebuild_analytics()` with a mode enum, OR
     - add `rebuild_analytics_track_a()`, `rebuild_analytics_track_b()`, `rebuild_analytics_all()`.

2. **Track B rebuild/backfill**
   - Clear/rebuild in a transaction (chunked for large DBs):
     - clear `token_usage`
     - clear `token_daily_stats`
     - reset conversation summary columns to NULL/0
   - Recompute `token_usage` deterministically from messages by:
     - joining `messages` + `conversations` + `agents` + `workspaces`
     - calling `connectors::extract_tokens_for_agent(...)`
     - writing one ledger row per message with `data_source` preserved (`api` vs `estimated`)
   - Recompute `token_daily_stats` to match ingest semantics (prefer reusing `TokenStatsAggregator` so codepaths cannot drift).
   - Recompute conversation summary columns from `token_usage` (must match `update_conversation_token_summaries_in_tx`).

3. **Meta + drift signals**
   - Record meta keys (names tbd, but stable):
     - last rebuild timestamp
     - which tracks were rebuilt (`a|b|all`)
     - schema versions
   - Drift signals used by:
     - `cass analytics status --json`
     - `cass analytics validate --json`

4. **Invariants / guardrails**
   - Track A: rollups match `SUM(message_metrics)` for sampled buckets.
   - Track B: `token_daily_stats` matches `SUM(token_usage)` for the same (day, agent_slug, source_id, model_family) slice.
   - Conversation summaries match `SUM(token_usage)` per conversation.
   - Sanity: no negative counters; `api_coverage_message_count <= message_count`, etc.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After `rebuild(all)` on a fixture DB:
  - Track A + Track B row counts are non-zero and stable across two runs (idempotent).
  - Drift detector reports `possible=false`.
  - Validate invariants pass.
- On an intentionally drifted DB (e.g. delete `token_usage` rows):
  - status reports drift and recommends action.
  - validate returns actionable failure output.

## Testing & Logging
- Integration: small DB spanning 2 days + 2 agents + 2 workspaces; rebuild(all) passes invariants.
- Integration: drift injection test (delete/alter one table) is detected.
- Logging: per-track rebuild spans include rows/sec + total rows; avoid per-row spam.
close_reason: done

title: Task: Plan analytics v2 (token attribution + heuristic refinement + rollup support)
description:
## Goal
Upgrade plan analytics from **message counts** (v1) to **token attribution** + better heuristics so cass can answer:
- plan token share (how much of a day/week/month was planning vs doing)
- avg tokens per plan message / per plan event
- trends by agent/workspace/source

This is required for high-quality "tokens per plan" benchmarks and for the ftui Plans view (`2noh9.4.18.12`).

## Current State (v1, already in code)
- `message_metrics.has_plan` exists (cheap heuristic).
- `usage_hourly/usage_daily.plan_message_count` exists.
- There are tests for plan heuristic detection (see z9fse.7).

Gaps:
- We cannot attribute **tokens** to planning; only message counts.
- The heuristic is intentionally simple and will have false positives/negatives across agents.

## Deliverables
### 1) Define "Plan" Semantics (Documented)
V2 must explicitly define what counts as planning:
- default: assistant messages that contain a plan section (role == assistant)
- clarify whether to include tool messages or user planning prompts (default: exclude)
- define whether "plan" is:
  - message-level (good enough for v2.0)
  - section-level (optional v2.1)
  - multi-message plan events (optional v3)

### 2) Token Attribution (v2.0)
For each message, compute plan-attributed tokens as:
- if `has_plan == 1`:
  - `plan_content_tokens_est = content_tokens_est`
  - `plan_api_tokens = api_tokens_total` (when api-sourced)
- else: 0

This yields:
- `plan_token_share_content = plan_content_tokens_est_total / content_tokens_est_total`
- `plan_token_share_api = plan_api_tokens_total / api_tokens_total` (coverage-aware)

### 3) Storage Options (Pick One)
We need O(#buckets) query-time for plan token share.

**Option A (preferred if schema churn is acceptable): add columns to existing rollups**
- Add to `usage_hourly` and `usage_daily`:
  - `plan_content_tokens_est_total`
  - `plan_api_tokens_total`
  - (optional) component breakdowns if needed for cost attribution later

**Option B: add dedicated plan rollup tables**
- `plan_usage_hourly(hour_id, agent_slug, workspace_id, source_id)`
- `plan_usage_daily(day_id, agent_slug, workspace_id, source_id)`
- Keep `usage_*` unchanged; queries join (or return both sections).

Selection criteria:
- Option A makes tokens command simpler but requires careful migration/upsert updates.
- Option B avoids touching stable PK tables but adds join complexity.

### 4) Ingest + Rebuild
- Ingest: when constructing `message_metrics`, compute plan-attributed token deltas and feed into the chosen rollup strategy.
- Rebuild: must recompute plan rollups deterministically from rebuilt `message_metrics`.

### 5) Heuristic Refinement (v2.1)
Improve `has_plan` without going LLM-heavy:
- Add a curated corpus across agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini) of:
  - true plan messages
  - false positives (e.g., tool output listing steps)
  - false negatives (implicit plans)
- Heuristic improvements (examples):
  - require both a plan header/intent marker AND a structured list of steps
  - down-weight if content is dominated by tool output markers
  - add an upper bound on plan header distance from start of message

We must track heuristic versioning (meta key) so rebuild results are reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On fixtures spanning multiple buckets:
  - plan token share metrics are computed and stable.
  - divide-by-zero safe: share is null when denom=0.
  - coverage-aware: API share is null/explicit when api_tokens_total=0.
- Rebuild is idempotent: two rebuild runs produce identical plan rollups.
- Heuristic refinement reduces false positives on the curated corpus (target thresholds documented in test).

## Testing & Logging
- Unit: heuristic corpus tests + boundary cases.
- Integration: fixture DB verifies rollups == sum(message_metrics) for plan-attributed totals.
- Logging: debug-only sampling of plan-detection misses (throttled), plus rebuild spans with rows/sec.
close_reason: Completed: plan-token rollups, migration v13, assistant-only heuristic + corpus thresholds

title: Task: Live ingest analytics (message_metrics + batched rollups)
description:
## Goal
Compute token/tool/plan metrics once at ingest time and maintain hourly/daily rollups with minimal indexing overhead.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add hour_id/day_id helpers (hour_id based on UTC hours since a fixed epoch; day_id consistent with existing daily_stats helper).
2. During batched message inserts:
   - compute message_metrics fields (created_at_ms, role, dims, content chars + est tokens)
   - extract API usage tokens via existing extract_tokens_for_agent() helpers
   - compute tool_call_count + has_tool_calls (start with existing extraction coverage)
   - compute has_plan (cheap heuristic)
3. Insert message_metrics rows in the same transaction as messages.
4. Accumulate rollup deltas in-memory keyed by (bucket_id, agent_slug, workspace_id, source_id).
5. Flush rollups via multi-value INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (no per-message upserts).

## Hard Constraints
- No JSON parsing in hot paths that already have parsed structures (reuse connector-normalized fields).
- Rollup flush is batched once per transaction/chunk, not per message.
- All writes must be transactionally consistent (messages, message_metrics, rollups update together).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New indexed messages always create exactly 1 message_metrics row.
- usage_hourly and usage_daily match summed message_metrics for a synthetic fixture (exact equality).
- Indexing throughput regression is negligible (measure before/after on fixture corpus; record results).

## Testing & Logging
- Unit: hour_id/day_id conversion edge cases (timezone, boundaries).
- Integration: insert synthetic conversations and assert fact+rollups correctness.
- Logging: emit a single per-batch debug log with counts + timing (no per-message logs).
close_reason: Implemented live ingest analytics pipeline: MessageMetricsEntry, AnalyticsRollupAggregator, has_plan_heuristic, batch insert/flush functions. Wired into insert_conversations_batched. 2 integration tests pass. All 2379 tests pass.

comments.text:
# Analytics CLI Contract (Robot-First)

This comment is the canonical CLI/JSON contract for the analytics surface. The intent is: **agents can use analytics without reading code**.

## Command Tree (v1)
- `cass analytics status --json`
- `cass analytics tokens --json`
- `cass analytics models --json`
- `cass analytics cost --json`
- `cass analytics rebuild --json`
- `cass analytics validate --json`

Notes:
- Subcommand names and flag names must remain stable once published.
- stdout = JSON data only; stderr = diagnostics.

## Common Flags (all analytics subcommands)
- Time window:
  - `--since <time>` / `--until <time>` (ISO, relative like -7d, keywords today/yesterday)
  - convenience presets: `--days N`, `--today`, `--week`
- Filters:
  - `--agent <slug>` (repeatable or comma list)
  - `--workspace <path>` (repeatable or comma list)
  - `--source <local|remote|all|source_id>`
  - `--role <user|assistant|tool|system|all>` (advanced; may require deep/slow path)

## Output: `analytics status`
Purpose: a fast, high-signal snapshot for both humans and automation.

Suggested JSON shape:
```json
{
  "db_path": "...",
  "tables": {
    "message_metrics": {"rows": 123, "min_ts": 0, "max_ts": 0},
    "usage_hourly": {"rows": 0, "last_updated": 0},
    "usage_daily": {"rows": 0, "last_updated": 0},
    "token_usage": {"rows": 0, "min_ts": 0, "max_ts": 0},
    "token_daily_stats": {"rows": 0, "last_updated": 0}
  },
  "coverage": {
    "api_usage_message_pct": 0.0,
    "model_name_message_pct": 0.0,
    "notes": ["..."]
  },
  "drift": {
    "possible": false,
    "signals": ["..."],
    "recommended_action": "none|rebuild_all|rebuild_message_metrics|rebuild_token_usage"
  },
  "_meta": {"elapsed_ms": 0}
}
```

## Output: `analytics tokens`
Purpose: time-series usage.

Required capabilities:
- group-by: hour/day/week/month (UTC)
- dims: agent/workspace/source
- metrics:
  - api tokens: total/input/output/cache_read/cache_creation/thinking
  - content tokens: content_tokens_est_total
  - counts: message_count, user_message_count, assistant_message_count, tool_call_count, plan_message_count
  - coverage: api_coverage_pct
- derived:
  - api tokens per assistant msg
  - content tokens per user msg
  - tool calls per 1k tokens
  - planning share (once v2 plan attribution exists)

Response should be stable and ordered:
```json
{
  "group_by": "day",
  "filters": {"since": "...", "until": "...", "agent": ["claude_code"], "workspace": [], "source": "all"},
  "buckets": [
    {"key": "2026-02-01", "metrics": {"api_tokens_total": 0, "content_tokens_est_total": 0, "message_count": 0, "api_coverage_pct": 0.0}, "derived": {"api_tokens_per_assistant_msg": null}}
  ],
  "_meta": {"elapsed_ms": 0, "path": "rollup|slow_path", "warning": null}
}
```

If we must scan `message_metrics` (slow path), `_meta.path` must say so.

## Output: `analytics models`
- top models by API tokens and/or content-est tokens
- model coverage (percentage of messages with model_name)
- unknown bucket must be explicit

## Output: `analytics cost`
- estimated USD totals using `model_pricing`
- coverage diagnostics:
  - unknown pricing models
  - estimate-only vs api-usage
- must never present USD with false precision

## Output: `analytics rebuild`
- must be explicit about what is rebuilt:
  - Track A: message_metrics + usage_* rollups
  - Track B: token_usage + token_daily_stats + conversation summary columns

If we support `--all` / `--track a|b`, document it here.

## Output: `analytics validate`
- invariants results with actionable errors
- include sample bucket IDs and expected vs actual for failures

## Implementation Constraint
All query semantics (bucket boundaries, week/month rules, derived metrics) must live in `crate::analytics` (z9fse.12) so CLI and FrankenTUI dashboards cannot drift.

description:
## Objective
Build the production-grade analytics CLI skeleton so all analytics commands share one stable robot contract and one centralized argument model.

This task is the hard foundation for every downstream analytics command (`status`, `tokens`, `tools`, `models`, `cost`, `rebuild`, `validate`). If this shape is wrong, every later task drifts.

## Why This Matters
- Gives other agents a deterministic command surface they can depend on.
- Prevents duplicated flag parsing and inconsistent JSON behavior.
- Makes analytics discoverable via `--help` and `robot-docs` before deep features land.

## Scope
1. Add `cass analytics` command tree in clap wiring.
2. Register subcommands with stable names:
   - `status`
   - `tokens`
   - `tools`
   - `models`
   - `cost`
   - `rebuild`
   - `validate`
3. Define shared analytics flags and parsing model:
   - time range (`--since`, `--until`, `--days`)
   - dimensional filters (`--agent`, `--workspace`, `--source`)
   - bucketing (`--group-by hour|day|week|month`) where relevant
   - output mode (`--json` and robot-safe behavior)
4. Add dispatch stubs for each subcommand (even if implementation is deferred).
5. Wire placeholder hooks for `cass robot-docs analytics` topics so docs work can attach to a stable route.

## Contract Rules
- `stdout` must be data-only JSON in robot mode.
- Human diagnostics must go to `stderr`.
- Exit-code semantics must follow existing cass conventions.
- Do not introduce ad-hoc per-command parsing; all analytics commands must reuse shared parser structs/helpers.

## Test + Logging Requirements
- Unit tests for clap parsing:
  - command aliases and required args
  - repeated filter args
  - invalid enum values produce actionable errors
- E2E CLI tests (non-interactive) for:
  - `cass analytics --help`
  - each subcommand help
  - `--json` mode parseability and deterministic top-level schema envelope
- Failure logs must include command, exit code, stdout, stderr, and elapsed milliseconds.

## Out of Scope
- Computing analytics data itself (owned by child command tasks and query library work).
acceptance_criteria:
1. `cass analytics --help` lists all required subcommands and shared analytics flags with consistent wording.
2. All analytics subcommands parse common filters identically and reject malformed values with clear errors.
3. Robot mode behavior is uniform (`stdout` JSON, diagnostics on `stderr`, stable exit-code handling).
4. CI includes unit + e2e tests for parsing/help output, with detailed failure logs.
5. Downstream command tasks can implement data logic without touching clap tree plumbing.
notes: Design intent: keep this task narrow but high leverage. It should enable fast parallel implementation of command-specific analytics tasks while preventing contract drift.

title: Task: CLI analytics status (row counts, freshness, coverage, drift warnings)
description:
## Objective
Implement `cass analytics status --json` as the canonical health/quality endpoint for analytics data.

This command should answer, in one shot, whether analytics is trustworthy right now and what action to take if it is not.

## Scope
1. Report table-level state for both analytics tracks:
   - Track A: `message_metrics`, `usage_hourly`, `usage_daily`
   - Track B: `token_usage`, `token_daily_stats`, plus conversation summary coverage signals
2. For each table include high-signal metadata:
   - row counts
   - min/max timestamp coverage where applicable
   - last update timestamp
3. Report coverage diagnostics (not just totals):
   - API-token coverage %
   - model-name coverage %
   - estimate-only share
   - unknown/empty-model counts
4. Detect drift and coherence failures between tracks:
   - one track fresh while other is stale
   - missing rollups while source facts exist
   - rebuild mode mismatch symptoms
5. Emit recommended remediation action in output:
   - `none`
   - `rebuild_all`
   - `rebuild_track_a`
   - `rebuild_track_b`

## Output Contract
- Deterministic, machine-parseable JSON schema with explicit sections:
  - `tables`
  - `coverage`
  - `drift`
  - `_meta`
- No hidden heuristics; include concrete drift signals list so operators understand *why* a warning fired.

## UX Requirements
- Fast path (<~200ms on medium DBs, barring cold I/O).
- Human-readable warnings on stderr in non-json mode; JSON stays clean in stdout.

## Test + Logging Requirements
- Unit tests:
  - drift heuristic evaluation
  - coverage math edge cases (zero rows, partial rows)
- Integration tests with fixture DB states:
  - healthy
  - stale Track A
  - stale Track B
  - contradictory row-count/timestamp states
- E2E tests for command output stability:
  - parse JSON and verify required keys exist
  - verify recommended action under seeded drift states
- Detailed logs on test failure must include:
  - fixture profile
  - computed drift signals
  - emitted recommendation
acceptance_criteria:
1. `cass analytics status --json` returns a stable schema containing table stats, coverage metrics, drift signals, and recommended action.
2. Drift detection correctly distinguishes healthy vs stale/misaligned analytics tracks on fixture databases.
3. Coverage values are mathematically correct and robust for sparse/empty datasets.
4. Command behavior is robot-safe (`stdout` JSON only, diagnostics on `stderr`).
5. Unit/integration/e2e tests exist with high-signal logs that make failures immediately actionable.
notes: This command is the first line of defense for analytics trustworthiness. Other analytics commands should be gated or at least annotated when status reports significant drift.
close_reason: done

title: Task: CLI analytics tokens (hour/day/week/month + dims + derived averages)
description:
Implement `cass analytics tokens --json`: time-series token/usage analytics.

## Required Capabilities
- `--group-by hour|day|week|month` (UTC buckets; weeks are ISO-8601 weeks, Mon-start)
- Filters (repeatable / comma-list):
  - `--agent <slug>`
  - `--workspace <path>` (resolved to workspace_id)
  - `--source <local|remote|all|source_id>`

## Metrics (v1)
Must be representable from rollups for O(#buckets) queries:
- Counts: `message_count`, `user_message_count`, `assistant_message_count`, `tool_call_count`, `plan_message_count`
- Content estimate: `content_tokens_est_total`, `content_tokens_est_user`, `content_tokens_est_assistant`
- API tokens: `api_tokens_total`, plus components (`api_input_tokens_total`, `api_output_tokens_total`, `api_cache_*`, `api_thinking_tokens_total`)
- Coverage: `api_coverage_message_count` and derived `api_coverage_pct`

## Derived Metrics (v1)
- `api_tokens_per_assistant_msg` (null if assistant_message_count=0)
- `content_tokens_per_user_msg` (null if user_message_count=0)
- `tool_calls_per_1k_tokens` (define denominator explicitly; include both:
  - per 1k API tokens (when api_tokens_total>0)
  - per 1k content-est tokens)
- Planning:
  - **v1**: `plan_message_pct = plan_message_count / message_count`
  - **v2** (z9fse.14): `plan_token_share` (token-attributed), either via new rollups or an explicit slow-path.

## Performance Contract
- Prefer rollups:
  - hour: `usage_hourly`
  - day/week/month: `usage_daily` (aggregate for week/month)
- If a requested slice cannot be served by rollups, return a structured slow-path indicator in `_meta` (and optionally require an explicit `--deep`).

## Output Contract
- Stable ordering by bucket key.
- stdout = JSON only; stderr = diagnostics.
- `_meta` must include `{ elapsed_ms, path: "rollup"|"slow", warning?: string }`.

## Testing & Logging
- Integration (z9fse.8): fixture spanning multiple days/hours; totals match across group-bys.
- Unit: ISO week/month boundary correctness + divide-by-zero derived metrics.
- Logging: query spans include group_by, filters, rows read, elapsed_ms.

title: Task: CLI analytics validate (rollup invariants + drift detection)
description:
## Objective
Implement `cass analytics validate --json` as the correctness gate for analytics math and rollup integrity.

`status` tells us if data *looks* healthy; `validate` must prove key invariants actually hold.

## Scope
1. Implement fast invariant checks (default mode):
   - non-negative counters/tokens
   - required key columns present and non-null for aggregate keys
   - rollup rows exist for periods with source facts
2. Implement aggregate consistency checks:
   - sampled bucket sums in rollups equal recomputed sums from fact tables within tolerance
   - per-dimension totals reconcile with global totals
3. Implement cross-track drift checks:
   - Track A totals vs Track B totals are directionally consistent where overlap exists
   - identify stale/partial recomputation patterns
4. Provide two validation depths:
   - `--mode fast` (default): high-signal checks under ~1s on fixture DB
   - `--mode deep`: broader recomputation windows for CI/nightly confidence

## Output Contract
Return deterministic JSON with:
- `summary` (pass/fail + severity)
- `checks` array (id, status, measured, expected, tolerance, message)
- `drift_signals`
- `recommendations` (specific actions, not generic)
- `_meta` (elapsed_ms, mode, sample strategy)

## Performance + Safety
- Must be read-only and safe on live DB.
- Must fail closed: if a check cannot execute, report explicit `error` status rather than silently passing.

## Test + Logging Requirements
- Unit tests per check function and tolerance logic.
- Integration tests with intentionally corrupted fixture datasets:
  - off-by-one rollup
  - negative token rows
  - stale track mismatch
- E2E tests:
  - validate success case returns `pass`
  - seeded failure case returns `fail` with actionable checks
- Logging on failure must include:
  - failed check id
  - measured vs expected values
  - bucket/dimension keys used in comparison
acceptance_criteria:
1. `cass analytics validate --json` emits stable JSON listing individual checks and an overall pass/fail summary.
2. Default mode runs quickly on fixture DB while still catching intentionally seeded corruption.
3. Deep mode increases confidence by expanding recomputation scope without changing check semantics.
4. Cross-track drift and rollup mismatch errors are clearly diagnosable from output alone.
5. Unit/integration/e2e coverage includes detailed logs for every failing check.
notes: This command will be used as a preflight gate before trusting dashboards and before performance benchmarking runs.

title: Task: CLI analytics cost (USD estimates + pricing coverage)
description:
## Objective
Implement `cass analytics cost --json` for transparent USD estimation with explicit uncertainty and pricing coverage diagnostics.

## Scope

   - input/output/cache/thinking token components when available

   - % token volume matched to known pricing

4. Provide derived economics metrics:
   - cost per 1k API tokens
   - cost per assistant message
   - period-over-period delta

## Output Contract
Deterministic JSON sections:
- `filters`
- `pricing_coverage`
- `buckets`
- `breakdowns`
- `totals`
- `_meta`

Every monetary value should include explicit units (`usd`) and nullable semantics where computation is impossible.

## Precision / Safety Rules
- Use decimal-safe handling appropriate for currency.
- Avoid hidden rounding; round only for presentation layers while retaining raw numeric fields.
- Expose caveats in output when cost is partial.

## Test + Logging Requirements
- Unit tests:
  - pricing rule matching
  - cost math across token classes
  - rounding and nullability behavior
- Integration tests:
  - mixed priced/unpriced model datasets
  - sparse API token coverage
  - period breakdown correctness
- E2E tests:
  - stable JSON schema
  - known fixture yields expected totals and warnings
- Logging on failure must include pricing match trace and unmatched-model diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
